title: fix: dedup Claude token usage by message.id+requestId, fix Opus-4-6 pricing
body:
## Summary

- Dedup Claude token usage in `GetDailyUsage` by `(message.id, requestId)` to
  eliminate double-counting from DAG-fork sessions and streaming snapshots stored
  across multiple session rows.
- Fix `claude-opus-4-6` fallback pricing — was at 1/3 real Anthropic rates
  (5/25/6.25/0.50 instead of 15/75/18.75/1.50), causing silent under-costing
  when the LiteLLM pricing fetch fails.
- Bump `dataVersion` to 9 so existing databases re-parse and backfill the new
  dedup-key columns on first run.

## Investigation Details

A user reported that agentsview and ccusage report different token totals. We
investigated and found **two independent bugs in agentsview** plus a
**correctness issue in ccusage**:

### Bug 1: No cross-session token dedup (agentsview)

Claude Code writes streaming progress snapshots as multiple JSONL lines with the
same `message.id` and `requestId`. agentsview's `collapseStreamingDuplicates`
only collapses *consecutive* entries within a single file. When the DAG-fork
parser splits a file into multiple sessions, the same API response can end up
stored in both the main session and fork sessions — `GetDailyUsage` then sums
all of them.

**Fix:** Extract `message.id` and `requestId` during parsing, persist as
`claude_message_id` / `claude_request_id` columns on the `messages` table, and
dedup by `(msgID, reqID)` struct-key set at query time. Matches ccusage's
`createUniqueHash` dedup strategy. Rows with either key empty (legacy data,
non-Claude agents) are always counted.

### Bug 2: Opus-4-6 fallback pricing (agentsview)

`internal/pricing/fallback.go` shipped `claude-opus-4-6` at Sonnet-tier rates
(input=5, output=25) instead of Opus-tier rates (input=15, output=75). Affects
offline mode and LiteLLM-fetch-failure fallback path.

### Finding: ccusage first-wins streaming bug (upstream)

ccusage's dedup (`data-loader.ts:530-540`) uses a `Set` to skip entries whose
`${messageId}:${requestId}` hash was already seen. This keeps the **first**
streaming snapshot per message — which has partial `output_tokens` (often 1-5
tokens from the first chunk). The final snapshot (with the actual complete output
token count) is discarded. On the author's machine this causes ccusage to
under-report output tokens by ~2.7x vs the authoritative last-snapshot values.

This means the reported discrepancy ("ccusage shows 20% more output tokens") is
machine-dependent: it depends on the ratio of old-format streaming files (where
snapshots have progressive output_tokens) vs new-format files (where all
snapshots have identical final values). On our test machine the effect was
reversed — ccusage reported *less* than agentsview.

**We did not attempt to replicate ccusage's under-counting.** agentsview's
dedup keeps correct (final) token values. The remaining ~4% gap between
agentsview and raw-file ground truth is from DAG-fork row duplication within
single sessions, which the query-time dedup partially addresses.

## Changes

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `internal/pricing/fallback.go` | Fix Opus-4-6 rates to 15/75/18.75/1.50 |
| `internal/pricing/fallback_test.go` | Pin correct rates with struct equality |
| `internal/parser/types.go` | Add `ClaudeMessageID`, `ClaudeRequestID` on `ParsedMessage` |
| `internal/parser/claude.go` | Extract `message.id` + `requestId` in `extractClaudeTokenFields` |
| `internal/parser/claude_parser_test.go` | Test parser populates both fields |
| `internal/db/schema.sql` | Add `claude_message_id`, `claude_request_id` columns |
| `internal/db/db.go` | Column migration + bump `dataVersion` 8 → 9 |
| `internal/db/messages.go` | Plumb new columns through struct, insert, and select |
| `internal/db/usage.go` | Dedup by `(msgID, reqID)` struct key + deterministic `ORDER BY` |
| `internal/db/usage_test.go` | Tests for cross-session dedup + empty-key fallback |
| `internal/db/orphaned.go` | Forward-compat: include new columns in orphaned copy probe |
| `internal/sync/engine.go` | Pass dedup keys through `toDBMessages` |

## Schema migration

Two `ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN` with `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` — O(1)
metadata change in SQLite (no row rewrite). The `dataVersion` bump triggers a
full resync on next open (~60-90s on a 6.8k-file DB) to backfill the columns
from source JSONL files.

**Limitation:** Orphaned sessions (source files deleted before upgrade) cannot
be backfilled. Their dedup keys remain empty and bypass dedup. Forward-compat
probe added so future version bumps carry the keys forward.

## Not in scope

- **PostgreSQL push parity** — deferred. When revisiting: add columns to PG
  schema, update `MessageTokenFingerprint` to include them (otherwise push
  fast-path skips re-sending backfilled rows), mirror in push INSERT.
- **DAG-fork row staleness** — the parser's DAG walk can produce more message
  rows than unique messages in the source file. Query-time dedup hides this for
  token sums. Fixing the parser itself is a separate, more invasive change.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -tags fts5 ./...` — all packages pass
- [x] `TestFallbackPricing_Opus46Rates` pins correct Opus rates
- [x] `TestParseClaudeSession_ExtractsMessageIDAndRequestID` verifies parser
  populates both dedup fields
- [x] `TestGetDailyUsage_DedupesByClaudeMessageAndRequestID` — shared message
  across main+fork sessions counted once
- [x] `TestGetDailyUsage_MissingDedupKeysCountedEveryTime` — empty-key rows
  not incorrectly deduped
- [ ] Manual: `make install`, quit/restart desktop app, verify `usage daily`
  output after resync

title: fix(usage): track cost for opencode and pi; sync codex exec sessions
body:
## Summary

The usage dashboard reported $0 for users running OpenAI models through opencode and pi. Their parsers did not store a per-message model id or token usage, so the usage query filter (`m.model != '' AND m.token_usage != ''` in `internal/db/usage.go:110-114`) excluded every row. Fresh web-only installs also saw $0 across all agents because `model_pricing` was only populated by the `agentsview usage` CLI. This PR also folds in a codex exec import fix so users get both under the single resync triggered by the data version bump.

## Changes

**opencode parser** — extracts `modelID` and `tokens.{input,output,cache.{read,write}}` from the assistant message data blob via gjson. Gates on at least one recognized field so foreign or empty `tokens` objects do not fabricate a zero row. Coverage flags follow field presence, preserving explicit zero usage from errored requests.

**pi parser** — extracts `message.model` and `message.usage.{input,output,cacheRead,cacheCreation}` from assistant entries, falls back to the most recent `model_change.modelId` when a message has no inline model. Same field-gating and zero-preservation rules.

**Session rollups** — both parsers now call `accumulateMessageTokenUsage` so `HasTotalOutputTokens`, `TotalOutputTokens`, and `PeakContextTokens` populate alongside Claude and Codex.

**Codex exec sessions in bulk sync** — `internal/parser/codex.go` drops the `includeExec` filter that skipped sessions with `originator=="codex_exec"` during bulk sync. `internal/sync/engine.go` and `internal/server/events.go` stop threading the flag through; `internal/parser/codex.go` exposes `IsCodexExecSessionFile` for discovery. Non-interactive codex exec sessions are now imported alongside interactive ones.

**Data version** — `dataVersion` bumps to 10 so existing databases reparse opencode, pi, and codex rows to pick up both the new usage fields and the previously skipped codex exec sessions in a single resync.

**Pricing seed on startup** — `seedPricingIfEmpty` upserts `pricing.FallbackPricing()` synchronously then refreshes from LiteLLM in a background goroutine. Fresh installs and resync swaps never observe an empty `model_pricing` table, and the server never blocks startup behind the 30s LiteLLM HTTP timeout. A follow-up to bundle a full LiteLLM snapshot as the offline fallback is tracked in #315.

**Cost Over Time chart** — reserves `TOP_PAD=10` headroom in the plot area and rounds the y-axis maximum up to the next `1/2/2.5/5/10 × 10ⁿ` step via `niceCeil`. The tallest bar and the top y-axis label ascenders no longer clip against the SVG viewBox edge, and tick labels land on round numbers.

title: Bundle LiteLLM pricing snapshot as offline fallback
body:
## Problem

The current `pricing.FallbackPricing()` hardcodes ~8 Claude/Codex
variants. Any user who is offline, air-gapped, or simply hasn't
completed the async LiteLLM refresh yet sees \$0 cost for every
model not on that list — including most OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex,
and Azure rates.

After #314 the server seeds the hardcoded fallback synchronously
and refreshes from LiteLLM in the background, so online users
converge quickly. Offline and air-gapped users remain stuck on
the hand-maintained list.

## Proposal

Bundle a snapshot of LiteLLM's `model_prices_and_context_window.json`
inside the repo and embed it via `go:embed`, replacing the
hardcoded rate table in \`internal/pricing/fallback.go\`.

1. Commit \`internal/pricing/litellm_snapshot.json\` (~500KB).
2. Change \`FallbackPricing()\` to call
   \`ParseLiteLLMPricing(embeddedBytes)\` so the existing pricing
   shape is reused.
3. Add a \`make refresh-pricing\` target that downloads the
   upstream JSON, parses it to validate, and writes the snapshot.
   Optional: monthly Dependabot-style automation opens a refresh
   PR.
4. Consider pruning the snapshot at build time to the providers
   agentsview actually supports, to keep the binary lean.

## Benefits

- Offline and air-gapped users get the full multi-provider
  catalog instead of \$0 rows.
- Fresh installs are instant and complete; the two-stage async
  refresh in runServe can collapse back to a single sync upsert.
- \`internal/pricing/fallback.go\` stops being a hand-maintained
  list that drifts out of sync with reality.

## Tradeoffs

- Binary grows by ~500KB. Pruning to relevant providers would
  reduce that.
- Snapshot goes stale between releases, but live LiteLLM fetch
  still runs when online and the refresh target / automation
  keeps the committed copy current.

## Related

- #314 — adds the two-stage seed this issue would simplify.

title: usage statusline --offline reports ~3x higher cost than without --offline
body:
I set up `agentsview usage statusline --offline --no-sync` in my starship prompt following the [docs example](https://www.agentsview.io/token-usage/#agentsview-usage-statusline), and noticed the amount differs significantly from running without `--offline`:

```
> agentsview usage statusline --no-sync --agent claude
$134.58 today (claude)

> agentsview usage statusline --offline --no-sync --agent claude
$387.43 today (claude)
```

Running `usage daily` with `--breakdown` shows the difference is entirely in `claude-opus-4-6` — the token counts are identical, only the cost changes:

```
# without --offline
claude-opus-4-6  10927  327804  9313923  119924396  $126.42

# with --offline
claude-opus-4-6  10927  327804  9313923  119924396  $379.27
```

Sonnet and Haiku costs are the same in both modes.

The fallback rates in `internal/pricing/fallback.go` have `claude-opus-4-6` at $15/$75 (input/output per MTok), while LiteLLM returns $5/$25. I believe this may have been introduced in #312, which changed the fallback from $5/$25 to $15/$75 treating the original rates as Sonnet-tier.

[Anthropic's pricing page](https://www.anthropic.com/pricing) currently lists Opus 4.5 and 4.6 at $5/$25, with the $15/$75 rates applying to Opus 4.0 and 4.1. Could the fallback rates for `claude-opus-4-6` need reverting to the pre-#312 values?

- Windows 11

title: Implement usage view support for PostgreSQL read-only mode
body:
## Problem

The multi-host PostgreSQL feature exposes session-level token fields, but the dedicated `/usage` view does not work there.

Today the PostgreSQL store explicitly returns `db.ErrReadOnly` for:
- `GetDailyUsage`
- `GetTopSessionsByCost`
- `GetUsageSessionCounts`

That makes the usage API endpoints return `501 not available in remote mode`. As a temporary UI safeguard, the read-only PG UI no longer shows the Usage route, but the real gap is missing PostgreSQL-backed usage queries.

## Goal

Implement usage parity for the PostgreSQL read-only store so the `/usage` page works.

## Required work

- Implement PostgreSQL versions of:
  - `Store.GetDailyUsage`
  - `Store.GetTopSessionsByCost`
  - `Store.GetUsageSessionCounts`
- Preserve SQLite semantics:
  - include/exclude filters for project/agent/model
  - timezone-aware date bucketing with padded UTC bounds
  - Claude dedup by `(claude_message_id, claude_request_id)`
  - pricing joins / cost calculations
  - per-day model/project/agent breakdowns
  - top sessions ordering and limits
  - session counts parity with daily totals
- Add PostgreSQL integration tests (`pgtest`) that mirror the existing SQLite usage behavior for parity-critical cases.
- Re-enable the Usage route in the read-only PG UI once the API endpoints are implemented and tested.

## Notes

Relevant code:
- `internal/postgres/store.go`
- `internal/db/usage.go`
- `internal/server/usage.go`
- `frontend/src/lib/components/layout/AppHeader.svelte`
- `frontend/src/lib/components/layout/ThreeColumnLayout.svelte`
- `frontend/src/App.svelte`

title: feat: add PostgreSQL usage support; rename remote_access to require_auth
body:
Closes #326.

## Summary

- Add PostgreSQL-backed `/usage` queries for read-only mode
  (`GetDailyUsage`, `GetTopSessionsByCost`, `GetUsageSessionCounts`)
- Add additive PostgreSQL `model_pricing` schema support and sync
  pricing rows during `agentsview pg push`
- Fall back to built-in pricing rows on PG-backed viewers so
  already-deployed instances keep returning usage data before every
  host has pushed fresh pricing metadata
- Rename `remote_access` config to `require_auth` and make token
  auth opt-in instead of auto-enabled for non-loopback binds

## PG Usage

Closes the parity gap where session-level token fields were already
visible on PG-backed multi-host views, but the dedicated `/usage`
page returned `501 not available in remote mode`.

The implementation keeps the same high-level semantics as the SQLite
usage pipeline: timezone-aware date bucketing, Claude dedup by
`(claude_message_id, claude_request_id)`, include/exclude filters for
project/agent/model, per-day breakdowns, top-session ranking by
computed cost, and aligned session-count totals.

On the storage side, PostgreSQL gets an additive `model_pricing`
table. `pg push` syncs local pricing rows into PG before usage
queries run. PG viewers also overlay built-in fallback pricing so
upgraded read-only deployments remain usable before every exporter
has refreshed pricing data.

## Auth Rename

`remote_access` was a confusing name for token auth enablement, and
it auto-enabled whenever binding to a non-loopback address -- forcing
users on private networks (Tailscale, VPN, LAN) to deal with token
auth they don't need.

Changes:
- Renamed `remote_access` to `require_auth` across Go, TypeScript,
  and Svelte
- Auth is now opt-in: set `require_auth = true` in config or pass
  `--require-auth` on the CLI
- Legacy `remote_access` TOML key still recognized for backward
  compatibility (deleted from persisted config when `require_auth`
  is saved)
- Auto-bind to 0.0.0.0 skipped when managed Caddy proxy is active
  to preserve the loopback-backend invariant

## Upgrade / Rollout

- PostgreSQL: additive schema change only; no drop/recreate required
- Exporters: upgrade host binaries and run `agentsview pg push`
- PG-backed viewers can start serving `/usage` immediately after
  upgrading the reader binary
- Existing `remote_access = true` configs continue to work

title: Bug w/ fix(insights): Claude Code CLI outputs JSON array, not single JSON object
body:
## Bug

`insights generate` with `agent=claude` always fails with **\"claude returned empty result\"**.

## Root Cause

`generateClaude` in `internal/insight/generate.go` expected `claude -p --output-format json` to return a single JSON object:

\`\`\`json
{"result": "...", "model": "..."}
\`\`\`

But Claude Code CLI (v2.1.x+) returns a **JSON array** of structured events:

\`\`\`json
[
  {"type": "system", "subtype": "init", ...},
  {"type": "assistant", "message": {...}, ...},
  {"type": "result", "result": "...", "modelUsage": {"claude-haiku-4-5-20251001": {...}}}
]
\`\`\`

`json.Unmarshal` into `struct { Result string; Model string }` silently fails on an array, so `result` is always empty, triggering the error.

## Fix

Added `parseCLIJSONArray` which unmarshals the output as `[]json.RawMessage`, finds the element with `"type":"result"`, and extracts `result` and the model name from `modelUsage`. Updated all affected tests to use the correct array format.

See PR / commit for details.

title: fix(insights): correctly parse Claude Code CLI JSON array output
body:
## Problem (identified in #328)

The insights feature invokes the Claude Code CLI with `-p --output-format json`
to generate session summaries. Claude Code v2+ changed the output format from a
single JSON object to a **JSON array of events**, where the actual result is
carried in the element with `type: "result"`:

```json
[
  { "type": "system_prompt", ... },
  { "type": "turn", ... },
  { "type": "result", "result": "...", "modelUsage": { "claude-opus-4-5": {} } }
]
```

The previous parser expected the legacy single-object format:

```json
{ "result": "...", "model": "claude-opus-4-5" }
```

As a result, insight generation silently returned an empty result for any
installation running Claude Code v2+, falling through to the error path with a
confusing "no usable output" message.

## Solution

Extract the parsing logic into a dedicated `parseCLIResult` function that:

1. **Tries the JSON array format first** — iterates events, finds the element
   with `type: "result"`, reads its `result` field, and derives the model name
   from the first (sorted) key of `modelUsage`.
2. **Falls back to the legacy single-object format** — preserves compatibility
   with older Claude CLI versions that still emit `{"result":"...","model":"..."}`.

The model-name extraction from `modelUsage` sorts the keys before selecting so
the result is deterministic when multiple models are reported.

## Changes

- `internal/insight/generate.go` — replaced the inline JSON unmarshal with a
  call to `parseCLIResult`; added `parseCLIResult` with array-first / legacy
  fallback logic.
- `internal/insight/generate_test.go` — updated all existing test fixtures from
  the legacy format to the array format; added a new `TestParseCLIResult` table
  test covering both formats, edge cases (no result event, empty input, garbage
  input).

## Testing

All existing tests pass with the updated fixtures. The new `TestParseCLIResult`
test covers:

- Array format with a `result` event
- Legacy single-object format (backward compat)
- Array with no `result` event
- Empty input
- Non-JSON garbage input

title: pg push: slow for large databases due to per-session PG round-trips
body:
## Problem

`pg push` is slow on large databases. With ~35K sessions, an incremental push that only needs to sync 8 changed sessions still evaluates ~54K candidate sessions against PG, each requiring multiple PG round-trips.

```
Pushing... 450/54038 sessions, 0 messages
```

Most sessions are no-ops (PG already matches local), but the current architecture checks each one individually inside a transaction.

## Root Causes

1. **Candidate window too wide** — `ListSessionsModifiedBetween` returns all sessions since `lastPush`, and fingerprint filtering only prunes if prior boundary state exists. When boundary state is empty or stale, all sessions pass through.

2. **Per-session PG round-trips** — `pushBatch` opens a transaction for each batch of 50 sessions, then for each session: upserts the session row, queries PG message count + content fingerprint, compares against local, and only then decides to skip. That's multiple PG queries per session even when nothing changed.

3. **Multi-row INSERT instead of COPY** — message inserts use `INSERT ... VALUES` in batches of 100 rows. PostgreSQL's `COPY FROM` protocol (supported natively by pgx's `CopyFrom`) is 5-10x faster for bulk loads.

## Potential Improvements

- **Batch fingerprint check** — query PG for all candidate session fingerprints in one query, filter locally, then only push sessions that actually differ
- **Use `COPY FROM`** — pgx supports `CopyFrom` natively; switch `bulkInsertMessages`, `bulkInsertToolCalls`, and `bulkInsertToolResultEvents` to use it
- **Narrow the candidate window** — investigate why boundary state is empty/stale after normal incremental pushes, causing the full session list to be evaluated
- **Parallel session processing** — process independent sessions concurrently (within connection pool limits)

title: pg push overwrites original machine name on remote-synced sessions
body:
## Problem

Sessions imported via `agentsview sync --host` retain their original machine name locally (e.g. `home-nuc`), but `pg push` overwrites the machine field with the local `pg.machine_name` for every session pushed.

In `pushSession` (internal/postgres/push.go:747):

```go
sess.ID, s.machine,
```

This means all sessions appear to originate from the pushing machine in PG, losing the original host provenance.

## Expected Behavior

Sessions should preserve their original `sess.Machine` value when pushed to PG, so multi-machine views correctly attribute sessions to the machine they originated on.

## Impact

PG-backed viewers show all sessions under a single machine name instead of per-host, breaking machine-based filtering and attribution.

title: feat: session intelligence (signals, health, analytics, UI)
body: ## Summary Adds end-to-end session intelligence: per-session signal computation, outcome classification, a penalty-based health score with letter grade, and the storage / analytics / UI to surface them. Roughly +8.6k / -1.2k across 66 files. ## Claude session parser (`internal/parser/claude.go`) - Records compact-summary assistant messages explicitly: detects the `isCompactSummary` field on any entry and emits a `ParsedMessage` with `IsCompactBoundary=true`, `IsSystem=true`, and `SourceSubtype="compact_boundary"`. This replaces the old token-drop heuristic with an explicit boundary marker, so transcripts and signal computation agree on where context was compacted. - Carries source identity through the parse: every message gets `SourceUUID` / `SourceParentUUID` (the JSONL UUID chain), `SourceType`, `SourceSubtype`, and `IsSidechain`. Sessions get `SourceSessionID` (Claude's own session UUID), `SourceVersion` (CLI version from the first entry), `Cwd`, and `GitBranch`. - Tracks parse health: `ParserMalformedLines` counts non-decodable JSONL lines; `IsTruncated` is set when the final non-empty line is invalid JSON without a trailing newline (an in-flight write rather than a corrupt record). ## Database schema (`internal/db/schema.sql`, migrations in `internal/db/db.go`) New `sessions` columns: - Source / context: `cwd`, `git_branch`, `source_session_id`, `source_version`, `parser_malformed_lines`, `is_truncated`. - Signals: `tool_failure_signal_count`, `tool_retry_count`, `edit_churn_count`, `consecutive_failure_max`, `final_failure_streak`, `compaction_count`, `mid_task_compaction_count`, `context_pressure_max`. - Outcome: `outcome`, `outcome_confidence`, `ended_with_role`. - Score: `health_score`, `health_grade`, `has_tool_calls`, `has_context_data`. - Lifecycle: `signals_pending_since` (ISO timestamp; non-NULL means scoring was deferred because the session ended too recently to classify) and a per-session `data_version` so individual rows can be re-processed when parsing logic changes without rebuilding the whole DB. New `messages` columns: `source_type`, `source_subtype`, `source_uuid`, `source_parent_uuid`, `is_sidechain`, `is_compact_boundary`. Partial indexes for `cwd`, sidechain, source_uuid, and compact boundary keep the common queries cheap. A stale per-session `data_version` now blocks the incremental JSONL path so old rows always get rewritten through `ReplaceSessionMessages` (and pick up the new metadata + compact-boundary rows). Pin restoration follows `source_uuid` first and falls back to ordinal for legacy rows, so an inserted compact boundary doesn't move a pin onto the wrong message. `UpdateSessionSignals` bumps `local_modified_at` so backfilled rows are re-selected by the next `pg push`. ## Signal computation (`internal/signals/`) New package with four pure-function modules — no DB access, all input via slices the caller already has in memory: - `toolhealth.go` — `FailureSignalCount` from tool_result events plus content heuristics (bash exit codes, permission errors, Python tracebacks, panics, JS stacks ≥3 lines); `RetryCount` from runs of 3+ identical tool calls; `EditChurnCount` from files edited 3+ times within a 10-message window; `ConsecutiveFailureMax`. - `context.go` — `CompactionCount` (>30% drop in context tokens between adjacent messages), `PressureMax` (peak tokens / model window from the agent's known limits), and mid-task compaction detection that counts boundaries where ≥2 *distinct* tool names overlap between the 10 calls before and the 5 after the boundary. - `outcome.go` — pure classifier returning `{completed, abandoned, errored, unknown}` with a confidence; uses ended-with role, final failure streak, last-assistant text patterns ("can't proceed", "i'm unable to"), recency, and message count to decide. - `score.go` — penalty model: starts at 100, subtracts deductions for outcome (errored 30, abandoned 15), tool failures (3×count, cap 30), retries (5×count, cap 25), edit churn (4×count, cap 20), consecutive failures (10 if ≥3), compactions (5×(count−1), cap 15), mid-task compactions (8×count, cap 18, weighted heavier), and high context pressure (10 if max > 0.9). Grade brackets: A ≥90, B ≥75, C ≥60, D ≥40, F < 40. ## Sync engine (`internal/sync/engine.go`, `signal_compute.go`) Signal computation runs *inline* during writes (`writeBatch` / `writeSessionFull` / `writeIncremental`) using the in-memory message slice the writer already holds, so the hot path adds one `UpdateSessionSignals` per session instead of seven extra round trips. A separate `BackfillSignals` runs once per database (guarded by a stats marker) for rows that predate the inline path. `runInitialResync` returns whether every session in the resulting DB went through the inline path; the startup only marks backfill done in that case, so aborted-fallback and orphan-copy paths still get their backfill. ## PostgreSQL (`internal/postgres/push.go`, `schema.go`, `sessions.go`, `messages.go`) PG `sessions` and `messages` schemas mirror the new SQLite columns, with idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` migrations applied before each push. `pushSession` includes the new columns in the INSERT, `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, and `IS DISTINCT FROM` clauses, and `sessionPushFingerprint` includes them so a recomputed signal column actually triggers a re-push. PG read-side scans (`pgSessionCols`, `scanPGSession`) load the new fields. ## Analytics (`internal/db/analytics.go`, `internal/server/analytics.go`) New `GET /api/analytics/signals` returning a `SignalsAnalyticsResponse` with `scored_sessions` / `unscored_sessions`, `grade_distribution`, `avg_health_score`, `outcome_distribution`, `outcome_confidence_distribution`, a `tool_health` summary (failure_rate as a 0–100 percent, totals for failures / retries / edit churn), a `context_health` summary (compactions, mid-task compactions, average context pressure), a daily `trend` series, and `by_agent` / `by_project` breakdowns with completion rates. The handler reuses the standard analytics filter set (date range, timezone, project / agent / machine, day-of-week, hour-of-day). The PG store has a placeholder that returns empty distributions until the same aggregation is ported over. ## Frontend UI - `SignalPanel` — opt-in panel above the transcript: large grade badge, score, outcome icon with confidence tooltip, "Based on:" basis chips with friendly labels (no raw `tool_health` strings), a compaction chip that turns red when mid-task compactions are present, and a "Penalties:" row showing each deduction. Renders an explicit "Not enough activity to analyze this session" line instead of empty chrome when there's no useful signal. - `SessionBreadcrumb` — adds a clickable grade badge that toggles the SignalPanel. - Session Health analytics section (`SessionHealthSection.svelte`) — five summary cards (avg score, % completed, % errored, tool-failure rate, total compactions) plus three sub-components: `GradeDistribution` (A–F bar chart), `OutcomeDistribution` (donut), and `HealthTrend` (avg score per day). Tables break the same data down by agent and project. - `CompactBoundaryDivider` — renders compact-boundary messages as a clear visual divider in the transcript. Focused transcript mode special-cases the boundary so it doesn't displace the assistant response that precedes it. - New `analytics.svelte.ts` store fetches `/api/analytics/signals` with caching; new keys on the UI store track SignalPanel visibility per session. ## CLI (`cmd/agentsview/health.go`) `agentsview health` (no args) prints a table of recent sessions: date, agent, grade, outcome, message count, final failure streak, project, short ID. `agentsview health ` prints full detail (metadata, grade + score, outcome + confidence, signal counts, context pressure, deferred-recompute marker if set). Both modes support `--json`; list supports `--limit` (default 20, max 500). Short-ID lookup goes through partial matching; an exact full-ID match wins when one of the partial results equals the input, but escalates to ambiguity when another match's displayed short ID also equals the input — so host-prefixed remote IDs (`host~`) still resolve correctly while genuine display collisions error. ## Dev tooling (`Makefile`) `make dev-snapshot` builds the binary and runs it against a WAL-safe `sqlite3 .backup` of the prod `sessions.db` (prod is never written, prod `config.toml` is never copied so PG push stays disabled). The recipe wipes and recreates the snapshot directory each run so stale config from a prior snapshot doesn't carry forward, and refuses to operate when `SNAPSHOT_DIR` resolves to empty, `/`, `\$HOME`, the repo root, or the prod data dir itself. `SNAPSHOT_DIR` accepts both relative and absolute overrides via `\$(abspath …)`. Inspired by some ideas from https://github.com/jakeefr/prism, a session history analysis project for Claude Code.

title: Usage dashboard is silently empty for Copilot CLI sessions
body: ## What I saw With only `copilot` and `vscode-copilot` agents selected over a 17-day window (13 and 139 sessions respectively), the Usage dashboard shows zeros and "No data for this period" everywhere — no explanation, no hint that it's an unsupported agent. The Model filter dropdown is also empty of Copilot's models — only Claude Code models appear, even though Copilot CLI sessions exist and report models like `gpt-5.3-codex` in their session events: The CLI has the same silent behavior: ```text $ agentsview usage daily --agent copilot --since 2026-04-01 DATE INPUT OUTPUT CACHE_CR CACHE_RD COST MODELS ---- ----- ------ -------- -------- ---- ------ ---- ----- ------ -------- -------- ---- ------ TOTAL 0 0 0 0 $0.00 ``` With no message, "$0.00" is easy to misread as "I didn't spend anything". I'm opening this to track the problem — not because I know how it should be resolved. ## Why it's empty The [token-usage docs](https://www.agentsview.io/token-usage/) note that only Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi record per-message `token_usage`. For Copilot this isn't just a parser gap — Copilot CLI session files in `~/.copilot/session-state//events.jsonl` do not contain input/output/cache token counts or cost information at all. The event stream is limited to model names, session/user/assistant/tool events, and context metadata. Copilot also doesn't use per-token billing. Subscribers have a monthly quota of "premium interactions", so even a populated `token_usage` wouldn't map onto the existing cost model cleanly. That's part of why a long-term answer is non-obvious. ## Near-term: make the gap visible Even without a full cost story, some signal that these agents aren't in the tokenized set would remove the "did I misconfigure something?" confusion. A few things that could help: - A note on the Usage page when the active filter is an agent that doesn't contribute `token_usage` (e.g., "Copilot CLI sessions don't record per-message token data — see [doc link]"). - Same note from the CLI when `--agent ` is passed, or when the filtered result is entirely empty because of agent selection. - Optionally, visually mark these agents in the agent filter itself (e.g., a "no token data" tag next to the entry). ## Longer-term: could quota data be the answer? For users whose primary agent is Copilot CLI — for example, roborev code-review workflows that invoke Copilot CLI per review — premium-interaction quota is the binding constraint, and there is currently no way to see how much is being consumed over time. GitHub exposes an undocumented endpoint that returns per-quota snapshots for the authenticated user. It is already used by Microsoft's Copilot extension in VS Code and by `oh-my-posh`, which suggests it is de facto stable even though it isn't in the public REST API reference: ```bash gh api copilot_internal/user ``` Mid-cycle example (values illustrative): ```json { "login": "", "copilot_plan": "business", "quota_reset_date": "2026-05-01", "quota_snapshots": { "premium_interactions": { "entitlement": 300, "remaining": 128, "percent_remaining": 42.7, "overage_permitted": true, "quota_reset_at": 0 } } } ``` Over-quota example (what the same shape looks like when overage is active): ```json { "login": "", "copilot_plan": "business", "quota_reset_date": "2026-05-01", "quota_snapshots": { "premium_interactions": { "entitlement": 300, "remaining": -6, "percent_remaining": -2.0, "overage_permitted": true, "quota_reset_at": 0 } } } ``` `remaining` goes negative while `overage_permitted` is true, so the shape is expressive enough to show both "you have X left" and "you're N over". Known references for the endpoint: - `microsoft/vscode` Copilot extension: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/copilot/CONTRIBUTING.md - `oh-my-posh` copilot segment: https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh/blob/main/src/segments/copilot.go The call can piggyback on `gh auth token` (no new PAT required). ## Open questions I don't know how this should integrate with the existing Usage model. Some things I'm not sure about: - Should quota live in Usage at all, or in a separate "Copilot" view? - How should it be presented when multiple agents are mixed in the same filter? - Is the undocumented-endpoint dependency an acceptable tradeoff, and if so, gated behind an opt-in flag or on by default? - Is there a way to show quota in terms comparable to cost (e.g., "interactions per day trend") so it at least fits visually next to the token charts? Happy to iterate on any of this based on what makes sense for the project. ## Constraints worth weighing - The quota endpoint is undocumented. It could change without notice. A graceful "quota unavailable" fallback would be important. - Agentsview already makes outbound calls (LiteLLM pricing, update checks), but those are unauthenticated. A quota fetch would introduce the first authenticated-call pattern: either shelling out to `gh` (new runtime dependency) or reading a token from config. - Quota data is user-global, not per-session, so it lives alongside the existing token aggregates rather than inside them — a real conceptual mismatch with the current Usage model. ## Related - Token-usage doc (lists supported agents): https://www.agentsview.io/token-usage/ - #35 — Insights for Copilot - #67 — Export and programmatic access to insights - #229 — Add token usage metrics (originating design; "allow blanks / partial values when a source does not provide token usage")

title: fix: token-use accepts raw session IDs
body:
## Summary

`agentsview token-use <id>` now accepts the raw session/thread ID emitted by an agent (e.g. codex `thread_id`, claude `session_id`) instead of requiring the internally-namespaced form (`codex:<uuid>`, `kimi:<proj>:<uuid>`, etc.). The raw-ID path is what integrators naturally have on hand; requiring the prefix leaked an agentsview storage detail and caused `roborev` to silently drop token data for ~938/940 codex review jobs.

The CLI resolves the input in three stages:

1. Canonical inputs (`host~…` or any registered agent prefix) pass through unchanged.
2. DB lookup matches either the exact `sessions.id` or a suffix of the form `:<input>`, using `SUBSTR` comparison so underscores/percent in raw IDs are not treated as SQL wildcards. Most-recent wins on ambiguity, with a stderr warning.
3. Disk probe iterates file-based agents and resolves via each `FindSourceFunc`; first hit yields `<prefix><input>`.

When resolution finds no evidence of the ID, the on-demand sync is skipped so the previous misleading `warning: sync failed: source file not found for <id>` no longer fires.

Exit codes now distinguish outcomes:

| code | meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | session has token data |
| 1 | error (bad args, DB open, etc.) |
| 2 | session not found |
| 3 | session known but no token data yet |

JSON output gains `has_token_data` so callers can branch without reading the exit code.

title: feat: live refresh dashboard views via SSE
body:
## Summary

- `GET /api/v1/events` SSE endpoint emits `data_changed` events (`scope` = `messages` | `sessions` | `sync`) after the sync engine writes. Usage, Analytics, and the Sessions list refetch in response, so new agent activity shows up within a few seconds instead of the previous 5-minute poll.
- Sync engine gains an `Emitter` interface; a new `Broadcaster` in `internal/server/` fans events out to connected clients. Emission runs outside `syncMu` so slow subscribers can't extend the sync critical section.
- `authMiddleware` allows `?token=` query-param auth on `/api/v1/events` for browser `EventSource` clients (which cannot set headers). PG serve mode returns 503; the frontend circuit breaker closes the stream after 5 consecutive errors without a successful (re)connect, so the browser doesn't retry forever.
- Frontend: `watchEvents` helper plus a ref-counted `events` store with a trailing-edge `subscribeDebounced` wrapper. Usage and Analytics pages subscribe in `onMount`; the sessions store subscribes on its first load. Each view keeps a 5-minute safety-net poll.
- Removed the \`{#if loading} skeleton {:else} data {/if}\` pattern from 15 dashboard components. Values now update in place via Svelte reactivity instead of swapping whole DOM subtrees on every refetch.

title: fix(parser): skip git-root walk for foreign-OS cwds
body:
## Summary

- `ExtractProjectFromCwdWithBranch` fed every cwd from session content into `findGitRepoRoot`, which walks upward statting each ancestor for `.git`.
- For sessions synced from a Linux host the cwd is `/home/<user>/...`. On macOS those paths sit under an autofs mount point (`/etc/auto_master` -> `/etc/auto_home` -> `+/usr/libexec/od_user_homes`), so each stat triggers `automountd` to ask `opendirectoryd` to enumerate every user record. Under `agentsview sync --host` this pegged `opendirectoryd` and `automountd` at 300%+ / 100%+ CPU for the duration of the sync.
- Generalise the existing `foreignWinPath` short-circuit in `ExtractProjectFromCwdWithBranch` into `isForeignOSPath`, which now also treats `/home/*` as foreign on darwin and `/Users/*` on linux. For those cwds the git-root walk is skipped and the function falls through to the worktree-layout / basename fallback.
- Route the walker's `os.Stat` calls through a package-level `osStat` var so tests can assert no stat calls happen on foreign paths.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` (all packages green)
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `make lint` reports 0 issues
- [x] New `TestExtractProjectFromCwd_ForeignPath_SkipsStatWalk` fails before the fix (9 stat calls, ~80ms of autofs on darwin) and passes after (0 stat calls)
- [x] New `TestExtractProjectFromCwd_NativePath_StillWalks` guards against over-skipping by confirming the walk still runs for `/Users/*` on darwin / `/home/*` on linux
- [x] Existing `TestExtractProjectFromCwd` / `TestExtractProjectFromCwd_Git` / `TestExtractProjectFromCwdWithBranch` suites still pass unchanged

title: feat: agentsview session CLI — programmatic surface over session data
body:
## Summary

- Adds `internal/service.SessionService` — a single interface (`Get`/`List`/`Messages`/`ToolCalls`/`Sync`/`Watch`) with two backends: a direct SQLite/PG-read backend and an HTTP backend that proxies to a running daemon. Both HTTP handlers and the new CLI route through this layer, so the on-disk and wire shapes stay in sync.
- Adds `agentsview session` CLI group: `get`, `list`, `messages`, `tool-calls`, `sync`, `export`, `watch`. Transport auto-detects a running daemon via the existing `server.<port>.json` state file; when none is present, the CLI opens the local archive directly. A `pg serve` daemon (read-only) is honored — `session sync` refuses with a clear error. Auth-enabled daemons (`require_auth: true`) are handled via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` threaded through `NewHTTPBackend`.
- Adds `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/tool-calls` and `POST /api/v1/sessions/sync` HTTP routes so CLI and web share the same DTOs.
- Extracts session polling from the SSE handler into `internal/sessionwatch` so HTTP SSE and CLI `watch` share the same logic, with a PG-read-only branch (`pollDBOnly`) for `pg serve`.
- Parser: promoted system subtypes (`continuation`, `resume`, `interrupted`, `task_notification`, `stop_hook`) now keep `Role=user` with `IsSystem=true`; `user_message_count` and `first_message` skip system-injected entries. Adds `messages.thinking_text` column with a non-destructive migration that preserves the column across full resync, plus PostgreSQL push/read wiring.
- Docs: `docs/cli-reference.md` covers every subcommand, stability guarantees, transport/auth behavior, and response shapes.

## Notes

Two findings from the roborev pass are deferred as follow-ups:
- `directBackend` `ToolCalls` still hydrates all messages before flattening — a dedicated `GetToolCalls` store method would avoid the extra work on large sessions.
- The `DirectReadOnly` transport fallback still calls `db.Open`, which runs migrations and version stamping against a DB the daemon owns. A read-only DSN open path that skips schema probe/migration would make the fallback truly read-only.

title: feat(cli)!: require explicit serve subcommand to start server
body:
## Summary

Bare `agentsview` now prints help instead of auto-launching the server. This matches conventional CLI behavior (git, docker, kubectl) where the top-level command shows usage when invoked without a subcommand.

- `--version`/`-v` still works at the root.
- Serve flags (`--host`, `--port`, etc.) are no longer registered on the root command, so `agentsview --port 9090` returns "unknown flag"; use `agentsview serve --port 9090` instead.
- `make dev` (`.air.toml`) and `make dev-snapshot` invoke `serve` explicitly.
- README quickstart updated.
- Tauri sidecar already invoked `serve` explicitly, so the desktop app is unaffected.

title: fix(desktop): surface login shell probe failure reason on arm64 flake
body:
## Summary

- `run_login_shell_env` collapses every failure path — spawn error, non-zero exit, `try_wait` error, timeout, seek/read error — into bare `None` and pipes stderr to `Stdio::null()`. When `run_login_shell_env_handles_large_stdout` flakes on arm64 Linux CI (e.g. [run 24617406040](https://github.com/wesm/agentsview/actions/runs/24617406040/job/71981905849?pr=353)), the panic says only "run_login_shell_env returned None" with no way to tell which branch fired.
- Split the implementation: `try_run_login_shell_env` now returns `Result<Vec<u8>, LoginShellEnvError>` with variants `TempFile`, `Spawn`, `Wait`, `Timeout { elapsed }`, `NonZero { code, stdout_len, stderr }`, `ReadStdout`. stderr is captured to a tempfile so `NonZero` carries the shell's error output. `run_login_shell_env` stays as the `Option`-returning facade production code depends on, via `.ok()` plus an `eprintln` diagnostic.
- Rewire the flaky test to call `try_run_login_shell_env` so the next arm64 flake panics with the real reason. Convert the existing timeout test to assert the `Timeout` variant. Add two new unit tests covering `Spawn` (missing binary) and `NonZero` (script that writes to stderr and exits 42) so the diagnostic pipeline itself is exercised.

title: fix(frontend): only self-heal events store on transient failures
body:
## Summary

The events store's heal timer added in #351 rebuilds the shared `EventSource` every 60s whenever it's in the CLOSED state. In PG serve mode (or any environment where `/api/v1/events` permanently returns 503), that turns into 5 failed requests every minute forever, defeating the circuit breaker's point of suppressing retry churn on known-dead endpoints.

This distinguishes permanent failure (circuit breaker trips without the `EventSource` ever reaching OPEN) from transient (worked once, later failed):

- `watchEvents` now accepts `opts.onPermanentFailure` and tracks a `hasOpened` flag. When the breaker trips with `hasOpened === false`, it calls the callback.
- The events store sets a sticky `permanentlyFailed` flag on that signal, clears the heal timer, and refuses to rebuild. The safety-net polls on each view still keep data fresh.
- Transient failures continue to heal every 60s.
- Flag clears when the subscriber set empties, so a fresh round of subscribers can retry after page/state changes.

Two tests added in `events.test.ts`: `does not heal after a permanent failure (never opened)` and `self-heals a closed EventSource after a transient failure` (the latter now calls `fireOpen()` first to classify as recoverable).

title: feat: track file inode/device to validate incremental parses
body:
Records `file_inode` and `file_device` on each session row alongside the existing size/mtime. Before running an incremental parse, compares the stored identity against the current file's; if it differs, skips the incremental path and full-parses instead.

This catches cases where a session file is replaced atomically (`mv`, `cp`, editor atomic write) — size and mtime alone can miss the swap, which causes the incremental parser to append unrelated bytes onto the prior session's state.

Unix captures identity from `syscall.Stat_t`. Windows stubs to `(0, 0)`, which disables the check and preserves current behavior.

title: tkmx-client integration: missing coverage vs. retired legacy collectors
body:
## Context

tkmx-client just retired four legacy collectors (`workflow.js`, `codex.js`, `outcomes.js`, and is preparing to retire `cursor.js`) in favor of `agentsview stats --format json`. Most of the coverage is clean — the session_stats v1 schema matches what tkmx-server renders. But a handful of gaps surfaced during the cutover that agentsview needs to close before the last legacy collector can be removed.

Filed as a single tracker issue so we can split into follow-ups as needed.

## Gap 1 — Cursor `ai-tracking.db` parity (blocks retiring `reporter/cursor.js`)

Cursor's primary value prop is per-commit **line-level attribution** (tab completion vs composer vs human). That data lives in `~/.cursor/ai-tracking/ai-code-tracking.db`, not in Cursor's session logs. `agentsview` currently only reads the session logs, so on this user's real data the Cursor session count was 8 total (most recent: 2026-02-27), while the legacy `cursor.js` reports active commit-level usage.

Fields tkmx-client's retired `cursor.js` emitted (shape for reference):

- `scored_commits` — count of commits the `scored_commits` table has attribution for
- `tab_lines_added`, `tab_lines_deleted`
- `composer_lines_added`, `composer_lines_deleted`
- `human_lines_added`, `human_lines_deleted`
- `ai_authored_pct` — (tab + composer added) / (total added)
- `conversations` — `{ \"<model>/<mode>\": count }` from `conversation_summaries`

Source schema:

- `~/.cursor/ai-tracking/ai-code-tracking.db` → `scored_commits` (columns include `commitDate`, `tabLinesAdded`, `composerLinesAdded`, `humanLinesAdded`, and the corresponding `*Deleted`)
- Same DB → `conversation_summaries` (columns include `model`, `mode`, `updatedAt`)

### What would land the gap

- Add a Cursor syncer that ingests `ai-code-tracking.db` alongside the existing session log sync
- Surface the line-attribution aggregates as either:
  - an extension to `session_stats.agent_portfolio.cursor` (e.g. a `cursor_attribution` sub-object), or
  - a new top-level `code_attribution` block that could also accommodate GitHub Copilot's similar telemetry in the future
- Model+mode conversation counts can fold into `session_stats.model_mix.by_tokens` (if token counts are available) or a separate `cursor.conversations` breakdown

The first shape is probably best — it keeps Cursor's quirks scoped.

## Gap 2 — `outcome_stats.commits = 0` on real repos with activity

`agentsview stats --format json --since 28d` reports `outcome_stats: {\"repos_active\": 50, \"commits\": 0, \"loc_added\": 0, \"loc_removed\": 0, \"files_changed\": 0}` on a machine with 462 commits across 19 active repos (confirmed via the legacy `outcomes.js` git-log path).

`repos_active` working correctly (repos are being discovered from session cwds), but the git-log aggregation isn't producing commit/LOC totals. Likely a data-path issue rather than a logic bug — maybe the author-email scoping or the `--author` anchor isn't matching once you're aggregating across worktrees with different git configs. Legacy `outcomes.js` applied a recent fix for this (\"scope author email to --local and anchor git log --author\") worth diffing against.

### What would land the gap

- Verify agentsview's git-log invocation matches the behavior `reporter/outcomes.js` lands at by v1.3.0 of tkmx-client (specifically commits `bbbf908` and `6b5be35` in that repo)
- Likely relevant: author-email discovery per-repo, de-duping commits by SHA across sibling worktree checkouts, `--no-merges` convention

## Gap 3 — `tool_mix.by_category` casing convention

`agentsview stats` emits TitleCase tool names (`Bash`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Write`, `Task`, `Other`, `Tool`). tkmx-server's renderer was originally built against lowercase (`read`, `edit`, `shell`, ...) and has been updated to accept both, but worth locking down a convention upstream.

### What would land the gap

- Document the canonical casing in the session_stats v1 schema (or add a `/docs/session-stats-v1.md` if it doesn't exist)
- Decide whether `Bash` vs `shell` is the preferred key for shell-type tools — legacy clients used `shell`, agentsview uses `Bash`

## Gap 4 — `reporter_timezone: \"Local\"` sentinel

On this user's machine, `temporal.reporter_timezone` came back as the string `\"Local\"` (from the Go `time.Local` sentinel) rather than an IANA zone like `America/Los_Angeles`. Downstream consumers (tkmx-server's canonical-TZ picker) treat this as a valid timezone and pass it to Luxon, which can cause subtle bugs in streak / heatmap computation.

### What would land the gap

- Resolve `time.Local` to its canonical IANA name before emitting the blob, or
- Emit an empty string in that case so the downstream picker's fallback chain (owner TZ → reporter TZ → UTC) kicks in correctly

## Priority

1. **Gap 2** (outcome_stats) blocks the cross-agent outcome display that's already shipping in tkmx-server's profile page — highest priority
2. **Gap 1** (Cursor) blocks retiring the final tkmx-client legacy collector
3. **Gap 4** (timezone) is a correctness issue for any non-IANA resolver
4. **Gap 3** (casing) is cosmetic / documentation

## Cross-references

- tkmx-client retirement: https://github.com/srosro/tkmx-client/commit/1c669a6 (workflow/codex/outcomes)
- tkmx-server branch waiting on these: `session-stats-profile`

title: agentsview stats: per-author git+session reporter
body:
## Summary

Adds a top-level `agentsview stats` command that aggregates SQLite session data with `git log --numstat` and `gh pr list` output to produce a per-author daily/weekly/monthly report. Data side renders into structured `SessionStats` types (totals, archetype mix, velocity, tool/model mix, cache economics, agent portfolio, hourly UTC bucket, outcomes) with a JSON or human formatter.

Supporting work:

- **Per-author git aggregation** discovered from session `cwd`s. Repo toplevels resolved via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree/submodule safe). PR counts pulled from `gh search prs created:A..B author:...`. Both layers are cached in a `git_cache` table keyed by sha256 of (repo, author, since, until, kind) with TTL.
- **Bucketed distributions** (`v1` boundaries locked behind assignment helpers) for messages, durations, tools-per-turn, etc.
- **Outcome mapping** from real session vocabulary (`completed`/`abandoned`/`errored`) onto `success`/`failure`/`unknown`.
- **CLI shell** wraps the service as `agentsview stats` with a JSON or human formatter and a golden-file integration test.

Schema and infra fixes pulled in alongside:

- `git_cache` table for the TTL cache above.
- `idx_tool_calls_message` and `idx_pinned_message` to back the existing `ON DELETE CASCADE` references on `messages(id)`. Without these, `ReplaceSessionMessages` was full-scanning `tool_calls` per deleted row, hanging sync once the table grew large.
- `ReplaceSessionMessages` bypasses the per-row `messages_ad` FTS trigger by bulk-deleting FTS entries via `INSERT INTO messages_fts(...) SELECT 'delete', id, content` and dropping the trigger for the duration of the messages DELETE. Probes `sqlite_master` first so the dance is skipped when FTS5 is not compiled in.
- Per-repo git aggregation failures are logged rather than swallowed.

title: Sync hang on large workloads: residual risks after FK-cascade fix (#359)
body:
## Background

PR #359 fixed a hard sync hang where `agentsview sync` would stall indefinitely partway through (reproducible at ~31% of a 23.5k-session sync on @wesm's machine). The root cause was that `tool_calls.message_id` and `pinned_messages.message_id` had `ON DELETE CASCADE` references to `messages(id)` with no supporting index, so SQLite full-scanned `tool_calls` once per deleted message row. With `tool_calls` grown to millions of rows mid-sync, `ReplaceSessionMessages` became O(messages_in_session × tool_calls_total) and stalled the writer.

The fix in #359 was minimal: add `idx_tool_calls_message` and `idx_pinned_message`. Schema is now clean — every `REFERENCES … ON DELETE CASCADE` has a backing index.

This issue tracks two **residual risks** that I deferred from #359 to keep the PR focused.

## 1. FTS bypass is local to ReplaceSessionMessages

`ReplaceSessionMessages` drops the per-row `messages_ad` trigger inside its transaction and bulk-deletes FTS entries via `INSERT INTO messages_fts(...) SELECT 'delete', id, content FROM messages WHERE session_id = ?`. This avoids N invocations of FTS5 tokenization for sessions with multi-MB content blobs.

But the underlying problem — that `DELETE FROM messages` triggers per-row FTS work — applies to **any other code path** that deletes from `messages`. If we later add a prune-by-id, prune-by-date, or per-message delete, it'll hit the same trigger cascade.

Options:
- Extract the bulk-delete + drop/restore pattern into a helper (e.g., `db.deleteMessagesWhere(tx, predicate, args...)`) and route all message deleters through it.
- Replace the FTS5 external-content tokens-on-delete model with a lazier rebuild strategy (e.g., periodic `DELETE FROM messages_fts WHERE rowid NOT IN (SELECT id FROM messages)`).
- Document that callers must drop the trigger themselves if they delete more than ~N rows.

## 2. Perf regression test doesn't cover the FK-cascade class

`TestReplaceSessionMessages_LargeSession` (added in #359) seeds 1000 messages including one ~5MB content blob and asserts the replace cycle completes in <10s. **It does not seed any `tool_calls` or `pinned_messages` rows for other sessions**, so it would not have caught the actual hang that motivated the PR. Future test cases should include:

- Seed ~10k `tool_calls` distributed across many sessions, then ReplaceSessionMessages on one of them. Asserts no per-row scan regression.
- Same with `pinned_messages`.
- Cross-session interference: replacing session A should not get slower as `tool_calls` for sessions B…Z grow.

## 3. Audit suggestion: index-coverage check on every schema change

This bug type is mechanical: every `ON DELETE CASCADE` (and `ON UPDATE CASCADE`, `SET NULL`, etc.) needs an index on the referencing column. SQLite gives you no help here — it'll happily full-scan forever.

A small CI check would prevent recurrence:
- At schema-load time in tests, parse the schema for `REFERENCES … ON DELETE …` columns and assert each has a covering index (or is itself a PK).
- Or: a pre-commit lint that grep-matches `REFERENCES` and requires a paired `CREATE INDEX` mention nearby.

The mechanical version is preferable since it can't be silently bypassed.

## 4. Diagnostics that would have shortened the debug loop

Two improvements that would have made this hang faster to triage:

- **`agentsview doctor`** subcommand that, among other checks, runs `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for the hot `DELETE FROM messages WHERE session_id = ?` against the actual db and warns when `SCAN` appears instead of `SEARCH`.
- **Periodic progress heartbeat in sync**: when a single session takes >30s, log the session ID and elapsed time. Right now the progress line freezes silently at the offending session and there's no way to identify it without SIGQUIT + sqlite shell.

## Out of scope

- Anything that changes the wire format of `SessionStats` (that's #359's territory).
- The pre-existing FTS rebuild-on-empty-module path; it works.

body:
I'd love the ability to look at session aggregates sliced by model and project.
An example: after Opus 4.7 was released ,there's been a lot of noise about whether the new tokenizer made it more expensive. Certainly, it uses more (input) tokens. However, Opus 4.7 seems to be less wordy and able to accomplish similar tasks at lower reasoning thresholds.

title: fix(parser): subtract cached tokens from codex input_tokens
body:
## Summary

Codex reports `input_tokens` as the full input count with `cached_input_tokens` as a subset. The parser stored this raw total under the Anthropic field name `input_tokens`, which the cost formula in `internal/db/usage.go` treats as the uncached remainder. The cached portion was therefore billed at the full input rate in addition to the `cache_read` rate, inflating reported codex cost by roughly 5x on cache-heavy sessions.

The parser now stores `input_tokens - cached_input_tokens` as the uncached input, keeps the cached subset under `cache_read_input_tokens`, and sets `context_tokens` to the true context size. `dataVersion` is bumped to 15 so existing databases re-parse codex files on next sync and rewrite the buggy rows.

title: fix(frontend): swap sidebar sessions atomically after multi-page load
body:
## Summary

The sidebar session count appeared to "animate" during live refreshes because `load()` in `sessions.svelte.ts` reassigned `this.sessions` and `this.total` after every paginated page arrived. With a page size of 500, a 1,500-session workspace saw the count jump `500 → 1000 → 1500` on each refresh. Combined with the 10-second sync poll and SSE-driven refetches, this produced a distracting ticker in the sidebar header every 10–15 seconds.

Pages are now accumulated into a local array and `this.sessions`, `this.nextCursor`, `this.total` are swapped once at the end, so the count updates in a single step. Existing sessions stay visible during the fetch, so users don't see a blank list mid-refresh.

Added a regression test that defers a later page's resolution and asserts the previous sessions remain visible until the full load completes.

title: perf(server): coalesce SSE emits to cap dashboard refetch rate
body:
## Summary

After #351, the sync engine emits a `data_changed` SSE event after every `SyncPaths` pass that wrote data. When agents are actively writing session files, the file watcher flushes every ~500ms–1s and each flush produces an emit. Every dashboard subscriber (sidebar session list, Analytics `fetchAll` with 10 parallel aggregations, Usage `fetchAll`) refetches on each event, cut only by a 300ms trailing-edge debounce on the frontend. The result is a sustained ~1/s cadence of analytics/sessions queries — versus the pre-SSE 5-minute poll — consuming CPU on the agentsview process while agents work.

This change rate-limits at `server.Broadcaster` with leading + trailing edge coalescing. The first emit after a quiet gap of at least 10 seconds broadcasts immediately; emits within the window update a pending event and schedule a single trailing broadcast that fires when the window ends. Subscribers now see at most one broadcast per 10 seconds. First-write latency stays low, and dashboards still refresh ~30× faster than the pre-SSE poll.

Trailing-timer state is versioned with a `timerGen` counter. A leading-edge broadcast bumps the generation; each `time.AfterFunc` callback captures the generation at schedule time and returns early on mismatch, so a timer whose goroutine already fired but was still waiting for the lock cannot consume a newer pending event installed by a follow-up emit.

title: feat: broaden automated-session detection + Codex parser fix
body:
## Summary

Extends the automated-session classifier in `internal/db/automated.go` to recognize four new tool-prompt patterns that were previously polluting the sidebar and skewing insights:

- **Claude Code conversation title generator** — every user turn spawns an internal Claude Code session that runs a "You are a conversation title generator" prompt. Matched as a substring (the actual message is wrapped with a leading `-\n`).
- **Claude Code Warmup ping** — model warmup with first-message content `Warmup`. Matched via a new exact-match category (`automatedExactMatches`), trimmed of surrounding whitespace, since the word is too generic for prefix or substring matching.
- **Roborev review combiner** — `You are combining multiple code review outputs into a single GitHub PR comment.` Matched as a prefix.
- **agentsview changelog generator** — `You are generating a changelog for agentsview` (release tooling). Matched as a prefix.

The existing `user_message_count <= 1` single-turn gate still wraps the classifier, so multi-turn sessions never get classified as automated.

Also fixes a Codex parser bug that was excluding ~573 legitimately-automated Codex sessions from classification: the parser was counting Codex's synthetic `<turn_aborted>` "user" message (emitted when `codex exec` is interrupted during shutdown) as a real user turn, inflating `user_message_count` to 2 and falling through the single-turn gate. `<turn_aborted>` is now filtered like the other Codex synthetics (`<environment_context>`, `<INSTRUCTIONS>`, subagent notifications) at parse time, so it doesn't affect message counts or message lists.

`insight.BuildPrompt` now sets `ExcludeAutomated: true` on its `db.SessionFilter`, so daily/agent-analysis insights ignore automation noise. There is no UI override — the sidebar toggle remains the only way to surface automated sessions.

The SQLite and PostgreSQL backfill markers both bump from `_v2` to `_v3` to trigger a one-time re-classification on next open against the patterns added in the first commit on this branch (Claude Code title generator, Warmup, roborev combiner). The agentsview changelog generator pattern is not retroactively backfilled; new sessions matching it are classified at upsert time. The SQLite marker is hoisted into an exported `db.IsAutomatedBackfillMarker` constant so the test file no longer carries a separately-drifting literal. `batchUpdateAutomated` now also bumps `local_modified_at` on changed rows so incremental `pg push` picks up the re-classified sessions; without this, `pg serve` would converge via its own marker bump but `pg push` deployments would silently miss the changes until a `pg push --full`. The Codex sessions affected by the `<turn_aborted>` parser bug get re-classified through the normal sync path the next time their source `.jsonl` files are re-parsed; sessions whose source files are gone (or whose mtime hasn't changed since last index) keep their stale `user_message_count` and remain unclassified until a manual re-sync.

The sidebar toggle relabels from "Include automated reviews" to "Include automated sessions" — the category is no longer review-only. URL parameter (`?include_automated=true`), API field, store names, and DB columns are unchanged.

Follow-up tracked in #370 (user-configurable automated patterns in `config.toml`).

title: Feature: user-defined automated session patterns in config.toml
body:
## Background

The automated-session classifier in `internal/db/automated.go` ships with a hardcoded list of patterns (roborev reviews, Claude Code title generator/warmup, etc.). Users with their own tooling that issues recognizable prompts — e.g. a custom changelog generator that always starts with \`You are generating a changelog for ...\` — currently have no way to tell agentsview to treat those as automated without forking the binary.

## Proposal

Add a \`[automated]\` section to \`config.toml\` that lets users append their own patterns to the classifier:

\`\`\`toml
[automated]
prefixes = [
  \"You are generating a changelog for my-project\",
  \"You are a release notes summarizer for\",
]
substrings = [
  \"invoked by my-internal-tool\",
]
exact_matches = [
  \"PingOnly\",
]
\`\`\`

These would be loaded once at startup, merged with the built-in lists, and used by \`IsAutomatedSession\`. The single-turn gate (or whatever gating model lands from the related fix) applies the same way.

## Out of scope

- Per-agent pattern overrides (only worth it if users hit it).
- Regex patterns (start with literal strings; revisit if real users need regex).
- Hot-reload on config changes (a restart is acceptable for now).

## Related

- Built-in patterns added in PR #369.
- Follow-up: a separate change is needed to revisit the \`user_message_count <= 1\` gate, which currently excludes many legitimate automated sessions when synced from a machine whose Codex parser counts user messages slightly differently. That fix is independent of this issue.

5.9.2 (April 18, 2026)

Fix SQL Injection via placeholder confusion with dollar quoted string literals (GHSA-j88v-2chj-qfwx)

SQL injection can occur when:

  1. The non-default simple protocol is used.
  2. A dollar quoted string literal is used in the SQL query.
  3. That query contains text that would be would be interpreted outside as a placeholder outside of a string literal.
  4. The value of that placeholder is controllable by the attacker.

e.g.

attackValue := `$tag$; drop table canary; --`
_, err = tx.Exec(ctx, `select $tag$ $1 $tag$, $1`, pgx.QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol, attackValue)

title: Subagent sessions invisible when their parent transcript is missing
body:
## Summary

Some Claude Code subagent sessions never appear in the agentsview sidebar because their parent session transcript file was never written to disk (or was later deleted). The subagent rows exist in SQLite with `relationship_type = 'subagent'` and a `parent_session_id` pointing at a session that does not exist as a row, so they fall through both the default sidebar query (which excludes subagents) and the parent-expansion query (which never fires for the missing parent).

In my local DB this affects **425 of 5517** subagent rows (~7.7%) across **272 distinct missing parent IDs**.

## Reproduction

Two examples from my local store:

```
agent-a66e3f1   parent=5c2f7691-754f-437b-ad07-85d0d8b36a1b   project=msgvault
agent-abd567c   parent=a2ac06c9-9efc-453e-8315-87f060a30919   project=roborev
```

The on-disk shape of the missing parents:

```
$ ls -la ~/.claude/projects/-Users-wesm-code-msgvault/5c2f7691-754f-437b-ad07-85d0d8b36a1b/
drwx------  3 wesm  staff   96 Feb  2 14:28 .
drwx------ ...                  ..
drwx------  4 wesm  staff  128 Feb  2 14:30 subagents
```

Note: the parent directory exists and contains a `subagents/` child, but **no parent `.jsonl` file**. Claude Code spawned subagents but never persisted (or later removed) the parent transcript.

To find the same situation on any DB:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM sessions
WHERE relationship_type = 'subagent'
  AND parent_session_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM sessions);
```

## What agentsview does today

`internal/db/sessions.go:307-310` (in `buildSessionFilter`):

```go
if !f.IncludeChildren {
    basePreds = append(basePreds,
        "relationship_type NOT IN ('subagent', 'fork')")
}
```

The default sidebar query has `IncludeChildren = false`, so any row with `relationship_type = 'subagent'` is excluded outright. When `IncludeChildren = true`, subagents *are* included via a subquery rooted at their parent (line 478: `OR parent_session_id IN ...`) — but only if the parent itself matches the filter. With no parent row, there is nothing to expand under, and the subagent never renders.

The sync side is correctly populating these rows: `internal/db/sessions.go:768` (`LinkSubagentSessions`) sets `parent_session_id` from `tool_calls.subagent_session_id` and the parser also derives it from the directory layout. The data is right; the display path drops it.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)

**(a) Promote orphan subagents to roots in `buildSessionFilter`.** Treat subagents as roots when their `parent_session_id` does not resolve to an existing session row. One-line predicate change, no schema work, and the subagent surfaces in the sidebar standalone (with its `subagent` relationship type still recorded for analytics).

**(b) Synthesize a placeholder parent at sync time.** When the parser sees a `subagents/` directory whose parent UUID has no `.jsonl`, write a minimal parent session row (zero messages, `display_name = '(missing parent)'`). Subagents then group under the placeholder, preserving the parent-expansion UI, but at the cost of placeholder rows that are not real sessions.

**(c) Render an explicit \"orphaned subagents\" section in the sidebar.** Most surface area to change; clearest UX signal that something on the Claude Code side dropped the parent.

I think **(a)** is the right call: smallest blast radius, no schema/data changes, and the orphan-subagent state is genuinely a tree-with-missing-root rather than something that warrants its own UI section.

## Notes

- Both subagent rows in question are from older sessions (Jan 29 and Feb 2 2026). The on-disk pattern (parent dir present, parent `.jsonl` absent) suggests Claude Code itself either started the parent without persisting a transcript or pruned it later. Worth checking whether current Claude Code versions still produce this shape, but agentsview should be defensive either way.
- The fork case (`relationship_type = 'fork'`) probably has the same defect — same predicate at line 309, same expansion path. A fix should cover both.

title: Config-driven automation prefixes and sidebar orphan-subagent fix
body:
## Summary

### User-defined automation prefixes
Adds an `[automated]` section to `config.toml` so users can register their own first-message prefixes that mark a single-turn session as automated (e.g. custom review or grading prompts). Prefixes are normalized and held in a process-wide singleton so every store-open path sees the same set. A SHA-256 hash over the built-in patterns, algorithm version, and user prefixes is stored in `stats.is_automated_classifier_hash`; when the hash changes on next open, `backfillIsAutomatedLocked` recomputes `is_automated` across the sessions table and stamps the new hash. PostgreSQL mirrors the same logic over `sync_metadata`.

`agentsview classifier rebuild` forces a reclassification and clears the stored hash. The command group is `Hidden: true` in `--help`.

### Resync reclassification gap
`ResyncAll` opens a fresh temp DB whose at-Open backfill stamps the current classifier hash on an empty table. `CopyOrphanedDataFrom` then imports orphan rows verbatim, so their pre-resync `is_automated` values would be frozen against the new stamped hash forever. `ForceBackfillIsAutomated` clears the hash and re-runs the backfill; `ResyncAll` calls it after the orphan copy and metadata merge. `classifierAlgorithmVersion` is bumped so already-poisoned DBs heal on the next Open.

### Sidebar filter correctness
`buildSessionFilter` (SQLite and PG) now uses `WITH RECURSIVE` to select rows reachable from rootMatch-passing roots via `parent_session_id`. Subagent and fork rows no longer surface as standalone sidebar groups when their parent chain is broken (parent JSONL rotated off disk, parent filtered by `is_automated`, or parent excluded by the relationship guard).

### Smaller fixes
- `cmd/agentsview session ...` accepts bare session UUIDs and errors on missing IDs instead of silently returning empty output.
- Codex `<skill>` template injections are classified as system messages so they don't inflate `user_message_count` past the single-turn gate.
- `dataVersion` bump to 17 triggers resync for the codex `<skill>` filter.
- `ClassifierHashKey` is exported and shared between the SQLite and PG paths.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix: narrow opencode watch roots to storage subtrees
body:
## Summary

`ResolveOpenCodeWatchRoots` now returns the three storage subtrees (`storage/session`, `storage/message`, `storage/part`) in storage mode instead of the configured root. `startFileWatcher` uses `WatchRecursive` for OpenCode (ShallowWatch is false), so returning the root caused fsnotify to recurse over the entire OpenCode data directory rather than just the paths that carry session data. SQLite mode still returns the root since the DB file sits directly under it.

Follow-up to #384.

title: Skip /clear and /effort in Claude first_message; audit is_automated despite matching hash
body:
## Summary

- Claude sessions whose first user turn is `/clear` or `/effort` now use the next real message as the sidebar preview. Command detection is word-boundary aware so `/clearly` is not affected. `user_message_count` still counts the skipped turn, so the single-turn `is_automated` gate behaves the same for such sessions.
- `dataVersion` bumped to 18 so existing Claude rows get re-parsed under the new `first_message` rule.
- `tryIncrementalJSONL` falls through to a full parse for Claude sessions where the stored `first_message` is empty but user turns exist — catches rows written before the bump whose first turn was a skippable command.
- `backfillIsAutomatedLocked` no longer short-circuits when the stored classifier hash matches the current one, and now scans all rows (not just `first_message IS NOT NULL`). Rows imported from other DBs (PG pull, remote machine sync, orphan copy) after the hash was stamped carry stale `is_automated` values; the hash alone is not a complete integrity marker. PG `syncClassifierHashAndBackfill` mirrors the same change.

title: Add NilAway lint checks
body:
## Summary

## Verification

title: Feature: CLI subcommands should optionally query the Postgres sync store, not just local SQLite
body:
Love this project!

I run a central Postgres instance that multiple machines `agentsview pg push` to. `agentsview serve` on that host gives me the web UI over the aggregated data, but CLI subcommands (`session list`, `usage daily`, `stats`, `session messages`, etc.) only query the local machine's SQLite — so I can only CLI-query whatever that one machine has generated, not the union across all my machines.

**Ask:** a `--pg` flag (or `AGENTSVIEW_PG_URL` env var) that routes read queries to the configured Postgres instead of local SQLite. Something like:

```
agentsview --pg session list --since 7d
agentsview --pg usage daily
agentsview --pg stats
```

Read-only would cover my use case; I don't need CLI writes against central PG.

**Alternatives considered:**

- `psql` directly against the Postgres store — loses agentsview's FTS, cost calculation, tool-call normalization, and the subcommand ergonomics.
- Hitting `agentsview serve`'s HTTP API — works but isn't a first-class CLI surface, and duplicates what the CLI already does.
- A hypothetical `agentsview pg pull` to hydrate local SQLite — would work but round-trips a lot of data just to run one query, and goes stale immediately.

**Use case:** multi-machine developer (laptop + workstation + VM) who wants unified CLI access to session history/usage without opening a browser.

> Related: #346 proposes a stable CLI surface; #326 shipped PG read-only for usage. This request is the natural composition — the CLI surface backed by the PG store.

title: fix(update): atomic binary swap to avoid partial state during update
body:
## Summary

`installBinaryTo` previously wrote the new binary directly to `dstPath` and `chmod`'d it afterward, leaving a multi-hundred-millisecond window in which `dstPath` existed but was either partially written or had mode 0644. Consumers running `agentsview` concurrently with the update (e.g. vibepulse) could spawn against a truncated or non-executable file and surface errors that persisted in the menu bar until the next scheduled refresh.

The new binary is now staged at `dstPath + ".new"` with the executable bit set, then atomically renamed into place. The existing binary is still moved to `.old` first so Windows can replace its running executable. Stale `.new` and `.old` artifacts from any prior failed update are cleaned up on entry, and the staging file is removed on any error path via defer.
