title: Claude parser drops `queued_command` attachments (user interrupt messages) from transcript
body:
## Summary

When a user sends a message while Claude Code is mid-tool-call, Claude Code records that message in the session JSONL as `type: "attachment"` with `attachment.type: "queued_command"`. The agentsview Claude parser drops these records, so the user's message never appears in the agentsview UI even though it's preserved on disk.

Same family of bug as #206 (user messages starting with a slash-skill invocation not shown in transcript), with a different trigger.

## Reproduction

1. Run `agentsview serve` so the watcher is active.
2. In Claude Code, ask Claude to do something that involves a tool call (e.g., a Bash command that takes a few seconds).
3. While Claude is mid-tool-call, type a message and submit it.
4. After Claude finishes the turn, look at the session in agentsview.
5. The mid-flight message is missing from the transcript even though Claude visibly acted on it.

## Evidence

In the session JSONL, the interrupt message looks like:

```json
{"type":"attachment","timestamp":"2026-04-26T23:13:04.537Z",
 "attachment":{"type":"queued_command","commandMode":"prompt",
 "prompt":"<user's message text>"}}
```

In `~/.agentsview/sessions.db`, the `messages` table has no row for that timestamp — DB ordinals jump straight from the assistant turn before to the assistant turn after, with no user-role record between them.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT source_type FROM messages WHERE session_id='<sid>';
-- only returns: user, assistant, system  (never attachment-derived)
```

## Root cause

`internal/parser/claude.go` uses an entry-type whitelist:

```go
// ~line 118: queue-operation explicitly handled (subagent DAG mapping, not surfaced as messages)
if entryType == "queue-operation" { ... continue ... }
// ~line 143: progress explicitly skipped
if entryType == "progress" { ... continue ... }
// ~line 154: anything not user/assistant is silently dropped
if entryType != "user" && entryType != "assistant" {
    continue
}
```

`type: "attachment"` falls through to that final check and gets dropped. There is no case in the parser that recognizes `queued_command` (or `task_reminder`, which gets dropped for the same reason — though that one is system-injected and arguably correct to drop, or at most surface as `source_type: "system"`).

## Suggested fix sketch

Add a case for `entryType == "attachment"`:

- `attachment.type == "queued_command"` → surface as a user-role message using `attachment.prompt` as the content. Optionally mark with a distinguishing `source_subtype` (e.g. `"queued_command"`) so the UI could render a "sent while tool was running" badge.
- `attachment.type == "task_reminder"` → either drop (current behavior) or surface as `source_type: "system"`.

## Environment

- agentsview `v0.25.0` (release commit `4ca65f67`).
- Audited against `main` HEAD `6bcd29c` — parser code is identical there.
- Linux (Ubuntu WSL2), Claude Code as the source agent.

title: fix(parser): surface Claude queued_command attachments
body:
## Summary

Closes #401.

The Claude parser dropped `type:"attachment"` entries with `attachment.type:"queued_command"` — the JSONL records Claude Code writes when a user submits a message while a tool call is still running. The parser's entry-type whitelist only admitted `user` and `assistant`, so the user's prompt never made it into the transcript even though Claude visibly acted on it.

The parser now collects `queued_command` attachments out of band (they have no uuid/parentUuid and would otherwise force linear fallback or get pruned by the DAG fork heuristic) and splices them into the main session by timestamp. They surface as `role=user`, `is_system=false`, `source_type=user`, `source_subtype=queued_command`, with ordinals renumbered and session counts (`first_message`, `user_message_count`, `message_count`, start/end bounds) refreshed. Other attachment types (e.g. `task_reminder`) and empty/whitespace prompts are still dropped.

`dataVersion` is bumped from 19 to 20 so existing databases re-parse their sessions on next startup and recover the mid-flight messages they previously missed.

title: feat: session duration UX
body:
## Summary

Replaces the right-column `ActivityMinimap` with a richer **Session Vital Signs** panel and decorates the conversation column with per-turn and per-tool-call timing data. All durations are computed from existing message and session timestamps; no schema changes.

The right panel has four sections:
- **Session summary** — total wall-clock, turn count, tool call count, slowest call (clickable to scroll), sub-agent count
- **Time spent** — per-category aggregate bars (click a row to filter the rest of the panel)
- **Timeline** — turns lane + per-category lanes + activity lane + legend
- **Calls** — chronological list with horizontal duration bars, parallel groups bracketed, sub-agent rows expandable inline

Inline in the conversation column: each `ToolBlock` gains a duration badge in its header; each assistant message gains a turn-summary line ("turn 2m 18s · 3 calls"); parallel `tool_use` runs render as a single `ParallelGroup` block with `≤duration` upper bound.

**Tool label normalization**: `ToolBlock` headers, the Calls list, and the slowest-call link render the normalized category (e.g. "Bash") rather than the raw `tool_name`, so codex's `exec_command` shows as "Bash" alongside Claude's. Collapsed `ToolBlock` headers now surface `$ <command>` from `input_json` directly, so bash invocations are legible without expanding the block. `makeInputPreview` dispatches on category and recognizes codex's `cmd` argument.

## Screenshots

Full session view with the duration showcase fixture (sidebar + conversation + Session Vital Signs):

![full session view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c591ebc-8764-47d8-919b-09f219df98a0)

Right panel detail — Session summary, Time spent, Timeline lanes, Calls:

![right panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78200053-8be2-4e40-bbcd-6701e7f4dba3)

Sub-agent inline expansion in the Calls section (chevron-toggled `.sa-expand` block reveals the child session's calls):

![sub-agent expansion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afcec7ad-1c8c-4583-9ac0-4a72e6b30370)

## Notable design decisions

- **Aggregate attribution rule**: when a turn contains a sub-agent whose wall-clock meets or exceeds the non-sub-agent remainder, the turn attributes to `Task`. This matches the user's mental model ("the sub-agent did the work") and keeps the Timeline turns lane honest when a parallel turn mixes a long sub-agent with short non-sub-agent siblings.
- **Per-call precision for parallel non-sub-agent calls is unknowable** from JSONL source data (one timestamp per assistant message). Parallel siblings render with a striped bar and `≤duration` label; only sub-agents inside parallel groups carry exact per-call durations.
- **Backend stays computable at query time** — both SQLite and PostgreSQL backends share the same `AssembleTiming` logic; only the dialect-specific SQL differs.

## Touched

- Backend: `internal/db/timing.go`, `internal/postgres/session_timing.go`, `internal/server/session_timing.go`, `internal/server/events.go`
- Conversation column: `frontend/src/lib/components/content/{ToolBlock,MessageContent,ParallelGroup,ToolCallGroup,MessageList,SubagentInline}.svelte`
- Right panel: `frontend/src/lib/components/content/{SessionVitals,CallRow,CallGroup,SubagentCalls,ActivityLane}.svelte`
- Layout: `frontend/src/App.svelte`, `frontend/src/lib/components/layout/ThreeColumnLayout.svelte`
- Frontend foundations: `frontend/src/lib/{api/timing.ts,api/types/timing.ts,utils/duration.ts,utils/categoryAttribution.ts,utils/categoryToken.ts,utils/toolDisplay.ts,stores/sessionTiming.svelte.ts}`
- Test fixture: `cmd/testfixture/main.go` adds a `test-session-duration-showcase` session covering solo/parallel/sub-agent/slow shapes

title: Feature: periodic SSH remote sync from `serve` (config-driven `[[remotes]]` list)
body:
## Background

`agentsview sync --host <h>` (in `cmd/agentsview/sync.go`, dispatching to `internal/ssh/sync.go:RemoteSync`) is a clean one-shot pull: it resolves agent dirs on the remote, streams them back via `tar` over SSH, and feeds the temp tree into `sync.Engine` with a path rewriter that prefixes sessions with `host:/remote/path`. The incremental cache in `remote_skipped_files` keeps re-pulls cheap.

`serve` already runs a periodic local sync via `runPeriodicSync` on a 15-minute `time.Ticker` (see `periodicSyncInterval` in `cmd/agentsview/serve_runtime.go`), which re-scans local agent dirs and recomputes pending sessions.

The two never meet. To keep remote sessions current, users have to wire up cron / launchd / systemd outside the binary, and remote sessions never appear in the live SSE stream until the next manual `sync --host` run.

## Proposal

Let `serve` poll a configured list of remote hosts on the same periodic cycle that already drives local sync.

```toml
# config.toml

[[remotes]]
host = "dev-vps"          # any value SSH would accept; uses ~/.ssh/config
user = "me"               # optional; falls back to ssh's default resolution
port = 22                 # optional
interval = "1h"           # optional; defaults to a sane value (e.g. 15m or 1h)
ssh_opts = ["-i", "~/.ssh/agentsview_ed25519"]  # optional; passthrough flags

[[remotes]]
host = "build-box.tailnet.ts.net"
interval = "30m"
```

On startup, `serve` would:

1. Validate each entry (host non-empty, interval parseable).
2. Spawn a goroutine per remote with its own ticker.
3. On each tick, run the equivalent of `RemoteSync.Run(ctx)` against that host, reusing the existing skip-cache so unchanged files aren't re-fetched.
4. On success, fire the same broadcaster events local sync uses so the SSE stream picks up new/updated remote sessions in real time.
5. On failure, log and back off (don't crash `serve`); surface the last error + last-success-at via `/api/v1/health` or a small `/api/v1/remotes` status endpoint.

## Why this fits the existing shape

- Reuses `RemoteSync` end-to-end — no new transport.
- Reuses `periodicSyncInterval` plumbing pattern (one ticker per remote instead of one for local).
- Path rewriter already namespaces sessions by host, so the UI already handles cross-host data correctly (see #332 for a related host-attribution edge case in `pg push`).
- The incremental cache already keys on remote host + mtime, so polling cost scales with churn, not corpus size.

## Behavior details worth pinning down

- **Concurrency**: serialize per host; allow parallel across hosts. A slow host shouldn't stall the others.
- **First run**: do an incremental pull on `serve` startup (or honor a `full_on_startup = true` toggle for users who want the equivalent of `--full`).
- **Auth**: SSH only; rely on the user's agent / `~/.ssh/config`. No password handling, no key material in `config.toml`.
- **Cancellation**: tie each remote goroutine to the server's root context so `Ctrl-C` interrupts mid-pull cleanly (`tar` over SSH should handle SIGTERM).
- **Observability**: per-remote counters in the existing stats endpoint — sessions synced, last error, last success timestamp.

## Out of scope

- Pushing local data to the remote (this is pull-only, mirroring today's `RemoteSync`).
- Hot-reload of `[[remotes]]` on config change. A `serve` restart is fine for v1.
- A UI for editing remote hosts. CLI/config is enough; a settings panel can come later (relates to #130).
- Non-SSH transports (HTTP API, rsync daemon, etc.).

## Alternatives considered

- **Recurring CLI flag** (`agentsview sync --host h --interval 1h`): smaller change but leaves users with an extra long-running process per host and no SSE integration. The whole point is for remote sessions to feel live in the same UI as local ones.
- **External scheduling docs** (cron / launchd / systemd snippets): works today, but every user re-derives the same setup, and remote sessions still only appear at sync-completion granularity rather than streaming through SSE.

## Related

- `cmd/agentsview/serve_runtime.go` — `periodicSyncInterval`, `runPeriodicSync`
- `cmd/agentsview/sync.go` — `runRemoteSync`, current CLI shape
- `internal/ssh/sync.go` — `RemoteSync` orchestration, path rewriter, skip cache
- `internal/db/schema.sql` — `remote_skipped_files` table
- #130 (Tauri remote server mode) — different shape (desktop talks to a remote server), but overlaps in the broader "multi-machine" theme
- #332 (pg push overwrites original machine name on remote-synced sessions) — confirms remote-host attribution is already a load-bearing concept

title: feat(cursor): ingest sessions from state.vscdb
body:
## Summary

Adds Cursor support backed by Cursor's global `state.vscdb` SQLite database in addition to the existing JSONL transcript ingestion. The vscdb source is the canonical one for live Cursor sessions; the parser reconstructs message threads from cursorDiskKV bubble headers and bubbles, persists tool calls with their results, and resolves project names from the adjacent `workspaceStorage/` directories.

When both vscdb and JSONL data exist for the same session, vscdb wins. SyncAll, SyncPaths, and the explicit per-session resync path all consult the stored file_path so a JSONL change does not overwrite the richer vscdb messages, and a `state.vscdb#<id>` virtual path now resyncs through `syncSingleCursorVscdb` when no JSONL fallback exists.

Other notable changes:
- Default `state.vscdb` location is platform-aware (`Library/Application Support/Cursor/...` on macOS, `AppData/Roaming/Cursor/...` on Windows, `.config/Cursor/...` on Linux), overridable via `CURSOR_STATE_DB`.
- SQLite paths are opened through `file:` URIs so reserved characters (`?`, `#`, `%`, spaces) in the filesystem path don't get parsed as DSN parameters.
- `extractWorkspaceProject` decodes `file://` workspace folder URLs with Windows drive-letter and UNC handling.
- vscdb change detection now reparses sessions when the stored `data_version` falls behind the parser's current version, matching the file-sync invariant.

## Origin and follow-ups

Rebased from @badliveware's original branch; review iterations addressed platform handling, dedup completeness across non-SyncAll paths, DSN safety, and data-version reparsing.

This still needs validation by Cursor users:
- Live updates from vscdb depend on the 15-minute scheduled SyncAll today. The file watcher observes only agent dirs; adding `CursorStateDB` to the watch set so vscdb writes propagate immediately is a known follow-up.
- The schema work in `internal/parser/cursor_vscdb.go` was developed against synthetic fixtures. Real-world Cursor schemas across versions need verification against actual installs. Goal is to be a drop-in replacement for the standalone vscdb parser in `~/code/tkmx-client`.

title: feat(frontend): render Claude Code bash shortcut wrappers as code
body:
## Summary

Claude Code emits user `!cmd` shortcuts and their output as literal
`<bash-input>`, `<bash-stdout>`, `<bash-stderr>` tags in the session
log. The viewer was passing them through, so transcripts showed the
raw pseudo-HTML in both message bodies and session-list previews.

- **Message body** (`utils/markdown.ts`): three `marked` tokenizer
  extensions consume each wrapper at the lexer level and emit a `code`
  token directly. `<bash-input>cmd</bash-input>` becomes a
  `language-shell` block prefixed with `!cmd`; stdout/stderr become
  unlabelled code blocks; empty wrappers are dropped. Because the
  extension runs in the tokenizer, occurrences inside fenced
  code blocks stay literal. Captured content is preserved verbatim
  so indented and blank-line shell output renders exactly.

- **Session previews** (sidebar, breadcrumb rename pre-fill, trash,
  pinned, command palette recents, analytics Top Sessions,
  confirm-delete modal): a new `previewMessage` helper in
  `utils/messages.ts` returns `{ text, isShell }`. Plain-text callers
  get the normalized string; the sidebar wraps shell-shortcut entries
  in `<code>` with a subtle monospace style.

title: Grouping worktrees into parent project
body:
I know that AgentsView has worktree support, so this is either a bug or that my usage patterns don't fit AgentsView's assumptions.

I typically create worktrees in a sibling folder from the parent repo, e.g. `.../{project}.worktrees/` adjacent to `.../{project}`. I also tend to use conventional commit prefixes in branch names, e.g. `feat/my-new-feature`, so I end up with worktree paths like `.../{project}.worktrees/feat/my-new-feature/`.

In AgentsView v0.25.0 (4ca65f6), a worktree set up in this way will show up as part of the `my-new-feature` project, rather than being associated with the parent project.

title: Better call duration bars and faster load for large sessions
body:
## Summary

- Scale call duration bars in the Calls list relative to the longest call in scope, not total session duration. The slowest call fills the bar; everything else is proportional, so call-vs-call comparison is legible even in long sessions where any one call is a tiny fraction of total wall-clock. Floor at 4% so very short calls remain visible.
- Drop the dark track behind the fill in `CallRow`. With near-zero fills it read as a redaction strip; transparent track keeps the colored fill as the only signal.
- Lower `FULL_SESSION_MESSAGE_THRESHOLD` in the messages store from 20,000 to 3,000. Sessions past that count now take the progressive load path (one fetch of the most-recent 1000, older pages lazy-loaded on scroll) instead of fetching every page on open and triggering full reactive rebuilds between each.

title: Compaction summary is truncated in transcript with no way to view full content
body:
## Description

When a Claude Code session has been compacted, the transcript shows a "Context compacted" divider followed by a one-line preview of the compaction summary, truncated at 140 characters. There's no way to expand it to see the full summary.

Subagent details and tool calls within the same transcript are expandable/collapsible to view their full content, so the lack of an equivalent affordance here feels inconsistent — the compaction summary often contains the most important context for understanding what the assistant carried forward from the prior conversation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Claude Code session that has been compacted (contains `isCompactSummary: true` entries in the JSONL)
2. Scroll to the "Context compacted" boundary in the transcript
3. Observe a single truncated line of the summary, with no control to expand it

## Observations

Looking at the codebase, the full summary text appears to already be parsed and stored:

- `internal/parser/claude.go` detects `isCompactSummary` entries and persists them as `compact_boundary` system messages with full content via `extractCompactSummary`
- `frontend/src/lib/components/content/CompactBoundaryDivider.svelte` renders only the first line, truncated at 140 chars, with no expand control

So the data is already in place — the gap is purely in the UI surface.

## Environment

- AgentsView v0.25.0 (desktop, Windows 11)
- Agent: Claude Code

title: 0.26.0: session view renders empty, session list pagination broken
body:
0.26.0 broke session viewing in the web UI; 0.25.0 against the same Postgres data works fine.

Symptoms in 0.26.0:
- Clicking a session loads the layout (sidebar, vitals header) but the message panel stays empty.
- The session list sidebar doesn't paginate past the first page on scroll.
- Reproduces in a Chrome incognito window. Hard reload doesn't help.

Backend looks healthy. nginx access log for one session click in 0.26.0 (cookies/CF redacted):

```
GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>                                            200    615 B
GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/timing                                     200    2.6 KB
GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/messages?from=0&limit=1000&direction=asc   200     23 KB
GET /api/v1/sessions?include_one_shot=true&...&limit=500             200     73 KB
GET /api/v1/sessions?...&cursor=...&limit=500                        200     61 KB
```

Bodies non-empty, nothing renders. `/api/v1/events` returns `503 {"error":"events not available in this mode"}` — appears to be by design in `pg serve` mode, but mentioning in case the UI's first-render path depends on it.

Verified by building from the v0.25.0 tag and running it locally against the same Postgres database (SSH tunnel, same data, same browser): session view renders, sidebar paginates.

Setup: `agentsview pg serve` packaged via numtide/llm-agents.nix, behind nginx + Cloudflare Access. ~3.6k sessions, all <3k messages, so #417's threshold change isn't being exercised.

Can grab a DevTools console trace if useful.

title: fix: keep timing response arrays non-null (#428)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #428. The `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/timing` endpoint, added in 0.26.0 (#408), emitted JSON `null` for `by_category`, `turns`, and per-turn `calls` whenever the underlying Go slices were nil. The frontend's `SessionVitals.svelte` and the TypeScript types in `frontend/src/lib/api/types/timing.ts` assume these fields are arrays, so `timing.turns.flatMap(...)`, `timing.turns.length`, `t.calls.some(...)`, etc. threw `TypeError` on null. Those throws happen inside Svelte 5 `$derived.by(...)` scopes, which explains both reported symptoms — empty message panel and sidebar scroll-pagination not advancing — even though the underlying API responses were healthy.

`AssembleTiming` in `internal/db/timing.go` now:

- Initializes `ByCategory` and `Turns` to empty slices in the struct literal so sessions with no tool-using turns marshal as `[]` instead of `null`.
- Guards the `callsByMsg[t.MessageID]` lookup so a turn flagged `has_tool_use=true` with no `tool_calls` rows produces `calls: []` instead of `calls: null`.

Both SQLite and PostgreSQL backends share `AssembleTiming` (`internal/postgres/session_timing.go:40`), so the single change covers `pg serve` mode as well as the local SQLite path.

The new test asserts on the rendered JSON bytes for both empty-collection scenarios so the wire contract is locked down rather than just the Go slice nil-ness.

title: fix(desktop): disable WebKit DMABUF renderer on Linux
body:
## Summary

Sets `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` at the top of `run()` on Linux when the variable is unset, so WebKitGTK falls back to its legacy compositing path instead of trying to bring up the DMABUF/EGL renderer.

WebKitGTK 2.40+ defaults to a DMABUF-based renderer that calls `g_error()` and aborts the process when EGL initialization returns `BAD_PARAMETER` — a known failure mode on certain NVIDIA proprietary driver combinations, headless/containerized environments, and some Wayland sessions. Field reports show the AppImage hitting `Could not create default EGL display: EGL_BAD_PARAMETER. Aborting...` immediately after the sidecar comes up, which then causes Tauri to SIGKILL the sidecar on its way out.

A user who needs the new renderer can still opt back in by exporting `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=0` before launch.

This is a stopgap for Linux specifically; it does not affect macOS or Windows.

title: fix(parser): extract OpenClaw per-message token usage and model
body:
## The gap

OpenClaw sessions are already discovered and registered (`agentsview session list --agent openclaw` returns them), but the parser never read the assistant turn's `model` or `usage` block. The downstream usage aggregator (`internal/db/usage.go`) requires both fields:

```sql
m.token_usage != '' AND m.model != ''
```

so every OpenClaw row was filtered out and `usage daily --agent openclaw` totalled $0.00 even when the underlying API spend was non-zero.

## Schema

OpenClaw writes one JSON object per line. Assistant `type:"message"` records carry per-turn provider, model, and usage:

```json
{
  "type": "message",
  "message": {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": [...],
    "provider": "anthropic",
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "usage": {
      "input": 3,
      "output": 91,
      "cacheRead": 0,
      "cacheWrite": 9612,
      "totalTokens": 9706,
      "cost": { "input": ..., "output": ..., "total": 0.037419 }
    }
  }
}
```

Field names are short (`input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`) — they don't match the Anthropic-style names the rest of agentsview reads.

## The fix

Mirror the OpenCode parser (`applyOpenCodeTokenUsage`):

- For each `type:"message"` record with `role:"assistant"`, read `message.model` and translate `message.usage.{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite}` onto the canonical `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` keys before storing as `TokenUsage`.
- Set `Model` per assistant message rather than relying on the standalone `model_change` event, so mid-session model swaps are attributed correctly.
- Call `accumulateMessageTokenUsage` so session-level `TotalOutputTokens` and `PeakContextTokens` roll up.
- Defensive about missing fields: a usage block without the nested `cost` object (older sessions) still extracts tokens cleanly.

## On `cost.total`

The OpenClaw `usage.cost.total` is **not** propagated into `ParsedMessage`. agentsview re-prices every message via the `model_pricing` table (loaded from LiteLLM) in `GetDailyUsage`, so trusting the gateway's at-request cost would skew totals against the canonical pricing source. Setting `Model` correctly is the load-bearing field — the existing pricing pipeline computes cost from the normalized token counts.

## Tests

Added two test cases to `internal/parser/openclaw_test.go` using **synthetic** JSONL fixtures (no real session content):

- `TestParseOpenClawSession_AssistantUsage` — full `usage` + `cost` block; asserts model, output tokens (91), context tokens (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite = 9615), normalized JSON shape, and session-level rollup.
- `TestParseOpenClawSession_AssistantUsageWithoutCost` — `usage` block missing the `cost` field; asserts no crash and tokens still extracted.

## Verification

```
go test ./internal/parser/...   # PASS
go build ./...                   # clean
```

The pre-existing `TestReplaceSessionMessages_LargeSession` failure in `internal/db` reproduces on stock `main` — unrelated to this change.

title: Add session termination status detection and StatusDot UI
body:
## Summary

Surfaces sessions that didn't pause/stop/terminate cleanly so users can find them via filter, see them flagged in the sidebar and Top Sessions, and rank them in analytics.

- Parser-side classification (Claude + Codex): \`clean\`, \`awaiting_user\`, \`tool_call_pending\`, \`truncated\`, or \`NULL\`. Claude reads \`stop_reason\` (\`end_turn\` → \`awaiting_user\`); Codex reads task lifecycle events (\`task_started\` / \`task_complete\` / \`turn_aborted\`).
- New \`termination_status\` column on \`sessions\` (SQLite + PostgreSQL), with index, idempotent migration, and full round-trip through sync, push, and reads. Incremental sync clears the field to \`NULL\` so stale flags can't leak in the UI for up to 15 minutes between full resyncs.
- New \`?termination=\` query filter accepting comma-separated values: \`clean\`, \`awaiting_user\`, \`active\` (< 10m), \`stale\` (10–60m + flagged), \`unclean\` (≥ 60m + flagged). Wired through \`/api/sessions\`, analytics, and the frontend stores.
- Shared \`StatusDot\` component renders one of working / waiting / idle / stale / unclean / quiet based on recency + termination_status. Used in the sidebar \`SessionItem\` (replacing the agent-color dot — agent identity moves to the right-side tag) and Top Sessions analytics column.
- Sidebar sort is now status-tier first (working → waiting → idle → stale → quiet → unclean), then group-freshness within a tier. Status filter is a three-pill multi-select (Active / Stale / Unclean) tinted with its dot color.

title: pg serve: messages.id always 0 → each_key_duplicate in ToolCallGroup → empty message panel
body:
Same observable symptom as #428 (empty message panel on session click in `pg serve` mode), but a different root cause that #429 didn't address. 0.26.1 still reproduces against the same Postgres data; 0.25.0 does not.

## Symptom

Session view in 0.26.1 (`pg serve` mode):

- Sidebar, breadcrumbs, vitals header all render.
- Message panel stays blank.
- Console shows a single `[pageerror]`:
  ```
  Error: https://svelte.dev/e/each_key_duplicate
      at ve (assets/index-B7DegnQc.js:3:423)
      at ... (Svelte 5 reconciler frames) ...
  ```
- All `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/...` responses are `200`. The 0.26.1 timing fix from #429 is observed to be live (`by_category`/`turns` are arrays).

## Bisect

| case | each_key_duplicate | message panel |
|---|---|---|
| dashboard alone | clean | n/a |
| 2-message session (no tool turns) | clean | renders |
| 15-message session (9 turns w/ tool calls) | **throw** | **empty** |
| 81-turn session | **throw** | **empty** |
| 489-turn session | **throw** | **empty** |

Direct URL navigation (`/sessions/{id}`, no sidebar click) reproduces identically — rules out any sidebar-render race.

## Root cause

The Postgres path returns `messages.id == 0` for every row, and the frontend keys an `{#each}` on `message.id`.

### Backend — pg path drops `id`

`internal/postgres/messages.go:30-43` (`GetMessages`) and `:70-82` (`GetAllMessages`):

```go
SELECT session_id, ordinal, role, content, thinking_text,
    timestamp, has_thinking, has_tool_use,
    content_length, is_system, model, token_usage,
    context_tokens, output_tokens,
    has_context_tokens, has_output_tokens,
    claude_message_id, claude_request_id,
    source_type, source_subtype, source_uuid,
    source_parent_uuid, is_sidechain,
    is_compact_boundary
FROM messages
```

`id` is missing. `scanPGMessages` at `internal/postgres/messages.go:531-541` correspondingly never scans into `&m.ID`, so `db.Message.ID` is left at Go's zero value (`0`) for every row.

The SQLite path is fine — `internal/db/messages.go:16` `selectMessageCols` starts with `id, session_id, ...`. So this is a `pg serve`-only bug.

Verified directly against the deployed `pg serve`:

```
$ curl /api/v1/sessions/<id>/messages?from=0&limit=1000&direction=asc | jq '[.messages[].id] | unique'
[0]
```

For sessions with 2, 15, 81, 489, and 713 messages — every `id` is `0`. `ordinal`, `source_uuid`, and `timestamp` are all unique.

Introduced in PR #167 (PostgreSQL push sync + serve, 2026-03-17). Latent until something downstream started keying on `messages.id` — see frontend section below.

### Frontend — `ToolCallGroup` keys on `message.id`

`frontend/src/lib/components/content/ToolCallGroup.svelte:188`:

```svelte
{#each messages as message (message.id)}
```

When this component mounts with ≥ 2 messages and they all have `id == 0`, Svelte 5's reconciler throws `each_key_duplicate`. The throw propagates out of a `$derived.by(...)` (same failure mode as #428) and tears down the message panel.

The 2-message session avoids the throw not because the data is different (its messages also have `id == 0`) but because it has zero tool-using turns — `ToolCallGroup` never mounts.

## Suggested fix (either alone resolves it)

**Backend** — three lines in `internal/postgres/messages.go`:

1. Add `id, ` to both SELECT statements (`GetMessages` and `GetAllMessages`).
2. Add `&m.ID,` as the first scan target in `scanPGMessages`.

This is the right fix: `id` is the documented PK and other code is likely to grow new dependencies on it.

**Frontend** — alternative one-liner in `ToolCallGroup.svelte:188`:

```svelte
{#each messages as message (message.source_uuid)}
```

`source_uuid` is unique per message (verified across all sample sessions). `ordinal` is also unique within a session. Either works as a key.

## Repro environment

- 0.26.1 self-hosted via `pg serve`, frontend bundle `index-B7DegnQc.js` confirmed served.
- ~3.6k sessions in PG, ranging from 2 to 700+ messages.
- Tested against the same DB rebuilt from the v0.25.0 tag — renders correctly there (presumably because the keyed `{#each}` on `message.id` either didn't exist or wasn't on the message-panel render path).

title: serve --host 0.0.0.0 reports 'public at http://127.0.0.1:8080' which is unreachable from Windows in WSL2
body:
When running agentsview inside WSL2 with `--host 0.0.0.0`, the startup message reports:

```
agentsview v0.26.1 listening at http://0.0.0.0:8080, public at http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

However, `127.0.0.1` is the WSL2 loopback and is **not reachable from the Windows browser**. The correct URL to use from Windows is the WSL2 `eth0` IP (e.g. `172.x.x.x:8080`), which changes on every WSL2 restart.

**Suggestion**: when `--host` is `0.0.0.0` and WSL2 is detected (presence of `/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop` or `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` env var), auto-detect the `eth0` IP and display it as the public URL, or at least add a note that `127.0.0.1` may not be reachable from Windows.

The `--public-url` flag is a workaround but requires the user to know and pass the dynamic WSL2 IP manually.

title: fix(pg): synthesize message.id from ordinal in pg serve (#439)
body:
## Summary

The PG `messages` table uses a composite primary key `(session_id, ordinal)` and has no `id` column. `scanPGMessages` was leaving `db.Message.ID` at the Go zero value (`0`) for every row, so the frontend's keyed `{#each messages (message.id)}` in `ToolCallGroup` collided on duplicate keys and Svelte 5 raised `each_key_duplicate`, tearing down the message panel.

This sets `Message.ID = int64(Ordinal)` in `scanPGMessages`, matching the existing convention used by `TurnRow.MessageID` and `CallRow.MessageID` in `session_timing.go`. The `turnByMessage.get(message.id)` join in `ToolCallGroup` and `MessageContent` now resolves correctly across the messages, turns, and calls payloads.

A pgtest regression (`TestGetMessagesIDPopulated`) covers the uniqueness invariant and the cross-check that every `TurnRow.MessageID` resolves to a `Message.ID` returned by `GetMessages`.

Fixes #439

title: fix(serve): degrade large watcher trees instead of failing startup
body:
## Summary

- Cap recursive file watcher setup at an internal process-wide budget of 8192 directories. When the budget is exhausted or `fsnotify.Add` returns `EMFILE`/`ENOSPC`, the affected root degrades to the existing periodic polling path instead of bubbling up as a fatal startup error.
- Defer file watcher startup until after the backend listener is bound, the managed Caddy proxy is reachable, and the state file/startup lock are published. Slow recursive watch setup can no longer block the web UI from coming up or stall daemon discovery.
- Report polled roots after the existing `Watching N directories` line so the operator can tell when degradation is in effect.

Fixes #364.

title: Add Forge agent support
body:
## Add Forge agent support

Adds [Forge](https://forgecode.dev) as a supported agent in agentsview, alongside a fix for a latent subagent-linking gap that surfaces with DB-backed agents.

### What this adds

Forge stores conversations in a SQLite database (`.forge.db`) rather than per-session files. New code in `internal/parser/forge.go` opens this DB read-only, lists conversations via lightweight metadata, and parses each on demand. The parser:

- Maps Forge's `message.text` and `message.tool` events to agentsview's user/assistant/tool model, including reasoning details (rendered as `[Thinking]…[/Thinking]`) and tool calls (with `task`/`skill` argument extraction for subagent ID and skill name).
- Pulls token usage from per-message `usage.{prompt,completion,cached}_tokens.actual` and aggregate `metrics.{input,output,cached_input}_tokens`, with a fallback to message-level accumulation when aggregates are absent.
- Resolves project name from the `<current_working_directory>` tag found in the system message context.

`internal/sync/engine.go` learns to handle DB-backed agents alongside its existing file-based ones: each conversation gets a virtual path (`<dbPath>#<conversationID>`) and a per-conversation mtime, so incremental sync only re-parses the conversations whose `updated_at` changed. `FindSourceFile`, `SourceMtime`, and `SyncSingleSession` all gain Forge support symmetric to the existing Warp paths.

The tool taxonomy in `internal/parser/taxonomy.go` adds nine Forge-specific names: `fs_search`→Grep; `patch`/`multi_patch`/`undo`/`remove`→Edit; `fetch`→Read; `todo_write`/`todo_read`→Tool; `parallel`→Task.

### Bulk-sync linking fix

While writing the integration test for parent→child subagent linking, I discovered that `LinkSubagentSessions` was being invoked inside `collectAndBatch` — which runs before the DB-backed (Warp, Forge) sync blocks. Bulk `SyncAll` was therefore never establishing links for those agents; only `SyncSingleSession` worked, because it calls the linker itself. This PR moves the call so it also runs after the DB-backed writes complete. The function is idempotent (filtered `UPDATE` plus the `idx_tool_calls_subagent` partial index), so the call is unconditional rather than guarded.

### Test coverage

13 new tests across the parser and sync packages:

- **Parser** — token/metrics fallbacks (no metrics column, output-only metrics, no cached_tokens, entirely absent usage); degenerate conversations (empty assistant message, missing `call_id`, `raw_content.Text` fallback); cwd extraction edge cases (no system message, missing tag, empty tag, tag in non-system message); `parseForgeTimestamp` across all five accepted layouts; `endedAt` fallback to `startedAt`; `forgeToolOutputText` top-level text fallback; `skill` tool name from both `arguments.name` and `arguments.skill`; reasoning details with no text fields.
- **Taxonomy** — table-driven test for the nine Forge tool mappings.
- **Sync integration** — multi-conversation incremental sync (only changed conversations rewritten); missing-conversation handling for `FindSourceFile`/`SourceMtime`/`SyncSingleSession`; non-existent session error path; parent→child subagent linking end-to-end through `SyncAll` (the test that surfaced the linking bug); failure isolation when one conversation has malformed JSON context.

Improve session navigation so browser-native behaviors work from the session list (sidebar / main list), and expose **Open in new tab** from the session row context menu.

## Motivation

- **Modifier-click** (e.g. Cmd+click on macOS, Ctrl+click / middle-click elsewhere) to open a session in a new tab only works reliably when the row is a real link (`<a href="...">`) or equivalent with correct `href`.
- Today the context menu appears limited to **Rename** and **Delete**; users who prefer menus over shortcuts should get **Open in new tab** there too.

## Requested behavior

1. **Session rows use proper URLs** — Each session entry should resolve to the same canonical session URL the app already uses for deep linking (e.g. path-based `/sessions/{id}` with any required sticky/query params), implemented as a semantic link where appropriate so **Cmd+click / Ctrl+click / middle-click** opens in a new tab without custom JS unless necessary.

2. **Context menu** — Add **Open in new tab** (wording can match platform conventions) alongside existing **Rename** and **Delete**, performing the same navigation as opening the session URL in a new browser tab.

## Notes

- Related prior work: URL-based session linking ([#180](https://github.com/wesm/agentsview/issues/180), [#225](https://github.com/wesm/agentsview/issues/225)); those enabled shareable URLs and middle-click for some subagent links—this issue is about **primary session list UX** and **context menu parity**.

## Acceptance criteria

- From the session list, modifier-click opens the session in a new tab with the correct URL.
- Context menu includes **Open in new tab** and it behaves consistently with modifier-click.
- Normal click still selects/opens the session in the current tab as today.

title: feat: syntax highlighting for code fences in session transcript
body:
## Summary

Add syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks in the session transcript / message renderer so languages are easier to read at a glance.

## Proposal

Use **[Shiki](https://shiki.style/)** for highlighting:

- Accurate, TextMate-grammar–based highlighting consistent with VS Code / common editor themes
- Works well in Vite + Svelte stacks; can align theme with the app (light/dark) if desired
- Apply to standard Markdown fenced blocks with a language tag (e.g. ` ```ts `)

## Scope (suggested)

- Client-side (or build-time) highlighting of user/assistant code fences in the main transcript view
- Graceful fallback for unknown languages or missing grammar (plain monospace, no broken layout)
- Performance: avoid blocking the main thread on very large blocks (virtualization or async highlight if needed)

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Optional: copy-as-formatted, line numbers, or theme switcher can be separate issues

## Acceptance criteria

- Fenced code in messages shows language-appropriate colors when a language is specified
- No regression for non-code content or unlabeled fences

title: feat: render Mermaid diagrams in Markdown content
body:
## Summary

Support **Mermaid** (` ```mermaid `) and similar diagram blocks in message Markdown so flowcharts, sequence diagrams, etc. render in the transcript instead of showing raw source.

## Proposal

For rendering, follow the approach / reference in **[Mermaid in AI coding agents (Craft)](https://agents.craft.do/mermaid)**—treat Mermaid as a first-class diagram format that agents already emit, and render it safely in the UI.

## Implementation notes

- Use the official **mermaid** library (or a thin wrapper) in the frontend; run init with a version appropriate for the app bundle
- Security: render in a sandboxed or isolated path (Mermaid runs user/agent-provided text); follow Same-origin and CSP constraints already used by the SPA
- UX: sensible max height / scroll for large diagrams; optional “copy source” affordance

## Scope (suggested)

- ` ```mermaid ` fenced blocks in assistant/user Markdown
- Loading/error state when diagram syntax is invalid (show fallback message, keep source visible or expandable)

## Acceptance criteria

- Valid Mermaid blocks render as diagrams in the session viewer
- Invalid diagrams fail gracefully without breaking the surrounding message
- Document any CSP or dependency implications for maintainers (short note in PR is enough unless docs issue is preferred)

## Related

- Syntax highlighting for code fences may land separately; diagram blocks should not depend on the highlighter for correctness (tracking: separate issue if filed).

title: feat(frontend): preview common tool inputs on collapsed tool header
body:
## Summary

Synthesize collapsed-header previews from input params for tools whose first line of `content` is a generic header that hides the useful info. Previews take precedence over `content.split("\n")[0]`.

- `TodoWrite` → `→ <in-progress todo content>` (falls back to the last todo)
- `TaskCreate` → `<subject>`
- `TaskUpdate` → `#<taskId> · <status>` (appends ` · <subject>` when present)
- `Skill` / `skill` → skill name from `skill` or `name`
- `ToolSearch` → first line of `query`
- `Task` / `Agent` / `*subagent*` (also `category === "Task"`) → `description` (falls back to first line of `prompt`)

title: docs: add forge to supported agents
Codex Archived Sessions Not accounted for
body:
The application does not account for Codex sessions which have been archived (stored at `~/.codex/archived_sessions`). I tried manually adding this directory to the `codex_sessions_dirs` in my config.toml but it had no affect on the results. I confirmed the path is correct, it contains many `.jsonl` files, and the settings view for the app even displays that directory under the codex settings, but the total count of sessions remains the same.

I frequently archive old sessions to prevent my codex UI from getting overloaded, but I would still like to track costs associated with those sessions.

This was discovered because I tried comparing my costs with the costs that codex itself could calculate using this prompt:
```
Estimate my total token usage per week for the entire history you have available. Use that to estimate my cost per week as well if possible
```

I then gave it a screenshot from the app where the totals didn't match up and asked codex to find out why and it spat this back out at me:
```
The screenshot is low because AgentsView appears to be importing only active/non-archived Codex session files, not the full local history.

For `2026-04-30` to `2026-05-07`, I see:

- Full Codex history: `19` sessions, `140.55M` total tokens, estimated around `$110`
- Non-archived `~/.codex/sessions` only: `12` sessions, `47.89M` total tokens
- Screenshot: about `2.3M` uncached input + `44.6M` cached input + `161.8K` output, total cost `$38.03`

That screenshot almost exactly matches the **non-archived sessions only** view. It misses the archived sessions in `~/.codex/archived_sessions`, including several large `gpt-5.5` sessions from May 4. The `gpt-5.4` cost of `$0.86` actually lines up with the one `gpt-5.4` session in that range; the missing cost is almost entirely `gpt-5.5`.

So the pricing math in AgentsView is probably fine for the records it imported. The wrong part is coverage: it is undercounting because it is not including archived Codex sessions.
```

title: fix(piebald): progress accounting, fork validation, generic CLI help
body:
## Summary

Follow-up fixes to #478 surfaced by post-merge review:

- **Progress accounting** — `stats.messagesIndexed` was tracking only the file-backed total, so the terminal `PhaseDone` callback regressed `MessagesIndexed` to the file-only count after Piebald/OpenCode/Warp/Forge work. Now updated inside `advanceDBProgress` so the cumulative count holds.
- **Fork ID validation** — `syncSinglePiebald`, `FindSource`, and `SourceMtime` strip the `-<row>` suffix from fork IDs to look up the base chat, but didn't verify the requested fork actually exists. Stale or typoed IDs like `piebald:42-999` could silently succeed or return mtimes for non-existent sessions. They now require an exact `Session.ID` match in the parsed results.
- **CLI help** — drop the hard-coded agent list from `agentsview --help`. The list went stale every time a new agent was added (most recently Piebald); the README's supported-agents table and per-agent env vars below stay authoritative.

title: feat: add configurable worktree project mappings
body:
Closes #416.

Adds user-configurable rules that map worktree paths back to a canonical
project, so worktree sessions group with the parent repo instead of becoming
a separate project derived from the branch name.

The built-in parser infers a session's project from its `cwd`, which works for
standard layouts but not custom worktree conventions like
`~/code/{project}.worktrees/feat/my-feature/` — those sessions end up under
`my-feature` rather than `{project}`. This branch adds a manual override that
lives in SQLite, is scoped to the current machine, and is applied both as new
sessions stream in and to existing sessions on demand.

## How it works

- New `worktree_project_mappings` table keyed by `(machine, path_prefix)` with
  an `enabled` flag. Path prefixes are cleaned and have trailing separators
  stripped so matches are stable regardless of how a user types the prefix.
- The sync engine loads the active mappings for the host machine on each pass
  and rewrites `project` for any session whose `cwd` falls under an enabled
  prefix. The resolver is wired into all ingestion paths: single-session
  writes, incremental sync, bulk resync, and the rebuild-and-swap full
  resync. Excluded, trashed, and skipped session files are left alone so the
  rewriter does not resurrect intentionally removed data.
- REST API under `/api/v1/settings/worktree-mappings` (list / create / update /
  delete / apply). The server derives the machine identifier itself instead
  of accepting it from the client, so a mapping created on one machine never
  bleeds into another machine's view of synced sessions.
- Settings panel in the SPA for adding, editing, toggling, and deleting
  mappings, plus an Apply action that runs the rewrite over already-imported
  sessions and reports how many were matched and updated.

## Notes

- Mappings are explicit and manual — there is no auto-discovery. The intent
  is to let users formalize their personal layout once and have it stick.
- Mappings only mutate `project`; the rest of the session record, including
  data carried through the bulk resync's rebuild-and-copy path, is preserved.

title: Support session stars and pinned messages in PostgreSQL / pg serve dashboards
body:
## Feature request

  Please support session stars and pinned messages when running AgentsView from PostgreSQL via `agentsview pg serve`.

  ## Use case

  I’m using AgentsView as a shared dashboard across multiple devices:

  - each device runs `agentsview pg push`
  - a hub runs PostgreSQL
  - the dashboard runs with `agentsview pg serve`

  This works well for viewing sessions across machines, but session stars and pinned messages do not work on the hub dashboard.

  ## Current behavior

  In `pg serve` mode, the dashboard is read-only. The PostgreSQL store returns `db.ErrReadOnly` for:

  - `StarSession`
  - `UnstarSession`
  - `BulkStarSessions`
  - `PinMessage`
  - `UnpinMessage`

  The API returns `501` / `"not available in remote mode"`, and the frontend mostly appears as if the action silently did not persist.

  Also, `ListStarredSessionIDs` and `ListPinnedMessages` return empty results in the PostgreSQL store, so existing stars/pins are not visible on the hub dashboard.

  ## Expected behavior

  Stars and pinned messages should work in PostgreSQL-backed dashboards, ideally as shared metadata stored in PostgreSQL.

  Expected behavior:

  - starring a session in the hub dashboard persists
  - pinning a message in the hub dashboard persists
  - stars/pins survive dashboard refreshes
  - stars/pins are visible from other devices using the same hub
  - optional: `pg push` can sync local SQLite stars/pins into PostgreSQL

  ## Why this matters

  In a multi-device setup, the hub dashboard is the main place where I inspect sessions. Stars and pinned messages are especially useful for marking important sessions/
messages across devices, so losing those features makes the shared dashboard less useful.

  ## Possible implementation

  A possible approach:

  - Add PostgreSQL equivalents of `starred_sessions` and `pinned_messages`.
  - Implement the star/pin methods on `internal/postgres.Store` instead of returning `db.ErrReadOnly`.
  - Make the PostgreSQL list methods read from those tables.
  - Optionally sync local SQLite stars/pins during `agentsview pg push`.

  If full write support is not desired for `pg serve`, another improvement would be to disable/hide the star and pin controls in remote mode and show a clear message instead
of failing silently.

  ## Environment

  - AgentsView Docker image: `ghcr.io/wesm/agentsview:latest`
  - Deployment style: hub PostgreSQL + `agentsview pg serve`, with multiple `agentsview pg push` devices

title: Updating fails in Windows due to agentsview.exe still running

title: Add OMP (Oh My Pi) agent support
body:
## Summary

[OMP](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) (Oh My Pi) is a popular fork of Pi that stores sessions in `~/.omp/agent/sessions/` using an **identical JSONL format** to Pi. Users running OMP cannot browse their sessions in agentsview today.

## Evidence of identical format

Both harnesses produce the same JSONL schema:
- Line 0: `{type: "session", version, id, timestamp, cwd, title}`
- Messages: `{type: "message", message: {role, content: [...]}}`
- Other: `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`

Filename convention is also identical: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-mmmZ_<uuid>.jsonl`

## Proposed change

1. Add `AgentOmp AgentType = "omp"` constant
2. Extract a shared `discoverPiStyleSessions(dir string, agent AgentType)` helper from `DiscoverPiSessions` (the only Pi-specific part is the `Agent` field on the discovered file)
3. Add `DiscoverOmpSessions` and `FindOmpSourceFile` backed by the shared helper + `FindPiSourceFile` logic
4. Add OMP `AgentDef` to Registry with `DefaultDirs: []string{".omp/agent/sessions"}`
5. Add test fixture + test

Since the parser is identical, `ParsePiSession` is reused directly — no new parser code needed.

## Context

Verified locally: 241 OMP sessions on a heavy-OMP machine, all parsing correctly when routed through `ParsePiSession`.

body:
## Summary
- fix Windows desktop self-update by downloading the update before stopping the bundled Go sidecar
- stop the sidecar only immediately before Tauri installs the downloaded update on Windows, so `agentsview.exe` is not locked
- replace the weak platform helper test with tests that assert stop/install ordering on Windows and non-Windows behavior

## Root Cause
The Tauri desktop app launches the Go backend as a bundled sidecar. On Windows, the running sidecar keeps `agentsview.exe` locked, so Tauri's installer cannot replace it during a desktop update.

Fixes #485.

## Validation
- `mise exec -- cargo fmt --check`
- `mise exec -- go test ./internal/update`
- `cargo test install_downloaded_update` through `VsDevCmd.bat` after preparing `desktop/src-tauri/binaries/agentsview-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe`

title: Feature: Add `insight_agent_paths` config option to override CLI binary paths
body:
When the Generate insight feature invokes an AI agent CLI (e.g. claude), it uses `exec.LookPath` to find the binary using the `agentsview` server process's PATH. This differs from the user's interactive shell PATH when the server is launched from a desktop launcher, a system service, or any environment that hasn't sourced the user's shell initialisation files.

The result is a confusing error like:

```
claude CLI not found: exec: "claude": executable file not found in $PATH
```
even when which claude works fine in the user's terminal.

**Proposed fix:** Add an insight_agent_paths table to config.toml (located at $AGENTSVIEW_DATA_DIR/config.toml, defaulting to ~/.agentsview/config.toml) that maps agent names to  explicit binary paths:

```
[insight_agent_paths]
claude = "/home/user/.local/bin/claude"
gemini = "/usr/local/bin/gemini"
```

In `internal/insight/generate.go`, the `GenerateStream` function currently calls `exec.LookPath(agentBinary(agent))` and fails if the binary isn't on the server's PATH. With this config, it would check the explicit path first and fall back to LookPath if none is set.

The Config struct in `internal/config/config.go` would gain a new field:

```
InsightAgentPaths map[string]string `json:"insight_agent_paths,omitempty" toml:"insight_agent_paths"`
```

This would need to be threaded through from the server to the insight handler so it can be passed into `GenerateStream`

title: chore(deps-dev): bump @playwright/test from 1.58.2 to 1.60.0 in /frontend
body:
Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.58.2 to 1.60.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.60.0

🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

tracing.startHar() / tracing.stopHar() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content, mode and urlFilter options as recordHar. The returned Disposable makes it easy to scope a recording with await using:

await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.

🪝 Drop API

New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
data: {
'text/plain': 'hello world',
'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
},
});

🎯 Aria snapshots

  • expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() now works on a Page, in addition to a Locator — equivalent to asserting against page.locator('body').
  • New boxes option on locator.ariaSnapshot() / page.ariaSnapshot() appends each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height], useful for AI consumption.

🛑 test.abort()

New test.abort() aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});

title: Add current Kiro SQLite session support
body:
## Summary
Sessions started under kiro-cli --classic are visible in kiro-cli chat --list-sessions, but Kiro stores them in ~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3 rather than the legacy ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/ JSONL directory that AgentsView previously read. In my reproduction, AgentsView only detected such a session after it was resumed into the newer Kiro TUI.

Thus, I planned and implemented these feature for AgentView:
- ingest current Kiro CLI sessions from `~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3`
- preserve legacy JSONL-backed Kiro history while preferring the current SQLite record when the same conversation exists in both stores
- add incremental sync, watch fallback, resume, and regression coverage for SQLite-backed Kiro sessions

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/parser -run Kiro -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/sync -run 'TestSyncEngineKiroSQLite|TestResyncAllKiroSQLiteOnly' -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/server -run 'TestResumeSession/kiro current-store command only' -count=1`
- `make build`
- manual verification against a live Kiro CLI store: classic-session conversations now appear in AgentsView without resuming them first

title: feat: add postgres curation metadata
body:
## Summary

  - add PostgreSQL-backed dashboard curation metadata for starred sessions and pinned messages
  - keep pg serve read-only for synced session content while allowing stars and pins to be written to PostgreSQL
  - preserve pinned messages across PostgreSQL message rewrites, including shifted ordinal runs and duplicate source_uuid repair cases
  - Closes #484.

  ## Details

  This adds starred_sessions and pinned_messages tables to the PostgreSQL schema and implements the corresponding Store methods for pg serve.

  Pinned messages use PostgreSQL’s synthetic message ID convention where message_id matches message ordinal. During pg push, pinned messages are reconciled by source_uuid so
  pins can survive message rewrites where ordinals move, such as compact-boundary rows being inserted before previously pinned messages.

  ## Validation

  - go test ./internal/db -run 'TestReplaceSessionMessagesPin'
  - go test -tags pgtest ./internal/postgres -run 'TestStoreStarsAndPins|TestPushPreservesMultiplePGPinsBySourceUUID|TestReconcilePinnedMessagesPrefersCurrentTargetPin' -v

title: test: harden temp dir cleanup for Windows SQLite locks
body:
## Summary

- On Windows, SQLite WAL and mmap'd database files can remain briefly locked after `*sql.DB.Close()` returns, especially when a query was interrupted by context cancellation. The previous 1-second retry budget in `tempDirWithRetryCleanup` was not always sufficient on slow CI VMs, and `dbtest.OpenTestDB` used bare `t.TempDir()` with no retry at all -- making `TestSearch_CanceledContext` and `TestHTTPBackend_Watch_CancelClosesChannel` flaky on `windows-latest`.
- Add a shared `dbtest.MkdirTempWithCleanup` helper that runs `runtime.GC()` first (so `mattn/go-sqlite3` stmt finalizers release mmap regions) and retries `os.RemoveAll` with exponential backoff up to 10 seconds.
- Route both `OpenTestDB` and `server_test.go`'s `tempDirWithRetryCleanup` through the new helper.

title: fix: skip any slash command when computing session first_message preview
body:
Fixes #487.

Session sidebar titles were set from the first user message without filtering slash commands, so sessions starting with `/login`, `/plan`, or similar showed those commands as the title instead of the first meaningful prompt.

Previously only `/clear` and `/effort` were excluded via an explicit allowlist. This replaces that list with generic slash command detection: any message that starts with `/` followed by one or more letters or digits (then end-of-string or whitespace) is treated as a command and skipped. File-path references like `/usr/local/bin gives an error` are not affected because the embedded `/` causes the check to return false.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Gemini usage cost is reported as zero in usage daily
body:
## Summary

Gemini sessions with parsed token data are appearing in `agentsview usage daily --json --breakdown`, but their token counts and costs are reported as zero.

In my local database, Gemini sessions have message-level `token_usage` JSON like:

```json
{
  "input": 6098,
  "output": 20,
  "cached": 2960,
  "thoughts": 539,
  "tool": 0,
  "total": 6657
}
```

The session list also shows non-zero `total_output_tokens` and `peak_context_tokens` for Gemini sessions. But `usage daily --json --breakdown` includes Gemini models in `modelsUsed` / `modelBreakdowns` with all token fields and `cost` equal to zero.

## Why this seems to happen

The Gemini parser stores the raw Gemini CLI `tokens` object using Gemini-style keys:

- `input`
- `output`
- `cached`
- `thoughts`

Relevant parser code:

- `internal/parser/gemini.go` reads `tokens.input`, `tokens.output`, `tokens.cached`.
- `parseGeminiMessage` stores `TokenUsage` as the raw `tokens` object.
- It separately computes `ContextTokens` as `input + cached` and `OutputTokens` as `output`, so session-level token coverage looks populated.

However, daily usage cost calculation in `internal/db/usage.go` only reads normalized keys from message `token_usage`:

- `input_tokens`
- `output_tokens`
- `cache_creation_input_tokens`
- `cache_read_input_tokens`

So for Gemini messages, `usageAmounts` parses the JSON successfully but reads zero for every counted field. This makes the usage report show Gemini models while charging them as `$0`.

Interestingly, token-presence detection already recognizes Gemini-style keys (`input`, `cached`, `output`), which explains why sessions can look like they have token data while daily cost still remains zero.

## Expected behavior

Gemini message token usage should contribute to `usage daily` token totals and cost estimates.

## Possible fix

Normalize Gemini token usage at parse time, for example:

```json
{
  "input_tokens": "input - cached",
  "output_tokens": "output + thoughts",
  "cache_read_input_tokens": "cached"
}
```

Or alternatively teach `usageAmounts` to also read Gemini-style `input`, `output`, `cached`, and `thoughts` keys. Parser-side normalization seems cleaner because it keeps the downstream usage/cost code agent-neutral.

One subtle point: if Gemini's `input` already includes cached tokens, then `input_tokens` should probably be normalized to `max(input - cached, 0)` to avoid double-counting cached input at the full input rate, similar to the Codex parser normalization.

## Local evidence

Example local `usage daily --json --breakdown` row showed Gemini models included but zeroed:

```json
{
  "modelName": "gemini-3-flash-preview",
  "inputTokens": 0,
  "outputTokens": 0,
  "cacheCreationTokens": 0,
  "cacheReadTokens": 0,
  "cost": 0
}
```

But direct message inspection showed non-empty Gemini `token_usage` JSON with `input`, `output`, `cached`, and `thoughts` fields.

body:

title: Support multiple named [pg.NAME] targets with per-target config
body:
## Background

pg push currently assumes a single PostgreSQL target per machine. PGConfig is a flat struct field on Config.PG, and ResolvePG() produces exactly one resolved config. runPGPush loads it and constructs one postgres.Sync. There is no way to declare multiple targets in config.toml, no way to select among them on the CLI, and no shared default to fall back to.

This blocks a few real use cases:
- Pushing different project subsets to different remotes (e.g. work projects to a team PG, personal projects to a private one).
- Pushing the same data to multiple remotes for redundancy or distinct consumers.
- Running multiple cron jobs against different targets without juggling config files or env-var wrappers.

The PG schema itself already supports multi-source data (sessions.machine TEXT NOT NULL partitions by machine name). The gap is purely client-side: config, CLI, and per-target sync state.

## Proposal

Extend config.toml to allow named [pg.NAME] blocks, each carrying the full set of current PGConfig fields:

```toml
default_pg = "work"   # required when more than one target is defined

[pg.work]
url = "postgres://..."
schema = "agentsview"
machine_name = "laptop-work"
projects = ["acme", "infra"]

[pg.personal]
url = "postgres://..."
machine_name = "laptop-personal"
exclude_projects = ["acme"]
```

CLI shape:

- `pg push` → push to the default target.
- `pg push <name>` → push to a specific target.
- `pg push --all` → push to every defined target, sequentially.
- `pg status [<name>]` and `pg status --all` mirror the same shape.

_Backward compatibility_ - A bare [pg] block continues to work and is treated as the implicit single target. pg push with no positional argument behaves exactly as today. Mixing [pg] and [pg.NAME] blocks is rejected at config-load time with a clear error.

 ### Why this fits the existing shape

- The PG schema already partitions by machine, so two targets pointing at the same DB with different machine_name values coexist correctly.
- PGConfig's current fields (url, schema, machine_name, projects, exclude_projects, allow_insecure) just move into a per-target block.
- #412 establishes the precedent for multi-entry remote config ([[remotes]]) on the pull side. This issue is the push-side analog.
- postgres.Sync is already constructed per-call inside runPGPush / runPGStatus, so producing one instance per target requires no global-state surgery.

### Behavior details worth pinning down

- Per-target sync watermarks. The keys last_push_at and last_push_boundary_state are stored as single global SQLite rows. Each target needs its own watermark otherwise pushing to target B will skip work already counted as "done" for target A. Migration: rekey existing values to last_push_at:<default-name> on first run after upgrade. Related to #186, which already flags watermark fragility.
- Reserved names. local is already reserved as a machine_name value. Target names should get a similar reserved-word check (e.g. block local, possibly all since it collides with the flag).
- machine_name provenance. Per-target machine_name interacts with #332 (push currently stomps the original sess.Machine). Both issues should converge on a clear rule: per-target machine_name applies to originally-local sessions; remote-sourced sessions keep their original attribution.
- CLI exit semantics for --all. On a per-target failure: log, continue with remaining targets, exit non-zero at the end. Don't abort on first failure.
- Env-var overrides. Current AGENTSVIEW_PG_URL / AGENTSVIEW_PG_SCHEMA / AGENTSVIEW_PG_MACHINE need a defined target-resolution rule. simplest: they override the default target only.

### Out of scope for v1

- Auto-push from serve (analog of #412's auto-pull). Follow-up once the multi-target plumbing lands. Suggested shape: auto_push = true per [pg.NAME] with an optional push_interval.
- Hot-reload of config changes. A restart on config change is fine for v1.
- pg push --target=<name> flag in addition to the positional. Positional matches git remote ergonomics; a flag is duplicative.

### Alternatives considered

- [[pg]] array-of-tables with a name field. Matches #412's [[remotes]] shape. [pg.NAME] reads better when targets have stable identities used as CLI arguments.
- Profile-based config (single [pg], selected via AGENTSVIEW_PG_PROFILE). Works for the "switch between two configs" case but doesn't enable pg push --all and forces every invocation through a shell wrapper.
- Status quo + per-invocation env vars. Already possible, but doesn't compose with cron and surfaces no shared defaults.

### Open questions

1. Does this overlap with pg-sync refactor spec mentioned in #186?
2. Preference between [pg.NAME] and [[pg]] array-of-tables?
3. Should default_pg be required when multiple targets are defined, or should the config silently pick one (alphabetical, first-declared)?

### Related
  - #412 pull-side analog: periodic SSH remote sync from serve with [[remotes]]
  - #186 watermark fragility on PG URL change; directly relevant to per-target watermarks
  - #332 pg push machine-name stomping; interacts with per-target machine_name semantics
  - #108 original "multi-machine aggregation" ask (closed)

Release notes

Sourced from @​tanstack/virtual-core's releases.

@​tanstack/virtual-core@​3.15.0

Minor Changes

  • iOS Safari momentum-scroll handling. Writing scrollTop while a finger (#1168) is on the screen, during momentum decay, or while the page is in the elastic-overscroll bounce zone all cancel the in-flight scroll in iOS WebKit. The virtualizer previously had no iOS-specific handling, which manifested as the recurring "scroll abruptly stops when content above resizes" complaints on Safari mobile.

    Adds three layers of protection, default-on, all transparent to consumers:

    • Touch event distinction. A touchstart→touchend window plus a 150 ms grace timer for the early-momentum phase. Scroll-position adjustments triggered during any of these states accumulate into a _iosDeferredAdjustment field instead of writing scrollTop.
    • Subpixel reconciliation. When the browser reports back a rounded scrollTop within 1.5 px of a value we just wrote, the virtualizer prefers the intended value rather than treating the round-trip as a user scroll.
    • Elastic-overscroll clamp. The deferred-adjustment flush is skipped when scrollTop is outside [0, scrollHeight - clientHeight], preventing a snap-back jolt at end-of-bounce. The next in-bounds scroll event retries.

    Non-iOS code paths are unchanged. iOS detection is SSR-safe and cached after first call. Bundle cost is ~370 B gzip in the consumer-minified production build — kept default-on because iOS Safari is a large share of mobile traffic for the apps that use virtualization heavily.

  • Skip the scroll-position adjustment while the user is scrolling backward (#1168) by default. When an above-viewport item resizes during backward scroll (images load, content reflows, etc.) the prior behavior wrote scrollTop to keep the visible window stable — but on backward scroll that write fights the user's direction and produces visible "items jump up while I scroll up" jank. title: feat: support Google Antigravity IDE and CLI sessions
body:
## Summary

Adds two new agents to agentsview's session registry:

- **Antigravity** (IDE) — `~/.gemini/antigravity/`. Per-session SQLite
  database; unencrypted. Parsed in full: messages, timestamps, brain
  artifacts.
- **Antigravity CLI** — `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`. Per-session
  protobuf streams under AES-GCM. Parsed in summary mode by default
  (user prompts from `history.jsonl` + plaintext `brain/` artifacts),
  with an optional decrypted-strings preview when `ANTIGRAVITY_KEY`
  is set.

The IDE side is feature-complete. The CLI side ships summary mode now
and falls back gracefully when the AES key is unavailable; full
transcript decryption requires HKDF parameters baked into the
Antigravity binary and has been deferred to a separate, dedicated
tool.

## What's in the diff

- `internal/parser/antigravity.go` — IDE SQLite parser
- `internal/parser/antigravity_cli.go` — CLI parser (summary + optional
  decrypted preview)
- `internal/parser/antigravity_crypto.go` — AES-CTR/CBC/GCM helpers,
  env-var key loader, brute-force-skip retry loop mirroring the
  reference Python decryptor
- `internal/parser/antigravity_proto.go` — stdlib-only protobuf wire
  walker (no third-party deps)
- `internal/parser/types.go`, `taxonomy.go`, `sync/engine.go` — registry
  entries, tool-name mapping, file-watcher classifiers
- `frontend/src/lib/utils/agents.ts` + `AgentDirSettings.svelte` — UI
  labels and violet accent color for both agents
- `internal/parser/antigravity_test.go` — wire-walker round-trip,
  IDE SQLite fixture, CLI discovery+parse (conversations/ and
  implicit/), AES-GCM round-trip, PKCS7 edge cases,
  `history.jsonl` robustness against malformed lines

## Known limitations

- **CLI full decryption requires `ANTIGRAVITY_KEY` to be set manually.**
  The on-disk key is HKDF-derived from the OAuth refresh token in the
  OS keyring, using salt/info baked into the Antigravity binary. The
  binary-RE work to extract those parameters and the keyring probing
  logic are out of scope here and tracked for a separate standalone
  tool.
- **IDE role inference is heuristic** (`step_type==14 → user`, else
  `assistant`). The full `CORTEX_STEP_TYPE_*` taxonomy is available
  via the Antigravity daemon's `GetCascadeTrajectory` RPC and can be
  ported in once the standalone tool's translator code is mature.

## Notes for review

- All new code uses stdlib only — no protobuf or HKDF dependencies
  added.
- `go fmt`, `go vet`, parser tests, and frontend tests all green
  locally and in CI on this branch (Linux + Windows).
- README's supported-agents table updated.
- `.antigravitycli/` (the agent's session directory, created if
  Antigravity CLI is run inside this repo) added to `.gitignore`.

title: fix: allow remote server connections through CSP connect-src
body:
The "Connect to Remote Server" feature points the SPA's fetch, SSE, and WebSocket calls at a user-supplied remote origin stored client-side. The page-serving instance emitted a `connect-src` pinned to its own host:port, loopback variants, LAN IPs, and public origins, so the browser blocked every request to the remote — the server cannot know the client-side URL when the policy is built. The Tauri config had the same loopback-only restriction.

`connect-src` is now widened to any `http`/`https`/`ws`/`wss` origin in both the Go CSP builder and the Tauri config, while every other directive stays pinned to the server origin so script execution remains gated to `'self'`. This matches the backend, where authenticated remote requests already bypass the host-check and CORS restrictions.

Remote connection failures now surface as a status-bar indicator instead of being swallowed in `console.warn`.

The widened `connect-src` is an intentional tradeoff documented in `buildCSPPolicy`: if an XSS executed in the app, a broad `connect-src` would make exfiltration easier; the remaining directives keep script execution locked to `'self'`.
