title: feat(parser): prefer agy-reader trajectory sidecars for Antigravity IDE sessions
body:
Antigravity IDE (Antigravity 2.0) stores conversations in a binary `.db` whose steps the parser could previously only decode heuristically — thinking, tool-use, and per-step model attribution were largely invisible. [agy-reader](https://github.com/mjacobs/agy-reader) can export a structured `<id>.trajectory.json` sidecar next to each `.db` by asking the running IDE's language-server daemon for the real transcript. This PR teaches the Antigravity IDE parser to prefer that sidecar when present.

How it works:

- When a `.trajectory.json` sidecar exists alongside the `.db` and its step count covers the raw step count read from the `.db`, the parser takes the sidecar transcript (reusing the existing Antigravity CLI trajectory parsing path) and promotes the session to `transcript_fidelity=full`. A lagging or malformed sidecar loses to the heuristic decode — coverage is the gate, so a stale sidecar can never hide newer steps.
- The sidecar joins the session's fingerprint companion set, so sidecar creation or updates trigger a re-parse, and archives synced before this change upgrade in place on the next sync. The watcher routes sidecar file events back to the owning `.db`.
- Usage merging is gated on the same coverage check as the transcript, and gen_metadata usage remains primary where it decodes.
- If the `.db` steps table is unreadable, the parser fails closed (parse error, no partial persist) rather than trusting the sidecar alone: Antigravity force-replaces messages on every successful parse, so persisting a sidecar-only result could clobber a previously stored fuller transcript. Lifting that restriction needs engine-level no-clobber support and is deliberately out of scope here.
- Without a sidecar, behavior is unchanged; nothing here requires agy-reader.

On real archives the difference is substantial: the same five IDE sessions that heuristic decoding rendered as 421 fragmentary messages parse to 244 real messages with thinking, tool-use, and model attribution, all at full fidelity.

Reviewers should look at `parseIDESession`/the sidecar-wins branch in `internal/parser/antigravity.go` (coverage gate, fail-closed path) and the companion/watcher wiring in `internal/parser/antigravity_provider.go`.

A known limitation: usage events synthesized from gen_metadata rows on heuristically-undecodable steps still lack timestamps/model when the sidecar wins; borrowing those from the sidecar is deferred to a follow-up to keep this PR to the stable core.

title: build: silence macOS cgo and rolldown build warnings
body:
Cleans up three warnings that appeared on every local macOS `make build`/`make install`, and fixes a pre-existing cgo optimization bug the first attempt surfaced.

**cgo deprecation warnings.** sqlite-vec's cgo bindings `#include "sqlite3.h"` and were picking up the macOS SDK header, which marks `sqlite3_auto_extension`/`sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension` deprecated and can drift from the amalgamation mattn/go-sqlite3 statically links. The Makefile now stages the bundled amalgamation's own header (`sqlite3-binding.h`) into a gitignored `.sqlite-include/` and exports `CGO_CFLAGS=-O2 -g -I...` globally — the same workaround the Linux release workflow and Dockerfile already use. The staging target is chained from `pricing-snapshot`, which every Go-compiling target already depends on. Since this changes the Go build cache key, the first build after this recompiles the cgo packages once.

**Missing `-O2 -g` in every existing `CGO_CFLAGS` override.** Setting the `CGO_CFLAGS` environment variable replaces Go's built-in default of `-O2 -g` rather than appending to it, so the SQLite amalgamation compiles unoptimized (the bench gate caught this on the first commit: FTS and substring search 2.6-2.8x slower). The Makefile export restates `-O2 -g`, and the same latent bug is fixed in `.github/workflows/release.yml` and the `Dockerfile`, which have been building release/container binaries with an unoptimized SQLite since the sqlite-vec header workaround landed.

**PLUGIN_TIMINGS.** This rolldown check is dominated (~80%) by vite-plus's internal `vitest-resolver` plugin, which isn't actionable from this config, so `checks.pluginTimings` is disabled in `vite.config.ts`.

**Chunk-size warning.** Heavy libraries (mermaid, shiki, katex, cytoscape) are already lazy chunks; the trigger is the 1.03 MB main entry (285 kB gzipped). The SPA is served from the local embedded Go binary, so chunk size has no network cost — `chunkSizeWarningLimit` is raised to 1200 instead of restructuring, keeping a tripwire if the entry grows further.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat: add provenance-backed session recall substrate
body:
AgentsView already archives agent sessions; this change adds an experimental Recall substrate for durable, reviewed knowledge derived from those sessions. Recall entries remain linked to exact transcript evidence and can be retrieved through the CLI or HTTP API without treating the transcript archive itself as a memory store.

## What this adds

- New, unreleased SQLite tables for Recall entries, evidence, query events, and ranked exposure snapshots, plus FTS5-backed lexical ranking and byte-budgeted context packing.
- Host-controlled review states and a fail-closed trusted predicate: trusted context requires an accepted, human-reviewed, transferable, provenance-valid entry. Model, eval, and omitted review states cannot self-promote.
- Host-authorized evidence windows with stable message endpoints and content digests. Transcript replacement and full resync remap unchanged evidence or revoke provenance with deterministic diagnostics; revocation never silently re-stamps changed parser output.
- Accepted/archived lifecycle and single-leaf supersession. Reviewed JSONL import is idempotent by candidate ID while new candidates still pass current evidence and supersession validation.
- Append-only query measurement with durable query IDs, miss reasons, ranked exposures, packed flags, strict calibration recording, and resync preservation.
- `agentsview recall` commands for list, get, query, brief, stats, dry-run extraction, and guarded import, with matching REST endpoints. Explicit remote servers require explicit remote credentials rather than receiving the local daemon token.
- A build-tagged eval-ingest inlet whose raw chunks remain quarantined as `eval_raw`, plus dedicated CI coverage for that build configuration.
- Zensical documentation describing the current guarantees, rebuildable data lifecycle, import safety boundary, and staged local-model research direction.

Because these Recall tables are new and unreleased, this branch defines their canonical schema directly rather than adding migrations. During the research phase, Recall entries and measurement rows may need rebuilding as schemas, parsers, scoring, and extraction policies change; the session archive remains authoritative and must not be deleted or recreated as a Recall reset.

## Tradeoffs and limitations

- Recall is SQLite-only and lexical in this change. PostgreSQL and DuckDB stores report it unavailable, and there is no Recall web UI or semantic retrieval over entries yet.
- This is the population foundation, not an automatic memory system. It does not ship model-backed distillation, write-through, bulk extraction, automatic trust promotion, or LongMemEval-v2.
- Ordinary query recording is best effort, while calibration can require strict recording. The append-only ledger has no pruning policy yet; retention, export, and request-size limits must be defined before calibration at volume.
- Raw eval chunks no longer pass `trusted_only`. Eval harnesses that inspect `eval_raw` rows must request `trusted_only=false`.
- Future extraction and judging are local by default. Any remote frontier judge requires explicit per-run disclosure and opt-in because candidate text and supporting transcript material leave the machine.

## Where to review

- Storage, import, evidence reconciliation, and measurement: `internal/db/recall*.go`, `internal/db/schema.sql`
- Ranking and context assembly: `internal/recall/`
- Service and transports: `internal/service/recall*.go`, `internal/server/recall*.go`, `cmd/agentsview/recall.go`
- Resync preservation: `internal/sync/engine.go`
- Experimental user documentation: `docs/recall.md`, `docs/commands.md`

title: session export returns the whole SQLite archive (rc=0) for every hermes session
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.36.1 (commit 4c4bb56, built 2026-07-03T19:21:24Z)

### Install method

Homebrew cask

### OS / platform

macOS 15.7.7 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), upstream 88a58ff1

### Which model(s)

n/a — affects every hermes session regardless of model

### What happened, and what did you expect

`agentsview session export hermes:<id>` exits **0** and streams a whole SQLite database
on stdout instead of that session's JSONL transcript. Every other adapter I have
(claude, codex, cowork, cursor) returns JSONL as documented.

```
$ agentsview session export hermes:cron_2d647784731c_20260708_150044 | head -c 16
SQLite format 3\0        # returncode 0, empty stderr
```

Expected: the JSONL transcript for that one session.

**The session id is validated, then ignored.** A bogus id is correctly rejected:

```
$ agentsview session export hermes:does_not_exist_at_all
fatal: session not in local archive: ...        # rc=1
```

But three *different* valid ids return byte-identical payloads:

```
hermes:cron_2d647784731c_20260708_150044   37,175,296 bytes   sha256 53ac5769ad225157…
hermes:cron_2d647784731c_20260708_050027   37,175,296 bytes   sha256 53ac5769ad225157…
hermes:cron_1ba0e70d34fd_20260707_114622   37,175,296 bytes   sha256 53ac5769ad225157…
```

That payload is `~/.hermes/state.db` verbatim — same byte count, same digest. The export
path resolves the session, then streams the backing store instead of the resolved
session's messages.

**It streams the *default profile's* database specifically.** Hermes supports profiles,
each with its own store:

```
~/.hermes/state.db                          37,175,296 bytes   (default)
~/.hermes/profiles/aphrodite-mood/state.db  24,899,584 bytes
~/.hermes/profiles/light-mood/state.db       9,940,992 bytes
```

Of the 29 hermes sessions in my most recent 500-session page, 2 live in
`profiles/aphrodite-mood`. For those, `session export` returns `rc=0` **and a database
that contains no rows for the requested session at all.** So this is not merely
"returns too much data" — for some sessions it returns the wrong database. A fix that
only scopes the export to one session's messages, without also selecting the right
profile store, would still not reach them.

### Why rc=0 is the actual defect

A nonzero exit would have degraded gracefully in every consumer. Returning **success**
with an off-contract payload is what turns "the hermes adapter cannot export yet" into
a crash downstream: a strict UTF-8 reader hits a NUL at offset 15 of the SQLite header
and dies mid-scan. Mine now sniffs the first 8 KiB for a NUL and skips the session, but
every consumer trusting `rc=0` + the documented JSONL contract inherits this.

There is also a cost: a 500-session scan reads and discards 29 × 37 MB ≈ 1.08 GB, the
same database 29 times over.

### Impact

- Hermes tool-call data is unreachable through the documented interface. Hermes
  contributes 0 tool calls and never appears in an agent breakdown.
- The data plainly exists. Joining `messages.tool_calls[].id → messages.tool_call_id`
  in `state.db` recovers 176 tool calls across those 29 sessions, 0 dangling — a count
  that agrees exactly with hermes' own `sessions.tool_call_count` column.

### Sample session file or snippet

Not attached: the payload is a 37 MB SQLite database containing my full message
archive. The header is enough to reproduce:

```
$ agentsview session export hermes:<any-valid-hermes-id> | head -c 16 | xxd
00000000: 5351 4c69 7465 2066 6f72 6d61 7420 3300  SQLite format 3.
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have hermes sessions in the local archive: `agentsview session list --agent hermes --json`
2. Export any one of them and inspect the first bytes:
   `agentsview session export hermes:<id> | head -c 16`
   → `SQLite format 3\0`, `rc=0`, empty stderr.
3. Export a *second, different* hermes id and compare digests:
   `agentsview session export hermes:<id2> | shasum -a 256`
   → identical to step 2's digest.
4. Compare against the on-disk store: `shasum -a 256 ~/.hermes/state.db` → same digest.
5. Confirm the id *is* validated: `agentsview session export hermes:does_not_exist_at_all`
   → `rc=1`, `fatal: session not in local archive`.

title: session list returns 89 hermes sessions where stats reports 789 (same archive)
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.36.1 (commit 4c4bb56, built 2026-07-03T19:21:24Z)

### Install method

Homebrew cask

### OS / platform

macOS 15.7.7 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), upstream 88a58ff1

### Which model(s)

n/a — the disagreement is in session enumeration, not per-model

### What happened, and what did you expect

`session list` and `stats` disagree about how many hermes sessions exist in the same
local archive, by 8.9×:

```
$ agentsview stats --agent hermes --format json | jq .totals.sessions_all
789

$ agentsview session list --agent hermes --json --limit 2000 | jq '.total, .next_cursor'
89
null
```

`next_cursor` is `null` and `total` is 89, so this is not a paging artifact — `list`
believes 89 is the complete set. Raising `--limit` to 2000 changes nothing.

I expected the two subsystems to enumerate the same sessions.

### Which is right?

`stats` appears to be. Hermes stores sessions in one SQLite DB per profile:

```
~/.hermes/state.db                          (default)
~/.hermes/profiles/aphrodite-mood/state.db
~/.hermes/profiles/light-mood/state.db
```

Counting `sessions` rows across all three gives **816**, close to `stats`' 789 and
nowhere near `list`'s 89.

The sessions `list` omits follow no obvious rule. Broken down by `sessions.source`:

| source | in archive | returned by `list` | dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| cron | 733 | 32 | 701 |
| tui | 46 | 28 | 18 |
| cli | 32 | 27 | 5 |
| unknown | 3 | 0 | 3 |
| photon | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| whatsapp | 1 | 1 | 0 |

It is not "cron is excluded" — 32 cron sessions *are* listed. It is not archived-vs-not
(`archived` is 0 on every row), nor parent/child (`parent_session_id` is set only on 4
of the *listed* rows), nor a dedupe on `session_key` or `title` (`session_key` is NULL
on all 733 cron rows; every title is distinct).

I could not derive `list`'s selection from any column in the archive, which is what
makes me think sessions are being lost rather than filtered.

### Impact

Any consumer that enumerates via `session list` sees ~11% of the hermes sessions that
`stats` reports. For a cross-agent comparison this is worse than a missing agent: hermes
is present, plausible, and quietly under-sampled, so per-agent rates computed off
`session list` are skewed with no signal that anything is wrong.

Relatedly, `stats` reports `sessions_automation: 0` for hermes even though 733 of the
archive's sessions have `source = 'cron'`. I have not dug into that one and am not
claiming it shares a cause; mentioning it only because it may be adjacent.

### Sample session file or snippet

n/a — this is an enumeration count, not a parse. Commands above reproduce it without
any session content.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a hermes archive with more sessions than `list` returns (mine: 816 rows across
   three profile DBs; any archive with a few hundred cron sessions should do).
2. `agentsview stats --agent hermes --format json | jq .totals.sessions_all`
3. `agentsview session list --agent hermes --json --limit 2000 | jq '.total, .next_cursor'`
4. Compare. Ground truth, if useful:
   `sqlite3 "file:$HOME/.hermes/state.db?mode=ro" "SELECT source, COUNT(*) FROM sessions GROUP BY source;"`
   (repeat for each `~/.hermes/profiles/*/state.db`)

### Note

Found while investigating #1047 (`session export` returns the whole SQLite
archive for hermes sessions). Separate defect, filed separately, but the two together
mean hermes tool-call data is currently both under-enumerated and unreadable.

title: Support for ZCode (Z.ai) coding agent
body:
### Agent name and link

ZCode - https://z.ai/zcode

### Where does it store sessions?

macOS:
~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite — full conversation data (sessions, messages, parts, tool_usage, model_usage, turn_usage, todos)
~/.zcode/v2/tasks-index.sqlite — lightweight task index (workspace_path, task_id, title, provider, model, status, timestamps, searchable_text)

The primary source is ~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite which contains everything needed: session metadata, messages with role/model/agent, individual message parts (text, tool calls), token usage per model request, tool usage stats, and per-turn aggregates.

Suggested env var: ZCODE_DIR or ZCODE_DB_PATH pointing to ~/.zcode/cli/ or ~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite

### File format

SQLite database (not JSONL). All sessions in a single db.sqlite file.

Key tables and their mapping to agentsview concepts:

- `session`: id, title, directory (=project path), project_id, workspace_id, parent_id (subagent sessions), time_created, time_updated, task_type, version
- `message`: id, session_id, time_created, data (JSON with role=user/assistant, model info, agent field, contextSnapshot with cwd)
- `part`: id, message_id, session_id, data (JSON with type=text/tool_use/tool_result/step-start, actual content)
- `model_usage`: session_id, model_id, provider_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, reasoning_tokens, duration_ms, status, error info, cost data
- `tool_usage`: session_id, tool_name, tool_call_id, duration_ms, status, exit_code, output_bytes, error info
- `turn_usage`: session_id, turn_id, aggregated token counts, tool_call_count, model_retry_count
- `todo`: session_id, content, status, priority
- `session_entry`: session_id, type, data (compaction events etc.)

Messages are split across `message` (metadata/role) and `part` (content fragments). A single user message has 1 row in `message` + N rows in `part` (text, tool_results, etc.). Same pattern for assistant messages (text, tool_use, thinking blocks).

Subagent sessions use `parent_id` in the `session` table.

~198 sessions in my local db, all structured and queryable via SQL.

title: fix(parser): export hermes state sessions as JSONL
body:
Fixes #1047.

Hermes sessions sourced from `state.db` now export as scoped JSONL instead of copying the SQLite container. The previous behavior could return rc 0 with binary archive bytes for any state-backed Hermes session, and legacy rows that still point at a physical `state.db` would keep repeating that failure until the archive was rebuilt.

The parser now records state-backed sessions with per-session `state.db#session` source paths while preserving aggregate freshness for sync. Export resolves those virtual or legacy physical paths back through the Hermes provider and synthesizes JSONL from the requested row/messages, including tool calls and tool results. Wrong or stale state-db hints are skipped when they do not contain the requested raw session id.

Reviewers should look at `internal/parser/hermes.go`, `internal/parser/hermes_provider.go`, `cmd/agentsview/session_export.go`, and the Hermes-only freshness fallback in `internal/sync/engine.go`. The fallback is intentionally scoped so other multi-session providers keep their existing stale-row behavior.

title: fix(docs): stop instant navigation freezing after loading the homepage
body:
Fixes #1049.

## Summary

Since the docs site enabled Zensical's `navigation.instant`, any instant navigation that fetched the homepage — most visibly clicking the header logo — permanently broke navigation: subsequent clicks updated the URL but the page content never changed again, so the site appeared frozen.

The root cause is in the Zensical theme bundle, not our markup handling per se: before swapping in a fetched document, the bundle absolutizes relative URLs by self-assigning the `href`/`src` property of every `[href], [src]` element. The homepage agent chips used `<svg><use href="#i-...">`, and `SVGUseElement.href` is a read-only `SVGAnimatedString`, so the assignment threw a `TypeError` inside the theme's shared RxJS pipeline. RxJS pipelines terminate on error, so document replacement died for the rest of the session while the independent `history.pushState` subscription kept running — URL changes, frozen content. The issue's suggested `history.back()`/same-URL theory turned out to be a red herring: the freeze reproduces when reaching the homepage from any page, and `history.back()` is never called.

The fix switches the 18 sprite references in `docs/index.md` to `xlink:href`, which the CSS `[href]` selector does not match (it only matches non-namespaced attributes); rendering is identical. `xlink:href` is deprecated in SVG 2 but universally supported, and it is the only spelling that sidesteps the theme bug.

Because the bug lives upstream (still present in Zensical 0.0.48, so upgrading would not help) and only triggers on pages containing plain `<use href>` — direct page loads mask it — `check_built_site.py` now fails the docs build when a built page contains one, so the pattern cannot be silently reintroduced. Worth filing upstream against Zensical; mkdocs-material carries the same unguarded loop.

## Where to look

- `docs/index.md` — the `xlink:href` swap (mechanical, 18 occurrences).
- `docs/scripts/check_built_site.py` — the new guard and its failure message.
- `scripts/docs_assets_test.go` — coverage for both the rejected and allowed spellings; the route list is now shared with a markdown-companion helper so the passing case exercises the full check.

title: docs: document 0.37.4 remote sync

0.37.4 changes HTTP remote sync from repeated whole-corpus transfers to a persistent mirror. The existing brief note did not give operators enough context to size storage, understand full-download fallbacks, preserve host identity, or recover stale mirrors.

This documents the transfer lifecycle, threshold, fallback and compatibility behavior, the Windsurf exception, deletion semantics, and security boundaries. title: feat(postgres): pgvector-backed semantic and hybrid search
body:
PostgreSQL-backed agentsview now supports the `semantic` and `hybrid` search modes that previously existed only on SQLite. Embeddings are never computed server-side: `pg push` replicates the local active embedding generation from `vectors.db` into pgvector tables, and `pg serve` (plus every `--pg` direct-read command) answers semantic and hybrid queries from PostgreSQL instead of returning HTTP 501.

## Push path

- `pg push` gains a vector phase after sessions/messages: it copies the active generation into per-generation `halfvec(N)` chunk tables with HNSW cosine indexes, plus a shared `vector_documents` mirror so snippets and hit anchoring reuse exact local semantics. Opt out with `--no-vectors` or `push_vectors = false` under `[pg]`.
- Generations are keyed by the existing config fingerprint, so machines with identical `[vector.embeddings]` configs share one generation and a serving host searches the union.
- Delta state lives in a PG-side `vector_push_state` table written transactionally with the data, so a PG reset is self-healing. The per-session aggregate hash covers full doc row identity, so metadata-only changes re-push.
- Doc replacement is park-to-sentinel (park existing rows at negative ordinals, upsert onto the freed slots, delete still-parked rows), because `doc_key` is stable while `UNIQUE(session_id, ordinal)` slots shift. Eviction is scoped to sessions the pusher owns per its owner marker (probed with `FOR UPDATE`) and, for filtered pushes, by local project membership.
- Databases without pgvector (CockroachDB, missing extension package, insufficient privilege) degrade gracefully: one notice, vector phase skipped, session/message sync unaffected, semantic search keeps returning 501.

## Read path

- `internal/postgres` implements the same `db.VectorSearcher` seam; the RRF merge, unit fusion keys, subordinate penalty, and snippet helpers are exported from `internal/db` and reused, so mode behavior matches SQLite by construction. Invalid-input parity is pinned by a 10-case cross-backend test.
- Startup fingerprints the host's encoder config and looks up a matching PG generation; a miss keeps semantic at 501 with an error naming the expected and present fingerprints.
- KNN fetches exactly k chunks and sets `hnsw.ef_search = clamp(k, 40, 1000)` per query (with an `iterative_scan` fallback probe past pgvector's ceiling) so large fetches aren't silently capped at the default candidate pool of 40.
- Hybrid fuses the vector leg with an ILIKE keyword leg resolved to document units via `vector_documents`. Known limitation: the PG keyword leg is recency-ordered rather than BM25-ranked (documented).

## Maintenance and infra

- New `pg vectors list` / `pg vectors drop <id>` commands for inspecting and retiring generations.
- The compose test image and CI service container switch to `pgvector/pgvector` images.
- Docs: PostgreSQL sections in semantic-search and pg-sync pages, CLI reference entries, and a maintainer-level "PostgreSQL replica" internals section covering the push/read invariants (including the deliberate cross-generation `vector_documents` sharing).

## Where to look

- `internal/postgres/vector_push.go` — delta, ownership, and park-to-sentinel replacement (the subtlest code in the PR)
- `internal/postgres/vector_search.go` — KNN, ef_search tuning, hydration
- `internal/postgres/search_content_hybrid.go` — keyword-leg unit resolution and fusion
- `internal/vector/export.go` — the vectors.db export API and its fail-closed version gate

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(parser): strip Codex recommended plugin context
body:
Recent Codex builds prepend a `<recommended_plugins>` envelope to the synthetic `role=user` context at the start of sessions. Because it appears before the existing AGENTS.md and environment envelopes, agentsview mistakes the whole item for user-authored content, polluting message history and previews while inflating user-message counts and disrupting automated-session classification.

Strip the envelope only while locating the first genuine user turn, preserving later user-authored mentions and the prompt when Codex places it in the same item. Data version 60 triggers the existing non-destructive resync so already indexed Codex sessions are repaired.

title: feat(search): add semantic modes to command palette
body:
The command palette now supports remembered Full text, Semantic, and Hybrid modes when an opt-in vector index is available. Ranked content is reduced to one best match per session, semantic snippets are rendered as untrusted plain text, and actionable vector setup or rebuild errors remain visible.

Semantic and Hybrid explicitly retain the Full text session scope, including one-shot and automated sessions. Content search can run through the configured encoder timeout instead of being cut off by generic daemon and proxy deadlines; if the encoder still times out, the palette explains that the first search may be warming the model and offers a kit-ui Retry action.

The user guides explain the vector-index prerequisite and remote-encoder latency tradeoff. Full text sorting, result navigation, in-session find, and non-SQLite backends remain unchanged.

title: docs: add 0.37.5 release notes
body: AgentsView 0.37.5 has shipped with parser and date-filter fixes, but the public release history still stops at 0.37.4. Document the patch release so users can see when Antigravity IDE transcripts gain structured sidecar data and understand the Codex and overnight date-filter corrections. Credit the merged contributors in the established changelog format.

title: feat(frontend): navigate between user prompts
body:
Long sessions currently require readers to move through every assistant and tool row to revisit the human instructions. This adds `Shift+J` and `Shift+K` to move among the visible user prompts while reusing the existing selection and virtualized-scroll path.

The change stays in the frontend. Plain `j` and `k`, arrow navigation, transcript filters, find-in-session behavior, live refresh, APIs, and persistent read-progress state keep their current behavior. The shortcuts modal documents the commands, and focused keyboard plus browser coverage exercises mixed-content navigation.

Refs #1057

title: feat(sessions): show read progress
body:
Session updates currently reload the transcript without retaining where the reader stopped, so later output has no boundary in the session view and no signal in the sidebar.

This change adds a read-only `latest_display_ordinal` to session detail and sidebar metadata in SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB. All three backends derive it with the same transcript visibility rules, so hidden system rows do not affect unread state. Browser storage persists one per-session `seenOrdinal`; the first visit establishes a baseline, visible rows advance it, and sidebar unread state compares the two cursors directly.

Message counts remain loading metadata. Progressive loading, equal-count rewrites, and sparse or one-based ordinals no longer infer transcript position from count values. Existing newest-first boundaries, divider placement inside tool groups, and exact tool-group child visibility remain intact.

The SSE watch path, parser behavior, database schema, and prompt-navigation scope remain unchanged. Prompt navigation continues separately in #1064.

Closes #1057

title: Feature request: support Grok CLI / Grok Build sessions
body:
## Summary

AgentsView does not appear to detect or record sessions from the [Grok CLI](https://grok.com/download) (also referred to as "Grok Build" in dev channels). In a local environment running Grok CLI v0.2.93 with an active session, the AgentsView `sessions.db` contains 0 rows with `agent = 'grok'` while other CLI agents (claude, codex, opencode, kimi, etc.) are tracked normally.

## Environment

- AgentsView CLI: v0.37.3
- Grok CLI: v0.2.93 (macOS aarch64, installed via official installer)
- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- Project cwd: `/Users/dinoel/1/appdb`
- Active Grok session PID: 96724 (comm=`grok`, cwd in project)

## Observed behavior

- `~/.agentsview/sessions.db` has 2,658 tracked sessions but `SELECT agent, COUNT(*) FROM sessions GROUP BY agent` shows no `grok` row.
- Grok CLI stores session metadata under `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<session_id>/signals.json` and `~/.grok/active_sessions.json`.

## Request

Please add native support for Grok CLI sessions so that:
1. AgentsView recognizes an active `grok` process/session.
2. Session metadata (model, message counts, tool failures, etc.) is ingested into `sessions.db` under `agent = 'grok'`.
3. If applicable, supports the separate "Grok Build" channel/binary if it uses a different process name or session layout.

## Reference files

- Grok active sessions: `~/.grok/active_sessions.json`
- Grok session signals: `~/.grok/sessions/<enc_cwd>/<session_id>/signals.json`
- Grok config: `~/.grok/config.toml`

### [`v0.2.2`](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/releases/tag/v0.2.2): vite-plus v0.2.2: Vite+ Beta

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/compare/v0.2.1...v0.2.2)

**Vite+ is now in Beta**: stable and ready for production adoption, fully open source under MIT. Read the announcement to see what Vite+ is about and where it is headed: [Announcing Vite+ Beta](https://voidzero.dev/posts/announcing-vite-plus-beta).

On top of the Beta milestone, this release brings cross-version upgrades via `vp migrate`, an official Docker toolchain image on GHCR, zero-config runner-aware `vp build` caching, and PGP-verified managed Node.js downloads.

##### Highlights

- **`vp migrate` upgrades existing Vite+ projects across versions**: previous release notes told users not to run `vp migrate` for upgrades. It now runs from the global CLI when the local one is older, re-pins `vite-plus` and the `vite` -> `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core` alias across dependencies, overrides/resolutions, and catalogs in every workspace package, aligns `vitest` / `@vitest/*` by actual usage, and defaults to a version-only upgrade (pass `--full` to also run the first-time setup bucket: hooks, editor, agent files, lint migration) ([#​1891](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1891)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- **Official Vite+ Docker toolchain image**: `ghcr.io/voidzero-dev/vite-plus` bundles `vp` plus a native build toolchain on `debian:bookworm-slim` (amd64/arm64, non-root). Since `vp` provisions the exact Node.js from `.node-version`, one image builds any project, and a documented multi-stage build copies the resolved Node.js into a small vp-free runtime stage ([#​1944](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1944)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- **Zero-config `vp build` caching via runner-aware Vite**: Vite reports its inputs, outputs, and tracked env reads to the `vp` runner over the new `@voidzero-dev/vite-task-client` IPC ([vite#22453](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22453)), so `vp build` caches correctly with no hand-written cache config: outputs are tracked and restored automatically, and a changed `VITE_*` env var invalidates the cache and is named in the cache-miss message ([#​1774](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1774)), by [@​wan9chi](https://redirect.github.com/wan9chi)
- **PGP-verified Node.js downloads**: installing a managed Node.js now verifies the release's clearsigned `SHASUMS256.txt.asc` against the vendored Node.js release keyring (pure Rust, no `gpg` required) before trusting any checksum, so a tampered archive is rejected before install; unsigned sources (musl builds, custom mirrors) fall back to checksum-only verification ([#​1848](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1848)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)

##### Features

- `vp check`: a `check` block in `vite.config.ts` (`check.fmt` / `check.lint`) can make plain `vp check` skip formatting or linting by default, mirroring `--no-fmt` / `--no-lint`; standalone `vp fmt` / `vp lint` and git hooks are unaffected, and a `note:` line keeps the config-based skip discoverable ([#​1981](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1981)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- `vp env list-remote`: highlight installed versions (color, or a `*` prefix when piped) and label the project-resolved `current` and global `default` versions; `--json` gains `installed` / `current` / `default` fields ([#​1907](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1907)), by [@​semimikoh](https://redirect.github.com/semimikoh)
- `vpr` ships as a `vite-plus` package bin, so the `vp run` shorthand works on clean installs without global PATH shims (Vercel build image, generic CI runners) ([#​1988](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1988)), by [@​kvnwolf](https://redirect.github.com/kvnwolf)
- Vite Task: `dependsOn` can select tasks from dependency packages, e.g. `dependsOn: [{ "task": "build", "from": "dependencies" }]` ([vite-task#479](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/479)), by [@​wan9chi](https://redirect.github.com/wan9chi)
- Vite Task: a task's `env` / `untrackedEnv` glob patterns support `!` negation (e.g. `["VITE_*", "!VITE_SECRET"]`) ([vite-task#425](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/425)), and an env-caused cache miss now names the variable inline, e.g. `cache miss: env 'NODE_ENV' changed` ([vite-task#438](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/438)), by [@​wan9chi](https://redirect.github.com/wan9chi)
- Upgrade upstream dependencies: vite `8.0.16 -> 8.1.2`, rolldown `1.1.1 -> 1.1.4`, oxlint `1.70.0 -> 1.72.0`, oxfmt `0.55.0 -> 0.57.0`, oxlint-tsgolint `0.23.0 -> 0.24.0`, and the oxc toolchain `0.136.0 -> 0.138.0` ([#​1924](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1924), [#​1989](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1989), [#​2000](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2000), [#​2009](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2009)), by [@​voidzero-guard](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-guard)\[bot]

##### Fixes & Enhancements

- Windows: `vp run` no longer hangs CI when a `node_modules/.bin` `.cmd` shim is routed through PowerShell; the npm/pnpm/yarn `.ps1` wrappers read stdin and block forever on a non-TTY pipe, so the PowerShell rewrite is now skipped when stdin is not an interactive terminal ([vite-task#491](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/491), via [#​1973](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1973)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- Vite Task: the task cache is stored in a per-schema-version directory (e.g. `node_modules/.vite/task-cache/v13/`), so switching between branches that pin different Vite+ versions no longer fails with `Unrecognized database version` ([vite-task#433](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/433)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- Vite Task: env values in cache fingerprints are stored only as SHA-256 digests and env cache-miss details report names without values ([vite-task#455](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/455)); prefix env assignments like `PATH=... command` now affect executable lookup during planning ([vite-task#440](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/440)); `package.json` / `pnpm-workspace.yaml` files with a UTF-8 BOM parse correctly ([vite-task#424](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/424)), by [@​wan9chi](https://redirect.github.com/wan9chi)
- `vp upgrade`: run the pinned pnpm with a managed Node.js LTS directly instead of re-entering `vp install`, so an incompatible session/project/system runtime can no longer make pnpm skip optional native binaries and leave the upgraded CLI broken ([#​1900](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1900)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ)
- Global package installs: each install writes to an immutable `packages/<name>#<uuid>` prefix that is activated via metadata after npm succeeds, so an interrupted reinstall can no longer leave the active package unavailable ([#​1906](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1906)), and stale interrupted-install directories are swept with file-lock protection for concurrent installs ([#​1945](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1945)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ)
- `lazyPlugins()`: skip plugin factories only while config metadata is being resolved instead of keying off `VP_COMMAND`, so builds spawned under `vp run` / `vp exec` keep the user's plugins and `vp format` no longer loads them ([#​1939](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1939)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- `vp migrate` (pnpm): add a direct `vite` devDep aliased to the core override wherever `vite-plus` is depended on, so vitest's `vite` peer binds to `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core` instead of pulling in a second upstream vite that broke the `vp test` cache ([#​1933](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1933)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- `vp pack`: bundle `@tsdown/exe` and `@tsdown/css` into core so `--exe` and CSS bundling work without a resolvable top-level `tsdown`; the native `lightningcss` becomes an optional peer loaded lazily with an actionable error ([#​1919](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1919)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- `vp env`: invalidate stale shim resolve cache entries when the project's Node.js version source changes ([#​1951](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1951)), by [@​jong-kyung](https://redirect.github.com/jong-kyung)
- Node shim: when the project declares npm via `packageManager` / `devEngines.packageManager`, child processes spawned from `node` resolve the managed npm instead of the Node-bundled one ([#​1938](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1938)); `vp env which` reports bins linked by an intercepted `npm install -g` (e.g. `tsc`) instead of "not found" ([#​1968](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1968)); bins with uppercase names (e.g. `vitePlus`) dispatch correctly ([#​1963](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1963)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ)
- `vp-setup`: pass the configured npm registry to the inner pnpm install so setup works behind custom registries ([#​1795](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1795)), by [@​daflyinbed](https://redirect.github.com/daflyinbed)
- Native binding: declare the platform packages' true ABI floor `engines.node >=20.0.0` so engine-strict package managers (pnpm) no longer skip the optional native dependency and fail with `Cannot find native binding` when a consumer's Node floor lands in a product-policy gap ([#​1993](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1993)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- `vp create`: run `git init` without creating an initial commit, so commitlint-configured templates no longer reject the hardcoded message and template placeholders are not baked into history ([#​2008](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2008)), by [@​forehalo](https://redirect.github.com/forehalo)
- `vp staged --debug`: inline the bundled lint-staged version so debug logging no longer crashes reading a `package.json` that does not exist in the bundle ([#​1925](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1925)), by [@​rokuosan](https://redirect.github.com/rokuosan)
- Installer: retry downloads truncated mid-body in `HttpClient::get_bytes` (the platform-tarball path for `vp upgrade` and the standalone installer) ([#​1940](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1940)), and clean up the temp dir when a package-manager install fails instead of leaking `.tmpXXXX` directories ([#​1949](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1949)), by [@​shulaoda](https://redirect.github.com/shulaoda)
- Windows/msys: normalize backslashes in the `env.fish` fallback path ([#​1954](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1954)), by [@​Aalivexy](https://redirect.github.com/Aalivexy)
- `install.ps1`: detect the missing VC++ runtime (`0xC0000135`) and print VC++ Redistributable guidance instead of a generic failure; interactive `irm | iex` installs keep the shell open ([#​1962](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1962)), by [@​cheezone](https://redirect.github.com/cheezone)
- `vp migrate`: preserve comments, key order, and trailing commas in existing `.vscode` / `.zed` JSONC configs by patching the original text instead of re-serializing it ([#​1956](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/1956)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)

title: docs: require explicit roborev requests
body: Automated review runs can consume resources and create persistent review state even when review was not part of the requested task. Make both direct `roborev review` invocation and roborev skill activation explicitly user-directed so agents do not treat either as an automatic completion step.

title: ci: run trusted macOS builds on self-hosted runners
body:
## Why

Persistent self-hosted runners are a trust boundary, and a guard inside a `pull_request` workflow is not sufficient because the pull request controls that workflow definition. Relevant pull requests still need Windows and Linux desktop feedback, but no PR-authored workflow may be able to select the homelab Macs.

## Security boundary

- `.github/workflows/desktop-artifacts.yml` is PR-capable and contains only fixed GitHub-hosted Windows and Linux labels
- `.github/workflows/desktop-macos-main.yml` is push-only for `main` and directly selects the `ci-runners` organization runner group
- runner selection is not delegated to a reusable workflow or caller-controlled input
- shared build mechanics live in a composite action, which cannot select a runner
- tag-based macOS release jobs remain GitHub-hosted

## Required before merge

This PR intentionally fails closed until the external runner policy exists:

1. Create the organization runner group `ci-runners` and allow the public `kenn-io/agentsview` repository.
2. Set Workflow access to Selected workflows with exactly `kenn-io/agentsview/.github/workflows/desktop-macos-main.yml@refs/heads/main`.
3. Re-register `m4-mini-01` and `mac-pro-intel` as organization-level runners in that group; repository-level runners cannot be protected by a runner-group workflow allowlist.
4. Remove the repository-level runner registrations and verify a PR cannot queue either Mac before merging this PR.

GitHub documents that only jobs directly defined in an allowlisted workflow can access a workflow-restricted runner group: https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/self-hosted-runners/manage-access#changing-which-workflows-can-access-a-runner-group

## Validation

- `actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/desktop-artifacts.yml .github/workflows/desktop-macos-main.yml .github/workflows/desktop-release.yml .github/workflows/release.yml`
- `zizmor --strict-collection --persona=regular --min-severity=low --no-online-audits .github/workflows/desktop-artifacts.yml .github/workflows/desktop-macos-main.yml .github/actions/build-desktop-artifact/action.yml` (no findings)
- `git diff --check`

The first self-hosted execution should be a trusted push to `main` after the runner-group policy is verified.

title: feat: add skill usage trends to analytics
body:
Skill analytics currently shows aggregate rankings, but it does not make it easy to see which skills are gaining or losing usage across the selected time range. The existing weekly aggregate also hides individual skill movement and cannot adapt to shorter or longer analysis windows.

This adds a dedicated multi-series Skill Usage Over Time panel with day, week, and month granularity. Series colors remain stable while skills are toggled, and lower-volume skills fold into an Other series so the chart stays distinguishable. SQLite, DuckDB, and PostgreSQL share the same bucketing behavior, including explicit zero-usage periods so gaps are not rendered as continuous activity.

Granularity changes are applied only after a successful response, preventing cached data from being relabeled while a request is pending or failed. Localized dates, keyboard navigation, and an assistive data table make the same timeline available beyond pointer-only interaction. The six named-series cap is intentional; it trades exhaustive individual lines for a readable comparison while preserving the full tail in Other.

title: docs: clarify roborev review restriction
body: The existing instruction can be read as restricting the roborev CLI generally. Clarify that only the `roborev review` subcommand requires an explicit user request and encourage normal use of every other roborev CLI command; roborev skills remain opt-in.

title: feat(frontend): make linked date ranges optional
body:
Sessions can query a one-year window cheaply, while carrying that same range into Usage or Activity can trigger substantially more expensive aggregation. Cross-page date linking is now a browser-local, off-by-default preference, leaving Sessions, Usage, and Activity on their useful one-year, 30-day, and current-day defaults.

Sessions and Insights retain independent date selections despite sharing the analytics data store. Restored rolling Sessions selections and rolling URLs preserve rolling route intent while refreshing concrete request bounds before the initial list load, including direct session-detail entries, without consuming message deep links. Explicit detail URL dates replace the shared range before loading. Explicit retained Insights selections restore fixed or rolling parameters and can establish an empty enabled shared range. Returning to bare Usage refreshes its rolling bounds before the first request, including after midnight. Bare defaults remain implicit across reloads and history until a picker, dated URL, or shared seed establishes date intent.

When linking is enabled, the latest explicit selection made while opted out becomes the initial shared range, and subsequent selections carry across Sessions, Usage, Activity, Trends, and Insights. Legacy yoke state migrates toward disabled and empty, Activity keeps its maximum-span protection, and the Settings and user guides describe the behavior. The preference remains last-writer-wins between open tabs.

The shared date picker is pinned to the reviewed kit-ui update: completed custom ranges use canonical YYYY-MM-DD bounds, retain a stable overflow-safe toolbar trigger, and keep responsive endpoint readouts in narrow layouts.

title: Subagent progress heartbeats trigger a full JSONL reparse on nearly every sync, growing daemon CPU/RAM and slowing all reads
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.37.5 (commit 8bd41f0b, built 2026-07-10T03:23:26Z)

### Install method

Scoop (r-bucket)

### OS / platform

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

### Which agent and version

Claude Code 2.1.206

### Which model(s)

n/a

## What happened, and what I expected

I have a Starship prompt module that shells out to `agentsview usage statusline --offline --no-sync --agent claude` with a 3000ms `command_timeout`. It's now regularly timing out — `Measure-Command { agentsview usage statusline --offline --no-sync --agent claude }` gave me 13.03s.

My `~/.agentsview/sessions.db` is 737MB. A `serve` daemon had been running for under an hour and had already burned 152.9 CPU-seconds and grown to 676MB RSS. `debug.log` shows the same session files getting logged as needing a full parse on nearly every watcher-triggered sync, while I have a couple of Claude Code sessions running with the Task tool (subagents) active — 783 "full parse" occurrences across roughly the last 25 hours of the log, clustering heavily around the windows where a subagent was active:

```
2026/07/10 17:08:33 incremental claude <redacted>.jsonl: incremental parse: appended Claude lines require full parse (explicit full parse fallback)
2026/07/10 17:08:33 sync: 1 file(s) updated
2026/07/10 17:08:36 watcher: 1 file(s) changed, triggering sync
2026/07/10 17:08:36 incremental claude <redacted>/subagents/agent-a6463adc0ee369d86.jsonl: incremental parse: DAG uuid detected (full parse)
2026/07/10 17:08:36 sync: 1 file(s) updated
2026/07/10 17:08:36 watcher: 1 file(s) changed, triggering sync
2026/07/10 17:08:36 incremental claude <redacted>.jsonl: incremental parse: DAG uuid detected (full parse)
2026/07/10 17:08:36 sync: 1 file(s) updated
```

I expected `--offline --no-sync` reads to stay fast regardless of what the daemon happens to be doing in the background, and I'd expect the daemon itself to settle into low CPU/RAM once a session is mostly caught up, rather than re-parsing the same multi-MB `.jsonl` file every few seconds for as long as a subagent is running.

## Technical context (my reading of the code, could be wrong)

Following the trail in `claudeParseSessionFrom`, the fallback that seems to be firing here is `needsClaudeFullParseForSubagentMap`:

https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/8bd41f0b7f77b87725fefbe8433fbce6ffa548dc/internal/parser/claude.go#L488-L493

https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/8bd41f0b7f77b87725fefbe8433fbce6ffa548dc/internal/parser/claude.go#L598-L631

As I read it, this bails to a full reparse whenever the newly appended lines contain a `queue-operation`/`progress` event that maps a `tool_use_id` into `subagentMap`, unless that same `tool_use_id`'s originating `tool_use` entry is *also* present in the current append batch (`appendedToolUseIDs`). In practice the `tool_use` that spawns a subagent is written well before that subagent's `progress`/`queue-operation` heartbeats start arriving, so the originating `tool_use_id` is essentially never in the same batch as a later heartbeat for it. If that's right, it means any session with the Task tool active gets a full re-parse of its `.jsonl` on nearly every watcher-triggered sync for as long as a subagent is running — in my case the watcher was firing every 1-8s.

This logic looks like it goes back to kenn-io/agentsview#800 (merged 2026-06-22), so it's not a same-day regression, but the cost seems to compound with archive size and concurrent subagent-heavy sessions — I have several worktrees/projects active at once, each triggering its own reparse cascade independently.

## It's not specific to `--offline`

I initially wondered whether `--offline` was itself contributing, since it skips daemon-transport detection and opens `sessions.db` directly via `db.OpenReadOnly` (https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/8bd41f0b7f77b87725fefbe8433fbce6ffa548dc/cmd/agentsview/archive_query_backend.go#L62-L91, which per kenn-io/agentsview#826 looks intentional). But dropping `--offline` and letting the same command attach to the already-running daemon over HTTP gave comparable numbers (11.64s and 10.38s across two runs, vs. 13.03s with `--offline`). So the slow path isn't specific to the direct-SQLite read — the daemon itself appears to be CPU-saturated by the reparse storm, and any read that touches it (in-process or over HTTP) is slow as a result.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have an active Claude Code session that uses the Task tool (subagents), so its `.jsonl` receives frequent `progress` / `queue-operation` appends while the subagent runs.
2. Have `agentsview serve` (or the auto-started daemon) watching the sessions directory.
3. Tail `~/.agentsview/debug.log` — while the subagent is active, the same session file gets logged as needing a full parse ("appended Claude lines require full parse (explicit full parse fallback)" or "DAG uuid detected (full parse)") on nearly every watcher-triggered sync.
4. Run `agentsview usage statusline --offline --no-sync --agent claude` (or time any other read command) during that window.

I don't have a minimal session file I can attach — triggering this needs the `queue-operation`/`progress` interleaving that only shows up in real subagent-heavy sessions, and my session files are not something I can share as-is.

## Related

- kenn-io/agentsview#1032 and kenn-io/agentsview#1022 — closed CPU/RAM complaints from before 0.37.1, but neither thread mentions this subagent-progress-linkage path, and I can still reproduce it on 0.37.5.
- kenn-io/agentsview#800 — where this incremental-resume logic was introduced.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files (none attached)

title: feat: add config-driven daemon lifecycle commands
body:
Background daemon management was coupled to `serve` flags and best-effort lifecycle behavior, which made automation difficult to reason about and allowed unsafe states to look successful. This adds an idempotent, config-driven `agentsview daemon start|status|stop|restart` surface for the writable SQLite daemon, with lifecycle serialization, complete writer-set validation, ownership revalidation, health and compatibility checks, and configuration preflight before replacement.

`serve --background` remains available for flag-driven compatibility cases such as `--no-sync` and one-off bind overrides. `serve restart` bridges to the canonical writable-only restart path, while the existing broader `serve stop` behavior for read-only PostgreSQL and DuckDB servers remains intentionally distinct.

The README and Zensical command, quickstart, configuration, remote-access, and homepage docs now make the canonical workflow, config-only boundary, authentication requirement for persistent non-loopback binds, and compatibility semantics explicit.

title: feat(export): add stable session evidence contract
body:
Activity, usage, and session consumers need durable source facts without treating mutable directory labels, private paths, credential-bearing Git URLs, or floating prices as evidence.

This adds one versioned, privacy-bounded export contract across those surfaces. It emits archive-scoped project keys with credential-scrubbed repository and worktree context, exact fixed-scale money with pricing provenance, and bounded JSON or NDJSON session summaries with opaque cursor and generation semantics that work without a running daemon. Resolved project labels remain exact across SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB usage filters and pairwise comparisons, including labels that contain commas and projects represented only by fork or subagent sessions. Per-session repository and checkout evidence, including historical unknown and machine-root observations, remains immutable across resyncs; root-derived evidence upgrades only when remote resolution becomes resolved or ambiguous. Legacy archives repair missing snapshots through a resumable background migration, and export status initializes compatible export schema, reports failures, and remains incomplete until repair converges. Full resync preserves real historical snapshots while leaving legacy orphaned or trashed sessions without source evidence eligible for repair; this reconciliation is indexed and limited to the copied batch.

PostgreSQL and DuckDB publication use revision-indexed deltas and durable tombstones with filter-scoped cursors, so routine pushes scale with changed identity rows instead of total archive size. Explicit full pushes and database-generation changes retain full repair behavior. Legacy shared stores without source archive rows use a deterministic response scope so unrelated project totals and catalog entries remain distinct without migrating or scanning sessions. Revision-trigger initialization is idempotent across concurrent archive opens, preventing schema migration races. Daemon-started sync commands announce their intent before startup, avoid redundant local work, and retain the initial local population pass for remote-only requests. A bounded daemon-side fallback performs a skipped local sync if the initiating request never arrives or is canceled. Startup signal and identity backfills wait for sync completion and hold the same exclusion lock as later sync and resync operations, so an archive swap cannot overlap maintenance.

The Zensical session-export reference documents the public contract and the limits of legacy evidence reconstruction. It exports source observations only and excludes organization mappings, accounting policy, prompts, transcripts, diffs, file contents, review bodies, and agent logs. The format is unshipped, so this establishes its canonical shape without a legacy compatibility layer.

title: fix: replay vscode copilot jsonl splice replacements
body:
VS Code Copilot session files (`chatSessions/*.jsonl`) can be parsed with responses truncated mid-stream. 

The issue is that indexed `kind=2` operations are treated as insertions. For response arrays, VS Code uses indexed `kind=2` operations with `i` defined as splice replacements: they replace the existing items starting at index `i`.

This PR updates `jsonlPush` so indexed `kind=2` operations replace `len(items)` existing items starting at the clamped splice index, instead of inserting before that index, if `i` is defined. Also, it updates regression coverage for indexed splice replacement in `TestReconstructJSONL`.

title: perf(sync): reduce background watcher and Codex append work
body:
Active agent sessions could keep the daemon waking every 500ms and repeatedly reparsing full Codex transcripts, which scaled background CPU, allocations, and battery use with the number of writers.

This change makes watcher scheduling event-driven and memory-bounded, with a five-second callback-start floor and overflow-safe force revalidation. It also restores safe Codex append parsing through bounded exact-offset cursors while retaining authoritative full-parse fallbacks for metadata changes, unsafe JSONL boundaries, rewrites, and source replacement.

Warm continuation parsing now scales with appended records rather than transcript history. Full-source fingerprinting and committed-prefix hashing remain intentionally linear and are documented as the next cost boundary.

title: perf(claude): apply subagent linkage incrementally
body:
Claude subagent progress and tool-result appends can arrive after the parent Task call has already been persisted, which made the incremental Claude path fall back to a full JSONL parse for linkage data that should be attachable in place. In subagent-heavy sessions that turns normal watcher activity into repeated reparses of the same large session file, raising daemon CPU and memory use and slowing read commands that should stay cheap.

This change carries subagent linkage through the incremental parser as explicit metadata, lets sync apply it to the existing tool call during the same incremental write path, and keeps the persisted content aligned with the canonical full parser. The update stays inside Claude parsing, incremental sync, and local tool-call persistence; it does not add a schema migration, watcher timing change, CLI shortcut, or backend-specific behavior.

Fixes #1073

title: artifact sync: sequential peer edits are overstated as conflicts and conflict rows diverge
body:
Follow-up from the [PR #731 distributed manual test](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/731#issuecomment-4918949322), accepted as a real non-blocking issue in [Wes's response](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/731#issuecomment-4920979763).

## Problem

Sequential cross-machine edits can be recorded as conflicts even when the second machine has already imported the first edit. In the manual test, machine B renamed a session about 38 seconds after importing machine A's rename. Convergence was correct, but both machines displayed the fork/conflict state.

This overstates the documentation's "close together" or concurrent-edit framing. Conflict records are also local and asymmetric: `conflict_count` can differ between machines, and the machine whose edit lost may show no conflict.

## Expected behavior

Either distinguish causally observed sequential edits from genuinely concurrent edits and only record the latter as conflicts, or redefine and document the ledger as edit history rather than concurrency conflicts.

For genuine conflicts, peers that have converged on the same artifact set should expose consistent conflict visibility and counts.

title: artifact sync watch: peer-only changes wait for the periodic interval
body:
Follow-up from the [PR #731 distributed manual test](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/731#issuecomment-4918949322), accepted as a real non-blocking issue in [Wes's response](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/731#issuecomment-4920979763).

## Problem

`agentsview sync --watch` watches local session directories, not the shared artifact target. An artifact published by another machine therefore does not trigger an inbound exchange; it is pulled only on the periodic `--interval` floor, which defaults to 15 minutes.

The original manual test also found watch mode silent after startup, without clear per-exchange or shutdown output. PR #731 has since added exchange logging, so that portion should be verified against the final implementation rather than assumed unresolved.

## Expected behavior

Watch the folder target for peer changes where practical, or explicitly document that peer-only changes wait for `--interval` and make the effective interval prominent.

Watch output should identify startup, successful or failed exchanges and their trigger, and the final shutdown flush.

title: artifact sync docs: identify --token as the peer auth_token and distinguish a missing token
body:
Follow-up from the [PR #731 distributed manual test](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/731#issuecomment-4918949322), accepted as a real non-blocking issue in [Wes's response](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/731#issuecomment-4920979763).

## Problem

The artifact-sync documentation shows `--token <peer-token>` but does not plainly state where that value comes from. It is the remote peer's `auth_token` in its `config.toml`, not a separate artifact-sync credential and not the caller's local token.

When `--token` is omitted against an authenticated peer, the error can say that the peer rejected the bearer token even though no bearer token was sent.

## Expected behavior

Document that `--token` takes the target peer daemon's `config.toml` `auth_token`. Clarify that local server credentials are not inferred for an explicit peer URL. Distinguish "authentication required but no token was provided" from "the provided token was rejected."

title: fix(hermes): export only the requested session transcript
body:
Hermes sessions imported from `state.db` all record the aggregate database as their source path, so `session export` currently succeeds by streaming SQLite bytes instead of the requested session's JSONL. Profile-backed sessions can also resolve through the wrong database, returning a payload that does not contain the requested session, and the first export fix still re-discovered from live roots instead of honoring the archived source path. It also stopped too early when the archived database missed the session or could not be read, even when the right transcript file was present in that same Hermes root.

This keeps Hermes export on the provider-owned path, but now starts from the archived `storedPath` and only falls back to root-based rediscovery when that exact source and its adjacent transcript directory cannot satisfy the raw session ID. Every Hermes session whose archived path resolves to `state.db` now goes through that filtered exporter, even when the archived row does not carry `SourceVersion` or `SourceSessionID`; in that case export derives the raw Hermes ID from the archived `hermes:<id>` session ID instead of falling through to raw file copy. When the selected source is a Hermes `state.db`, export now uses the same transcript-selection rule as archive parsing, so `session_<id>.json` or `<id>.jsonl` wins whenever it is at least as complete as the database transcript. A same-root `state.db` miss now continues into transcript discovery for that profile, and missing, unreadable, or schema-incompatible stored databases now search the adjacent `sessions` directory before live-root rediscovery, so a duplicate raw ID in an earlier configured root cannot steal the export. Transcript-backed Hermes sessions continue through the same provider authority, while Aider, Visual Studio Copilot, Windsurf, and ordinary raw-file exports keep their existing behavior.

The change is limited to session export and Hermes source serialization. It does not change Hermes ingestion, archive schema, session list or stats behavior; the separate count mismatch remains tracked in https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/1048. Focused tests cover the SQLite-header regression, stored-path precedence, explicit fallback rediscovery, transcript-vs-state export parity, same-root transcript fallback after database misses, adjacent transcript priority across changed roots and duplicate raw IDs, unreadable stored-database fallback, missing sources, and non-Hermes export preservation.

Fixes #1047

title: feat(grok): add a metadata-first session provider
body:
Grok Build stores headless sessions under `~/.grok/sessions`, but agentsview had no Grok entry in the supported-agent registry or provider factory dispatch, so those sessions never entered the sync pipeline and never produced `agent = 'grok'` rows. The initial provider slice fixed discovery and parsing, but sync still overwrote the parser's summary-derived counts with `0`, and search still missed those sessions because the metadata-first provider treated `firstPrompt` as metadata only.

This adds a Grok provider rooted at the official `.grok/sessions` tree and uses the vendor-proven session files to emit stable `grok:<session_id>` rows. `summary.json` is the primary session source, because the official Grok binary describes it as the session index entry carrying the summary, first prompt, model ID, timestamps, and message counts. Optional `signals.json` data is used only for counters that are actually present. Freshness follows the parser's semantic inputs, `summary.json` and optional `signals.json`; the provider watches, classifies, and fingerprints only those parsed files. The parser treats a non-empty `firstPrompt` as proof of one user turn, floors `MessageCount` at that authoritative user-turn minimum, emits that prompt as one synthetic user message for search, and the sync engine preserves those parser-owned summary counts instead of recomputing them from an empty message list.

The scope stays inside `internal/parser` plus the sync write seam: one new `AgentGrok` registry entry, one provider factory case, one provider-authoritative migration mode, a Grok provider or parser pair that own discovery, lookup, and metadata decoding, and a parser-owned count-preservation flag that keeps summary-derived counts intact through sync. It does not decode `updates.jsonl` into a full transcript; it emits only the summary-proven first prompt as a synthetic user message. xAI's own docs and binary strings describe Grok Build and the `grok` CLI as one shared `.grok` session tree, so one provider covers both names here. A second persisted format remains out of scope unless a future artifact proves it exists. Focused parser and sync tests cover discovery, lookup, composite fingerprinting, malformed-artifact boundaries, prompt and summary searchability, and persisted count preservation using synthesized vendor-shaped fixtures built from the official storage contract.

Fixes #1066

title: Date-range preset persisted as fixed dates never rolls forward — app silently stops showing new sessions
body:
## Summary

(Issue posted with an agent🤖, I experienced it, troubleshooted with the agent(fable) and had it draft this commit) The macOS desktop app persists the dashboard/sidebar date range as **fixed calendar dates** (`"mode": "fixed"`) in the webview's localStorage. A range that originated as a rolling preset ("Last year") never advances past the day it was saved, so after a few days the app silently stops showing new sessions — it looks like sync is broken, when in fact the backend is ingesting everything in real time.

## Environment

- AgentsView v0.37.5, macOS desktop app (Apple Silicon, macOS 26)
- Backend healthy: `agentsview serve` syncing in real time, `/api/v1/sync/status` current

## Symptoms

- Desktop app sidebar showed 640 sessions, newest "3d ago"; dashboard activity charts ended days in the past.
- The same server opened in a regular browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` showed 763 sessions with live "just now" activity — the two views diverge because each webview has its own localStorage.
- The only visual hint is the small green dot on the sidebar filter funnel icon.

## Root cause

The desktop webview's localStorage contains a pinned range that matches "last year as of the day the app was first run" (installed Jul 7):

```json
// session-filters
{"dateFrom": "2025-07-07", "dateTo": "2026-07-06", ...}

// yoked-dates
{"version": 1, "range": {"from": "2025-07-07", "to": "2026-07-06", "mode": "fixed", "updatedAt": 1783717314532}}
```

`updatedAt` keeps refreshing, but the range itself never rolls forward. With `dateTo` stuck at 2026-07-06, every session after that date is filtered out of the sidebar and all analytics. Confirmed against the API: `/api/v1/sessions/sidebar-index?...&date_from=2025-07-07&date_to=2026-07-06` returns nothing newer than 2026-07-06.

I can't say for certain whether I explicitly picked a custom range at some point, but the stored dates exactly match "Last year" computed on the install date, which suggests a preset was serialized to fixed dates rather than kept relative.

## Expected behavior

- Presets like "Last year" / "Last 30 days" should be stored as relative ranges and re-resolved against the current date on load; `"mode": "fixed"` should be reserved for explicitly user-chosen custom ranges.
- When an active date filter excludes today, show an explicit indicator (e.g. a banner like "Showing sessions through Jul 6") — the green dot on the funnel icon is easy to miss, and the failure mode reads as "sync is broken".

## Workaround

Clear the date range via the sidebar funnel icon (or re-select a preset in the dashboard date picker).

title: feat(parser): ingest ZCode transcript messages and tool calls (#1050)
body:
ZCode sessions already sync into agentsview with metadata and aggregate token usage, but their transcript tables were not parsed, so every ZCode session rendered with zero messages. The session data already lives in message and part rows under ~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite; agentsview was stopping at session and model_usage.

This change extends the ZCode provider to read the transcript rows and build normal parsed messages from them. Role and model come from each message row, text and reasoning blocks become message content, tool-call blocks become categorized tool calls, tool-result blocks become tool results, and session message counts now reflect the ingested transcript. The parser accepts ZCode's native OpenCode-style part rows, including reasoning blocks and tool blocks with tool, callID, nested state.input / state.output, and failed-tool state.error payloads, while still handling the earlier thinking, tool_use, and tool_result shapes. Missing transcript tables still parse as metadata-plus-usage sessions, so older databases keep their current fallback behavior.

Token totals stay sourced from model_usage, which is the existing ZCode usage authority. The parser data version bump reparses existing archived ZCode sessions so the next full resync backfills transcript content already present in the database.

Closes #1050

title: fix(stats): align session counts with list visibility (#1048)
body:
agentsview stats counted a broader session population than the default session list because the stats path bypassed the one-shot and automated visibility predicates that the list applies by default. That made the same Hermes archive report 89 sessions in the list and 789 in stats.

This change moves those default visibility predicates behind one shared database helper and applies them to stats at the two public entry points that own the default contract: the CLI stats command and the HTTP session-stats endpoint. Internal raw-service callers keep explicit control over whether they want default visibility or the broader population. The HTTP stats client now also sends include_one_shot and include_automated when default visibility is disabled, so direct and HTTP-backed stats return the same result for the same filter.

The result is one default visibility contract shared by the session list and stats across both transports.

Fixes #1048

title: Support custom agent labels for Claude SDK sessions
body:
We run different Claude SDK agents (triage, review, code, fix) via CI and collect their transcripts into AgentsView. Works great for browsing runs, but every session shows up as "claude" — there's no way to tell which agent type ran.

The JSONL already has an `agentSetting` field per session (e.g. `{"type":"agent-setting","agentSetting":"triage"}`), and `entrypoint` distinguishes `cli` from `sdk-cli`. Neither is used for the agent label today.

Two asks:

1. Let `agentSetting` (or a similar field) override the agent display name — e.g. show "fs-triage" instead of "claude" when present.
2. Surface `entrypoint` somewhere (filter, badge, column) so users can distinguish CLI from SDK from web sessions even without a custom label.

title: perf(sync): bound background watcher memory
body:
Active watcher events were loading every persisted source path for providers that never consume those hints. On large archives, passive daemon work therefore scaled with total archive size, creating sustained allocation churn, avoidable CPU use, and a growing physical-memory high-water mark.

Changed-path scheduling now treats stored source hints as an explicit provider capability. Only providers with observable deletion or tombstone behavior opt in; Codex, Aider, and other non-consumers stay on an archive-size-independent path. Exact capability inventory, real-provider tombstone coverage, and a small-versus-large allocation regression keep both memory bounds and persistent-archive semantics enforceable.

Repository guidance now makes a few-hundred-megabyte passive budget, cardinality-scaling tests, isolated profiling, and long-run heap/physical-memory checks standing requirements. The main maintenance tradeoff is that new direct hint consumers must declare the capability and add behavior coverage.

The scheduling gate is in internal/sync/engine.go, provider declarations are under internal/parser, and the engine-boundary regressions are in internal/sync/stored_source_hints_test.go. A four-hour isolated retention observation is still in progress.

title: fix: show live daemon version in status
body:
Daemon status can omit or stale-report the running version when its runtime record is incomplete, making it harder to confirm which binary is active.

Use the authenticated, PID-confirmed ping identity as the version authority. Runtime-record metadata remains a fallback when the daemon is unresponsive or returns no version, so status retains useful diagnostics without writing to the runtime store.

title: perf(parser): reuse JSONL reader workspaces
body:
JSONL-backed parsers allocated two 64 KiB buffers for every source file before doing useful parsing work, making reader setup dominate allocation volume for small and incremental imports. This reuses the composite reader workspace through `sync.Pool`, avoids allocating scratch storage for normal single-fragment lines, and applies the lifecycle consistently across all JSONL-backed agents.

Representative Codex benchmarks reduce allocated bytes from 139–142 KiB to 8–11 KiB per parse (92–94%) and improve the tool-call workload median from 48.7 µs to 34.1 µs. Scratch buffers larger than 256 KiB are discarded on release so exceptional long records do not remain retained.
