title: Improve full remote sync performance and phase visibility
body:
## Problem

`agentsview sync --full` can be disproportionately slow for large remote archives.

The current flow appears to make `--full` force two expensive operations:

- Download and extract the complete remote mirror archive, even when the local mirror manifest is already current.
- Bypass the persistent skip cache and reprocess every discovered session.

These are separate concerns. A full parser/database refresh does not inherently require retransferring and rewriting every unchanged mirror file.

The progress label `Downloading session archive` also covers several different operations: remote directory traversal, tar creation, gzip compression, network transfer, local gzip decompression, and tar extraction. A single aggregate timer makes it difficult to identify whether CPU, network, or disk work is dominant.

## Proposed direction

- Decouple full session reprocessing from full mirror repair.
- Let `sync --full` use manifest-based incremental mirror updates while still reprocessing all sessions.
- Provide a separate explicit repair option when the entire remote mirror must be fetched again.
- Avoid extracting or overwriting unchanged mirror files during ordinary full syncs.
- Report separate progress and elapsed time for archive generation/transfer, decompression/extraction, discovery, and session processing.
- Include compressed bytes transferred and processing throughput where available.

## Acceptance criteria

- A full sync against an unchanged remote archive does not transfer the complete archive unless repair is explicitly requested.
- Full sync still reparses all sessions when requested.
- Progress output distinguishes transfer from local extraction and processing.
- Regression coverage demonstrates that mirror transfer work is bounded by changed files rather than total archive size for the ordinary full-sync path.
- Existing deletion, tombstone, and persistent-mirror behavior remains intact.

title: feat(settings): show embeddings build status and ETA
body:
Vector index builds were only observable from the CLI: the daemon already served `/api/v1/embeddings/status` and `/generations`, and the frontend's generated client covered both, but nothing consumed them. Users running semantic search had no way to tell from the UI whether indexing was running, how much remained, when it would finish, or whether the last build failed.

Settings now includes an Embeddings section showing the configured model and dimension, the build phase with chunk progress, percentage, smoothed throughput, elapsed time and ETA, the last build's outcome or error, and each generation with its state and embedded/missing coverage.

The ETA is a tqdm-style exponentially weighted moving rate over monotonic polling samples rather than a naive elapsed-time average: it stays in an explicit estimating state until two positive progress deltas exist, smooths bursts, counts stall time against the resumed rate, and resets when the build identity, phase, or total changes or progress moves backwards. To make build identity reliable across page reloads, `vector.BuildStatus` explicitly gains `build_id` and `started_at` (plus the configured `model`/`dimension` so the section renders before any generation exists) instead of the frontend guessing that two unrelated builds are continuous.

Polling is bounded and self-cleaning: 2s while a build runs and the page is visible, a slow idle tick to notice CLI- or scheduler-started builds, nothing while the tab is hidden or after a 501, and full teardown on unmount. An unconfigured or lock-disabled vector store (501) renders as an explicit unavailable state carrying the server's reason rather than an error. All four locale catalogs gain the new keys with plural variants; numbers and durations are locale-aware.

Tradeoffs and scope: build/activate/retire controls are intentionally out of scope (status and observability only), and `build_id` is per-daemon-process rather than persisted, which is sufficient for estimator resets. The first commit is unrelated generated-client drift (push routes had moved to streaming on main without a regen) committed separately so the feature diff stays reviewable.

Where to look: `internal/vector/manager.go` for the BuildStatus extension, `frontend/src/lib/utils/etaEstimator.ts` for the rate model, and `frontend/src/lib/components/settings/EmbeddingsSettings.svelte` for the polling lifecycle and states.

title: feat(vector): support reduced output dimensions for embedding models
body:
The configured `dimension` only validated response length and joined the generation fingerprint; it was never sent as the OpenAI-compatible `dimensions` request field. That made Matryoshka dimension reduction unusable with models such as Qwen3-Embedding through Ollama, where the server only reduces output when the request asks for it — the only options were the model's native dimension or a hard dimension-mismatch failure.

A new opt-in `[vector.embeddings] request_dimensions` sends the configured dimension on every embeddings call. Because every encoder is constructed through the single `newVectorEncoder` path, document builds and search-query encoding always request the identical length, on every configured server. When the flag is unset the request body is byte-identical to before, so endpoints without dimension selection are unaffected.

Reduction is never faked client-side, because truncating locally would silently change the embedding space relative to what the server would produce. An endpoint that rejects the `dimensions` field fails fast with an error naming `request_dimensions` and the fix (deliberately unlike the `encoding_format` rejection, which downgrades transparently since it is transport-only), and an endpoint that silently ignores the field and returns native-length vectors hits the existing dimension check with the same guidance. Both errors keep their `HTTPStatusError` classification, so a config-level rejection aborts a build rather than skip-stamping the corpus.

The flag joins the generation fingerprint only when enabled, following the `input_suffix` precedent: configs written before the key existed keep their fingerprints, while enabling it cuts a new generation and the staleness gate forces a rebuild — reduced vectors are renormalized prefixes, not byte-identical to native output at the same length, so reusing an existing index would be wrong even when the dimension value is unchanged.

Reviewers should look at the error-classification changes in `internal/vector/encoder.go` (the new rejection path sits next to the encoding_format downgrade and must not disturb the retry/permanence rules), the fingerprint param in `cmd/agentsview/embeddings.go`, and the end-to-end reduced-dimension test in `internal/vector/search_test.go`, which drives a real HTTP encoder against a Matryoshka-style stub through build and search. `docs/semantic-search.md` gains a section with the Ollama/Qwen3 example. One limitation: there is no client-side probe for whether a model supports reduction — the first build or query surfaces the endpoint's answer as an actionable error.

title: perf: bound passive daemon memory and warm sync work
body:
Large local archives could leave the daemon with high passive memory because every SQLite connection retained a large cache, startup maintenance streamed full prompt bodies, and each scheduled sync rehashed every unchanged Claude and Codex transcript. Those costs compounded even with no new sessions and made passive resource use scale with archive size.

This bounds SQLite cache residency and automation-audit transfer, narrows Codex title reads, and lets explicitly opted-in local providers reuse process-local verified filesystem signatures. Codex trust includes the shared title index identity and change time, so missed watcher events and same-stat title rewrites still self-heal. Trust is also invalidated by transcript changes, overflow, resync, incomplete discovery, and persisted row, file-metadata, parser-version, or project-health failures; forced and remote sources retain deep verification. The Go classifier remains the sole classification authority, with matching SQLite and PostgreSQL behavior.

On an isolated 47,081-source archive, a 20m45s retention run ended at 144 MiB physical footprint and 65.6 MiB forced-GC heap, with a 214.6 MiB active peak. The current unchanged scheduled sync completed in 1.028s versus the earlier 10.736s baseline, and 47,000 retained trust records use 10.65 MiB.

title: test(parser): skip allocation check under race detector
body: Race instrumentation changes sync.Pool behavior by randomly discarding returned values, so the hard allocation ceiling can fail despite unchanged parser behavior. Make race builds explicitly skip this unsupported measurement while retaining the normal allocation regression guard. Behavioral parser coverage continues to run under the race detector.

title: feat(frontend): show transcript read progress
body:
Adds browser-local transcript read progress: sessions that change after being read show an unread indicator in the sidebar, and reopening one places a last-seen divider at the stored ordinal. Markers remain bounded in localStorage, and first visits establish a baseline instead of marking every existing session unread.

A backend-neutral `transcript_revision` now advances transactionally with visible message and tool content, while metadata-only edits such as renaming a session leave read state unchanged. SQLite owns the revision, DuckDB and PostgreSQL mirror it, both mirror backends perform target-scoped one-time full backfills, and full resyncs preserve the prior revision for unchanged transcripts while advancing changed content and retaining archived orphans.

Read acknowledgement is coupled to the refreshed message window: a fetched revision is published only after its messages arrive, and newest-first traversal must cross the unread endpoints before the session is marked read. Precise in-session change ordinals preserve narrow boundaries; reopened revisions without durable change metadata conservatively begin at the earliest displayed message. This keeps the indicator accurate for appended messages, earlier rewrites, grouped tool output, filtered transcript views, and either sort direction.

Closes #1057

title: perf(sync): keep full HTTP remote sync incremental
body:
`agentsview sync --full` currently treats "reparse every HTTP-remote session" and "repair the persistent mirror cache" as the same operation, so unchanged remotes still download and re-extract the whole dir-scoped archive before parsing. This change keeps ordinary full sync on the manifest-backed mirror path, reparses every remote session as requested, and moves whole-mirror repair behind the explicit `--repair-mirror` path instead of baking it into every full sync. Explicit repair still reparses every imported remote session after refreshing the mirror bytes.

The transfer decision stays bounded by the existing mirror rules: bootstrap, half-or-more changed files, or a rejected delta still fall back to a full archive, file-scoped exports still fetch as their own small full archives, and mirror deletions remain non-destructive to the local database. This follows the scoped direction in #1094 from @wesm, keeping ordinary full sync work proportional to changed mirror files rather than total archive size while preserving repair as an explicit action.

Progress output is also split into archive transfer, archive extraction, discovery, and session processing so the elapsed timers line up with the actual work. Remote progress continues to show compressed transfer bytes, and the processing phase now reports throughput when the session and message counters make that meaningful for operators watching long remote syncs.

Closes #1094

title: fix(serve): surface runtime-record write warnings in serve logs (#1097)
body:
When a serve process binds successfully but fails to persist its daemon runtime record, the one actionable warning lands only in `debug.log`. Background launches point users at `serve.log`, so the visible lifecycle output shows the normal banner and log path while hiding the reason discovery broke.

This change routes that post-bind runtime-record warning through the same visible stream as the serve banner, while keeping the existing startup behavior intact. The writable local serve path adds the owner-fix hint in the log text, and the read-only PostgreSQL and DuckDB serve paths reuse the same visible-warning contract without changing their discovery semantics. PostgreSQL now reaches the real post-bind runtime-write branch through a narrow pre-bind startup seam, so the regression proof exercises the production warning path instead of a test-only shortcut. The lifecycle fallback and stop recovery stay in the sibling slice.

The scope and failing log-path trace came from https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/1097#issuecomment-4948947592. Focused runtime-warning entrypoint tests, `go vet ./cmd/agentsview`, formatting, diff checks, and the final adversarial rerun all passed on this branch.

Refs #1097

title: fix(daemon): recover recordless writable daemons after startup-state lock acquisition
body:
Kit v0.7.1 and agentsview #1107 resolve the Administrator-owned-directory trigger from #1097 through the normal runtime-record path. This PR covers a separate failure mode: a writable daemon has already acquired the trusted startup-state lock and bound successfully, but publishing its runtime record then fails.

The daemon now records its bound endpoint, process identity, compatibility versions, launch options, and managed-Caddy identity in startup state when that post-lock write fails. Runtime records remain authoritative when present; otherwise discovery accepts the fallback only while the lock is held and the live ping matches the recorded process. If runtime-store enumeration itself fails, discovery and lifecycle commands use the same confirmed fallback; without one, they preserve the original inspection error. Stale state, incompatible daemons, and read-only servers continue to fail closed.

Status and transport discovery can use the recovered endpoint, while stop, restart, and upgrade paths can safely target the confirmed recordless writer. This preserves the existing policy of keeping an already-bound server alive after runtime-record publication fails instead of leaving that server running but undiscoverable.

Refs #1097

title: Include the session's recorded model in the generated resume command
body:
The resume command agentsview generates doesn't pin the model the session was recorded with, so resuming drops you into whatever model the harness currently has active. It should carry the recorded model flag, e.g. `--model` for Claude Code and `-m` for Codex.

## Why

Neither Claude Code nor Codex re-selects a resumed session's original model on its own, so you silently continue under the wrong one. Codex at least warns:

```
⚠ This session was recorded with model `gpt-5.5` but is resuming with `gpt-5.6-luna`. Consider switching back
  to `gpt-5.5` as it may affect Codex performance.
```

Claude Code says nothing. Pinning the model avoids both the performance drift Codex warns about and a cost hit: prompt caches are per-model, so resuming under a different model re-sends the whole accumulated context at full uncached input rate instead of the cheap cache-read rate.

agentsview already knows the model (`sessions.model`, and per-event `usage_events.model`), so filling the template in is straightforward. When a session used more than one model, which one to pin is the maintainer's call.

## Where

The templates in `internal/server/resume.go` only interpolate the session ID:

```go
var resumeAgents = map[string]string{
    "claude":   "claude --resume %s",
    "codex":    "codex resume %s",
    ...
}
```

So the emitted command is `claude --resume <id>` / `codex resume <id>`, with no model pinned.

## The ask

Fill the recorded model into the command for agents whose CLI takes a model flag:

- `claude --resume <id> --model <model>`
- `codex resume <id> -m <model>`

Leave templates unchanged for agents whose CLI has no model flag.

title: fix(deps): update kit for trusted Windows directory owners
body:
AgentsView remained pinned to kit v0.2.1, so Windows data directories created by elevated processes could still fail runtime-store validation when owned by built-in Administrators.

Update to kit v0.7.1, which aligns protected private-directory ownership with the trusted DACL principals while retaining the stricter file-owner boundary. Normal start-lock and runtime-record discovery can now handle the #1097 ownership case; the module graph also adopts the telemetry and terminal-width versions required by current kit packages.

Refs #1097

title: Speed up configured full HTTP remote syncs
body:
Large configured HTTP remotes made a full sync disproportionately expensive because unchanged source archives were retransferred and remote sessions were written through the active database with live FTS maintenance. That made remote processing several times slower than reparsing an equivalent local corpus.

This separates mirror transfer decisions from full reparsing. HTTP mirrors are reconciled before database work, then local sources and prepared HTTP remotes share one batched temporary-database rebuild with FTS rebuilt once and the result swapped atomically. Rebuild safety is evaluated independently for local and remote contributors, and the aggregate guard includes only participating sources so deferred SSH history cannot block the swap.

Local ingestion now identifies sessions with the operating-system hostname instead of the ambiguous `local` label. Contributor safety counts are also scoped by their remote ID namespace, so a collector and remote with the same hostname remain independent. The data-version bump reparses existing source-backed sessions into the hostname identity while preserving orphaned archive history.

Preparation, contributor, cancellation, and rebuild failures leave the active archive intact. HTTP sync entry points use one cleanup-before-engine lock order, and failed temporary-resource cleanup retains every distinct owner for retry—including joined failures and extraction setup errors—until all resources release. Retryable per-host cleanup remains attributed as one sanitized remote failure rather than being reported as a local sync failure.

Hashed Claude and Codex skip-cache entries now use a source-family index built when cache state is loaded. Watcher replacement is constant work regardless of archive size, remote cache injection scales with the incoming batch, and ambiguous legacy duplicate families reparse once instead of retaining an arbitrary stale key.

Configured SSH-only syncs retain the legacy aborted-resync fallback, while mixed HTTP and SSH syncs run SSH imports after a successful atomic swap. Remote-only syncs retain their active-archive behavior.

Collectors remain compatible with older HTTP-capable spokes through the legacy full-archive endpoint. A collector-only upgrade gains the bulk-ingest improvement; upgrading spokes additionally enables manifest-delta transfer. The durable remote-sync documentation describes that rollout boundary and the manual repair procedure for same-stat mirror corruption.

The branch also records the reviewed follow-up design for daemon startup readiness, startup version reporting, and host-local contributor progress; those UX changes are not implemented here.

Closes #1094

title: feat(cli): add stable version JSON contract
body:
Adds a versioned machine-readable identity response that succeeds without daemon, configuration, or database state.

The existing plaintext `agentsview --version` and `agentsview version` surfaces remain unchanged for compatibility. Machine consumers can opt into the shared CLI output convention through either `--format json` or its `--json` shorthand, require the documented schema version, and ignore future optional fields.

title: fix(ci): retry transient SSH image builds
body:
Transient Docker Hub authentication or registry outages can currently discard an integration run after the PostgreSQL suite has already passed. That makes external availability indistinguishable from a product or test regression.

Route the SSH test image build through a bounded three-attempt retry with linear backoff while preserving the final failure status. The helper is behaviorally covered for recovery, exhaustion, argument forwarding, backoff timing, and invalid configuration. Persistent build errors remain visible after at most 30 seconds of additional waiting.

title: fix(activity): advance calendar date without refresh
body:
When Activity stays mounted across local midnight, its calendar previously kept the old maximum selectable date and rejected the newly current day until refresh.

Keep the bound aligned to the browser local day with a component-scoped one-shot midnight schedule. Each run samples the current clock before calculating the next local boundary, so delayed background tabs and initialization-to-mount rollovers catch up correctly while unmount cleanup remains bounded.

title: test: make DuckDB warning helper condition-based
body:
The DuckDB visible-warning regression helper stopped itself three seconds after process start. On a loaded Windows runner, startup consumed that cutoff and the process exited cleanly before emitting the warning, leaving the assertion with empty output.

Make completion follow the observable stdout warning instead. The parent bounds and reaps the helper after that condition while preserving early-exit and timeout diagnostics; the child timer remains only as a distant orphan guard. This removes runner speed from the assertion while continuing to exercise the real DuckDB serve path.

title: fix(server): prevent stale SPA asset fallbacks
body:
Browsers can retain an older SPA entry document after upgrading the embedded frontend. When that document requests an obsolete fingerprinted bundle, the server currently returns the SPA entry HTML with status 200, leaving the interface partially broken and hiding the underlying cache mismatch.

Entry documents now require revalidation, while fingerprinted assets retain long-lived immutable caching. Missing `/assets/` requests return a real 404 instead of entering the client-route fallback; normal SPA routes and reverse-proxy base paths retain their existing behavior.

title: fix(daemon): report restart progress until ready
body:
Canonical daemon restarts currently wait silently for five seconds, then report a fatal-looking timeout while a healthy child continues database or sync startup. That makes routine restarts look failed and forces users into a second status command without showing what work is underway.

Keep the canonical restart attached to authoritative runtime readiness and surface trusted startup phases, detail updates, and bounded heartbeats. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM releases only the CLI wait and identifies the continuing child; signals received after stopping the old daemon still allow the replacement launch to proceed. Daemon start, automatic startup, background serve, and compatibility restart retain their existing finite behavior.

Make-driven lint also keeps analyzer state in an ignored checkout-local cache. The default shared cache can carry stale findings and fix positions across sibling worktrees.

Prompt-navigation browser coverage now selects its fixture using exact sidebar project and count fields. Broad descendant-text matching could select a larger session and fail before exercising the shortcuts.

title: Desktop in-app update reliably fails: 10s backend-stop timeout races serve stop's own 10s grace and daemon startup sync
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.37.1 (commit 9621af85, built 2026-07-08T14:36:14Z) — desktop app (also reproduced with v0.37.5 sidecar; the relevant code is unchanged on `main`)

### Install method

GitHub release binary (desktop NSIS installer)

### OS / platform

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

### Which agent and version

n/a

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened

Accepting the desktop app's update prompt reliably ends in an **"Update Failed"** dialog ("Failed to install the update. Please try downloading manually…"), so in-app updates never complete. It looks like a download failure to the user, but the download actually succeeds.

Captured stderr from the desktop app during the failure:

```
[agentsview] timed out waiting for serve stop before update install
[agentsview] serve stop did not report success, but no detached daemon port is known
[agentsview] update install failed: backend did not stop before update install
```

I verified the release artifacts themselves are fine: the `updater/latest.json` manifest, asset URLs, and minisign signature for `AgentsView_0.37.5_x64-setup.nsis.zip` all check out, and `update.download()` completes. The failure is in the stop-backend-before-install phase.

### Root cause

Two nested timing problems in `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` since the daemon-first change (#826):

1. `UPDATE_SIDECAR_STOP_TIMEOUT` is 10s for the whole stop phase (spawn `serve stop` + graceful daemon shutdown + port-free wait), but `serve stop` itself waits up to `serveStopGraceTimeout` = 10s for a graceful shutdown before escalating. The outer deadline always expires first whenever shutdown isn't near-instant (e.g. WAL checkpoint / active sync on a large archive — mine has ~4.6k sessions).
2. While the daemon is still running its startup sync (~34s on my archive), `serve stop` exits non-zero with `serve stop: a server is starting; retry once it is ready`. `stop_detached_backend_for_update_with_port` treats one failed attempt as fatal and aborts the update. Since `schedule_auto_update_check` fires 5s after launch — exactly inside the startup-sync window — accepting the update prompt shown at startup fails essentially every time.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a reasonably large archive so daemon startup sync takes >15s.
2. Launch the desktop app on a version with an available update.
3. Accept the "Update Available" prompt when it appears shortly after launch.
4. Download progresses, then "Update Failed" appears; stderr shows the lines above.

### Fix

PR incoming: give the stop phase a larger budget (120s), retry `serve stop` until the daemon is ready to stop instead of aborting on the first non-zero exit, and show a distinct dialog message for the backend-stop-timeout case so it is no longer reported as a download/install problem.

title: fix(desktop): retry backend stop before update install
body:
Fixes #1117

Accepting the desktop update prompt shortly after launch could finish the download but fail before installation. The updater allowed only ten seconds for the complete backend-stop phase even though `serve stop` can spend that entire interval on graceful shutdown, and it treated the daemon's temporary startup refusal as a terminal failure.

The updater now gives backend shutdown a 120-second budget shared across launcher termination, retry attempts, and detached-daemon shutdown. It retries only the explicit "server is starting" response; command errors and other non-zero exits still fail immediately. A backend-stop failure also gets a distinct dialog instead of being presented as a download problem.

title: test: eliminate Windows flake in embed scheduler burst test
body:
## Summary

`TestEmbedSchedulerBurstOfNotifyProducesExactlyOneBuild` intermittently fails on Windows because the test's notification loop can cross its debounce boundary.

The failure observed two builds instead of one:

```text
TestEmbedSchedulerBurstOfNotifyProducesExactlyOneBuild
expected: 1
actual:   2
```

- Failed job: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/29221572361/job/86727611902
- Unchanged rerun passed: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/29221572361/job/86728714695

## Likely cause

The test sends 10 notifications with a 2 ms sleep between each one while using a 20 ms debounce interval. On a slower or coarsely scheduled Windows runner, the loop can take longer than 20 ms. That allows the scheduler to issue one build before the loop finishes, then issue a second build for the remaining notifications.

This is a timing assumption in the test rather than evidence of a production scheduler regression.

## Suggested fix

Make the burst deterministic without relying on wall-clock timing. For example, queue the notifications before starting `Run`, or introduce controllable timer synchronization if needed. Avoid fixing this only by increasing sleeps or debounce durations, which would preserve the same race with a wider window.

The revised test should continue to prove that a burst of notifications collapses into exactly one build and should pass reliably under repeated Windows CI runs.

title: feat: add agent deep links and dynamic local ports
body:
## Summary

Add local desktop deep links for terminal-created Codex and Claude Code sessions while keeping the desktop backend on an OS-assigned localhost port.

## Requirements

- Open local terminal-created Codex sessions in Codex Desktop from the existing session Resume menu.
- Open local Claude Code sessions from the same menu using the official Claude Code deep-link scheme.
- Avoid generating desktop links for remote sessions.
- Avoid reserving the commonly used `8080` port for the desktop sidecar.

## Changes

- Add `codex://threads/<thread-id>` for local Codex sessions.
- Add `claude-cli://open?cwd=<encoded-session-directory>` for local Claude Code sessions.
- Add localized Codex Desktop and Claude Code menu labels.
- Allow the Tauri wrapper to forward `codex://` and `claude-cli://` URLs to the operating system.
- Start the desktop sidecar with `--background --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0` so the OS assigns an available local port.
- Keep the desktop documentation focused on the Tauri app and its dynamic local backend URL.

## Scope

This PR does not include a macOS menu-bar companion or a Tauri status item. Those implementations are retained separately for possible future work. Claude Code deep links open a new terminal session in the selected working directory; they do not resume an existing session by ID. See the [Claude Code deep-link documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/deep-links).

title: test(frontend): pin prompt navigation fixture
body:
Prompt-navigation E2E coverage was previously identified by display metadata. That avoided one broad-text collision but can become ambiguous again if fixture data adds another session with the same project and user-message count, allowing the test to select a nested or unrelated session and fail before shortcut behavior is exercised.

Pin the setup to the fixture's stable session ID and wait until the message pane confirms that ID. This keeps future fixture changes from reintroducing the same class of CI flake while retaining the shortcut assertions.

title: test: make embed scheduler burst deterministic
body:
The embed scheduler burst regression test relied on ten sleep-spaced notifications completing within a 20 ms debounce interval. On slower or coarsely scheduled Windows runners, that synthetic burst could cross the debounce boundary and legitimately produce two builds, creating a false product-regression signal.

Queue the notifications before the scheduler starts so the test exercises the scheduler’s documented pre-reader coalescing contract directly. The exactly-one-build assertion remains intact without depending on runner speed.

Fixes #1119

title: Project selector crashes (each_key_duplicate) when the database contains a project with an empty name (e.g. Antigravity CLI summary-mode sessions)
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.37.5 (commit 8bd41f0b, built 2026-07-10T03:17:25Z)

### Install method

install.sh / install.ps1

### OS / platform

macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

Antigravity CLI (agy) 1.1.1

### Which model(s)

n/a (UI regression; any Antigravity CLI summary-mode session triggers it regardless of model)

### What happened, and what did you expect

Clicking the project selector in the header shows the focus ring but the popover never opens; the control is effectively dead. Expected the dropdown to open and list projects. Worked on v0.34.5 with identical data; broke immediately after upgrading to v0.37.5. Reproduced in a clean incognito profile with all extensions disabled, on two different origins (direct IP and reverse-proxied HTTPS).

The console shows an uncaught Svelte error on every click:

```
Uncaught Error: https://svelte.dev/e/each_key_duplicate
    at index-client-*.js:30 ...
```

#### Root cause

kit-ui's `Typeahead.svelte` renders its options with a keyed each-block keyed on `option.name`:

```svelte
{#each rows as row, i (row.option.name)}
```

`ProjectTypeahead.svelte` prepends an "All projects" option with `name: ""` to the project list:

```ts
const allOption = { name: "", label: m.shared_all_projects(), ... };
```

When the API's project list itself contains a project named `""`, two rows share the key `""` and Svelte 5 throws `each_key_duplicate` mid-render, killing the popover.

On <= v0.36.0 the selector was the local `OptionTypeahead.svelte`, whose each-block was unkeyed (`{#each filtered as option, i}`), so the duplicate was harmless. This is why the regression first appears in v0.36.1 (the #957 migration to shared @kenn-io/kit-ui components).

#### How an empty-name project arises

Google Antigravity CLI (`agy`) sessions parsed in summary mode (plaintext `history.jsonl` / `brain/`, no trajectory sidecar) carry no cwd, so they sync with an empty project name. In my case, 53 `agy` sessions (created via roborev's Antigravity backend, see kenn-io/roborev#951) produced a "(none)" project with `name: ""`, and the selector has crashed on every load since the upgrade. Any database with such sessions reproduces this.

#### Suggested fix

Any of:

- Key the Typeahead rows by something unique (e.g. index, or a caller-supplied `key` falling back to index) in kit-ui;
- Give the injected "All projects" option a sentinel key that cannot collide with a real project name;
- Normalize empty project names at sync/API time (e.g. to a reserved `(none)` name), which would also make the "(none)" bucket selectable/filterable in the UI.

#### Aside: password managers grab the same input

While in that component: the Typeahead's `<input type="text">` carries no `autocomplete` attribute, so password-manager inline menus (Bitwarden confirmed, others likely) classify it as a fillable login/identity field and overlay their menu on the project filter. Adding `autocomplete="off"` plus the opt-out attributes (`data-bwignore`, `data-1p-ignore`) to kit-ui's Typeahead input would fix this for all consumers.

### Sample session file or snippet

```text

```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sync at least one session that yields an empty project name (e.g. any Antigravity CLI summary-mode session), or insert a project row with `name = ''`. `agentsview projects` will show a "(none)" entry.
2. Load the web UI and click the project selector in the header.
3. The selector highlights but never opens; the console shows `each_key_duplicate`.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: docs: document 0.38 releases and correct export contracts
body:
The 0.38.0 release spans desktop, daemon, recall, semantic search, ingestion, analytics, and stable contract work, while 0.38.1 restores Codex subagent lineage and titles. This aligns the release history and durable guides with the shipped CLI behavior, credits contributors, and refreshes the complete screenshot set against the corrected parser.

The project-evidence shape introduced in 0.38 changed the earlier usage, activity, and session-summary v1 contracts incompatibly. Current builds now report those shapes as v2, and the docs identify 0.38.0/0.38.1 as transitional mislabeled payloads. Screenshot extraction also removes project-identity sources and publication journals before PostgreSQL push, preventing generated assets from retaining local machine or repository context.

title: fix(parser): restore Codex subagent lineage and titles
body:
Current Codex multi-agent rollouts encode child lineage in session metadata and lifecycle events, while spawn results no longer carry the legacy child ID. Agentsview previously treated affected children as roots, failed to link parent spawn calls, and could expose opaque encrypted tool parameters as transcript text.

Parse the current lineage and lifecycle formats while retaining legacy compatibility. Addressed plaintext agent messages remain visible, encrypted payloads stay out of transcripts and search, and encrypted child sessions use their task path for a useful title. The existing data-version bump reparses source-backed archives non-destructively to recover the corrected relationships, links, messages, and titles.

When an archive has a newer data version than the running binary, startup and sync diagnostics now identify the compatible build or backup versions instead of assuming an update will resolve the mismatch. The fatal error also confirms that the refused startup left the archive unchanged.

title: Usage attribution chart colors aren't always distinct

Unsure what factors into the colors chosen, but I encountered this with claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-4-8 when aggregating by model: ### Sample session file or snippet ```text ``` ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Checklist - [x] I searched existing issues - [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: test: make runtime warning helpers condition-based
body:
Runtime warning entrypoint tests stopped helper processes after one second. On loaded runners, startup can consume that cutoff and exit cleanly before the warning is emitted, producing an empty-output failure unrelated to product behavior.

Helper lifetime now follows an expected stdout marker with a bounded deadline and distant orphan guard. The serve regression deliberately crosses the old cutoff, and PostgreSQL shares the same marker-driven path already used for DuckDB, removing the same latent runner-speed dependency.

title: Reject and repair invalid embedding vectors
body:
Embedding providers can return dimensionally valid data that is still unusable for cosine search. AgentsView now rejects null components, non-finite values, and zero-norm vectors at the endpoint and persistence boundaries so faulty output is never stamped as complete.

Add an explicit embeddings build --repair-invalid recovery mode that scans one existing generation, durably queues only affected document keys, and resumes them after endpoint failures or cancellation. Repair status preserves exact remaining work when possible, repair scans keep document-content allocation bounded by the scanned batch, and failed targets remain available for later retries.

Repair runs on an isolated path: it does not refresh or expand the mirror, create or reset generations, change generation state, or fill unrelated missing work. Full rebuild and backstop modes remain mutually exclusive with repair.

Daemon compatibility now covers the expanded repair status contract. Embeddings commands resolve only the writable daemon and report restart guidance when an older writable daemon is still running, including when a compatible read-only server is also available.

Document standard Ollama configuration and the cache constraints required when using a direct multi-slot llama-server endpoint.

title: ci: retry transient Go module downloads in releases
body: Transient module-proxy transport failures can currently abort a single platform build and block every downstream release artifact and PyPI publication. Prefetch the complete Go module graph through the existing bounded retry helper before both release build matrices begin compilation. Persistent dependency errors and all compile, package, and publication failures remain terminal, while the Linux SQLite header and CGO path are unchanged.

title: fix(parser): keep encrypted Codex collab payloads out of transcripts
body:
Follow-up to #1125. Codex multi-agent v2 encrypts inter-agent task payloads server-side (openai/codex#26210, reported in openai/codex#32753): `spawn_agent`/`send_message` arguments arrive as opaque Fernet tokens. #1125 suppressed the child session's inbound ciphertext, but the parent side still exposed it — in formatted `spawn_agent` message bodies, collab tool argument previews, and stored `tool_calls.input_json` — all of which reach the transcript UI, markdown export, resume rendering, and FTS.

This PR removes the ciphertext at ingest, repairs existing archives on every backend, and blocks outdated binaries from writing it back.

## Parser (ingest)

- Redaction is scoped to the three collab tools that carry encrypted arguments (`spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`). A legitimate Fernet token anywhere else — a shell command decrypting one, a user quoting one — is preserved.
- Redaction runs before preview truncation: a clipped token no longer validates and would leak a ciphertext prefix.
- Encrypted child sessions record a placeholder user turn naming the sending agent instead of silently dropping the task delivery. Replay detection digests the original ciphertext, so distinct tasks with identical placeholder text cannot shadow each other.

## SQLite archives (upgrade path)

- dataVersion 69 triggers the standard non-destructive resync and exhaustive certification without trusting either the cached tool-use flag or a surviving tool row. Versions 67 and 68 belong to Antigravity parent links and Hermes skill metadata, respectively, so the Codex watermark sits above both and neither can be mistaken for certified. (64 briefly existed with ingest redaction but no copy repair; 65–66 were unrelated Claude bumps.)
- Orphaned rows with no source file are scrubbed by a copy-time pass that mirrors the ingest scope, including tokens clipped by preview truncation.
- The watermark is stamped only on sessions the scrub can vouch for: token-free rows, plus token-bearing rows whose content every applicable redactor already treats as final (deliberately preserved literals). Rows the scoped scrub cannot examine — a lost `tool_calls` row, a child never linked to its parent — stay below the watermark so push-time verification keeps re-checking them.

## PostgreSQL

- The same historical repair runs in place for previews, message roles/content/lengths, and tool names/inputs. It persists UTF-8/control-byte normalization before redaction and preserves SQL `NULL` for absent tool inputs, guarded by write triggers that reject legacy ciphertext from outdated binaries.
- Version 69 rechecks every older row. After the scoped destructive repair, a metadata-independent certification pass examines previews, all token-bearing messages, and collab tool inputs. Token-free and verified-literal sessions advance to the watermark; anything an applicable redactor would still rewrite remains legacy, and read-only serving fails closed rather than exposing it.
- The repair transaction marks its own compatibility version so installed guards allow the scoped rewrites while sessions are still legacy. Promotion happens only afterward and only for sessions that pass exhaustive certification.
- Certification examines token-bearing formatted blocks even when `has_tool_use` is false and no `tool_calls` row survives. A block is safe only when its header cannot be produced by a canonical collab tool, covering both the mixed-tool residue case and the combined stale-flag/missing-row case.
- A collab `tool_calls` row is authoritative even when a legacy message's cached `has_tool_use` flag is false. Archive and mirror repair predicates follow the collab row, and shared-storage normalization does the same.
- Legacy write guards use the same conservative evidence boundaries: encrypted previews and user turns are rejected regardless of relationship metadata, formatted collab headers are derived from the canonical tool list and need neither metadata signal, and PostgreSQL rechecks `has_tool_use` transitions.
- Vector documents get a one-time sweep with a completion marker. A per-ensure scan still catches stale vectors pushed independently of session versions (a compatibility-marked writer can do this); a partial index keeps that scan proportional to the normally empty suspicious set.
- Compatibility probes count only guards enabled for ordinary writes (O or A); disabled and replica-only triggers fail closed, and writable migrations reinstall them.
- Read-only `pg serve` fails closed until a writable current build has repaired and certified the schema.

## CockroachDB

- Same guards, staged install: `autocommit_before_ddl` makes an atomic migration impossible, so triggers install as autocommitted DDL and the repair follows in a serializable retry transaction.
- Because CockroachDB cannot narrow triggers with `UPDATE OF`, its session guard explicitly admits trash/restore updates only when payload and relationship evidence is unchanged; an upgrade-tested `v7` trigger replaces the earlier body.
- Servers without trigger support (pre-24.3) can still use scan mode for repair verification, but direct `--pg` reads and `pg serve` fail closed because their later queries do not share the scan snapshot. Trigger-capable CockroachDB is required to serve the archive.

## DuckDB mirrors over Quack

- DuckDB has no triggers, so reads gate instead of writes: every remote store read embeds the legacy-version check in the same statement, which executes under one remote snapshot — a legacy push cannot land between a separate check and the read it was meant to cover.
- The mirror uses the same v69 repair-then-certify policy as PostgreSQL, including persisted UTF-8/control-byte normalization and preservation of nullable tool inputs. Rows that cannot be certified remain below the watermark, so Quack and local DuckDB reads reject the mirror instead of treating the unrelated v67/v68 parser versions as certification.
- A transient legacy-Codex preflight read failure is counted as a session push error and pins the watermark. The session retries on the next push instead of falling through to a later read that could publish it without durable local certification.
- Guard failures map back to the repair sentinel on every error surface (query, scan, iteration, close), including single-row reads. Two reads that previously bypassed the gate — branch listing and usage session counts — now go through it.
- Startup compat and post-repair checks probe the indexed version watermark instead of running content scans whose outcome the probe already decides; over Quack that is one remote statement instead of five.
- Additively migrated certification columns are read with safe defaults so older compatible writers cannot make typed session reads fail by omitting them.

## Cross-cutting

- Push-time verification (`PrepareSessionForSharedStorage`) applies the same metadata-independent checks as copy-time and mirror certification: a user turn is checked as an inter-agent delivery even when the session was never linked to its parent, and a formatted tool message is checked even when both its cached tool-use flag and collab `tool_calls` row were lost. Sessions that fail are withheld from PG and DuckDB mirrors — logged, skipped without counting as push errors (a permanent condition must not pin the push watermark), and their vector documents are deferred via a durable local-version gate that outlives the incremental push window.
- Certification evaluates the exact `SanitizeUTF8` form that PostgreSQL publishes, including preview, role, message content, collab tool name, and tool input. Preserved-row repair sanitizes before redaction and exhaustively checks every copied legacy Codex session, so control or invalid bytes cannot hide a token until after certification.
- The collab tool list is rendered from `parser.CodexCollabToolsSQL()` at every SQL site, and the watermark is one exported constant (`db.CodexRedactionDataVersion`) aliased by both mirror backends, so neither can drift.
- PostgreSQL and DuckDB push keep the exact message/tool snapshot that passed certification, bind it to the transcript revision, and release snapshots after each bounded batch. Vector documents carry the same revision and defer when it differs from the locked remote session.
- The local vectors.db mirror schema version bumps so stale embeddings are rebuilt.
- Fixes a pre-existing bug that broke every Quack push carrying project identity snapshots (named string types rejected by the remote literal renderer).

## Limitations

- PG trigger bodies are frozen at first install; changing the guard predicates requires renaming the trigger constants so existing schemas reinstall (the session guard is at `_v7`, the message guard at `_v5`, and the tool and vector guards at `_v4`; the DDL drops prior names).
- Uncertified orphan or mirror rows keep their content and stay below the watermark. Local push-time verification withholds them and mirror read gates reject them rather than certifying potentially encrypted content.

## Where to look

- Parser redaction and formatted-block proof: `internal/parser/codex.go` (`RedactCodex*`, `CodexStoredToolContentIsProvablyNonCollab`, `CodexStoredToolContentNeedsCollabRedaction`, `CodexCollabToolHeaderLikePatterns`)
- Orphan copy scrub and certification: `internal/db/orphaned.go`, push-time verification in `internal/db/shared_storage.go`
- PG/CRDB migration, guards, vector sweep: `internal/postgres/codex_redaction.go`, `internal/postgres/crdb.go`
- Quack read gate: `internal/duckdb/codex_redaction.go` (`codexGuardedQuackReadSQL`) and the gated reads in `internal/duckdb/store.go`

title: Queued <task-notification> messages count as real user turns, inflating user_message_count and defeating the single-turn filter
body:
agentsview version: v0.38.1 (commit 1e173b95, built 2026-07-13T19:59:48Z)
Install method: Windows installer (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\agentsview`)
OS / platform: Windows 11 (10.0.26100)
Agent: Claude Code

## What happened, and what I expected

I have orchestration sessions where I send **one** real prompt and the agent then spawns background Agent/Task work. With **Hide single-turn** (a.k.a. `include_one_shot=false`) selected, I expected these to drop out, since I only typed one message. Several of them stay visible.

Digging into one, agentsview stored `user_message_count = 3` for a session that has exactly one real user prompt. The other two "user" turns are `<task-notification>` completion messages that Claude Code queued while the assistant was mid-response. Those got counted as real user turns, so the session sits above the single-turn threshold and the filter can't touch it.

The interesting part: the **inline** path already handles this correctly. `<task-notification>` is in `classifyClaudeSystemMessage`, so an inline notification is promoted to `is_system=1` and excluded from the count. The bug is that **queued** notifications take a different path that never runs the classifier.

## Repro

1. Run a Claude Code session that spawns background tasks (Agent/Task tool) so completion notifications arrive while the assistant is still generating — Claude Code queues them as `attachment.type=queued_command`.
2. The session's real user input is a single prompt.
3. Ingest into agentsview, open the session list, and turn on **Hide single-turn**.
4. The session still shows. `session list --json` (default filters) also returns it, and its `user_message_count` is `1 + (number of queued notifications)`.

## Evidence from my DB

Session `883331d3-25ce-40ef-b984-71c8a2d9c9e7` (project `agentsview`, started 2026-07-13T22:00:01Z):

```
user_message_count = 3      # expected 1
message_count      = 29
is_automated       = 0
parent_session_id  = NULL

messages (role=user):
  ordinal  is_system  source_subtype    content
  0        0          (none)            "Your final response is captured verbatim into ..."   <- the only real prompt
  44       0          queued_command    "<task-notification>\n<task-id>a29fa76dc1fa3212f..."
  49       0          queued_command    "<task-notification>\n<task-id>a5db2a604af3b5fcd..."
```

Both notifications are stored with `is_system=0` and `source_subtype="queued_command"`, so `firstMessageAndUserCount` counts them as real user turns.

## Root cause (my reading, current `main` @ `de472aab`)

The two code paths for user messages diverge:

- **Inline user messages** run through the system-message classifier, which demotes `<task-notification>` (and continuation / resume / interrupted / stop-hook) to `is_system=1`:
  - https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/de472aab8a2f6f6247fb96192a4d17e001da537b/internal/parser/claude.go#L750
  - https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/de472aab8a2f6f6247fb96192a4d17e001da537b/internal/parser/claude.go#L1704
  - classifier + `<task-notification>` case: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/de472aab8a2f6f6247fb96192a4d17e001da537b/internal/parser/claude.go#L2118-L2142

- **Queued-command messages** are built by `queuedCommandMessage`, which hardcodes `IsSystem: false` and never calls the classifier — the comment even says it should count as a real user turn:
  - https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/de472aab8a2f6f6247fb96192a4d17e001da537b/internal/parser/claude.go#L1199-L1210

`firstMessageAndUserCount` then skips only `IsSystem` messages, so the queued notifications survive into the count:
  - https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/de472aab8a2f6f6247fb96192a4d17e001da537b/internal/parser/claude.go#L2040-L2063

And the single-turn filter is purely `user_message_count <= 1`, so an inflated count defeats it:
  - https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/de472aab8a2f6f6247fb96192a4d17e001da537b/internal/db/sessions.go#L475
  - https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/de472aab8a2f6f6247fb96192a4d17e001da537b/internal/db/query_dialect.go#L657

So the assumption in `queuedCommandMessage` that a queued command is always a real user prompt is what breaks: a queued item can just as easily be a `<task-notification>` (or a `<system-reminder>` / stop-hook), which shouldn't count.

## Suggested fix

Run the queued-command content through the same classifier before deciding `IsSystem`, so queued and inline notifications are treated identically. Roughly: in `queuedCommandMessage`, if `classifyClaudeSystemMessage(q.prompt)` returns a subtype, set `IsSystem: true` and `SourceSubtype: <subtype>` instead of the flat `queued_command`. That keeps genuine queued prompts counting as real turns while excluding queued system notifications, and fixes the count without needing any changes to the filter itself.

This isn't a stale parse — it reproduces on the latest build parsing a session that's minutes old.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: Assign distinct colors across active attribution series
body:
Usage attribution could assign the same palette token to multiple active model series because each chart element hashed its identifier independently. Colliding regions and legend entries then became visually indistinguishable even though the underlying attribution data was separate.

Color selection now happens once for the active identifier set. The shared frontend allocator keeps the existing palette and hash preference, resolves occupied slots deterministically while palette capacity remains, and defines stable overflow behavior. Attribution rows, treemap items, time-series paths, and legend dots consume the same assignment map, so chart and legend colors cannot drift.

Grouping, ranking, cost calculations, exclusions, and the muted “Other” series are unchanged. The reported collision pair and screenshots came from @mslynch's issue report (https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/1126).

Fixes #1126

title: Fix project selector crash on empty project names
body:
Opening the header project selector crashed with Svelte's `each_key_duplicate` when the database contained a project with an empty name (e.g. Antigravity CLI summary-mode sessions): kit-ui's Typeahead keys options on `option.name`, and the empty-name project collided with the built-in All projects option, which also uses `""`.

Omit empty-name projects from the option list. A row for them was never functional because `""` already means the unfiltered state in the app-wide filter contract, and their sessions stay reachable under All projects. Named projects and the selection contract are unchanged.

Fixes #1123.

title: fix(parser): classify queued system prompts before single-turn counting (#1131)
body:
Queued Claude sessions that contain one real prompt plus queued runtime messages are being stored with an inflated `user_message_count`, which defeats the single-turn filter. A concrete repro in issue #1131 shows session `883331d3-25ce-40ef-b984-71c8a2d9c9e7` recorded as `user_message_count = 3` even though the only real user turn is the opening prompt; the extra counted turns are queued `<task-notification>` messages. The same path also misclassifies queued `Stop hook feedback:` and queued `<system-reminder>` content.

Claude parsing currently splits this behavior in two places. Queued `queued_command` attachments bypass `ClassifyClaudeSystemMessage`, so `queuedCommandMessage` hardcodes them as non-system user messages and they increment the count before the single-turn filter ever runs. Complete leading `<system-reminder>` blocks also reach command handling and compatibility fallbacks before their terminal remainder is classified, which leaves reminder-prefixed command envelopes as raw XML and lets reminder-prefixed `/usage` probes miss the existing exclusion.

The fix keeps the parser as the single source of truth. The shared queued-message merge now delegates message construction back to each provider, so Claude can classify queued runtime content as semantic system messages while OpenClaude still preserves accepted prompt attachments as counted `queued_command` user turns. Complete leading reminder blocks are normalized before Claude command handling, which lets reminder-prefixed command envelopes resolve to slash-command text and lets reminder-prefixed `/usage` probes hit the existing exclusion. The same terminal-remainder rule now drives the Go fallback, the generated SQLite/PostgreSQL/DuckDB predicates, and the frontend hidden-message fallback, while `VISIBLE_SYSTEM_SUBTYPES` stays unchanged so system reminders remain hidden rather than turning into visible boundary cards.

Termination classification now follows the final non-system assistant turn without dropping later system-carried tool results. Claude and OpenClaude both skip trailing compact boundaries or queued system notifications when deciding whether an assistant is waiting for the user, while orphaned-tool detection still scans later system messages so a matching tool result can resolve the final tool call. The filter itself stays untouched. No `user_message_count > 1` SQL predicate changes, because the bug is a wrong count flowing into a correct filter. `dataVersion` advances so existing stored sessions receive the corrected flags and counts through the repository's existing non-destructive reparse path, while ordinary queued prompts and queue-operation task-notification linkage keep their current behavior. This refines PR #406's queued-command ingestion contract by preserving real queued prompts while classifying queued system prompts and reminder-prefixed fallback content before they are counted or hidden.

Closes #1131

title: Preserve Claude session identity metadata
body:
Claude session identity can appear on appended SDK transcript lines that are not typed `agent-setting`, so incremental sync could miss the metadata and keep the generic Claude label.

This change treats top-level `agentSetting` and `entrypoint` as session identity metadata wherever they appear on appended Claude rows, forces that incremental path through a full parse, and keeps the existing plain-Claude fallback when metadata is absent. The identity fields still flow through SQLite, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, sidebar payloads, and breadcrumb/session labeling without fragmenting the stable `claude` agent filter.

The added coverage exercises absent metadata, late metadata on appended rows, and cross-backend persistence.

Closes #1089

title: Pin recorded models in resume commands
body:
Resume commands could ignore the model recorded in the session and fall back to the CLI default, which breaks prompt-cache reuse.

This change keeps the backend and frontend resume paths aligned on the same selected model, preserves shell quoting for model values, and matches JavaScript UTF-16 tie-break ordering when multiple models have the same usage count. Backend resume generation now uses compact per-model counts instead of hydrating full transcripts, and the model-aware command is reused for command-only responses, launcher paths, and clipboard fallbacks.

Frontend local fallback pinning now stays behind a store-owned complete-history predicate. The breadcrumb and keyboard fallbacks pin only when the requested session matches a successfully complete, current, idle history; partial pages, later-page failures, and in-flight or failed reloads stay unpinned, while display-only model badges remain unchanged.

Message-point forks and sessions without model data keep their existing behavior.

Closes #1104

title: feat(embeddings): keep ETA in daemon memory
body:
Embedding ETA was calculated independently in each Settings page, so opening or reloading the page discarded the warmed rate and different clients could report different estimates for the same build.

This makes the build manager the single owner of the tqdm-style EWMA and publishes estimate readiness, throughput, and remaining time through build status. Settings now renders the daemon snapshot on its first response, while phase changes and discontinuous progress reset the estimator at the source.

Estimator state is intentionally limited to daemon memory: it does not change SQLite, the vector index, configuration, or migrations. Restarting the daemon simply warms a fresh estimate from the next build's progress callbacks.

title: fix(test): give remotesync liveness guards a Windows-safe deadline
body:
## Summary

`TestPreparedHTTPSyncContributorKeepsLockUntilClose` failed on windows-latest twice in two days (runs 29300492349 and 29213539491) with `timed out waiting for rebuild` at `http_test.go:1309`. The test's 1-second guard fired while the full resync it was waiting on — fresh DB build, FTS rebuild, atomic swap — was still making progress: the buffered test output shows the resync logging mid-run, and the second failure's 6.78s total test time (vs ~0.15s locally) confirms a stalled runner rather than a hang. This is the same failure class as #951: cold windows-latest runners blow through 1-second deadlines.

The waits are already condition-based channel receives; only the fatal guard deadline was arbitrary. This replaces every fatal 1-second `time.After` guard in `internal/remotesync` tests with a shared 30-second `backgroundWaitTimeout` constant. A generous deadline costs nothing when the code is healthy — the receive completes as soon as the goroutine finishes — and only delays failure output when something genuinely hangs.

Negative assertions (the 20ms "concurrent work must not start" window in `cleanup_registry_test.go`, the 30–50ms "lock must not be acquirable" probes, and the 50ms best-effort rendezvous in the shared-host ordering test) keep their short waits, since lengthening those would either slow every run or weaken the assertion.

Where to look: the constant and its comment at the top of `internal/remotesync/http_test.go`; the remaining sites are mechanical substitutions in `http_test.go`, `archive_test.go`, and `archive_unix_test.go`.

### [`v2.21.0`](https://redirect.github.com/opral/paraglide-js/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#2210)

##### Minor Changes

- [`ab5bfc7`](https://redirect.github.com/opral/paraglide-js/commit/ab5bfc7): fix `emitTsDeclarations` with TypeScript 7 [#​711](https://redirect.github.com/opral/paraglide-js/issues/711)

  TypeScript 7 (the Go-based compiler) no longer ships the in-process compiler API that Paraglide used to generate `.d.ts` files, which made `paraglide-js compile --emit-ts-declarations` fail with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ESNext')`. Paraglide now detects this and invokes TypeScript's `tsc` CLI instead. TypeScript 5 and 6 keep using the compiler API as before.

  Note that the declaration output of TypeScript 7 differs cosmetically from TypeScript 5/6 (quote style, declaration ordering, `export declare const` vs `export const`) but is semantically equivalent.

### [`v0.2.3`](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/releases/tag/v0.2.3): vite-plus v0.2.3: config extraction, create, and vp run reliability fixes

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/compare/v0.2.2...v0.2.3)

A patch release that fixes static config extraction for `vite.config.ts` files whose `defineConfig` comes from a preset or custom wrapper (no longer misread as Vite+'s own), fixes `vp create` for org templates on registries that strip custom package fields, cleans up terminal output after Ctrl-C during `vp run`, and updates bundled Vite to 8.1.3.

##### Highlights

- **Custom `VP_HOME` is honored on every run**: the global `vp` now respects a user-set `VP_HOME` for its home directory instead of falling back to `~/.vite-plus`, and persists it in the generated env files, so a custom install location no longer produces multiple instances or unusable packages ([#​2029](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2029)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ)

##### Features

- Upgrade bundled Vite from `8.1.2` to `8.1.3` (inlined CSS after the shebang line, CSS preload for nested dynamic imports, SSR stacktrace column fix) ([#​2042](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2042)), by [@​voidzero-guard](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-guard)\[bot]

##### Fixes & Enhancements

- `vp run` no longer misreads a `vite.config.ts` when its `defineConfig` comes from a preset or a custom wrapper instead of `vite-plus` or `vite`. Such configs are now evaluated at runtime rather than assumed to be Vite+'s own, so projects that use them no longer wrongly report `Task "build" not found` ([#​2060](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2060), [#​2075](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2075)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ) and [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
