title: Grok usage undercounted up to ~200x: turn_completed usage is per-turn, but only the last snapshot per session is ingested
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1193 / #1206. The Grok usage ingestion added in #1206 treats `params.update.usage` objects in `updates.jsonl` as **cumulative session snapshots** and keeps only the **last** one per session (`parseGrokUsageEvents` overwrites `usage` on every candidate line, then emits one event per (session, model) with dedup key `session:<id>:<model>`).

Grok Build's `turn_completed` usage is actually **per-turn**, so this captures a single turn per session and drops the rest. On a real 44-session archive (2,976 `turn_completed` records), agentsview main (`75b9e8b`) reports:

| metric | agentsview | sum of per-turn records | undercount |
|---|---|---|---|
| input (net of cached) | 662,978 | 18,985,293 | 28.6x |
| output | 53,230 | 2,661,643 | 50x |
| cachedRead | 12,658,048 | 2,582,853,120 | **204x** |

**Exact-match confirmation:** independently summing only the *last* usage object per session over the same raw files reproduces agentsview's totals to the exact token (662,978 / 53,230 / 12,658,048) — so the delta is fully explained by last-snapshot-per-session semantics, not by parsing gaps.

## Evidence that usage is per-turn, not cumulative

- `cachedReadTokens` across consecutive `turn_completed` events in one session goes 11264 → 11264 → 6016 → 128 → 25472 — non-monotonic, impossible for a cumulative counter.
- `inputTokens` across those turns grows by ~50–70 per turn (25340 → 25411 → 25463…) while each turn actually resends a ~25k-token context — consistent with per-turn totals, not cumulative increments.
- `usage.modelCalls` resets per turn (e.g. 13 for a single multi-call turn).

## Secondary issue: date bucketing

`occurredAt` is set from the session's `endedAt`/`startedAt`, so a session's entire usage lands on one calendar day. Long-running sessions (days-long agent sessions are common) make the daily breakdown wrong even once totals are fixed — in the archive above, the single heaviest day (929M tokens) is missing entirely from `usage daily` output because its sessions ended on other days.

## Suggested fix

Emit one usage event **per `turn_completed` line** (per model from `usage.modelUsage`), with:
- dedup key `session:<sessionId>:<prompt_id>:<model>` (`prompt_id` is unique per turn — verified collision-free across the archive),
- `occurredAt` from the line's top-level `timestamp` (unix seconds),
- the existing `max(input - cachedRead, 0)` netting kept as-is (it's correct).

Happy to provide additional record samples or test against a branch.

title: fix(grok): emit one usage event per turn instead of last-snapshot-per-session
body:
Fixes #1227.

## Problem

`parseGrokUsageEvents` treats `params.update.usage` payloads in `updates.jsonl` as cumulative session snapshots and keeps only the last one per session. Grok Build's `turn_completed` usage is actually **per-turn** (`cachedReadTokens` is non-monotonic across a session's turns; `modelCalls` resets each turn), so multi-turn sessions are undercounted by orders of magnitude and all usage lands on the session's end date. Full evidence incl. an exact-token reproduction of the undercount is in #1227.

## Change

- Emit one usage event per usage payload and model (from `usage.modelUsage`, with the existing top-level fallback), instead of one per session.
- Dedup key gains a turn component: `session:<sessionID>:<prompt_id>:<model>` — `prompt_id` is unique per turn and stable across re-parses (verified collision-free on a 2,976-turn archive); a `turn-<n>` ordinal covers payloads without `prompt_id`.
- `OccurredAt` comes from each payload's own top-level `timestamp` (unix seconds), falling back to the session window when absent — a days-long session now buckets each turn on the day it happened.
- The existing `max(input − cachedRead, 0)` netting and `costUsdTicks` handling are unchanged.
- `dataVersion` 69 → 70 (same convention as 51, the Gemini cumulative-to-delta reparse) so existing Grok rows are re-parsed on upgrade.

## Before / after on a real archive

44 sessions / 2,976 `turn_completed` payloads, `usage daily --agent grok` totals:

| metric | before (main `75b9e8b`) | after | ground truth (independent re-parse of raw files) |
|---|---|---|---|
| input (net) | 662,978 | 19,023,100 | 19,023,100 |
| output | 53,230 | 2,674,197 | 2,674,197 |
| cachedRead | 12,658,048 | 2,591,768,960 | 2,591,768,960 |
| days present | 6 | 8 | 8 |

The heaviest day of the archive (929M tokens) was previously missing entirely from the daily output (its sessions ended on other dates); it now reports correctly.

## Testing

- `go test -short ./internal/...` passes; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.
- Reworked `TestGrokProviderLatestUsageSnapshot` → `TestGrokProviderPerTurnUsageEvents` (two payloads → two events, non-monotonic cache preserved, session total output = sum).
- New: `TestGrokProviderPerTurnUsageDedupsByPromptID` (multi-model turn, prompt_id-keyed dedup) and `TestGrokProviderPerTurnUsageDatesByTurnTimestamp` (multi-day session buckets per turn; timestamp-less payload falls back to the session window).

title: fix(frontend): label inline teammate transcript messages

Explicit subagent context still wins first, true teammate child sessions keep their ancestry-based label, ordinary user messages remain `User/U`, and wrapper text inside fenced code blocks stays unclassified. title: feat(sync): add local-first multi-machine artifact synchronization
body:

This adds immutable, conflict-aware artifact synchronization through folders, HTTP peers, and S3-compatible storage while keeping SQLite authoritative for each local archive.

title: Qoder IDE sessions not synced — actual session data stored in SharedClientCache, not .qoder/projects
body:
### Agent name and link

https://qoder.com/

### Where does it store sessions?

C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Qoder\SharedClientCache\cli\projects\


### File format

# Qoder IDE sessions not synced — actual session data stored in SharedClientCache, not .qoder/projects

## Description

After starting agentsview, Qoder IDE sessions are not discovered or synced. The default configured directories (`~/.qoder/projects/` and `~/.qoderwork/projects/`) are empty or do not exist on my system.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 22H2
- **agentsview version:** v0.38.1
- **Qoder IDE version:** 1.17.3

## Investigation Findings

### Expected directory (empty)
- `C:\Users\<user>\.qoder\projects\` — exists but `transcript/` subdirectory is empty
- `C:\Users\<user>\.qoderwork\projects\` — does not exist

### Actual session data location
Qoder IDE stores session transcripts in:
- `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Qoder\SharedClientCache\cli\projects\`

This directory contains 16 session files in the format:
```
task-<uuid>.session.execution.jsonl
task-<uuid>.session.execution-session.json
```

Example `-session.json` content:
```json
{"id":"task-10f849241e06451d9c9c.session.execution","title":"abc","working_dir":"d:/x/x/x/xx", ...}
```

The JSONL files contain standard session messages (user/assistant/tool roles with parts, model, timestamps) that appear compatible with the existing Qoder parser.

### Why the parser doesn't pick them up

There are two blockers preventing the current parser from discovering these files:

1. **Flat directory structure:** Files are stored directly under `SharedClientCache\cli\projects\` without per-project subdirectories. The parser expects `<root>/<project_dir>/<session_id>.jsonl`.

2. **Session ID validation fails:** Session IDs like `task-10f849241e06451d9c9c.session.execution` contain periods (`.`), but `IsValidSessionID()` only accepts alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores.

### Other Qoder data locations found

| Path | Content |
|------|---------|
| `AppData\Roaming\Qoder\User\workspaceStorage\<hash>\` | `state.vscdb` (SQLite) + `chatEditingSessions/` |
| `AppData\Roaming\Qoder\SharedClientCache\cache\ai_tracker\projects\<hash>\` | AI tracking JSONL data (code change attribution, not transcripts) |
| `AppData\Roaming\Qoder\SharedClientCache\cli\projects\` | **Session transcripts (JSONL)** — the data we want |
| `.qoder\projects\` | Transcript export target (currently empty) |

## Expected Behavior

agentsview should discover and sync Qoder IDE sessions from wherever Qoder actually stores them.

## Possible Solutions

1. **Update `DefaultDirs`** for the Qoder agent to include the `SharedClientCache\cli\projects\` path (platform-specific, e.g. `%APPDATA%\Qoder\SharedClientCache\cli\projects` on Windows)
2. **Update the parser** to handle flat directory layout (no project subdirectory) and accept session IDs with periods
3. **Alternatively**, if Qoder IDE has a transcript export feature, document how to enable it so files land in `.qoder/projects/` in the expected format

title: OpenCode: prefer session.directory over project.worktree for cwd
body:
## Summary

OpenCode SQLite sessions that belong to the synthetic `global` project are imported with `cwd=/` and project `unknown`, even when `session.directory` holds a real working directory.

This mis-groups recent OpenCode work under **unknown** instead of the actual path-derived project (and blocks worktree mappings).

## Observed impact

On a production-scale local archive (~330 `unknown` sessions):

| Source cwd in agentsview | Agent | Count | Date range |
|---|---|---:|---|
| empty | opencode (mostly legacy) | ~123 | 2025-06 → 2025-09 |
| `/` | opencode | ~203 | 2026-03 → 2026-07 (ongoing) |
| empty | codex / gemini | 4 | older one-offs |

Spot-check of recent agentsview rows with `cwd=/` against OpenCode's `opencode.db`:

- agentsview: `cwd=/`, `project=unknown`, `project_id` path via OpenCode `global`
- OpenCode source: `session.directory` is a real path, e.g.
  - `/home/…/Videos/ready-for-agent`
  - `/home/…/tmp`
  - `/tmp`
  - `/home/…`
- OpenCode `project` row for `id=global` has `worktree=/`

So the lossy step is in the agentsview parser, not missing data in OpenCode.

## Root cause

DB-backed OpenCode parse resolves cwd exclusively from the **project** map:

```go
// internal/parser/opencode.go
worktree := projects[s.projectID]
// ...
Cwd: worktree,
project := ExtractProjectFromCwd(worktree)
```

`loadOpenCodeProjectsCached` reads `SELECT id, worktree FROM project`. Sessions under OpenCode's `global` project therefore always get `worktree=/` → `ExtractProjectFromCwd` yields empty → project falls back to `unknown`.

`session.directory` is present on the OpenCode session row (and is already modeled on the file-backed storage path via `Directory`), but the SQLite session load path does not use it for cwd/project.

## Expected behavior

For OpenCode SQLite sessions:

1. Prefer `session.directory` when it is a non-empty, usable path (not `/`, not blank).
2. Fall back to `project.worktree` when `session.directory` is missing/unusable.
3. Derive `project` from the chosen cwd (existing `ExtractProjectFromCwd` + worktree mappings).
4. Keep fingerprint/hash inputs consistent with the cwd that is stored on the session so resync updates stale `unknown` rows.

File-backed OpenCode storage should keep current behavior unless it has the same project-vs-directory split.

## Proposed fix

- Load `directory` in `loadOneOpenCodeSession` / bulk session queries.
- Add a small resolver, e.g. `resolveOpenCodeWorktree(sessionDirectory, projectWorktree string) string`, that prefers a concrete session directory.
- Treat `/` (and empty) as unusable project worktrees when a better session directory exists.
- Unit tests:
  - `project_id=global`, `project.worktree=/`, `session.directory=/home/user/code/app` → cwd and project from directory.
  - normal project worktree still wins when session directory is empty.
  - session directory `/` or empty falls back to project worktree.
- After fix, existing archives should correct on normal OpenCode resync/apply (no manual SQL).

## Evidence pointers

- `internal/parser/opencode.go`: project worktree selection (~L335), `buildOpenCodeParsedSession` cwd/project (~L801–L826)
- OpenCode schema: `session.directory`, `project.worktree` (global project uses `/`)
- Related product surface: Settings → Worktree Project Mappings cannot help when cwd is `/`

## Out of scope

- Empty-cwd legacy OpenCode rows from mid-2025 (no directory in source) — separate backfill/heuristic if desired.
- Mapping `/tmp/...` paths via worktree rules (already configurable once cwd is correct).

title: Add artifact wire format and docbank-backed local store
body:
PR1 of the artifact-sync split (supersedes the closed #1239, extracted and pared from its reference branch with @maphew as co-author).

This lands the foundation of `internal/artifact`: the frozen v1 wire format and the local content-addressed store, with no export/import pipeline, transports, server, db, or CLI integration yet.

**What's here**

- Wire format types (checkpoint, manifest, segment message, metadata event, raw source) with key-sorted canonical JSON encoding and golden-hash tests. The goldens are byte-identical to the reference implementation and are the frozen v1 format going forward; the `raw_source` contract (SHA-256 identity, size cap, `application/jsonl` media-type allowlist, sanitized relative paths) is frozen and validated here even though capture lands in PR3.
- A reflection parity test that pins `manifestSession` to `db.Session`'s JSON-visible fields, so incidental session-struct growth cannot silently re-hash every manifest.
- Zstd wire codec with pinned decoder window, encoded/decoded byte limits, and hash-verified reads (corruption-grade robustness; truncation and bit-rot detection).
- `ArtifactStore` interface and the Docbank-backed implementation (`go.kenn.io/docbank`, new dependency, plus a kit upgrade), with a contract suite that runs against both SQLite drivers (mattn and modernc).
- `Repository`: open-on-demand vault ownership under `$AGENTSVIEW_DATA_DIR/artifacts`. Nothing creates the vault for users who don't opt in; `serve` integration comes later.
- `config.ValidateArtifactOriginID` with table tests.

**Deliberately absent, arriving in later PRs**

- Export ledger/pipeline and import (PR2), raw JSONL capture (PR3), folder transport + sync CLI (PR4), metadata/HLC machinery (PR5), GC/maintenance/quarantine listing and the pack scheduler (PR6). A few reference symbols whose only consumers live in those PRs were deferred with them (`contextArtifactReader`, decoded-limit consts, quarantine listing surface, compression tests); each returns verbatim with its consumer. `ErrArtifactUnsupported` is frozen store vocabulary whose returning consumer is PR6 maintenance.
- `canonicalArtifactPath` is temporarily duplicated into `repository.go`; PR2's sync.go extraction must reconcile to a single copy.
- `Quarantine` keeps its `reason` parameter (currently discarded): PR6's quarantine listing may persist it once docbank can store a reason.

**Where to look**

- `internal/artifact/wire.go` + `format_test.go` — the format freeze and golden hashes.
- `internal/artifact/canonical_json.go` — deterministic encoder (byte-identical to the reference; it determines every content hash).
- `internal/artifact/store_docbank.go` + `store_contract_test.go` — store semantics: immutable create, conflict detection, verified reads, quarantine/trash, two-driver matrix.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Scoped vector pushes still run a full-archive coverage count in the readiness check
body:
Follow-up from #1207.

That PR scopes change-triggered PG vector reconciliation: the local doc-hash read (`SessionEmbeddedDocHashes`) and the PG push-state read now scale with the changed session set instead of the whole generation. One full-archive term stays on the hot path though.

The readiness gate in `vectorPushSource.Generation` calls `Index.GenerationByID`, whose `generationCoverageQuery` counts embedded and missing docs across the entire generation. It runs on every push, including scoped ones (once up front, and again in the pre-eviction re-check when there's eviction work), so a single-session change against a large archive still does O(total docs) work. That's a local SQLite aggregate, not PG round-trips, but it does bound how "incremental" the per-event cost really gets.

Two ways to close it:

1. Make the readiness count scope-aware: count coverage only over the changed session IDs on a scoped push, and keep the full count for generation-wide reconciliation.
2. Persist an O(1) generation-complete marker the build maintains, and have readiness read that instead of counting rows.

The thing to preserve either way: the coverage gate refuses exporting a generation whose embeddings are transiently missing during an in-place rebuild (the same-fingerprint full rebuild that clears and refills a still-active generation). A naive scope-aware count could green-light a scoped push when the changed sessions happen to look complete while the rest of the generation is mid-refill, reintroducing the partial-view eviction the gate prevents. So a scope-aware version should keep a cheap generation-level in-progress guard (the generation `state`, not a row count) rather than trusting the scoped count alone. Worth a rebuild-in-flight / interrupted-build test beyond a small-vs-large perf assertion.

Kept out of #1207 since the scan predates it and that PR's boundary was the change-scope reconciliation state, but it's the natural next step.

title: Nested subagents (depth ≥ 2) get parent_session_id pinned to the main session
body:
**agentsview version:** v0.38.1 (commit 1e173b95, built 2026-07-13T21:41:46Z)
**Install method:** install.sh
**OS / platform:** Linux (Ubuntu, x86_64), kernel 6.8

> Heads up: I'm not a deep-code person — I used Claude Code (AI) to investigate this
> properly and write the patch. It traced the root cause, produced a fix plus a
> regression test (fails before, passes after), and I verified the patch applies cleanly
> to current `main` (`34d326c`). PR incoming that fixes this. Happy to point the AI at any
> follow-up questions.

## Summary

In a Claude Code session where a subagent spawns its **own** subagents:

```
main → orchestrator → {codex, kimi}      (spawnDepth 1 and 2)
```

agentsview indexes all four sessions and captures every tool call correctly, but
`sessions.parent_session_id` for the depth-2 sessions points at the **main session**
instead of the orchestrator. The stored tree is flat:

| session | stored parent | true parent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| orchestrator | main | main ✅ (correct by luck) |
| codex | main | **orchestrator** ❌ |
| kimi | main | **orchestrator** ❌ |

`tool_calls.subagent_session_id` already has the correct nested edges
(main→orchestrator, orchestrator→codex, orchestrator→kimi) — the authoritative data is
in the DB; only the session hierarchy discards it.

Consequences: `GET /sessions/{orchestrator}/children` returns empty; per-session usage
rollups (BFS over `parent_session_id`) attribute the whole subtree to the main session.

## Root cause

Two parent sources fight, and the wrong one wins for depth ≥ 2:

1. **Path-derived parent (parse time):** `claudeCompanionParentSessionID`
   (`internal/parser/claude.go`) takes the path segment before `subagents/`. Claude
   Code stores **all** depths flat in `<main-session>/subagents/`, so every subagent
   gets parent = main and `relationship_type = 'subagent'`.
2. **Authoritative parent (post-parse):** `LinkSubagentSessions()`
   (`internal/db/sessions.go` ~L1552) re-points parents from
   `tool_calls.subagent_session_id` — but its `WHERE relationship_type != 'subagent'`
   guard skips every row mechanism (1) already tagged. The correction never runs for
   nested subagents.

Depth 1 is correct only by luck (its flat path-parent equals its true parent);
depth ≥ 2 stays wrong.

## Fix (one clause)

Drop the `relationship_type` guard; re-point whenever the authoritative parent differs
(null-safe, so it still covers the existing continuation→subagent upgrade):

```sql
UPDATE sessions
SET parent_session_id = (
      SELECT tc.session_id FROM tool_calls tc
      WHERE tc.subagent_session_id = sessions.id LIMIT 1),
    relationship_type = 'subagent',
    local_modified_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now')
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tool_calls tc
              WHERE tc.subagent_session_id = sessions.id)
  AND parent_session_id IS NOT (
      SELECT tc.session_id FROM tool_calls tc
      WHERE tc.subagent_session_id = sessions.id LIMIT 1);
```

## Verification

- New regression test `TestLinkSubagentSessionsReParentsNestedGrandchild`
  (main → orchestrator → grandchild with the buggy stored state + correct tool_calls
  edges): **unpatched → FAIL** (grandchild parent `main`, want `orchestrator`);
  **patched → PASS**.
- All existing `Subagent|LinkSubagent` tests in `./internal/db` stay green, incl.
  `TestLinkSubagentSessionsOverridesContinuation`.
- No frontend change needed for reachability — transcript drill-down
  (`ToolBlock` → `SubagentInline`) is already driven by `tool_calls.subagent_session_id`
  at any depth. The fix makes `/children` and usage rollups correct.

## Optional follow-ups (not in the PR)

1. **Sidebar visual nesting:** the sidebar renders a root's descendants as one flat
   "Subagents (N)" list (`emitGroupItems`,
   `frontend/src/lib/components/sidebar/session-list-utils.ts`). Per-row
   `parent_session_id` is already in the payload; indenting grandchildren under their
   spawner is a client-only change.
2. **Claude sidecar metadata:** Claude Code writes `subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json` with
   explicit `parentAgentId` + `spawnDepth`; the Claude parser doesn't read it (Codex's
   `parent_thread_id` already gets this treatment in `internal/parser/codex.go`).
3. **Cross-agent lineage:** a `codex exec` run from inside a Claude subagent's Bash tool
   creates a standalone Codex session (indexed from `~/.codex/sessions`) with no link to
   the Claude session that spawned it — two unlinked views of the same event.

title: Fix nested subagent hierarchy: re-parent depth≥2 subagents to their spawner
body:
Fixes #1246.

## Problem

Nested Claude Code subagents (`main -> orchestrator -> grandchild`, spawnDepth >= 2) all
live in the same flat `<main-session>/subagents/` directory, so path derivation assigns
`parent_session_id = main session` at every depth and tags each row
`relationship_type = 'subagent'`. `LinkSubagentSessions()` — which corrects the parent
from the authoritative `tool_calls.subagent_session_id` spawn edge — skipped those rows
because of its `WHERE relationship_type != 'subagent'` guard. The hierarchy stayed flat
past depth 1: `GET /sessions/{orchestrator}/children` was empty and per-session usage
rollups attributed the whole subtree to the main session.

## Change

All in `internal/db/sessions.go`, plus one call-site change in `internal/sync/engine.go`:

- **Re-parent from the spawn edge.** The linking predicate now updates a session when it
  is not yet tagged `subagent` (the pre-existing upgrade path) or when its stored parent
  differs from the spawn edge (null-safe `IS NOT`). The tool-call edge records the actual
  spawn, so it is authoritative over the path heuristic.
- **Deterministic conflict resolution** (`subagentSpawnerExpr`). Copied or forked history
  can leave several sessions claiming the same child. Resolution is a pure function of
  the stored edges — never of ingestion order — so a link written from a partial view
  self-corrects on a later sync: candidates are ordered by start time (a fork derives
  from its source, so it starts later), with `started_at` normalized via `strftime`
  because raw RFC3339Nano strings do not sort chronologically when fractional seconds
  are stripped. Unknown or malformed start times rank last, and the session id breaks
  remaining ties.
- **Cost bounded by edges, not archive.** The global statement is driven from the
  `idx_tool_calls_subagent` partial index (`s.id IN (SELECT tc.subagent_session_id ...)`)
  instead of a full `sessions` scan, so bulk-sync linking cost tracks the number of spawn
  edges rather than archive size.
- **Watcher syncs bounded by the batch.** `SyncSingleSessionContext` — called by the
  session watcher on every file change — now uses `LinkSubagentSessionsForSessions`,
  which restricts the pass to children reachable from the sessions that sync wrote
  (spawner-side and child-side branches, both index seeks). Bulk paths (full sync,
  reconciliation, resync) keep their coalesced global pass. Query-plan tests pin both
  cost shapes at two archive sizes.
- **All single-session branches link.** The incremental append path (which can
  introduce a spawn edge when the Task tool_use and its subagent mapping land in the
  same append) links scoped to the appended session, and children referenced by a
  batch's pre-write edges are captured (`SubagentChildSessionIDs`) before rewrites or
  parser-exclusion deletes cascade those edges away, so a former child still
  re-resolves to its remaining spawner in the same sync.

## Tradeoffs and limitations

- When conflicting edges exist and the real spawner has no usable `started_at`, a dated
  copy wins; protecting it would require reading the child's stored parent, which
  reintroduces ingestion-order dependence. The link self-corrects once the spawner's
  start time becomes known. Documented in `subagentSpawnerExpr`.
- Fork/copy provenance policy (self-edge guards, deeper lineage tracking) is scoped to
  #1250.
- No frontend change: transcript drill-down already follows `tool_calls` at any depth;
  this fix makes `/children` and usage rollups correct.

Reviewers should start at `subagentSpawnerExpr` and the two linking statements in
`internal/db/sessions.go`, then the `SyncSingleSessionContext` call site.

---

Disclosure: investigated and written with Claude Code (AI).

title: OpenCode: recover legacy JSON session cwd from project metadata
body:
## Summary

Legacy file-backed OpenCode sessions can remain under project `unknown` with an empty cwd even though OpenCode still has enough metadata to recover their working directory.

Older files under `storage/session/<project-id>/<session-id>.json` often do not contain a `directory` field. The corresponding `storage/project/<project-id>.json` file can contain a concrete `worktree`, but agentsview currently does not consult it while parsing the session.

This is separate from #1235, which fixes SQLite-backed sessions by preferring `session.directory`.

## Current behavior

`parseOpenCodeStorageFile` decodes the session JSON and passes only its optional `directory` into `buildOpenCodeParsedSession`. When old session JSON omits that field, cwd is empty and project derivation falls back to `unknown`.

The project ID is already encoded by the parent directory of the session path, and OpenCode stores matching metadata at `storage/project/<project-id>.json`, for example:

```json
{
  "id": "<project-id>",
  "vcs": "git",
  "worktree": "/path/to/repository"
}
```

Archived sessions may have already reached the current data version while retaining the empty cwd, so merely changing parsing is not sufficient to refresh unchanged rows.

## Expected behavior

For file-backed OpenCode sessions:

1. Prefer a usable `session.directory` when present.
2. Otherwise read the matching project metadata and use its concrete `worktree`.
3. Derive the project through the existing `ExtractProjectFromCwd` path.
4. Preserve `unknown` only when neither source contains a usable directory.
5. Reparse existing archived rows after the fix.

## Proposed implementation

- Derive `<project-id>` from the validated `storage/session/<project-id>/<session-id>.json` path.
- Load `storage/project/<project-id>.json` and decode its `worktree`.
- Reuse the same usable-path precedence as SQLite parsing: concrete session directory first, then project worktree.
- Treat missing project metadata as a normal fallback miss, but report malformed or unreadable metadata consistently with other related-source failures.
- Include the project metadata state/content in the session source fingerprint so worktree changes invalidate the archived result.
- Ensure discovery/watcher classification causes affected sessions to refresh when a project metadata file changes, without scanning every stored session per event.
- Bump the agentsview data version so unchanged legacy sessions with stale empty cwd/project are reparsed.
- Keep OpenCode-format provider behavior explicit because Kilo and MiMoCode reuse the file-backed parser; use the fallback only where the provider storage layout supports matching project metadata.

## Tests

Add coverage for:

- Old session JSON without `directory` plus project metadata with `worktree` resolves cwd and project.
- Session `directory` takes precedence over a different project worktree.
- Missing project metadata keeps the current empty-cwd/unknown fallback.
- Malformed or unreadable related metadata does not silently replace a previously archived good cwd.
- A project metadata worktree change invalidates and reparses affected sessions.
- A data-version upgrade refreshes an unchanged archived legacy session.
- Cardinality regression: a project metadata event does work bounded by that project's changed batch, not the total OpenCode archive size.

## Scope

This addresses legacy JSON sessions whose project metadata still exists. It cannot recover cwd for orphaned SQLite sessions whose source row and event history have already been deleted.

title: Stale daemon runtime record causes permanent "backend not responding" deadlock after reboot/update
body:
## Summary

After a reboot (or unclean shutdown), AgentsView Desktop can enter a permanent deadlock where:

- The desktop UI shows **"AgentsView backend is not responding — A backend process is running, but it is not answering health checks"**
- `agentsview serve --background` logs **"agentsview serve --background is already in progress."** and exits immediately
- The UI loops endlessly: launch sidecar → sidecar exits code 0 → repeat

The backend never starts.

## Root Cause

AgentsView writes a daemon runtime record to `~/.agentsview/daemon.<pid>.json` on startup. On shutdown/crash, this file is **not cleaned up**. On the next launch, the liveness check does:

```
kill(pid, 0)  // "is this pid alive?"
```

On macOS, **PIDs are reused** after reboot. The stale PID will very likely be assigned to a completely different process (in my case, `FindMyMacd` reused pid `1594`). The liveness check returns "alive", so AgentsView concludes its backend is already running but unhealthy — and `serve --background` refuses to start a new instance.

The desktop app has no path out of this state. It cannot distinguish between:
1. A genuine unhealthy agentsview backend
2. An unrelated process that happened to inherit a reused PID

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run AgentsView (any version)
2. Shut down without cleanly stopping the backend (reboot, hard kill, crash, etc.)
3. `~/.agentsview/daemon.<old_pid>.json` remains on disk
4. After reboot, macOS reuses `<old_pid>` for a different process
5. Launch AgentsView Desktop → permanent "backend not responding" deadlock

More likely after a **version upgrade** (e.g. v0.32.1 → v0.36.1) since users often reboot between versions.

## Workaround

Remove the stale runtime record manually:

```bash
# Find stale daemon records
ls -la ~/.agentsview/daemon.*.json

# Inspect it (check: is version old? is started_at from before last reboot?)
cat ~/.agentsview/daemon.<pid>.json

# Verify the PID belongs to something else (not agentsview)
ps -p <pid> -o comm=

# Rename/remove the stale record
mv ~/.agentsview/daemon.<pid>.json ~/.agentsview/daemon.<pid>.json.bak

# Relaunch the app
osascript -e 'quit app "AgentsView"'
open -a AgentsView
```

Note: First launch after a version upgrade may take **2+ minutes** if a DB migration/resync runs. This is normal — wait for it.

## Suggested Fix

The liveness check should validate **process identity**, not just PID existence. At minimum, one of:

1. **Check process name/cmdline** — confirm the living process is actually `agentsview`
2. **Store process start time** in the runtime record, then compare against actual process start time — start time mismatch = PID was reused
3. **Health-check before concluding "already running"** — if the pid is alive but the health endpoint is unreachable, treat the record as stale and start a fresh instance
4. **Clean up the runtime record on shutdown** — register a signal handler (SIGTERM/SIGINT) that deletes the daemon JSON file before exiting

Option 3 alone (probe the health endpoint before refusing to start) would prevent this with minimal code change.

## Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon)
- AgentsView Desktop v0.36.1
- Stale record was from v0.32.1, dated 2026-06-13
- Backend was healthy once the stale record was removed

## Desktop UX Suggestion

When the desktop detects "pid alive but health check failing", surface a **"Clear stale lock and restart"** button rather than looping indefinitely. Current UX gives the user no actionable recovery path.

title: LinkSubagentSessions: provenance for conflicting fork/copy spawn edges (follow-up to #1247)
body:
## Summary

`LinkSubagentSessions()` resolves a subagent's `parent_session_id` from the
authoritative `tool_calls.subagent_session_id` edge. When a child session is
referenced by spawn edges from **more than one distinct session** — reachable
via **copied/forked history** (e.g. after `CopyOrphanedDataFromExcluding`) — the
"real" parent is ambiguous, and `tool_calls` alone doesn't carry enough
provenance to disambiguate.

PR #1247 made the common case correct and safe (unambiguous edges resolve to the
one spawner; ambiguous edges fall back to preserving the current parent via
`COALESCE(<grouped subquery>, parent_session_id)` instead of an arbitrary
`LIMIT 1`). This issue tracks the remaining, deeper fork-reconciliation gaps that
are out of scope for that depth-2 parenting fix.

## Known gaps

1. **Ingestion-order dependence** (flagged by roborev on `c544f11`).
   If a forked/copied edge is stored *first* (initially the only edge), linking
   provisionally re-parents the child to it. When the real edge arrives later and
   the child becomes ambiguous, `COALESCE(..., parent_session_id)` permanently
   retains the (possibly wrong) provisional parent. Normal fork ordering is safe
   because a fork's source is parsed first, but reconciliation/copy paths don't
   guarantee that ordering.

2. **No self-edge guard.**
   Nothing prevents `tool_calls.subagent_session_id == session_id` (only
   reachable from a corrupt/crafted transcript). It would yield a self-parent.
   Consequences are bounded — every parent-chain consumer uses `UNION` recursive
   CTEs that dedupe and terminate on cycles, so no loop/crash; the row just drops
   from the sidebar. A one-line `AND tc.session_id <> sessions.id` on the
   subqueries + `EXISTS` closes it (and also lets a self-edge + a real edge
   resolve to the real spawner).

## Possible approaches

- Resolve ambiguous edges via **stable provenance** — e.g. the earliest-started
  spawner (`ORDER BY started_at`), which is stateless and self-correcting
  regardless of ingestion order.
- Or retain enough **source-parent state** to reverse a provisional linkage once
  candidates become ambiguous.
- Add the self-edge guard.

## Suggested regression tests

- Call `LinkSubagentSessions` **before and after** inserting the conflicting edge
  and assert the child converges to the correct spawner (roborev's suggestion).
- A self-edge case asserting no self-parent.

## Context

Split out of #1247 (nested subagent depth ≥ 2 re-parenting). The core fix there
is a strict improvement over the previous behavior; this is the follow-up design
work the maintainer may want to weigh in on.

title: Add artifact publication ledger and export pipeline
body:
Second PR in the artifact-sync split (follows #1242, which froze the wire format and added the docbank-backed store). Extracted from the closed #1239 branch with review fixes applied during extraction.

## What this adds

- **SQLite publication ledger** (`internal/db`): `artifact_export_queue`, `artifact_publications`, `artifact_publication_revisions`, `artifact_checkpoint_heads`/`_floors`, plus session triggers that enqueue owned-session changes. Triggers are origin-gated — they fire only once an artifact origin exists in `pg_sync_state` — so archives that never opt in carry no queue writes. Trigger DDL lives in Go and is installed after column migrations (drops run before), so no trigger references session columns while migrations run.
- **Go enqueue hooks** for child-only mutations that don't touch trigger-covered session columns: batch message writes (queue generation sampled around the batch, enqueues exactly once when the triggers didn't fire), standalone usage-event replacement, and token-coverage backfill. Queue bootstrap is an explicit call at origin creation, not a migrate-time backfill.
- **Origin lifecycle** (`internal/artifact`): `EnsureOrigin`/`AdoptOrigin`/`StoredOrigin`. Creating or adopting an origin bootstraps the export queue; a failed bootstrap rolls the origin back (deleting the key when there was none before, since the gates test key existence) so a retry re-runs population. Adopting over a different established origin force-requeues every owned session with a generation bump, because prior acknowledgements belong to the old origin.
- **Checkpointed export pipeline** (`internal/artifact`): claims pending queue rows, publishes content-addressed session manifests and segments into the store, records publication revisions, and advances per-origin checkpoint heads with monotone sequence reservation. Stale claims (a writer advanced the generation mid-export) roll back atomically. Incremental export is bounded by the dirty batch; an unchanged archive costs a catalog identity check only. Full export streams all bodies, then re-checks the queue up to 32 settle rounds — hitting the bound returns the accumulated result with an error meaning "made progress, run again."
- **Resync carriage**: `CopySyncStateFrom` carries queue, publication, revision, and checkpoint state across a full resync and re-dirties every copied queue row — the origin gate keeps triggers silent in the rebuild's temp DB, and a parser bump changes manifest hashes anyway, so the exporter must re-verify each session (unchanged content is cheap to skip, being content-addressed).

## Scope and limitations

- Export-side only. Nothing wires the pipeline to the daemon or CLI yet; that lands with folder transport and import in a later PR. There is no import/read path here.
- The ledger is local SQLite state. PostgreSQL push and shared query shapes are untouched.
- The wire format is unchanged: no golden churn, format stays frozen at v1.

## Where to look

- `internal/db/artifact_publication.go` — queue and ledger SQL, origin-gated enqueue
- `internal/db/db.go` — trigger DDL split around column migrations, bootstrap/requeue
- `internal/artifact/export.go` — publish → manifest → checkpoint ordering and claim lifecycle
- `internal/artifact/origin.go` — origin lifecycle and rollback semantics
- `internal/db/orphaned.go` — resync carriage and the pending-flag decision

title: fix(claude): keep ide context out of session titles
body:
the claude code vscode extension writes file-open and selection hints as standalone user-role xml envelopes. agentsview currently treats them as operator prompts, so they can become sidebar titles, count as user turns, and render raw markup.

complete standalone `ide_opened_file` and `ide_selection` envelopes now promote to hidden system metadata with distinct subtypes. the match is intentionally strict, so malformed wrappers and messages with real prompt text remain ordinary user content.

dag fork selection applies the same user-text preprocessing before counting turns, so reminder-prefixed ide context cannot promote an obsolete branch. incremental sync keeps promptless ide and continuation appends bounded to the new bytes, falling back to a full parse only when the first title-eligible prompt arrives.

the source data version advances to 74 because main now uses 73 for opencode bash exit-failure detection. existing sqlite archives are reparsed on upgrade, and duckdb mirrors rebuild on their next push through the independent source data-version gate; the mirror schema is unchanged.

closes #1238

title: parser: capture sessionKind and promptSource from Claude Code transcripts
body:
## What

Capture two Claude Code launch/prompt-provenance fields that the indexer currently reads past and discards:

- **`sessionKind`** — session-level (e.g. `"bg"`). Present on background/headless sessions, absent on interactive ones. Lands in a new `session_kind` column on `sessions`.
- **`promptSource`** — per user turn (e.g. `"typed"`, `"queued"`, `"system"`, `"sdk"`). Marks whether a turn was a human-typed prompt or a queued/system/SDK-injected one. Lands in a new `prompt_source` column on `messages`.

## Why

Both signals exist on essentially every current Claude Code transcript but are thrown away at parse time, so the archive can't answer two questions it otherwise has the data for: was a session interactive or headless, and was a given prompt typed by a human or injected. This mirrors the recently-added `entrypoint` capture — same shape of information, same reason to keep it.

## How

The change follows the existing `entrypoint` / `agent_label` and `source_type` / `is_sidechain` handling rather than inventing a new pattern:

- `sessionKind` is treated as a session-identity field alongside `entrypoint`: first-non-empty-wins across the file, wired into the incremental identity-escalation check, and blanked by the Cowork and Qoder parsers that reuse the Claude parse body (exactly as they blank `entrypoint`).
- `promptSource` is treated as a per-message source column alongside `source_type`/`is_sidechain`, including the retained-field whitelist in `compactClaudeEntry` and the message token fingerprints the PG/DuckDB push fast-paths compare against.

Both columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, so transcripts that predate the fields and other agents that never emit them read empty and are otherwise untouched. A `dataVersion` bump (79) triggers the standard reparse so existing Claude rows backfill both fields. Capture is mirrored across the SQLite, Postgres, and DuckDB stores (mirror `SchemaVersion` 9) and the artifact wire format, where the manifest advances to v3 and message segments to v2: older artifacts still decode with the fields empty, while pre-provenance peers park new artifacts behind the existing future-version gate instead of silently dropping the fields. The fields also round-trip through artifact import, re-enqueue a published session's export when only `session_kind` changes, and count toward the export preflight's message-byte bound.

## Scope / limitations

- Pure field capture — no counting, aggregation, health-signal, or automation-classification logic is touched.
- `session_kind`/`prompt_source` backfill via the dataVersion-79 reparse; rows whose source files no longer exist stay empty.
- No new API/CLI surface or UI is added; the columns are available for consumers that read the archive directly.

## Where to look

- `internal/parser/claude.go` — the capture site (`sessionKind` next to `entrypoint`; `promptSource` next to `isSidechain`) and the `compactClaudeEntry` retained-field whitelist.
- `internal/parser/claude_provider.go`, `provider.go`, `internal/sync/engine.go` — incremental identity threading for `sessionKind`.
- `internal/db/{schema.sql,db.go,sessions.go,messages.go}` — SQLite columns, migrations, and read/write plumbing.
- `internal/postgres/*` and `internal/duckdb/*` — the mirrored columns and fingerprints.

The source of truth for both fields is the Claude Code transcript format, where `sessionKind` and `promptSource` appear as top-level keys on session JSONL entries.

title: Support opencode tool failure detection (tool: invalid format)
body:
## Description

AgentsView doesn't detect tool call failures from **opencode** sessions. All opencode sessions show `tool_failure_signal_count: 0` despite confirmed invalid tool calls in the session data.

## Root Cause

Opencode stores invalid tool calls differently than Claude Code/Codex. The opencode format records failures as:

```json
{
  "type": "tool",
  "tool": "invalid",
  "callID": "call_00_...",
  "state": {
    "status": "completed",
    "input": {
      "tool": "playwright_browser_fill",
      "error": "Model tried to call unavailable tool 'playwright_browser_fill'..."
    },
    "output": "The arguments provided to the tool are invalid: ...",
    "title": "Invalid Tool",
    ...
  }
}
```

Key differences from Claude Code format:
1. Uses `tool: "invalid"` instead of `tool_name: "invalid"`
2. Error message is nested in `state.input.error` (not top-level)
3. `state.status` is `"completed"` (not `"error"`)
4. Contains `state.title: "Invalid Tool"` as another signal

## Session Data Location

Opencode stores sessions in a SQLite database at:
- `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`
- `message` table has `data` JSON column with role/agent info
- `part` table has `data` JSON column containing tool calls (including invalid ones)
- Invalid tool call parts: `SELECT data FROM part WHERE data LIKE '%tool: invalid%'`

## Suggestion

The opencode parser should detect tool failures by checking for:
- `part.data.tool == "invalid"`
- Or `part.data.state.title == "Invalid Tool"`
- Or `part.data.state.input.error` presence

## Impact

- 37 opencode sessions analyzed, all showing `tool_failure_signal_count: 0`
- At least 5+ confirmed invalid tool calls in a single session
- Missing data skews tool health metrics and health scores for opencode users

## Environment
- AgentsView v0.38.1
- Opencode (latest)
- Windows 11

title: fix(parser): detect opencode invalid tool calls as failures
body:
Fixes #1254

## Problem

Opencode stores failed tool calls with `tool: "invalid"` and `state.status: "completed"` — the parser never emitted a `ResultEvent`, so `ComputeToolHealth` had no error signal to detect. All opencode sessions showed `tool_failure_signal_count: 0` despite confirmed invalid tool calls.

## Fix

In `extractOpenCodeToolCall()`, when `d.ToolName == "invalid"`, attach a `ResultEvent{Status: "errored"}` so the signal pipeline (`extractToolCallRows` → `signals.IsFailure` → `ComputeToolHealth`) counts it as a failure.

## Test

Added `TestParseOpenCodeDB_InvalidToolCall` that seeds a session with an invalid tool part and asserts `ResultEvents[0].Status == "errored"`.

All existing opencode tests continue to pass.

title: feat(parser): detect opencode bash tool failures from metadata.exit
body:
## Problem

On Windows (and occasionally Linux), bash tool failures leave `metadata.exit > 0` in the tool state but the output text does NOT contain the Linux-style `exit status N` pattern that AgentsView's `isBashFailure()` checks. Example outputs from real sessions:

- `'choco' is not recognized as an internal or external command` - exit=1, no "exit status" text
- (empty output) - exit=1, no text at all
- `rsync error: some files could not be transferred` - exit=1

The exit code is reliably recorded in `metadata.exit` by the agent, but the parser never reads it.

## Impact

On a Windows machine with 273 opencode sessions, 1233 bash tool failures are missed because they lack the Linux-style output pattern. Only 51 are currently detected (via the `tool:"invalid"` fix). The remaining ~1200 are invisible to signals, insights, and health scoring.

## Proposed Fix

In `extractOpenCodeToolCall()`, after parsing the tool state, check `metadata.exit`:

```go
if len(state.Metadata) > 0 {
    var m struct { Exit int `json:"exit"` }
    if err := json.Unmarshal(state.Metadata, &m); err == nil && m.Exit > 0 {
        isFailure = true
    }
}
```

This is opt-in per agent - only opencode records metadata.exit. Other agents are unaffected.

## Branch

https://github.com/ajinkyajacob/agentsview/tree/feat/opencode-metadata-exit-failure-detection

## Risk

- Non-zero exit doesn't always mean failure (e.g., `grep` returns 1 for no match). However, AgentsView's existing `exitStatusRe` already makes the same assumption via output text. This just adds parity for the metadata path.
- Only applies when `metadata` key exists in the tool state (opencode format), so other agents are isolated.

title: fix(poolside): correct Linux default directory to .local/state/poolside
body: Poolside stores trajectory files under the XDG state directory (~/.local/state/poolside/trajectories/), not the data directory. The merged PR #1241 used the wrong path, preventing session discovery.

title: fix(parser): bound Gemini reconciliation work
body:
Lost-event recovery rehydrates discovered Gemini sources in bounded pages. Gemini previously routed every candidate back through changed-path classification, rebuilding root-wide project metadata and repeating filesystem and Git resolution once per session. Large recoveries could therefore keep an otherwise idle daemon CPU-bound long after discovery completed.

Teach the Gemini provider to reconstruct the exact discovered source from its spooled path and project hint. This preserves the project selected by authoritative discovery while keeping reconciliation work proportional to the candidate batch. A scaling regression covers both small and larger archives.

title: fix(ssh): deduplicate resolved Poolside targets
body:
Poolside support in #1241 registered three platform-specific default directories behind the single `POOLSIDE_DIR` override. The SSH resolver evaluates that override while iterating each default, so a non-empty override emits the same `trajectories` target three times. The Linux fallback correction in #1258 changed one default path but did not cause or resolve this duplication.

Deduplicate resolved directory targets per agent before archive construction, preserving first-seen order and allowing different agents to share a path independently. Strengthen the Poolside override regression to require one parsed transfer target. This addresses the post-merge roborev finding on #1241.

title: Add Codebuff/Freebuff agent support
body:
Parses Codebuff and Freebuff sessions from `~/.config/manicode/projects/<project>/chats/<timestamp>/`. Both agents share the same on-disk layout; sessions are classified by the `agentType` field in `run-state.json`.

### Highlights

- Full transcript parsing: user/ai/error messages, tool calls with skill attribution, thinking blocks, subagent invocations
- Block types: text, tool, agent, mode-divider, plan, ask-user, image
- Credits tracking: extracts `creditsUsed` from `run-state.json` and maps to cost (1 credit = $0.01)
- Freebuff auto-classification: sessions with "free" in `agentType` appear as a separate filter

### Unique considerations

- Freebuff shares the Codebuff provider (single registration) to avoid double-discovery and skip-cache contention
- The `agentType` field is an agent template name (e.g. `base2-free-deepseek`), not the actual LLM model -- the real model is selected server-side
- `contextTokenCount` provides context window size but per-message token breakdown is not available in the on-disk format

### Limitations

- Mid-session model switches are invisible -- the on-disk format has no per-turn model field
- Freebuff has no credits (ad-supported); cost tracking only applies to Codebuff
- The `agent` field on `ChatMessage` is not populated in the persisted format, so per-turn agent attribution relies on subagent blocks only

title: fix(sync): bound OpenCode background work across watcher and polling modes
body:
Degraded polling now retains provider-owned watch scopes end to end. Persistent polling reasons carry their originating watch scopes, so a shared configured dir keeps a single complete owner when one exists and falls back to generic only for mixed or incomplete ownership. Provider-scoped polling reconciles only the exact selected configured roots, which keeps an unchanged nested OpenCode scope suppressed while a changed parent scope still syncs through the existing provider path.

One predicate now answers whether a pass reaches a configured root, and both discovery admission and tombstone accounting call it. A provider-scoped pass therefore reports only the roots it actually selected as covered, so a session relocated into a configured nested root the pass did not select is not read as deleted; that tombstone waits for a pass covering every configured root. Descendant scopes a pass excludes are excluded by the ownership query rather than after its rows are paged, so a small selected scope no longer does work proportional to a large unselected nested archive.

Each provider-owned directory carries its own polling obligation once a reason covers more than one, matching what the runtime watcher fallback already did. One obligation carries one probe, so a probe no longer answers for a directory it never observed. Obligation keys are namespaced by the reason that created them, which keeps two reasons on the same root distinct without either having to be split per directory to tell them apart.

The group-scoped acknowledgement reset from the prior rebuild stays intact, and every eligible polling group still runs in deterministic order. The bounded journal change feed remains deferred to a follow-up for issue #1208.

Part of #1208

title: fix(test): synchronize daemon startup wait

title: `duckdb push` through the local daemon does not expand `~` in `[duckdb].path`
body:
### agentsview version

`agentsview v0.38.1 (commit 1e173b95, built 2026-07-13T19:56:19Z)`

### Install method

Homebrew cask

### OS / platform

macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

n/a (configuration / CLI bug, not agent-specific)

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened, and what did you expect

With a tilde path under `[duckdb]` in `~/.agentsview/config.toml`, `agentsview duckdb push` fails:

```toml
[duckdb]
  path = "~/mirror.duckdb"
```

```
fatal: duckdb push: opening duckdb file: database/sql/driver: could not connect to database:
IO Error: Cannot open file "/tmp/~/mirror.duckdb": No such file or directory
```

The `~` is left literal, and the remaining relative path is joined onto the caller's current working directory.

Expansion is inconsistent in two dimensions. Same binary, same config value:

| `[duckdb].path` | In-process push | Push via local daemon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `${HOME}/mirror.duckdb` | expands | expands |
| `~/mirror.duckdb` | expands | literal `~`, joined to CWD |
| `$HOME/mirror.duckdb` | literal, joined to CWD | literal, joined to CWD |

Expected: `~` expands on both paths. The README documents tilde values in `config.toml` (`copilot_dirs = ["~/.copilot/jetbrains-sessions"]`), and the README also states that `duckdb push` auto-starts the daemon when needed, so the daemon path is the default one and the broken case is the one users hit first.

It also raises two more questions:

1. Is `${HOME}` supposed to be supported in config values? It works on both code paths today, but bare `$HOME` never expands. Go's native `os.ExpandEnv` would treat the two forms identically.
2. Is CWD-relative resolution intended for a relative `[duckdb].path`? For a value that lives in a config file, resolving against `$HOME` or against the config file's own directory would be more predictable, and would make a failed expansion produce a clearer error than a path with `~` in the middle of it.

Workaround for anyone hitting this: use `${HOME}/…`. It works on both code paths and stays portable across machines with different home prefixes, which matters when `config.toml` is shared through a dotfiles repo.

### Sample session file or snippet

n/a, no session data involved.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
# ~/.agentsview/config.toml
#   [duckdb]
#     path = "~/mirror.duckdb"

# Broken: plain push auto-starts the daemon, tilde stays literal and is
# joined onto the caller's CWD.
cd /tmp && agentsview duckdb push
# Cannot open file "/tmp/~/mirror.duckdb"

# Correct: no daemon reachable, so the push runs in-process and expands.
agentsview daemon stop
cd /tmp && AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1 agentsview duckdb push
# resolves to /Users/<user>/mirror.duckdb
```

Prior daemon state does not matter on its own, because a plain push starts one. The isolating variable is only whether a daemon is reachable:

| Run | Went via daemon | Resolved path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| daemon stopped, plain push | yes (auto-started) | `/tmp/~/mirror.duckdb` |
| daemon running, plain push | yes | `/tmp/~/mirror.duckdb` |
| daemon stopped, `AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1` | no | `/Users/<user>/mirror.duckdb` |
| daemon running, `AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1` | yes | `/tmp/~/mirror.duckdb` |

Minor side observation from that last row: `AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1` only prevents starting a daemon, it does not bypass one that is already running.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (no match for tilde, path expansion, duckdb path, or home directory config)
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: fix(claude): keep IDE-context envelopes out of first_message previews
body:
Fixes #1238.

Claude Code's VS Code extension sometimes prepends an IDE-context wrapper
(`<ide_opened_file>` or `<ide_selection>`) onto the user's real prompt inside a
single transcript entry. Those sessions showed raw markup as their first
message and in the transcript.

After this change:

- The parser splits such entries into a hidden metadata row plus the visible
  prompt, so `first_message` and the transcript show only what the user typed.
  Only well-formed leading wrappers with a non-empty remainder are split;
  malformed or mid-message markup is left alone.
- Data version 88 re-parses existing sessions so already-archived rows are
  cleaned up too.
- Pins survive that re-parse. The split inserts a row and shifts ordinals, so
  pin restoration now follows one rule, applied identically in SQLite and
  PostgreSQL: a unique source UUID follows its row; any other pin follows its
  message's role, content, and position among identical messages, provided
  that group kept its size. Unchanged messages keep their pins across inserted
  rows, ordinal shifts, and metadata reclassification, and a streamed partial
  response that completes in place keeps its pin as well.
- Uploads no longer discard parser metadata: hidden/system status, source
  identity, sidechain, and compact-boundary fields are preserved, so uploaded
  sessions render the same as locally synced ones.

Two limits are deliberate. Editing a pinned message that has no source UUID
drops the pin in both stores: the edit destroys the only identity the pin
could follow, and dropping consistently beats guessing. And while the one-time
re-parse push is rewriting a session, pin, unpin, and star on that session
wait for the push batch to commit.

Where to look: the split logic in `internal/parser/claude.go`, pin
restoration in `internal/db/messages.go` and `internal/postgres/push.go`,
resync copying in `internal/db/orphaned.go`, and the upload field mapping in
`internal/server/upload.go`.

title: fix(test): filter recall evidence log capture to recall lines
body:
The seven recall-evidence tests in `internal/db/recall_evidence_window_test.go` capture the global `log` output via `captureRecallEvidenceLog` and assert on the whole buffer — mostly exact-equality against a single expected `recall: revoked provenance ...` line, plus two empty-buffer checks on rollback paths. That is stricter than the tests' intent: any unrelated line written to the global logger inside the capture window fails them.

One such line exists in practice: `ReplaceSessionMessages` logs a `db: ReplaceSessionMessages ...` diagnostic when the call exceeds `slowOpThreshold` (100ms). Under the coverage job's instrumentation the call crossed the threshold and the diagnostic landed in the captured buffer, failing `TestRecallEvidenceReconciliationLogsStableReason/missing_digest` on an unrelated PR (run 30135996204).

This change filters at the capture point instead of loosening assertions: `captureRecallEvidenceLog` now returns a writer that retains only `recall: `-prefixed lines (the only prefix the revocation flush emits) and discards everything else. Since the writer embeds `bytes.Buffer`, all seven call sites — `String()`, `Reset()`, the `assert.Empty` checks — are unchanged, and the exact-equality assertions keep their full strength for recall lines specifically. A small regression test replays the pollution scenario directly.

The slow-op diagnostics themselves are intentional production instrumentation and are untouched. Other log-capture helpers in the repo (`cmd/agentsview`, `internal/config`, `internal/parser`, `internal/duckdb`) already use substring/count-based assertions and are not affected by this failure mode, so they are deliberately left alone.

Reviewers should look at the `recallEvidenceLogBuffer.Write` prefix check: it relies on the stdlib `log` package issuing one `Write` per formatted line, which holds because the helper clears flags and prefix while installed.

title: ClassifyOutcome grades a session completed when it ends on a raw, unrecovered API error - giveUpPatterns doesn't match error-shaped final messages
body:
**agentsview version:** agentsview v0.38.1 (commit 1e173b95, built 2026-07-13T21:41:46Z)

**Install method:** install.sh (`curl -fsSL https://agentsview.io/install.sh | bash`)

**OS / platform:** Arch Linux (rolling), x86_64

**Which agent and version:** Claude Code 2.1.205 (the affected session's own recorded `version` field)

**Which model(s):** claude-opus-4-8

## What happened, and what did you expect

`internal/signals/outcome.go`'s `ClassifyOutcome` grades a session `completed` (medium confidence) when
its transcript ends on a raw, never-recovered API/connection error.

Looking at the current source: `OutcomeInput` only carries `EndedWithRole`, `LastAssistantText`,
`FinalFailureStreak`, `MessageCount`, `IsAutomated`, `LastActivity` - nothing about whether the final
assistant message was a genuine answer vs. a transport-level error (`isApiErrorMessage` /
`"error":"server_error"` on the raw transcript entry never reaches this struct). For a session that ends
on `EndedWithRole == "assistant"`, the only check protecting against a bad final message is
`hasGiveUpPattern`, which substring-matches a fixed phrase list (`"i'm unable to"`, `"i can't proceed"`,
`"i don't have access"`, `"i cannot proceed"`, `"i am unable to"`). A raw error string like
`"API Error: Unable to connect to API (ConnectionRefused)"` doesn't match any of them, so the session
falls through to the generic `completed`/`medium` branch.

Expected: a terminal message that is a raw API/connection error (not the agent's own prose) shouldn't be
treated the same as a delivered answer - either a distinct `outcome` (you already have `errored` for the
`FinalFailureStreak >= 3` case) or at minimum a lowered `health_grade`/`outcome_confidence`.

## Repro

Confirmed on a real session, `sync --full`'d immediately beforehand so this isn't stale data (I found and
discarded a look-alike earlier that turned out to be pure sync lag - the source file was still growing;
this one's file size/mtime exactly match what's ingested, so it's genuinely final):

- Transcript's last line is a raw error entry, e.g.:
  ```json
  {
    "type": "assistant",
    "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": [
      { "type": "text", "text": "API Error: Unable to connect to API (ConnectionRefused)" }
    ]},
    "error": "server_error",
    "isApiErrorMessage": true
  }
  ```
  with no further lines ever appended after it (2 weeks old at time of filing, so not in-flight).
- Derived row: `outcome=completed`, `outcome_confidence=medium`, `health_grade=A`, `ended_with_role=assistant`.
- Corpus check (local `sessions.db`, after a full resync): 1 match out of 1110 `subagent`-relationship
  sessions whose ingested final message begins with the literal string `API Error:`. This is a narrow,
  literal-prefix detector on a small local corpus, not a rate - just what I could confirm by hand.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)

Same shape as the existing `giveUpPatterns` check: add a check for a terminal message that's a raw
transport error (either pattern-match `"API Error:"`/similar prefixes the same way `hasGiveUpPattern`
does, or thread the raw `isApiErrorMessage`/`error` field through into `OutcomeInput` for a precise
check) and route it to `errored` or a lowered confidence, instead of falling into the generic
`completed`/`assistant` branch.

Happy to share the full anonymized transcript or run more queries against my local DB if useful.

title: Route trusted Linux builds to managed runners
body:
Same-repository pull-request branches are controlled by repository collaborators and should use organization-managed Linux capacity. Fork pull requests remain arbitrary code—even when the author is an organization member—and must continue to use GitHub-hosted runners.

Each PR now triggers only `pull_request`, so required checks are associated with the current PR revision. The dispatcher calls a main-pinned reusable workflow, and that immutable workflow independently requires both the head and base repositories to equal `github.repository` before selecting the managed public fleet. The caller supplies no runner or trust input.

The organization runner policy restricts access to the exact main-branch reusable workflows. Main pushes use the managed Linux fleet; Windows, macOS, ARM Linux, tags, and fork PRs retain their hosted runners.

title: Bind trusted runner routing to canonical PR revisions
body:
Trusted Linux jobs should select the managed runner only when the workflow is executing in the canonical repository. Fork-local events must remain on GitHub-hosted labels even when their branch and repository identities match each other.

The PR dispatchers call main-pinned reusable workflows without runner, trust, or checkout inputs. Those workflows independently derive trust from the canonical head and base repository identities, while checkout uses the immutable SHA GitHub associated with the caller event.

The managed image is intentionally lean, so the desktop composite explicitly installs a commit-pinned stable Rust toolchain instead of relying on hosted-image defaults. Playwright CI is bounded to eight workers because the host exposes more logical CPUs than each runner pod requests.

The coverage fixture now waits for the filesystem to expose a new change-time tick before asserting same-size rewrite detection, avoiding false failures on fast overlay filesystems without weakening the signature assertion.

title: Vector build aborts fatally on empty/whitespace-only embedding input instead of skip-stamping
body:
## What I was doing

Running an embeddings build over a large session archive.

## What happened

The build embedded thousands of documents successfully, then aborted fatally
on one document instead of skipping it:

```
Embedded 20501 documents (20532 chunks), skipped 0, stale 0
fatal: encode document <doc>: encode batch at 0: [vector.embeddings] status 400: {"error":{"message":"Invalid embedding input: Input strings must not be empty or whitespace-only","type":"embedding_error"}}
```

Some document apparently produced an empty or whitespace-only chunk, and the
embeddings endpoint rejected the batch with a 400.

`HTTPStatusError.Permanent()` in `internal/vector/encoder.go` is supposed to
classify input-specific 400/413/422 rejections as permanent so
`skipPermanentEncodeError` in `internal/vector/build.go` can skip-stamp just
that one document and let the build continue — the doc comment on
`skipPermanentEncodeError` explicitly lists "whitespace-only content some
servers refuse" as a case this is meant to cover:

```go
// skipPermanentEncodeError implements kitvec.FillOptions.OnEncodeError: a
// document the embeddings endpoint permanently rejects for input-specific
// reasons (e.g. a token-window overflow, whitespace-only content some servers
// refuse, or a content-policy rejection) is skipped ...
```

But the actual classifier, `hasDocumentSpecificEmbeddingError`, only
recognizes two message shapes: an overflow body (a size word like "too
long"/"length"/"limit"/"exceed"/"maximum" paired with "token"/"context"/
"input"/"text") or a content-policy body ("content" + "policy"). The message
"Input strings must not be empty or whitespace-only" matches neither pattern,
so `Permanent()` returns `false` and the whole build aborts instead of
skip-stamping the one poison document, contradicting the documented intent.

## Why it matters

A single document with empty/whitespace-only chunk content wedges the build
at that scan position: since pending documents are scanned in doc-key order,
later documents never get embedded, a first build never reaches `Missing==0`,
and auto-activation never fires — the exact "poison document" failure mode
`skipPermanentEncodeError`'s own comment warns about.

`hasDocumentSpecificEmbeddingError` in `internal/vector/encoder.go` needs a
case for empty/whitespace-only input rejections (e.g. "empty" or
"whitespace-only" paired with "input" or "string"), alongside the existing
overflow and content-policy cases.

title: Use local Go cache on self-hosted Linux
body:
Managed Linux jobs pass setup-go the literal cache value false using the same pre-dispatch repository and matrix facts that select the managed runner. They continue using the runner-provided GOMODCACHE and GOCACHE directories, so module and build caches remain local to each machine without archive restore or upload collisions.

Hosted fork builds and non-Linux jobs receive the literal value true and keep GitHub Actions caching. The main-pinned reusable workflow boundary remains unchanged.

The canonical-main routing arm now requires an explicit push event because pull_request_target also exposes the base branch ref. Only main pushes and same-repository pull requests can select the managed runner.

title: fix(cli): expand leading tilde in DuckDB mirror paths
body:
DuckDB config resolution currently leaves a leading `~` literal in `[duckdb].path`, so daemon-backed pushes can canonicalize the server mirror path against the daemon working directory instead of the user's home directory.

This expands leading-home shorthand during DuckDB config resolution, alongside the existing defaulting and env expansion, so the daemon and in-process callers resolve the same mirror path from the same config value. `${HOME}` expansion, default-path fallback, and non-leading tildes keep their current behavior. The change stays in `internal/config` with focused resolution regression coverage.

The config snippet and daemon-vs-in-process repro came from @halms's issue report.

Closes #1264

title: fix(signals): treat raw terminal API errors as errored outcomes
body:
Outcome classification currently marks a session completed when its final assistant message is a raw unrecovered API error, because the assistant-ended branch only lowers confidence for give-up prose.

This adds a dedicated terminal API-error discriminator before the generic assistant-completed branch and leaves the rest of the outcome ladder intact. User-ended sessions, repeated failure streaks, give-up phrases, and normal assistant answers keep their current classifications. The change stays in `internal/signals` with focused outcome regression coverage.

The terminal transcript entry and local corpus check came from @godilley's issue report.

Closes #1269

title: fix(vector): classify whitespace-only embedding rejections as permanent
body:
Vector builds currently abort when the embeddings endpoint rejects one document as empty or whitespace-only, even though the same surface already skip-stamps other document-specific permanent rejections.

This extends the existing `hasDocumentSpecificEmbeddingError` classifier so whitespace-only input rejections route through the shipped permanent-error path instead of creating a second special case in the build loop. Token-window overflow and content-policy rejections keep skipping, while auth, routing, model, media-type, rate-limit, and server failures still abort the build. The change stays in `internal/vector` with focused classifier regression coverage.

The fatal error body and build symptom came from @jesserobbins's issue report.

Closes #1272

title: docs: document the 0.39.0 release
body:
AgentsView 0.39.0 spans new provider support, guided semantic setup, multi-machine usage reporting, and substantial correctness and scalability work. The public documentation now matches the tagged implementation and release range, while deliberately presenting Recall and the portable artifact foundation as experimental rather than mature user workflows.

The release notes absorb the shipped DuckDB mirror changes from Unreleased, call out the local-only `duckdb push` compatibility change, and acknowledge every human contributor in the range plus the artifact collaborator. Supporting guides cover the new providers, French localization, session-search age, trace context, teammate labels, daily machine breakdowns, and current Recall retrieval/evidence behavior. The new semantic-setup screenshot is generated by the Docker harness and published through the synchronized `docs-generated-assets` orphan branch, keeping binary media out of the feature branch.

title: feat(frontend): compact settings navigation
body:
The settings page rendered every section in one narrow scrolling column, so finding a specific control became progressively harder as the surface grew. Keeping that document-style layout would also make each new setting increase the cost of navigating all the others.

This adopts the shared kit-ui settings pattern already used by Middleman: localized Preferences, Data, and Connections navigation; keyword search; and one visible panel at a time. Panels stay mounted across category changes and empty searches so drafts survive exploration, while panel changes reset the internal scroller to the new heading.

The route now provides the bounded flex host that the shared layout requires, keeping navigation and Full Resync fixed while long panels scroll independently. The kit-ui pin advances to the public commit that owns this responsive and accessible behavior, and the repository design guidance now reflects that component ownership.

Reviewers should focus on the panel metadata boundary, the zero-result search sentinel that preserves mounted state, and the settings-specific scroll ownership in the app shell.
