title: feat(db): add staged SQLite archive compaction
body:
Adds a staged, crash-safe compaction workflow for the local SQLite archive. `agentsview db compact` estimates reclaimable space (`--dry-run`), builds the compacted archive with `VACUUM INTO` in a caller-selected staging directory, verifies it (integrity, schema, row counts, SHA-256), and installs it with an atomic rename. An optional original backup (`--keep-backup`) and a recovery manifest cover interrupted replacements. A writable daemon serves the same operation via `POST /api/v1/data/compact` (localhost only), sharing the archive maintenance barrier with sync and resync. A production archive went from 11.85 GiB to 7.06 GiB with this workflow, reclaiming 4.79 GiB; that is a free-page/WAL result specific to that archive.

The command does not compress or deduplicate live tool-result payloads and does not change future growth from them; transparent payload compression remains a separate follow-up to #1375. This partially addresses #1375.

## Lifecycle and safety model

The lifecycle is built around an explicit commit point with two durable manifest phases:

- **prepared** — the verified candidate and backup are durable and writes are barred, so recovery may roll the replacement forward or back without losing anything. Recovery also accepts a content-verified archive whose hash moved only because the WAL-mode reopen rewrote the journal header.
- **committed** — written after post-install verification succeeds. From then on the installed archive is authoritative: recovery only cleans up staged artifacts and never restores the backup, so writes that land after a compaction can never be discarded by a later startup.

During the build, the archive stays readable while writes fail fast with the same retryable maintenance error a worker pass uses (`ErrWriterClosed`, mapped to 503 + Retry-After); connections pause only for the final swap. Compactions are serialized per archive (a concurrent attempt returns 409), and the barrier is enforced in the writer handle itself, so writer paths that do not take the database mutex are barred too, from the start of the build until the committed record is durable. Verification and commit run on an operation-owned context, so a client disconnect after the swap cannot roll back a completed compaction. The candidate is converted to WAL mode before hashing so its bytes stay stable across the install, and rollback prefers keeping or renaming an intact original over a second full-archive copy.

Manifest recovery runs only for the canonical archive under the write-owner lock (not in the generic `db.Open`), so derived databases such as a resync temp in the same directory never interpret the archive's manifest, and a relocated data directory recovers instead of refusing to start. Startup also sweeps staging directories abandoned before their manifest became durable. Failure paths restart the WAL checkpoint loop and the usage-cache backfill.

## Where risk concentrates

`internal/db/compact.go` carries the state machine: `Compact` (barrier, build, swap, commit), the swap failure paths, and `RecoverCompactManifest` with its prepared/committed recovery rights. The regression tests in `internal/db/compact_test.go` encode the guarantees: committed recovery preserves post-commit rows, hash-moved-but-verified archives are kept, cancel-after-install still succeeds, writes are barred mid-build and restored after, backfill restarts, recall FTS survives compaction, and derived opens ignore the manifest.

## Scope

Excludes zstd row compression, payload deduplication, automatic VACUUM after sync, and compact semantics for PostgreSQL or DuckDB mirrors.

title: feat(parser): add t3code session support
body:
# feat(parser): add t3code session support

t3code (`pingdotgg/t3code`, MIT) is an event-sourced desktop agent. It keeps
every thread in one SQLite database under its userdata root rather than a
session tree, so this registers it as a multi-session container provider on the
existing shared base: discovery surfaces `state.sqlite` once and Parse fans it
out into one session per thread, addressed by `<db>#<threadID>`. Change
detection is therefore per thread, so one live thread's writes never invalidate
its neighbours.

The append-only event log is folded into `projection_*` read models, and those
projections are the only tables a reader can interpret without replaying the
log. The visible conversation comes from `projection_threads` joined to
`projection_thread_messages`, with `projection_projects` supplying the workspace
root and `projection_thread_sessions` the backing provider. Threads are
soft-deleted via `deleted_at` and are skipped.

**`RemoteSyncExcluded` is the load-bearing part of this change.** t3code stores
its transcripts and its credentials in the same directory: `clerk-tokens.json`,
`cloud-auth-token.json`, and a `secrets/` directory of encrypted blobs are
siblings of `state.sqlite`, and the database itself carries `auth_sessions` and
`auth_pairing_links`. No part of the root can be copied off the machine safely,
so the agent opts out of every remote sync artifact.

## Tradeoffs and limits

Change detection is per thread and uses two signals, like Shelley. The mtime
token is the latest of the thread's, its messages', and its project's
created/updated timestamps -- message `updated_at` so an in-place edit advances
it, the project stamps because `workspace_root` determines the session's cwd
and project. A digest over every parser-observed thread, project, and message
field is stored in `file_hash` and compared under `UnchangedResultMTimeAndHash`,
because t3 is event-sourced: refolding the event log after an app update
rewrites projection rows whose timestamps derive from the events and do not
move, and the accepted legacy generations lack message and project `updated_at`
entirely -- the digest is the only signal that sees either. Discovery and parse
compute both signals from the same fields in the same order, so a
fingerprint-triggered reparse is never discarded as unchanged. The digest also
gates freshness in both directions: `FingerprintHashRequiredForFreshness` keeps
a timestamp-blind rewrite (size and mtime still matching the stored row) from
being skipped pre-parse, and t3 joins Hermes in
`providerFingerprintHashEstablishesFreshness` because members inherit the
shared container's stat -- another thread's growth moves every member's size,
and the matching digest is what keeps reconciliation from reparsing the whole
archive after every write anywhere in the database. The live watcher's token
folds the digest into the timestamp's unused sub-millisecond bits, the same
way Shelley's does, so a watched session also reacts to timestamp-preserving
rewrites instead of computing the digest and discarding it.
Session activity ends at the latest of the thread's and its messages' stamps,
so a message recorded past the thread's `updated_at` -- the defensive case the
token covers -- also moves `EndedAt` rather than leaving ordering and date
windows stale. Project stamps stay out of `EndedAt`: a workspace rename
advances the change token but is not conversation activity. Tombstone passes
resolve membership for all stored threads with one query via the
batch-presence seam. The digest is computed from the rows the parser
reads anyway; hashing the multi-megabyte `state.sqlite` file itself on every
fingerprint would add nothing on top of it, so `CompositeFingerprint` stays
declared unsupported rather than declared and not delivered.

A database event no longer fans out the whole container. The multi-session
base gains an opt-in `WithChangedContainerWatermarkListing` option: when the
caller allows watermark-merged sources and supplies stored freshness -- the
same generic `StoredMemberFreshnessPager` seam the OpenCode format consumes --
the base emits only the members whose watermark advanced, reusing the existing
paging cursor. t3 answers it with a session-row watermark listing -- one
indexed thread row plus its project row per live thread, never the messages
table -- so a no-op WAL touch emits nothing and one thread's write emits one
member. A message stamped without the thread row moving is deferred the same
way timestamp-blind rewrites are: the full meta scan catches it at scheduled
reconciliation. The persisted fingerprint embeds the session-row watermark
behind a versioned prefix (decoded on the stored side the same way the
OpenCode child digest's metadata watermark is), so the merge compares row
watermark against row watermark -- a stored file_mtime dominated by a late
message cannot mask a later thread or project update. Hashes from before the
format simply fall back to file_mtime and re-emit once. Without stored authority, or on a listing failure, the container
answer is preserved unchanged, and no other agent's behavior moves unless it
opts in. Like the OpenCode watermark listing, the merge cannot see a
timestamp-blind rewrite; the digest catches those during scheduled
reconciliation and full parses. Zed, Shelley, Trae, and Kiro still fan out
their containers; the new option is available to them but adopting it is their
own change.

t3code migrates its projection columns in place: `model_selection_json`
replaced a bare `model` column, and `attachments_json` and
`provider_instance_id` were added after the projections were introduced.
Optional columns are probed with `PRAGMA table_info`, so an older database
still parses with its model read from the legacy column. Required columns are
validated and a database without them fails closed.

Content coverage is deliberately narrow. Thinking, tool calls, tool results,
and per-message token usage are not projected into the message table; they live
in `projection_thread_activities` and the event log. Attachments render as
`[Image: name]` placeholder lines -- the shape the Codebuff and Claude-web
parsers use -- appended after any text the message carries, so an image-only
turn is not blank and a text-plus-image turn does not silently lose the
attachment. The capability declaration
says so rather than silently returning empty. t3code delegates execution to
another agent, so usage stays in that provider's own transcripts, which
agentsview already indexes separately.

`zedDBCompositeMtime` and `shelleyDBCompositeMtime` were byte-identical. They
are replaced by one `sqliteContainerCompositeMtime` rather than adding a third
copy for t3.

## Where to look

`internal/parser/t3.go` holds the reader and the schema probe;
`internal/parser/t3_provider.go` is the options wiring onto the multi-session
container base. The `internal/sync/engine.go` touchpoints follow the Shelley,
Zed, and Hermes patterns: deleted-container recognition, container composite
mtime, skip-cache exemption, the hash-establishes-freshness listing, and the
watcher's per-member source mtime, which routes to the digest-bearing token
before the generic provider-fingerprint path because t3 is not file-based.
`docs/internal/session-format-sources.md` records the format with pinned
upstream evidence.

title: fix(parser): recover Antigravity CLI cwd
body:
Populate Antigravity CLI session CWD from the current `cache/last_conversations.json` workspace mapping, with `history.jsonl` retained for older installations and untagged-session fallback. Exact conversation matches are preferred; missing, relative, or ambiguous workspace values leave CWD empty.

The absolute workspace remains the CWD for local sources. Project labels preserve recognized anchored worktree layouts for standalone or missing branch repositories, while linked-worktree metadata explicitly tied to the recorded path can supply the canonical repository identity. Remote and foreign-machine sources retain workspace-derived project grouping but are marked remote, so archive reconciliation clears their CWD instead of treating another machine's path as local. Their project labels stay lexical instead of probing recorded paths on the importing host. Workspace mappings participate in discovery and fingerprints, and the archive data version advances so existing sessions are reparsed non-destructively.

The cache path participates in the watch plan and changed-path routing, and its modification time contributes to effective source freshness so cache-only workspace updates remain eligible during incremental sync when file watching is unavailable.

title: feat(rawsync): add raw upload transport client and checkpoint state
body:
## Summary

Adds the laptop-side half of the hosted raw-ingest transport, as one feature
commit on top of the merged server surface (#1459, #1473, #1488).

`internal/rawclient` is the HTTP client for the authenticated raw-sync
surface:

- scoped-token exchange with TTL-aware caching and single-flight refresh,
  plus one forced re-exchange retry on unauthorized responses;
- missing-object negotiation (`POST /objects/missing`);
- resumable chunked uploads (`POST`/`PATCH` on `/uploads`) with
  authoritative offset recovery on `upload_offset_conflict`, terminal
  `checksum_mismatch`, and a final empty PATCH when a resumed session
  already sits at the full offset but was not finalized (server crash
  window between append commit and finalization);
- manifest-last commit returning the durable receipt, with typed
  `head_conflict` surfacing the current receipt and generation.

`internal/rawcheckpoint` is the small dedicated local SQLite database for
transport state: one-row device identity and per-source head
receipts/generations keyed by `(provider, configured_root_id, source_key)`,
using the same dual mattn/modernc driver split as `internal/vector`. Head
advancement refuses anything without a durable receipt, so the checkpoint
can only trail server acknowledgment. The device credential is injected
through `Config` and never persisted or logged.

Tenant identity is never sent by the client; it stays derived from the
authenticated server context (spec invariants 3 and 4).

Proof comes from three layers: wire-contract unit tests against scripted
handlers, a full-cycle end-to-end test against the real huma server stack
with real rawsync services and in-memory stores, and a `pgtest` end-to-end
against the durable PostgreSQL stores that also covers interrupted-upload
resume (durable offset row plus spool prefix observed before and after a
fresh client re-uploads) and the stale-parent head conflict.

Known limits, deliberately deferred to the capture-agent slice: negotiation
calls are unbatched against the server's 1 MiB control-plane cap (roughly
9-10k object refs per call against the 16384-object manifest ceiling), and
there is no status scope because no server route exists yet.

Reviewers should start at `internal/rawclient/upload.go` (offset recovery
and finalization), `internal/rawclient/tokens.go` (refresh discipline), and
`internal/rawcheckpoint/store.go` (receipt-gated advancement).

title: Kiro CLI 1.0.288 sessions not discovered — transcripts moved to ~/.kiro/sessions/<workspace-hash>/sess_<id>/messages.jsonl, not ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/*.jsonl
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.41.1 (commit a902515a, built 2026-08-18T13:35:26Z)

### Install method

install.sh / install.ps1

### OS / platform

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64)

### Which agent and version

 Kiro CLI 1.0.288 (ec90738d3f0da2389adcb94a6661b5abf1fc20e8, x64)

### Which model(s)

qdev::auto — it's on reasoningModelId in assistant records; session.json.modelId is null

### What happened, and what did you expect

The kiro provider only discovers the flat legacy layout `~/.kiro/sessions/cli/<uuid>.jsonl`. Kiro CLI now writes transcripts per workspace instead:

`~/.kiro/sessions/<workspace-hash>/sess_<uuid>/messages.jsonl`

So no Kiro session has been ingested on this machine since 2026-08-13, although I use Kiro daily and today's sessions are on disk. Expected: sessions created after the layout change show up like any other agent's.

The daemon is otherwise healthy — it incrementally syncs Claude Code sessions in the same watch cycle, and no error is logged. The only hint is the discovery count, which looks plausible (`~/.agentsview/debug.log`):

```
2026/08/24 10:39:27 discovered 297 files (93 claude, 1 codex, 159 copilot, 0 gemini,
  0 cursor, 0 amp, 0 zencoder, 0 iflow, 16 vscode-copilot, 0 visualstudio-copilot,
  0 pi, 0 omp, 24 kiro, 0 zed, 0 vibe) in 93ms
```

That 24 kiro is exactly my 23 stale legacy .jsonl files plus `~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3`. The 32 current transcripts under the new layout are not in the set. Newest kiro rows in `~/.agentsview/sessions.db` confirm it:

```
kiro:e8e37560-c9c7-44fa-9412-d5ebe79ade3d  ended 2026-08-13T06:08:44Z  176 msgs
kiro:ea09aafc-0c15-4e2d-8514-a0df1492b28a  ended 2026-08-13T05:46:09Z  110 msgs
```

Two things make this harder to work around than it looks:

- `~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3` is already known to the binary (kiroDBPathForEvent, kiroDBUnderRoot), but on 1.0.288 both conversations and conversations_v2 are empty (0 rows). Transcripts are filesystem-only.
- `~/.kiro/sessions/cli/ still gets a sess_<uuid>.history` file per session — prompt-input history, no transcript — so the legacy directory keeps a fresh mtime while holding nothing ingestible.
- There's no KIRO_SESSIONS_DIR equivalent to CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR / TRAEX_SESSIONS_DIR / VSCODE_COPILOT_DIR, so there's no user-side override either.

Suggested fix, alongside kiroLegacyPathUnderRoot: also walk `~/.kiro/sessions/*/sess_*/messages.jsonl`; dispatch the parser on record shape ({kind,version,data} → legacy, {id,timestamp,payload} → new); take the session id from the sess_<uuid> directory name and title/timestamps/project from the sibling session.json (workspacePaths[0] is more reliable than reversing the workspace hash); skip `sessions/cli/sess_*.history`. Legacy sessions keep parsing unchanged, so this can be purely additive. A KIRO_SESSIONS_DIR override would be a bonus.

The kiro provider only discovers the flat legacy layout `~/.kiro/sessions/cli/<uuid>.jsonl`. Kiro CLI now writes transcripts per workspace instead:

`~/.kiro/sessions/<workspace-hash>/sess_<uuid>/messages.jsonl`

So no Kiro session has been ingested on this machine since 2026-08-13, although I use Kiro daily and today's sessions are on disk. Expected: sessions created after the layout change show up like any other agent's.

  The daemon is otherwise healthy — it incrementally syncs Claude Code sessions in the same watch cycle, and no error is logged. The only hint is the discovery count, which looks plausible (~/.agentsview/debug.log):

```
2026/08/24 10:39:27 discovered 297 files (93 claude, 1 codex, 159 copilot, 0 gemini,
    0 cursor, 0 amp, 0 zencoder, 0 iflow, 16 vscode-copilot, 0 visualstudio-copilot,
    0 pi, 0 omp, 24 kiro, 0 zed, 0 vibe) in 93ms
```

That 24 kiro is exactly my 23 stale legacy .jsonl files plus `~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3`. The 32 current transcripts under the new layout are not in the set. Newest kiro rows in `~/.agentsview/sessions.db` confirm it:

```
  kiro:e8e37560-c9c7-44fa-9412-d5ebe79ade3d  ended 2026-08-13T06:08:44Z  176 msgs
  kiro:ea09aafc-0c15-4e2d-8514-a0df1492b28a  ended 2026-08-13T05:46:09Z  110 msgs
``` 
Two things make this harder to work around than it looks:

  - `~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3` is already known to the binary (kiroDBPathForEvent, kiroDBUnderRoot), but on 1.0.288 both conversations and conversations_v2 are empty (0 rows). Transcripts are filesystem-only.
  - `~/.kiro/sessions/cli/ still gets a sess_<uuid>.history` file per session — prompt-input history, no transcript — so the legacy directory keeps a fresh mtime while holding nothing ingestible.
 - KIRO_SESSIONS_DIR / kiro_dirs exist, but can't express the new layout: legacy discovery only matches .jsonl files directly in the root, so pointing either at ~/.kiro/sessions still finds nothing two levels down.

Suggested fix, alongside kiroLegacyPathUnderRoot: also walk `~/.kiro/sessions/*/sess_*/messages.jsonl`; dispatch the parser on record shape ({kind,version,data} → legacy, {id,timestamp,payload} → new); take the session id from the `sess_<uuid>` directory name and title/timestamps/project from the sibling session.json (workspacePaths[0] is more reliable than reversing the workspace hash); skip `sessions/cli/sess_*.history`. Legacy sessions keep parsing unchanged, so this can be purely additive. A KIRO_SESSIONS_DIR override would be a bonus.

title: fix(activity): keep overlay selector inside chart card
body: On WebKit, the Activity concurrency chart's overlay selector could extend beyond the right edge because the Typeahead flex basis was not included in the overlay group's intrinsic width. Give the selector an explicit 96px width while retaining its fixed flex basis, and cover the card boundary with a Playwright regression that runs in Chromium and WebKit.

title: feat(api): opt in to session source paths
body:
Session-list consumers that validate transcript lineage cannot recover source paths consistently across storage backends. This adds an opt-in `include_source=true` query parameter and carries it through direct and HTTP service backends so SQLite, DuckDB, and PostgreSQL return `file_path` only when requested.

Default list responses stay path-free on every backend. The option changes only list projections; pagination, filtering, and stored session data are unchanged.

title: test(ci): stabilize retry timing coverage
body:
PR #1500 exposed two independent CI timing flakes. The watcher integration no longer processes 257 deferred sources to cover a count boundary already pinned directly; it uses the one-source byte-overflow case to exercise the same retry and backoff path.

The capture retry test now keeps the production-default 15-second finalization window instead of an artificial five-second deadline, so slower Windows ingestion can complete without weakening the failure-preservation assertions.

title: fix(frontend): route arrows by focused or clicked pane (#1481)
body:
Plain ArrowUp and ArrowDown now follow the sessions list after keyboard focus
or a deliberate click there. Clicking the message pane routes them back to
message navigation. Passive pointer movement no longer changes the target.

Session arrows follow the sidebar's rendered order, including grouping,
collapsed sections and lineages, expanded children, and starred filtering.
Inputs, dialogs, disconnected lists, and existing bracket shortcuts keep their
previous behavior.

Closes #1481

title: feat(cli): query retained soft-deleted sessions (#1471)
body:
Agentsview's CLI list and content-search commands now accept an explicit
`--include-deleted` option for retained soft-deleted sessions. The option works
through direct and daemon-backed requests and includes both root and child
sessions.

Semantic and hybrid search reuse compatible vectors created before a session
was soft-deleted. Vector builds filter already-deleted transcripts before any
encoding call, so deletion never causes a new embedding request. If a
compatible vector does not already exist, semantic and hybrid search omit that
deleted session even when `--include-deleted` is set.

Default queries still hide soft-deleted sessions. Permanently excluded sessions
remain hidden, hard deletion still removes vectors, and unrelated sidebar,
usage, analytics, and synchronization paths keep their existing policy.

This change adds no table, corpus version, vector recreation, or migration.

Closes #1471

title: fix(sync): keep sessions browsable when sources disappear (#1471)
body:
Missing source files no longer hide or remove archived sessions. The session,
messages, and usage remain available. Sync records source absence separately and
reparses the source if it returns.

PR #1154 represented a missing source by setting `deleted_at` with
`deletion_cause = 'source_missing'`. Sync could distinguish that state from user
deletion, but ordinary reads only check `deleted_at`. They therefore hid intact
history when a source file disappeared.

The first version of this PR added `preserve_missing_sources` to avoid writing
that state. That was the inverse of the behavior we need: it kept sessions
visible by preventing sync from remembering that their source was gone.

The corrected model keeps the two facts independent:

- `deleted_at` records direct user intent. It controls trash, restore, and
  permanent removal.
- `source_missing_at` records local source availability. It disables freshness
  and incremental shortcuts until a successful reparse clears it.

A remaining provider path still treated a missing one-file-per-session source
as a parser exclusion and hard-deleted the archived row. Proven file absence now
uses `source_missing_at` there too. A present source that the parser deliberately
excludes still follows the existing parser-exclusion behavior.

The marker stays set until the returned session row, transcript, usage, and data
version have been written successfully. A failed refresh therefore keeps the
old archive visible and eligible for a later retry. This preserves the existing
eventual-consistency contract.

Existing SQLite rows with `deletion_cause = 'source_missing'` are migrated out
of `deleted_at`, making them visible again. PostgreSQL rows written with the old
state are repaired. The new source-availability marker stays SQLite-local
because it describes the filesystem seen by the local sync process.

The config setting is removed because preserving archived data is unconditional.

Windows SQLite test jobs now retain structured Go test events on failure and
show active, slowest, and last completed tests in the job summary. This does not
raise the timeout; it makes future overruns diagnosable. Fork pull requests run
the workflow pinned to `main`, so these diagnostics start applying after merge.

Refs #1471

title: fix(parser): support current Kiro CLI session layout
body:
Kiro CLI workspace sessions stored outside the legacy cli directory are now recognized, including direct and one-workspace sess_<id>/messages.jsonl layouts. The provider parses the documented fields and preserves literal producer identity across lookup, watcher, SQLite, and reconciliation paths.

SQLite outranks current JSONL, current JSONL outranks legacy JSONL, and configured root order breaks same-class ties before recency and canonical path. The same winner drives normal discovery, changed-path handling, scoped sync, persistence, lookup, and reconciliation. Missing sidecar bounds use parsed message timestamps before transcript mtime. History, snapshot, traversal, invalid-ID, and symlink escapes remain rejected; incomplete SQLite reads fail closed without replacing archived authority, while clean empty databases remain authoritative. Existing archive preservation and row-removal behavior remain unchanged.

Closes #1499.

title: fix(remotesync): curate editor remote targets
body:
Remote sync currently recurses through broad Cursor, VS Code Copilot, and Zed roots, copying unrelated editor data into persistent mirrors. This bounds those providers to parser-required Cursor transcripts, VS Code chat sessions plus workspace metadata, and standalone Zed `threads.db` snapshots through the existing `TargetSet.Files`, manifest, delta, mirror, and import paths.

Empty Cursor and VS Code roots remain explicitly file-scoped when no sessions are discovered, so credential, settings, cache, and extension files cannot fall back to recursive export. When the last VS Code chat disappears, its workspace metadata is omitted with the stale chat and the persistent mirror evicts both entries.

Zed exports use SQLite online backup so committed WAL data becomes one consistent database without transferring WAL or SHM sidecars. Authenticated target selection preserves root and symlink confinement, unchanged mirrors produce no repeat fetch, and deletion races evict stale files without widening the selected set.

Closes #1492.

title: SKILL.md's search recipe cannot find identifiers: --fts excludes tool_input, and prescribes it exactly for identifier hunts
body:
The generated `agentsview-finding-history` SKILL.md teaches a search recipe that silently cannot find the thing agents most often look for: **who did this, and when**. Identifiers — issue/bead ids, file paths, commands, error strings — live in tool calls, and the recipe the skill teaches excludes tool calls.

Observed on `agentsview v0.40.1 (commit 9ef48912)`; `v0.41.1` release notes touch nothing in this area.

## 1. `--fts` and `--in` are mutually exclusive, and SKILL.md never says so

```
$ agentsview session search "<id>" --fts --in tool_input
fatal: --fts searches messages only; drop --in or --fts
```

This is client-side argument validation, so it applies to every install, local or `--server`.

SKILL.md's Core Workflow says to use `--hybrid` for concept questions and **`--fts` for "exact identifiers (paths, error strings, tool names)"** — precisely the case where `--fts` is the wrong mode, because those strings are usually in `tool_input`/`tool_result`, which `--fts` cannot reach. Plain search (neither `--fts` nor `--hybrid`) does reach them and is never mentioned as a mode at all.

The Rationalization Table reinforces it: *"Tool output matches are just as good." → "Start in messages for concepts"*. For an identifier hunt that advice inverts the correct order.

### Measured

Hunting the session that created a tracker id, same daemon, same query:

| Mode | Hits in the session that actually created it |
| --- | --- |
| `--fts` (what SKILL.md prescribes) | **0** — only the *currently running* session's chatter came back |
| plain + `--in tool_input` | **19** (plus 3 in a sibling session) |

The causer session is invisible on the prescribed path. Nothing errors; you get a smaller answer that reads like a finding. That is the part worth fixing — a wrong mode here does not fail loudly.

**Suggested fix:** give SKILL.md an explicit mode table, e.g.

| Hunting | Mode |
| --- | --- |
| prose, reasoning, "why did we…" | `--fts` (messages only) |
| identifiers: ids, paths, commands, error strings | plain search + `--in tool_input,tool_result` |

and drop `--fts` from the "exact identifiers" line in Core Workflow.

## 2. No way to exclude the running session

The archive ingests the live session, so for anything the current conversation just discussed, its own echoes are the freshest matches and outrank real history. With the skill's suggested `--limit 8` they can fill the page.

SKILL.md already tells the agent to *"down-rank active-session echoes"*, but there is no mechanism: `session search` has no `--exclude-session`. The workaround is `--limit 60` plus filtering the session id in post-processing, which the skill does not mention.

**Request:** `--exclude-session <id>` (repeatable), or `--exclude-current-session`.

## 3. Remote-daemon installs: every generated example is wrong

Where the archive is a shared remote daemon, every SKILL.md example is missing `--server` / `--server-token-file` and therefore silently queries the local SQLite index instead — under-reporting without any signal. There is no way to make the configured server the default, so the only fix is a hand-maintained sidecar file that says "override every example above", plus a post-`skills install` hook to inject a pointer to it. That works, but it means `skills install --force` regenerates guidance that is wrong for the deployment on every upgrade.

**Request:** let `skills install` bake a configured server (or `AGENTSVIEW_SERVER` / a config key) into the generated examples, or emit them server-agnostic.

---

Happy to send a PR for (1) if you point me at where the skill text is generated. (2) and (3) are your call on shape.

### [`v1.12.1`](https://redirect.github.com/stretchr/testify/releases/tag/v1.12.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/stretchr/testify/compare/v1.12.0...v1.12.1)

This is the first release which has the minimum dependencies practical in testify v1. The last remaining dependencies are github.com/stretchr/objx which itself has no dependencies, and go.yaml.in/yaml/v3. Removing objx would require v2, it cannot be vendored. Removing YAML would require vendoring the yaml library, which would do more harm than good. It's better to become aware of vulnerabilities in the official yaml package than to attempt to maintain our own.

title: feat(data): add a project-first mapping workspace
body:
Adds an opt-in, project-first Data workspace for correcting project classification. The existing rules view remains the default when `VITE_PROJECT_MAPPING_WORKSPACE` is unset.

Shift-click selects projects for bulk correction. The destination picker and Save stay above an independently scrolling folder list. Suggestions come from observed working directories, collapsing known worktree layouts and immediate shared parents. They remain grouped by project, then machine, with larger groups first within each machine.

An optional date picker narrows project counts, folder suggestions, and paged session previews. Automated previews are hidden by default. Folder rules still match across all dates; bulk previews count each session once and require confirmation when rules reach unselected projects. Save shows progress as individual corrections complete.

Individual sessions can be reassigned from previews or the Sessions list. Overrides survive resync and take precedence until cleared. Read-only mirrors remain inspection-only; writes belong to the Source Agents View.

Review candidate selection in `internal/db/worktree_candidates.go`, the Data workspace components, and override persistence in `internal/db/session_project_assignments.go`. Chunked saves, retry improvements, and correction history/Undo remain follow-up work.

title: feat(pricing): resolve historical rates by usage time
body:
Timestamped usage now resolves the price that was active when the usage event
occurred. Previously, every estimate used the current flat LiteLLM/OpenRouter
catalog, so provider price changes could reprice older sessions.

Agentsview now applies exact reported-model custom pricing first, canonical
custom pricing second, Pydantic GenAI Prices v2 at the raw event timestamp
third, and the existing flat catalog as the fallback. Effective timestamps
remain responsible for filtering, ordering, display, and deduplication. Records
without a raw timestamp skip historical selection and use the flat fallback
instead of borrowing the session start date. Cache-economics estimates follow
the same timestamp and precedence rules.

The parser covers upstream provider and model matching, ordered start-date and
UTC time-window conditions, token rates, and whole-request tiers. The complete
versioned upstream JSON remains intact in a singleton pricing document, with an
embedded snapshot for offline use and refresh support ahead of LiteLLM. SQLite
owns the document, and PostgreSQL and DuckDB mirror it alongside the existing
flat rows. Pydantic currently supplies both GPT-5.6 Luna price periods. Models
it does not contain, including Grok 4.6, continue through LiteLLM.

The highest-risk review areas are the schema-compatible parser in
`internal/pricing/catalog/genai.go`, precedence and provenance in
`internal/export/pricing.go`, and the raw pricing timestamp flow through the
SQLite, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, and usage-cache paths.

Closes #1453

### [`v1.62.1`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/compare/v1.62.0...26a9e470a7b3c7822084b09fb7f13902c5f37b51)

### [`v1.62.0`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.62.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/compare/v1.61.1...v1.62.0)

##### 🧱 New component testing model

[Component testing](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-components) moves to a **stories and galleries** model.
A **story** wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a

**gallery** page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new [fixtures.mount()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-fixtures#fixtures-mount) fixture navigates
to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a [Locator](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator) scoped to the story's root element:

```js
test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});
```

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use `update(props)` /
`unmount()` on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

##### 🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a `signal` option that takes an
[`AbortSignal`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal), letting you
cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

```js
const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });
await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });
```

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass `timeout: 0` to disable it.

##### 🖼️ WebP screenshots

[expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-pageassertions#page-assertions-to-have-screenshot-1) and [expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-have-screenshot-1)
can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a `.webp` name:

```js
// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.
await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });
```

[page.screenshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-screenshot) and [locator.screenshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot) also accept `webp` as a `type`,
where quality `100` (the default) is lossless and lower values use lossy compression.

##### 🧩 Custom test filtering with Reporter.preprocess()

New [reporter.preprocess()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-reporter#reporter-preprocess) hook runs after the configuration is resolved and before
[reporter.onBegin()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-reporter#reporter-on-begin), letting a reporter mark individual tests as skipped, excluded,
fixed, or failing through a [TestRun](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testrun) object:

```js
class MyReporter {
  async preprocess({ config, suite, testRun }) {
    for (const test of suite.allTests()) {
      if (shouldSkip(test))
        testRun.skip(test);
    }
  }
}
```

##### 🔁 Isolated retries

New [testConfig.retryStrategy](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-retry-strategy) controls when failed tests are retried. The default
`'immediate'` retries as soon as a worker is free; `'isolated'` runs all retries at the end,
one by one in a single worker, to minimize interference with the rest of the suite:

```js
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  retries: 2,
  retryStrategy: 'isolated',
});
```

##### New APIs

##### Browser and Context

- New option [`credentials`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-storage-state-option-credentials) includes the context's virtual WebAuthn [Credentials](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-credentials) (passkeys) in the storage state, so they can be persisted and re-seeded into later contexts.

##### Actions

- New `scroll` option (`"auto"` | `"none"`) on actions to opt out of Playwright's automatic scroll-into-view.

##### Network

- New [apiResponse.timing()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apiresponse#api-response-timing) returns resource timing information for an API response.

##### Evaluation

- New [locator.waitForFunction()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-wait-for-function) waits until a function — called with the matching element — returns a truthy value.
- [page.evaluate()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-evaluate) and related methods now accept functions as evaluate arguments.
- [page.addInitScript()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-add-init-script) / [browserContext.addInitScript()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-add-init-script) now accept functions as init-script arguments.

##### Command line & MCP

- Playwright now bundles the [Playwright MCP](https://playwright.dev/docs/getting-started-mcp) server and [`playwright-cli`](https://playwright.dev/docs/getting-started-cli), runnable via `npx playwright mcp` and `npx playwright cli`.

##### Reporters

- The HTML report's **Merge files** grouping — previously only a UI toggle — can now be enabled from the config with the new `mergeFiles` reporter option:

```js
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [['html', { mergeFiles: true }]],
});
```

##### Announcements

- ⚠️ Debian 11 is not supported anymore.

- Chromium 151.0.7922.34
- Mozilla Firefox 153.0
- WebKit 26.5

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:

- Google Chrome 151
- Microsoft Edge 151

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/TanStack/virtual/compare/@tanstack/virtual-core@3.17.6...@tanstack/virtual-core@3.17.7)

##### Patch Changes

- [#​1239](https://redirect.github.com/TanStack/virtual/pull/1239) [`a5417b4`](https://redirect.github.com/TanStack/virtual/commit/a5417b4b0d3c82876747bb9635db7239c28d3e44) - Fix a one-frame viewport jump when above-viewport rows resize while scrolling up ([#​1227](https://redirect.github.com/TanStack/virtual/issues/1227)). `resizeItem` writes `scrollTop` synchronously inside the ResizeObserver callback to compensate for the size change, but then notified asynchronously — so the browser could paint a frame with the new `scrollTop` and the old item transforms, making the content jerk by the resize delta and snap back. When a compensation actually moves the scroll position, `resizeItem` now notifies synchronously so the transform commit lands in the same paint as the scroll write. Resizes that don't move the scroll position (below-fold measurements, iOS-deferred adjustments) keep the cheaper async notify.

title: Gemini message-only JSONL files can block watch-root reconciliation
body:
## Problem

Gemini CLI can leave a `.jsonl` session file containing message records but no metadata record with `sessionId`. The parser currently returns a hard `missing sessionId` error for that durable source shape.

During watch-root reconciliation, the hard error marks the provider pass incomplete. The same page is then retried indefinitely, healthy sibling sessions are delayed, and a daemon can spend sustained CPU and I/O reprocessing the poisoned source.

## Expected behavior

A Gemini session-shaped file without a stable session identity should be treated as an unsupported source, not a fatal provider failure. Reconciliation should continue while preserving any archived session previously associated with that path.

Other Gemini parse failures should remain fatal.

## Proposed coverage

- Message-only multi-record JSONL is skipped as an unsupported source.
- A single message record in a `.jsonl` file without a trailing newline follows the same JSONL path and is skipped.
- Reconciliation processes a healthy sibling when another Gemini file loses its metadata record.
- A previously archived session for the incomplete path is preserved rather than retired.

title: fix(parser): skip Gemini sessions without metadata
body:
## Summary

- classify Gemini files with no `sessionId` as unsupported sources instead of fatal parser failures
- recognize `.jsonl` by extension even when a message-only file contains one record and no trailing newline
- let watch-root reconciliation continue through healthy siblings while preserving any archived session for the incomplete path

Closes #1518.

## Test plan

- `go test -tags fts5 ./internal/parser -run 'TestGeminiProviderMissingSessionIDIsUnsupportedSource|TestParseGeminiSession_EdgeCases' -count=1`
- `go test -tags fts5 ./internal/sync -run TestReconcileGeminiMissingSessionIDDoesNotBlockHealthySources -count=1`
- `go test -tags fts5 ./internal/parser ./internal/sync -count=1`
- `go vet -tags fts5 ./...`
- `go test -short -tags fts5 ./...` passes for every package except the existing environment-sensitive `TestRunDaemonArtifactExchangeConnectsToIPv6LocalhostListener` failure on nv1
- `go test -short -tags fts5 ./cmd/agentsview -skip '^TestRunDaemonArtifactExchangeConnectsToIPv6LocalhostListener$' -count=1`

title: fix(pricing): price Claude 1h cache writes at the 1h rate
body:
Claude Code transcripts split cache writes by TTL in the nested message.usage.cache_creation object, but pricing read only the flat counter and billed every write at the 5-minute rate. Anthropic bills 1h writes at 2x input, so sessions using 1h prompt caching under-reported cost: issue https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/1452 's sample session prices at $0.157539 where Claude Code's own total_cost_usd reports $0.225533.

Fact extraction now carries the 1h subset (clamped to the authoritative flat counter), the LiteLLM parser reads cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr into a new rate stored on all three backends and available as a custom-pricing key, and cost and savings bill each TTL portion at its own rate. A model without a published 1h rate, a row without the nested breakdown, and every non-Claude source price exactly as before. SQLite prices through facts including the timezone-exception tier, PostgreSQL extracts the nested path at query time, and DuckDB normalizes it in SQL; the pgtest parity fixture pins the corrected total across backends.

The usage cache format and DuckDB mirror schema bump, so both disposable stores rebuild once after upgrade. The wire provenance gains cache_write_1h_cost_per_mtok additively, and the pricing digest emits the rate only when set so unchanged content keeps its digest. The embedded fallback snapshot predates the field; the generator now emits it, and republishing the pinned artifact is a follow-up release step needing maintainer access to the snapshot branch, following #1305's flow. Reviewers should start at CostForTokensScoped in internal/export/pricing.go, then priceUsageFact and the exception-tier columns in internal/db.

cf. #1305, which introduced the band-companion parsing that this extends and deliberately deferred the 1h field, and #1454 for the usage-cache generation contract the format bump follows.

Fixes #1452.

title: OpenCode sessions are invisible unless the install channel is latest, beta, or prod
body:
### Agent name and link

OpenCode — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode

Already supported; this is about sessions the existing provider cannot see.

### Where does it store sessions?

`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-<channel>.db`, where `<channel>` is the installation channel. Released builds (`latest`, `beta`, `prod`) use `opencode.db`, which agentsview reads; any other build, including one from source, uses a channel-suffixed filename such as `opencode-local.db`, which it does not.

### File format

SQLite, same schema family as the `opencode.db` the provider already parses. The problem is the filename, not the format.

---

## Summary

The `opencode` provider reads only `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. OpenCode names its database after the **installation channel**, so anyone not running a released build writes to `opencode-<channel>.db` instead — for a build from source, `opencode-local.db`. agentsview never opens those files, so every session is missing with no error or warning.

This is not a store migration and not an undocumented format. The naming rule is explicit in OpenCode's source.

## The rule, from OpenCode's source

`packages/core/src/database/database.ts`:

```ts
export function path() {
  if (Flag.OPENCODE_DB) {
    if (Flag.OPENCODE_DB === ":memory:" || isAbsolute(Flag.OPENCODE_DB)) return Flag.OPENCODE_DB
    return join(Global.Path.data, Flag.OPENCODE_DB)
  }
  if (
    ["latest", "beta", "prod"].includes(InstallationChannel) ||
    process.env.OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB === "1" ||
    process.env.OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB === "true"
  )
    return join(Global.Path.data, "opencode.db")
  return join(Global.Path.data, `opencode-${InstallationChannel.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, "-")}.db`)
}
```

`packages/core/src/installation/version.ts`:

```ts
export const InstallationChannel = typeof OPENCODE_CHANNEL === "string" ? OPENCODE_CHANNEL : "local"
```

`OPENCODE_CHANNEL` is injected at build time by the release pipeline, so a build from source leaves it undefined and the channel falls back to `"local"`.

So the set of possible database filenames is:

- `opencode.db` — channels `latest`, `beta`, `prod`, or `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB=1`
- `opencode-local.db` — any build from source
- `opencode-<channel>.db` — any other channel, sanitised to `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]`
- an arbitrary path or filename — when `OPENCODE_DB` is set

agentsview currently handles only the first. The filename is hard-coded at `internal/parser/discovery.go:109` (`dbName: "opencode.db"`), and `internal/` contains no reference to a channel suffix.

## Effect

On this machine, after switching to a source build:

| | `opencode.db` | `opencode-local.db` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sessions | 576 | 111 |
| Newest session | 2026-03-08 | 2026-04-22 |
| Tables | 10 | 14 |

```
sqlite> SELECT MAX(started_at) FROM sessions WHERE agent='opencode';
2026-03-08T18:22:27.847Z
```

That ceiling is exactly where `opencode.db` stopped being written. The 111 sessions since — real work, with ordinary titles — are absent from the archive. Session IDs are near-disjoint (2 of 111 shared), and the newer database carries additional tables (`account`, `account_state`, `event`, `event_sequence`), so the two cannot be treated as copies of one another.

`agentsview doctor sync` reports the root as `(ok, ...)`, because the directory and `opencode.db` both genuinely exist. Nothing signals that a live database beside them is being skipped.

## Suggested handling

The discovery rule is mechanical, so it can mirror the upstream logic:

- Glob `opencode*.db` in the data directory rather than hard-coding one name.
- Treat each matching database as a source in its own right. A user who has
  switched channels will legitimately have several, each holding a distinct
  slice of history, and dropping the older ones loses sessions.
- De-duplicate by session ID where databases overlap, since a channel switch
  can copy or share some rows.
- Optionally honour `OPENCODE_DB`, which can point anywhere, including outside
  the data directory.

A narrower fix — adding `opencode-local.db` alone — would cover builds from source but still miss `opencode-beta.db` and any custom channel.

## Workaround

Setting `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB=1` makes a non-release build write to `opencode.db`, which agentsview already reads. That is useful to know, but it requires knowing the mechanism exists, and it does not recover sessions already written to a channel database.

## Environment

- agentsview `5b03a2b4` (v0.41.1-41-g5b03a2b4), built from source 2026-08-25
- Linux
- OpenCode data directory `~/.local/share/opencode/`

Also reproduced on the released v0.40.1. Re-checked after a full resync on the newer build: `MAX(started_at)` is unchanged, so this is not a stale-archive artefact.

## Related

An earlier OpenCode storage change is handled correctly and is **not** what this report is about: v1.2.0 (2026-02-14) migrated flat JSON files to a single SQLite database, and agentsview reads that result.

[`ctx`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx), an unrelated session-search tool, has the same gap: at `8c6d670` (2026-08-25) it documents `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` as its source and the string `opencode-local` appears nowhere in its repository.

Note also that OpenCode's canonical repository appears to have moved from `sst/opencode` to `anomalyco/opencode`, which may be worth reflecting in the provider's documentation independently of this issue.

I am happy to supply schema dumps or row counts from either database, and to test a fix against a machine that has both.

title: chore(release): remove repository release automation
body:

CLI, PyPI, desktop, and container publication workflows; the changelog and
tagging scripts; the desktop updater health checks; and the obsolete release
setup guide.

Reusable build capabilities remain in place, including the PyPI wheel builder
and its tests, the Dockerfile and runtime inputs, local release build targets,

title: ci(desktop): run the full desktop unit suite in the Windows lane
body:
The Desktop Unit Tests (Windows) lane was added in #488 to cover the Windows update stop/install ordering, and its cargo test invocation filtered to `install_downloaded_update`. That filter means the rest of the desktop crate's unit tests run nowhere in CI: this is the only lane that executes desktop Rust tests, and the macOS desktop workflows only build artifacts.

This drops the filter so the lane runs the whole `--lib` suite. The full test module already compiles in this lane today (cargo's test filtering happens at runtime), so the added cost is only test execution, which is sub-second. Platform-gated tests are behind `#[cfg(unix)]` and the remaining tests use tempdirs and missing-binary spawns that behave the same on Windows.

Reviewers: the only change is the test step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (name + dropped filter).

title: Open desktop sessions through agentsview:// deep links
body:
### Problem / motivation
External tools can resolve session IDs but cannot open them directly in the desktop app. Browser URLs require a known server port, and links to sessions that have not synced yet render a blank message pane.

### Proposed solution
Register `agentsview://sessions/<session-id>` for the desktop app, support an optional `?msg=<ordinal|last>` anchor, and handle links both at launch and while the app is running. Defer navigation until the backend is ready, focus the existing window for later links, and show a retryable not-found state that recovers when the session appears.

### Alternatives considered
Continue opening `http://<host>:<port>/sessions/<session-id>` in a browser. This remains a useful fallback when the desktop scheme is unavailable, but callers must discover the active server address and cannot target the desktop app directly.

title: feat(desktop): open sessions through agentsview deep links
body:
Registers the `agentsview://` scheme so external tools can open `agentsview://sessions/<session-id>` in the desktop app, optionally forwarding `?msg=<ordinal|last>` to the frontend message anchor. Unsupported paths, invalid anchors, and unrelated query parameters are discarded or ignored.

Deep-link dispatch now focuses the existing window, defers launch-time links until the sidecar is ready, and re-enters the deferred state before the backend republishes its port so restart redirects cannot overwrite the requested route. A link that arrives while the startup redirect itself is navigating queues behind it and replays once it lands, so the newest link always wins. Windows and Linux use single-instance forwarding for links delivered through a second launch, and diagnostics are mirrored to `agentsview-desktop.log` for packaged builds without usable stderr, including deferred routes that are dropped or fail to navigate.

The frontend distinguishes a missing session from an empty one across every selection path: detail fetches, sidebar-row hydration, and the message loader's metadata probe all report 404s, so a session deleted behind a cached sidebar row shows a retryable not-found state instead of a blank pane. The not-found flag stays set until a fetch for the session succeeds, and recovery re-runs the per-session loaders in place rather than bouncing the selection, so retries and late-arriving sessions keep the URL, history, and `?msg=` anchor intact. Stale hydration responses are guarded by the sidebar's version and epoch checks, stale message-load failures are ignored unless they belong to the current load, and other request failures are displayed as before.

The scheme is available only with the desktop app. macOS development builds do not receive scheme events because registration comes from the bundled app, unsupported links are logged without an in-app error, and Linux single-instance forwarding depends on a session D-Bus. Review the `DeepLinkDispatch` transitions and URL validation in `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, plus the not-found and retry flow in the sessions store and message list.

The branch also carries a small CI repair: the usage guide's Session API link now points at the docs path, and the Codex capture integration test no longer overrides the finalization wait, which had made it time out.

Closes #1524

title: fix(skills): document tool-source search for identifier hunts
body:
## Summary
- SKILL.md's finding-history template told agents to use `--fts` for exact-identifier searches, but FTS only indexes message content — identifiers that only appear inside `tool_input`/`tool_result` (a command, an argument value) never match.
- Corrects the documented recipe to plain substring search with `--in tool_input,tool_result` for that case, and rewrites the surrounding "myth" table entry to state the FTS/tool-source distinction directly instead of the vaguer previous wording.

## Root cause
`agentsview session search "<exact string>" --fts` builds an FTS5 query against the messages table only. An identifier embedded solely in a tool call's `InputJSON` (e.g. a shell command argument) is never indexed there, so the documented recipe silently returns zero matches for exactly the case it says to use it for.

## Scope
Doc/template + regression tests only — no change to search behavior itself. Doesn't touch the FTS index, the `--in` flag's existing implementation, or any other skill template.

## Testing
- `go test ./cmd/agentsview/... -run TestSessionSearchDocumentedIdentifierRecipeFindsToolInput -v` — PASS (new: seeds a session whose only occurrence of an identifier is inside a tool call's `InputJSON`, confirms the corrected recipe finds it)
- `go test ./internal/skills/... -run TestRenderDocumentsToolSourceIdentifierSearch -v` — PASS (new: asserts the rendered template contains the corrected command and explanation)

title: fix(parser): group Antigravity CLI sessions across git worktrees
body:
Antigravity CLI sessions from different git worktrees of the same repo now group under one project in the Sessions sidebar, matching how Codex and Claude sessions already behave. Previously the raw workspace filesystem path from `history.jsonl` was stored as `ParsedSession.Project` with no normalization, so each worktree showed up as its own project group (#1484).

The fix threads `context.Context` through `parseSessionWithStatus` and routes the workspace path through the shared `ExtractProjectFromCwdWithBranchContext` normalizer, which resolves a worktree path back to its parent repository name. Because of this, stored Antigravity project names change shape: raw paths like `/home/user/my-cli-project` become `my_cli_project`. The parser data version is bumped to 92 so archives written before the change reparse: their sources are byte-identical, so nothing fingerprint-side could otherwise trigger the renormalization, and the same repo would stay split between a path-named group and the normalized one. A sync integration test pins that boundary by stamping a raw-path row with version 91 and asserting an ordinary incremental sync renormalizes it.

Remote (SSH-imported) parses keep the lexical normalization but skip local git-root discovery, gated on `Config.PathRewriter` — the same remote signal the Cursor provider uses. Without the gate, a remote workspace path that also exists on the importing host would be attributed to the importer's local repository.

The engine's `DisableFilesystemProjectDiscovery` option now holds on every entry point: previously only `SyncPaths` put the policy on the parse context, so a discovery-disabled engine running a full sync, streamed reconciliation, single-session refresh, source lookup, or parse diff would still walk the local filesystem for git roots. A `parsePolicyContext` helper is applied at each funnel, and an integration test drives a git-worktree workspace through `SyncAll` on a discovery-disabled engine to prove the stored project stays lexical.

Review focus: the normalizer call and remote gate in `internal/parser/antigravity_cli.go`, the data-version bump in `internal/db/db.go`, and the `parsePolicyContext` call sites in `internal/sync/engine.go`; the rest is context plumbing and test fixtures (history.jsonl lines are built with `json.Marshal` so Windows workspace paths with backslashes survive JSON decoding).

title: feat(parser): add Cursor IDE (GUI) session provider
body:
Cursor IDE, the GUI editor, stores chats in a VS Code-style global-state SQLite database (`state.vscdb`, table `cursorDiskKV`) rather than the `agent-transcripts` files the existing `cursor` (Cursor Agent CLI) provider reads, so GUI sessions were never discovered. This adds a distinct `cursor-ide` provider on the shared `multiSessionContainerSourceSet` framework (the same shape as Zed and Omnigent): `composerData:<uuid>` rows decode into sessions, and each session's `fullConversationHeadersOnly` array orders lookups into sibling `bubbleId:<composerId>:<bubbleUuid>` rows for message content, tool calls, and timestamps. The existing `cursor` provider is untouched.

Freshness and deletion semantics, where reviewers should look:

- Fingerprinting never hashes the full database (86MB+ observed locally, 500MB+ reported in the wild). The container fingerprint uses size, composite mtime, and a SQLite transaction-state hash over just the database and WAL headers (change counter, schema cookie, WAL size and salts), declared with `FingerprintHashInCacheKey` and `FingerprintHashRequiredForFreshness`, so a rewrite that lands on the same size and mtime still misses the skip cache. The per-composer fingerprint digests every parse input — the raw `composerData` document plus that composer's bubble rows — so an equal-length bubble rewrite, a header reorder, or a rename that leaves `lastUpdatedAt` untouched still reparses under `UnchangedResultMTimeAndHash`.
- A chat deleted inside Cursor IDE is marked source-missing and stays browsable, never hard-deleted. Stored-source hints fan a `state.vscdb` change event out into per-member tombstones using a batched single-connection membership check, and `internal/sync/engine.go` includes cursor-ide in complete-container ownership reconciliation, in the emptied-container source-missing seam, and in the whole-container skip-cache exemptions generalized from Omnigent (no stored row of its own, parser data version in the cache key, cache-after-write). Removing `state.vscdb` itself preserves every archived session.
- `state.vscdb` co-locates Cursor's live auth tokens (`ItemTable`) and per-composer sync encryption keys, so the provider is `RemoteSyncExcluded`, matching the Omnigent `chat.db` precedent.

Deletion, reconciliation, emptied-container, stale-edit, and same-size/same-mtime rewrite behavior is pinned by `internal/sync/cursor_ide_integration_test.go`; parsing and fingerprinting by `internal/parser/cursor_ide_test.go`. The `docs/internal/session-format-sources.md` entry records the schema evidence per the provenance convention.

title: fix(vector): cap embedding batches by token budget
body:
Embedding builds now accept a global model-context limit and a per-server aggregate input-token cap, then conservatively bound request width by floor(max_batch_tokens / model_context_tokens). This prevents deterministic oversized batches from being replayed forever after provider-side truncation.

The bound intentionally charges every input at the full model context instead of guessing model-specific tokenization. That can create smaller requests for short documents, but it guarantees the configured provider cap for ordinary and repair builds. Existing configurations keep document-count batching until both limits are declared.

The main review points are config validation and server wiring in internal/config and cmd/agentsview, plus the shared batch sizing in internal/vector/build.go.

title: fix(vector): cap embeddings-build batches by token budget
body:
Embedding builds now cap each provider request by both the configured batch size and a worst-case token budget. Operators can set the model's `model_context_tokens` once and a provider server's `max_batch_tokens` where needed. Agentsview passes those limits to kit v0.22.0, which derives the safe request width and rejects invalid budgets before scanning documents.

The bound treats every input as potentially filling the model context because provider truncation can make that the effective token cost. This prevents a repeatable 400 response when `batch_size * model_context_tokens` exceeds the provider's aggregate cap, at the cost of leaving some request capacity unused. Servers without `max_batch_tokens` keep the existing count-only batching behavior. Ordinary builds and invalid-vector repair share the same kit options.

Closes #1356

title: fix(vector): keep embedding builds alive through rate limits
body:
## Summary

- Document embeddings builds now retry an HTTP 429 (honoring `Retry-After` when present, capped exponential backoff otherwise) until it succeeds or the build is canceled, instead of spending the normal `max_retries` budget on it.
- Query encoders are unchanged: latency-sensitive, so a 429 still counts against `max_retries` and fails fast, same as before.
- Daemon shutdown now cancels a detached API-started build instead of waiting for it to finish. With unbounded 429 retries, waiting could block shutdown forever when a provider's quota never recovers. Build progress is durable, so a canceled build resumes incrementally on the next start; scheduler-driven builds already stopped with the daemon context, and API-started builds now behave the same way.

## Root cause

`embeddings build` treated a 429 as just another retryable error under the shared `max_retries` budget. A 429 is the one error class a provider tells you exactly how to handle (it clears with time, the request itself isn't broken) -- treating it like a permanent failure meant a large first build died partway through and needed an external retry loop wrapped around the command by hand (repro in the issue: 28,085 of 142,161 documents embedded, then a 429 aborted the whole run).

## Scope

`internal/vector/encoder.go`'s retry loop, a `RetryRateLimits` field threaded through the existing document-vs-query encoder constructors in `cmd/agentsview/embeddings.go` (only document builds enable it), and `internal/vector/manager.go`, where detached builds now run on a manager-owned cancellable context with a `Shutdown` method that `vectorServing.Close` calls before waiting. Reviewers should look at the reworked retry loop in `encode` and at the `Shutdown`/`Wait` ordering in `Manager` and `vectorServing.Close`.

**Note:** #1356's fix (separate PR, already up) touches the same `embeddings.go`/`config.go`/`docs/semantic-search.md` files for an unrelated reason (per-batch token-cap). Whichever of the two merges second will need a small conflict resolution against the other -- I hit that conflict myself while preparing this PR and reconciled it manually rather than force-resolving; happy to help resolve it again here once one lands.

title: feat(rawcapture): add durable capture outbox
body:

## Why

This delivers the durable local capture layer needed before hosted raw sync can run continuously. Provider code remains responsible for physical source membership, while generic capture and checkpoint code enforce containment, stability, capacity, and server-chain ordering.

## Usage

There is no new runtime command in this slice. The new package APIs are ready for the uploader and scheduling work in the next stacked change.

Refs #1352

Stacked on #1498.

body:
Stop the scripts CI job from invoking two desktop release health tests that are

files.

title: fix(pg): preserve legacy offset timestamps during push
body:
## Summary

`agentsview pg push` silently converts some valid legacy SQLite timestamp strings into PostgreSQL zero/NULL timestamps. A single affected root session can then make the Usage page's All-time range return HTTP 500.

## Reproduction

A preserved archive row contains timestamps in a space-separated, fractional, numeric-offset form:

```text
created_at = 2026-04-14 04:09:28.922+00
started_at = 2026-03-09 22:48:29.937+00
ended_at   = 2026-03-14 00:32:16.577+00
```

The row and its message timestamps are valid in SQLite. After a full PostgreSQL push:

- `created_at` becomes `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`
- `started_at`, `ended_at`, and message timestamps become `NULL`

`ParseSQLiteTimestamp` accepts RFC3339 and a space-separated seconds-only form, but not fractional seconds plus a numeric offset. `pushSession` also discards the parse result for required `created_at`:

```go
createdAt, _ := ParseSQLiteTimestamp(sess.CreatedAt)
```

That passes Go's zero `time.Time` to PostgreSQL. Nullable timestamp helpers silently return `NULL` on the same parse failure.

When `/api/v1/stats` reports the zero date as `earliest_session`, the frontend's All-time Usage range requests `from=0001-01-01`. PostgreSQL usage filtering pads the lower bound by 14 hours, producing a year-0 timestamp (`0000-12-31T10:00:00Z`) and a 500 (`SQLSTATE 22008`).

## Expected behavior

- PostgreSQL push accepts valid legacy/round-tripped timestamp representations, including fractional seconds with numeric offsets.
- A non-empty timestamp that cannot be parsed must not silently become year 1 or `NULL`; push should return a contextual error instead of corrupting the mirror.
- Usage date-bound handling should not turn a boundary underflow into an internal server error.

## Suggested coverage

- Unit cases for space-separated fractional timestamps with `+00`, `+00:00`, and non-UTC offsets.
- PostgreSQL push regression proving `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, and message timestamps survive the mirror.
- A usage-bound regression for `from=0001-01-01` (either safe clamping or a client error rather than HTTP 500).

title: fix(pg): preserve legacy offset timestamps
body:
Closes #1534.

Legacy and imported SQLite archives can retain valid space-separated timestamps with fractional seconds and numeric UTC offsets. PostgreSQL push previously failed to parse those values, silently mirrored nullable timestamps as `NULL`, and used Go's year-1 zero time for required `created_at` values.

The PostgreSQL timestamp parser now accepts both short and colon numeric offsets. Session, message, usage-event, and tool-result push paths reject any remaining non-empty unparseable timestamps with contextual errors before committing corrupt mirror data.

A target- and filter-scoped migration marker forces one full republish after upgrade, repairing timestamps that an earlier incremental push may already have mirrored as `NULL` or year 1. The marker is recorded only after the session push completes without errors, so interrupted or partially failed repairs retry automatically. Regression coverage exercises both the original legacy-format mirror and this upgrade repair against a real PostgreSQL database.

Usage candidate bounds now clamp timezone padding at year 1 in both SQLite and PostgreSQL, preventing an anomalous earliest-session value from underflowing into an invalid year-0 PostgreSQL timestamp. Normal date-range behavior is unchanged.

title: build: define release OCI targets with Bake
body: This adds the source-owned Docker Bake contract used by the central release pipeline. The matrix exposes independent amd64 and arm64 OCI archive targets, so the pipeline can build only a missing canonical platform artifact while AgentsView keeps its Dockerfile inputs and public image labels here.

title: feat(parser): ingest Posit Assistant usage-events sidecar
body:
**tl;dr:** Posit Assistant tracks its cache warming mechanism in `usage-events.jsonl`. This PR ingests that file so warm-cache spend is part of cost calculation. I also quickly checked again some existing PA sessions I have on disk with cache warm events.

Posit Assistant records auxiliary per-request usage that never appears in the `lm-messages.jsonl` transcript — cache-keepalive pings and classifier calls — in an append-only `usage-events.jsonl` sidecar next to each conversation (subagents carry their own). That spend was previously invisible: idle sessions receive repeated keepalive pings that never reached the usage tables.

Each sidecar line becomes a request-scoped usage event with `Source` = `"posit-assistant-" + kind`, the same model-family cache-write normalization as message usage, a `MessageOrdinal` when its anchor node resolves, and a synthesized dedup key. The sidecar is supplementary to per-message usage — events are emitted only from sidecar lines and session token totals stay message-derived — so the additive messages-plus-usage-events cost queries never double count. Posit Assistant may add new kinds (e.g. `posit-assistant-greeting`) so `strings.HasPrefix` is used.

The sidecar also joins the composite source fingerprint and changed-path classification, so a keepalive append on an otherwise idle session triggers resync.

The request-scoped source policy previously lived in two hand-synced copies (`db.UsageSourceIsRequestScoped` and `usagefacts.sourceIsRequestScoped`); it is now consolidated in `usagefacts.SourceIsRequestScoped` with `db` delegating. The new sources are registered there by prefix (`posit-assistant-`) rather than as exact literals: one-request-per-line is a property of the sidecar format, not of specific kinds, so a future PA event kind stays correctly request-scoped (and gets per-request pricing, including long-context bands) without a second list to maintain.

Because existing archives predate sidecar events, the data version moves 91 → 92 so those sessions re-parse through the normal non-destructive resync path.

title: Support provider specific billing calculations?
body:
### Problem / motivation

Providers like Posit AI charge a model rate, plus a documented [10% premium on top of model rates](https://docs.posit.co/posit-ai/user/faq/#how-are-credits-included-with-the-pro-plan). Currently agentsview calculates only the underlying model rates, so does not include the 10% premium.

### Proposed solution

I would probably just lean towards only calculating the model rates for now (which is fairly well represented by the LiteLLM catalogue). But I'm happy to do any research / work on what provider-specific rates would look like.

### Alternatives considered

* Leave as is (I think this is reasonable).
* Add support for Provider dependent cost calculations (e.g. for Posit Assistant), but use model calculations by default.
* Do a sweep across Providers to evaluate how useful calculating Provider cost would be.

title: Historical session costs should use pricing effective at session time
body:
## Problem

Historical session costs are recalculated from the current `model_pricing` catalog. When a model price changes, the displayed cost for an older session can change as well, even though the session usage and provider pricing at that time have not changed.

## Expected behavior

For computed costs, select the pricing that was effective when each usage event or session occurred, rather than always using the latest price. Historical results should remain stable and auditable after future pricing updates.

The implementation should consider retaining a pricing snapshot or version/effective-date history with the usage data. The pricing provenance should remain visible so users can understand how a historical amount was derived.

Provider-reported costs such as `cost_microdollars` should remain authoritative when present. Model/provider variants should also remain distinct when the recorded model identity contains them, for example `gpt-5.6-sol`, `us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, and `global.openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, since they can have different pricing.

## Impact

Recalculating old sessions with today\s catalog can make session history, daily totals, and aggregate usage reports inconsistent over time and can produce amounts that do not represent the price applicable when the usage occurred.

title: feat(pricing): apply Posit Assistant billing premium
body:
Posit Assistant usage previously inferred billing from the session agent, so managed Posit AI and bring-your-own-provider rows in the same session could not be distinguished. Computed usage therefore applied one billing rule to both cases.

This rework carries the provider identity from Posit Assistant message metadata and usage-event sidecars through usage facts, SQLite, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, cache rollups, activity reports, and session views. The exact `positai` provider receives the 11/10 managed-service adjustment after model, historical timestamp, request-band, and cache-tier selection. `anthropic`, empty, and other provider IDs remain at base rates, and custom pricing remains as configured. Explicit reported costs stay authoritative, cache savings for those rows use the resolved billed rates, and fixed web-search fees stay outside the adjustment.

Usage data version 94, usage-cache format 6, DuckDB schema 13, and export schema versions 6, 7, and 6 invalidate stale persisted results and document the changed cost semantics. No billing inference is made from model names, provider prefixes, or the session agent when row-level provider metadata is available.

Closes #1538

title: build: keep dependencies on current majors
body:
Moves the docs formatter and CI setup action onto their current major release
lines. `mdformat` advances to 1.0, and the incompatible `mdformat-tables`
plugin is removed because the existing MkDocs integration already supplies
GitHub Flavored Markdown table support.

The docs CI job now pins `setup-uv` v10.0.1. Same-major minor and patch
