title: fix(parser): discover OpenCode channel databases
body:
OpenCode source builds and non-release channels write sessions to `opencode-<channel>.db`, while AgentsView currently discovers only `opencode.db`. Sessions in source-build stores such as `opencode-local.db` therefore remain absent after a full resync, even when the database is inside the configured OpenCode directory.

This extends the existing OpenCode provider with a closed, direct-child container rule for `opencode.db` and producer-defined channel databases, then carries each physical path through discovery, lookup, watch, changed-path handling, freshness, parsing, and reconciliation. File-backed storage remains canonical for overlapping IDs, SQLite duplicates use stable canonical-first ordering, and Kilo, MiMoCode, Icodemate, and arbitrary external `OPENCODE_DB` paths retain their current scope.

The reported 576 release rows, 111 local rows, and two overlapping IDs came from @aspiers's issue report.

Closes #1521

title: Add hosted raw watch daemon
body:
## What changed

- Adds `raw-sync watch` and `raw-sync status` for continuous laptop-side raw
  capture and upload.
- Captures SQLite-backed providers through bounded online backups and file
  providers through ordered snapshots, append generations, and tombstones.
- Persists device-fenced checkpoints, durable retries, receipts, coverage
  state, and bounded outbox usage without storing parsed chat data.
- Reconciles missed watcher events with rotating audits while keeping upload
  and capture work serialized.

## Why

This advances the laptop watcher and uploader stage in #1352. Hosted raw mode
now has a durable local daemon path that can survive offline periods, watcher
gaps, source replacement, transport conflicts, and process restarts without
advancing an unsafe checkpoint.

## Limits

Remote transport requires HTTPS. Loopback HTTP is available only through the
explicit development flag. S3 roots stay out of this laptop filesystem watcher
and continue through their existing ingestion path.

title: fix(sync): report full resync finalization work
body:
Large full resyncs could display a completed session counter for minutes while database writes, source-state persistence, relationship repair, memory release, database-backed provider checks, final linking, and skip-cache persistence were still active.

This adds a bulk-only finalization phase with named steps and zero counters. Normal syncs keep their existing counted progress, while database-backed work keeps its accounting for final totals without replacing the finalization status. The command line, desktop startup status, status bar, and resync modal now render the named work; the modal hides its counter bar for uncounted phases.

Operation order, transactions, cancellation behavior, memory policy, and the database swap remain unchanged.

title: feat(pricing): add OrcaRouter as an online pricing source
body:
Add OrcaRouter's model catalog as a first-class pricing source, mirroring the existing OpenRouter integration. AgentsView already merges LiteLLM, OpenRouter, and the embedded fallback into the `model_pricing` table; OrcaRouter joins that set so sessions that route through OrcaRouter get accurate per-token costs. OrcaRouter publishes the same OpenRouter-shaped catalog envelope, so the fetch and parse paths are shared, and its rows are reconciled into the same marketplace ownership sentinel to keep the resolver free of duplicate spellings.

Like OpenRouter, OrcaRouter is an OpenAI-compatible AI gateway exposing a provider/model namespace across many models — but it also combines adaptive routing, automatic failover, zero-markup inference, observability, guardrails, and agent-tool governance on the same endpoint, plus gateway-level zero-trust security that screens every prompt/response and governs tool calls on a default-deny basis with no application changes. [OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai)

Verified: `go test ./internal/pricing/... ./internal/pricingrefresh/... ./internal/db/... ./internal/export/...` all pass, and a live fetch of `https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1/models` returns 167 priced models through the shared parser.

title: feat(frontend): use the standard kit-ui splitter and make the analysis panel resizable
body:
The session list splitter was a bespoke pointer-capture resizer that predated kit-ui's `SplitResizeHandle` and looked different from the standard divider used across kenn apps — the code even carried a `kit-ui-check-ignore` comment marking the swap as a tracked follow-up. The sidebar now uses the shared 4px handle, which also brings keyboard resizing via arrow keys; both ignore markers are gone and `kit-ui-check` reports zero findings.

The right-hand session analysis (vitals) panel was fixed at 320px, so charts and long repository paths could not get more room. It now gets the same handle on its left edge: drag deltas are inverted (moving the divider left widens the panel), and the width persists per browser (`agentsview-vitals-width`) the same way the sidebar width does. The resize handle's accessible label is new copy, added to all six locales.

Both panes clamp against one shared width budget with the content column. The sidebar clamp reserves the analysis panel's minimum footprint while the panel is visible, and the panel yields whatever the actual sidebar leaves over, so the 480px content minimum holds at any layout of 990px or wider. Precedence when space runs out: pane minimums, then the content minimum, then preferred widths — below 990px the pane floors bound the squeeze rather than a responsive collapse, which stays out of scope. Each separator advertises the layout-effective maximum in `aria-valuemax` rather than a storage cap the window cannot grant. (Before this PR the fixed 320px panel could squeeze the content column to 161px; the independent clamps in an earlier revision allowed 195px — review 12657 flagged that, and the shared budget resolves it.)

Sidebar behavior carried over unchanged: localStorage persistence and the guard that keeps a wider stored preference intact when a drag stays inside the clamp. Pointer mechanics (capture, pointer-id filtering, cancel handling) now live in kit-ui, so the tests that policed the bespoke plumbing were removed; jsdom lacks pointer capture, so the vitest setup stubs it alongside the existing ResizeObserver stub.

Reviewers should look at the budget arithmetic and the inverted delta in `ThreeColumnLayout.svelte`, and the cross-pane tests asserting the 510/280/480 split at a 1280px layout.

title: ffix(parser): discover Qoder CLI CN sessions
body:
Fixes #1405

Qoder CLI CN 1.1.21 stores its project-scoped JSONL sessions under `~/.qoder-cn/projects/`, while AgentsView currently scans the existing Qoder roots only.

Add the CN projects root to the existing Qoder default directories so the current provider discovers these sessions without introducing a separate agent or parser. The existing `QODER_PROJECTS_DIR` / `qoder_project_dirs` override behavior is unchanged.

Also updates the focused default-directory regression and the Qoder configuration/provenance documentation, keeping the CN storage observation explicitly user-reported rather than treating it as producer-side evidence.

title: test(capture): surface the run error when source observation flakes
body:
`TestCaptureDistinguishesAnObservedSourceThatDisappears` failed once on Windows CI (PR #1549's first run) with nothing but `Condition never satisfied` after its 20-second `Eventually`. The test only read the capture run's result channel after the manifest recorded an observed source, so any run that aborted early — transient ACL setup failure, manifest rename contention with the test's 10ms reads, helper spawn error — burned the whole timeout and discarded its actual error.

The `Eventually` is now a select loop with the same manifest polling and the same assertions afterward, but it fails immediately with the run's exit code and error when the capture finishes before the source is observed, and reports "run still in flight" when the timeout fires with the run still going. The next flake will name its cause on sight instead of reproducing an opaque timeout; the two failure shapes also discriminate between an early abort and a stalled run (for example a virus scanner stalling the freshly copied helper binary).

No production code changes; the test's contract is unchanged. Stacked on #1549 only to keep CI history linear — the change is independent and can be retargeted to main if the base merges first.

title: DSH parser already holds the seedLength and compaction boundaries — offering a regression gate for both
body:
I have been auditing token accounting in DeepSeek Harness consumers, and yours is the most complete external fold I have read. More complete than upstream's own.

`internal/parser/deepseek_harness.go:154-157` derives `ownedFrom` from `header.SeedLength` and drops events below it, so an ordinary fork does not bill its parent's inherited prefix. `:283-288` goes further and rejects a `seedLength` larger than the decoded event count rather than passing it through. And `:261-265` gives `compaction/summary` its own arm through `deepSeekHarnessCompactionUsage`, with the same check repeated on the validation path at `:489-491`.

Those two are the ones consumers usually miss. The fork case has no bound on its error: it is the ratio of inherited work to own work, and one fork in my corpus reported 263,790 tokens for 11,442 tokens of its own work. The compaction case is worth 48,895 tokens across three events on the same corpus, and upstream still does not fold it. At `cd5ef814` (0.1.2-alpha.1), `usageOf()` in `packages/llm/token-meter/src/usage-projection.ts` matches `assistant/chunk` and `assistant/message` and nothing else, and `compaction/summary` appears nowhere in the file.

So this is not a defect report. It is an offer of a regression gate for what you already hold.

[dsh-conformance](https://github.com/lizhuojunx86/token-accounting-conformance/tree/main/dsh-conformance) grades seven folds over a committed synthetic fixture and prints a named residual rather than pass or fail. One command, stdlib Python only, no corpus and no vendor account, so it works as a CI gate that needs nobody's data. If a future refactor drops the `seedLength` filter, it comes back as `gap_inherited` by name rather than as a total that is merely wrong.

One wiring note that cost someone else time: run it with the working directory inside the checkout being graded.

If you want it wired in, I will open the PR.

Li Zhuojun

title: Add DSH-style session timing overview
body:
Adds a full-width session timing overview above every open transcript, modeled on DSH's Trajectory view. Input, model, and tool spans share an interactive timeline with duration/sequence projections, range focus, zoom and pan, transcript jumps, local search, and progressive history loading.

Tool spans prefer recorded execution start/completion events. Missing per-call timing remains visibly approximate rather than fabricated, while model spans use the timestamps available across supported session formats.

The toolbar also connects Turns to focused transcript mode and Calls to tool-detail visibility. The old right-column activity lane and its now-unused frontend fetch/store path are removed; Session Vital Signs remains available for aggregate and per-call analysis.

Primary review points are `TimingOverview.svelte`, `timingOverview.ts`, and the `MessageList.svelte` integration.

title: fix(ci): reduce transient main failures
body:
Main CI hit two unrelated failures: GitHub returned 504 while Tauri downloaded
a bundler tool, and capture lost its `no_session` classification when its
context expired during source lookup.

Desktop bundling now retries the build once. The race job keeps capture and
sync in the shared suite but caps package fan-out at four; that shared suite
completes under the existing timeout. Capture now preserves finalization state
when source lookup returns a cancellation or deadline error, so scheduler timing
does not change the reported reason.

The download retry is deliberately broad and limited to one extra attempt. This
keeps the action small and avoids parsing dependency output for HTTP status
codes.

title: fix(daemon): keep readiness wait alive during startup progress
body:
A detached serve can spend longer than five seconds on a healthy initial sync while continuously publishing structured startup progress. The parent currently treats that fixed wall-clock limit as failure, reports that the server did not become ready, and can leave users with a running daemon that the command declared unavailable.

This changes the five-second readiness limit into an inactivity window: each newer startup snapshot renews it, while a daemon whose progress stalls still times out normally. The timeout boundary also rechecks both the canonical writable runtime and the latest progress snapshot so publication in the final polling interval is not discarded.

The tradeoff is that the parent may remain attached beyond five seconds while startup is demonstrably advancing. The CLI reference documents that behavior. The readiness loop and advancing, stalled, and timeout-boundary regressions are in cmd/agentsview/serve_background.go and cmd/agentsview/serve_background_test.go.

title: perf(sync): skip unchanged OpenCode sessions within a changed container
body:
Follows up on #1208. The scheduling fixes in #1307, #1319, and #1355 resolved the continuous 100% CPU loop from poll starvation (idle CPU now reaches 0%). Residual 200-700% CPU spikes during active agent streaming remain (#1208, berendeboer Aug 19 comment).

### Root cause

The SQLite container gate (`opencode_container_gate.go`) is binary: container changed or not. During active streaming the WAL genuinely grows, so the gate correctly identifies the container as changed. When it does, the engine fans the event to every session via `sqliteSources` → `ListOpenCodeSessionMeta` → `SELECT id, time_updated FROM session` (all rows), and each session proceeds through the full parse path: `parseOpenCodeDBSession` opens the DB, queries session + message + part tables, builds the model, computes a content fingerprint. `dropUnchangedSharedSQLiteResults` then filters unchanged sessions post-parse by fingerprint comparison, but the parse work has already been done.

### Measured impact

On a live 1.2 GB OpenCode database with 123 sessions, sampling `time_updated` at 5-second intervals (matching the dispatch floor) across three consecutive cycles:

```
Interval 1: 1 changed, 122 unchanged (99%)
Interval 2: 1 changed, 122 unchanged (99%)
Interval 3: 1 changed, 122 unchanged (99%)
```

Different session IDs changed across intervals (2 distinct active sessions), confirming the signal isn't aliased. Every cycle, 122 sessions are fully parsed and discarded.

### Proposal: session-level time_updated pre-filter

After the container gate says "changed," compare per-session `time_updated` values from `ListOpenCodeSessionMeta` (already a lightweight index-only query) against a cached map. Only send sessions with a changed `time_updated` to the parse path.

The container gate comment at `opencode_container_gate.go:14` notes that a message or part row can change without bumping `time_updated`. This is real at the schema level (the test seeder confirms it). A periodic full-verification escape handles it: every Nth cycle (e.g. every 5th, roughly every 25 seconds at the 5s dispatch floor), bypass the pre-filter and verify all sessions by content as today. This bounds the staleness window while keeping the common path fast.

The active session's `time_updated` is being bumped during streaming (new messages arriving), so the fast path covers the dominant case.

title: [Bug][Windows Desktop] Stale startup-state.json after failed initial sync blocks all launches with "startup is still in progress"
body:
### Summary / 问题概述

On the **Windows Desktop app**, AgentsView can get permanently stuck on "Preparing your workspace / Launching local service" after a sync worker fails during startup. A stale `startup-state.json` records an `initial sync` that never completed (the sync child died), so every subsequent launch is rejected with "startup is still in progress" / sync reports "sync already in progress", and the local server never listens on 127.0.0.1:8080.

Windows 桌面版在某个初始 sync 失败后，会永久卡在 "Preparing your workspace"：`startup-state.json` 残留了未完成的 initial sync（sync 子进程已死），之后每次启动都被 startup 锁挡住，本地 server 永远起不来（8080 无监听）。

### Environment / 环境
- agentsview v0.41.1 (commit a902515a, built 2026-08-18)
- OS: Windows 11
- Install: `Agent Zero`... no — AgentsView Desktop (Tauri, app id `io.agentsview.desktop`), data dir `%USERPROFILE%\.agentsview`

### Steps to reproduce / 复现步骤
1. Have any source session file fail reconcile during the initial sync (logs show `fatal: sync worker startup: failed`, and earlier `watch root reconciliation failed processing page: N failures`).
2. The initial-sync child process dies; `%USERPROFILE%\.agentsview\startup-state.json` is left with `{"pid": <dead-pid>, "phase": "initial sync", ...}`.
3. Restart the Desktop app (or `agentsview serve restart`): `fatal: daemon restart: startup is still in progress (pid <dead-pid>) ... retry agentsview daemon status`; `agentsview sync` prints `sync already in progress`. The backend never binds 127.0.0.1:8080, so the GUI waits forever.

### Actual behavior / 实际行为
- serve.log ends with `fatal: sync worker startup: failed` (and for v0.41.1, `ERROR: startup sync worker ran but did not complete: startup worker pass reported failed (surfacing incomplete pass; not re-syncing in process)`).
- `startup-state.json` keeps a stale pid/phase and is never reconciled, so boot is permanently blocked.

### Workaround (what fixed it) / 临时解法
1. Delete `%USERPROFILE%\.agentsview\startup-state.json` (stale/in-progress marker; pid no longer alive).
2. Optionally remove the damaged reconcile db (`.agentsview-reconcile-<id>.db*`).
3. Run `agentsview.exe serve` in the foreground (NOT `serve restart`, which re-spawns and can re-wedge behind the same stale marker). The initial sync then completes to 100% and the server binds 127.0.0.1:8080.
4. Reopen the Desktop app; it connects.

### Suggested fix / 建议
- `startup-state.json` should be cleared/self-healed when the recorded `pid` is no longer alive (orphan detection), like other daemon lock files.
- A failed `sync worker startup` should surface a clear error to the UI instead of leaving a permanent boot blocker; and `serve restart` should not refuse when the recorded startup pid is dead.

### Checklist / 检查清单
- [x] I searched for existing issues. (Related: #1403 is a different hang; #1081/#1082 cover daemon-autostart sync oddities.)
- [x] I removed sensitive information.

title: recall: add [recall.extract] candidate_findings = "allow" to gate extraction on definite findings only (#1404)
body:
Adds an opt-in for Recall extraction to ignore candidate-confidence secret
findings while continuing to block definite findings:

```toml
[recall.extract]
candidate_findings = "allow" # default: "block"
```

Candidate findings are false-positive-prone heuristics that remain recorded for
review. With `"allow"`, they no longer exclude a session during discovery,
pre-send scanning, commit and activation guards, or corpus reconciliation. The
same policy applies when extraction is disabled but an existing corpus remains
served.

The default remains `"block"`, so existing configurations keep treating every
recorded finding as an extraction boundary. `recall extract doctor` reports the
active policy. This change does not alter the database schema.

Addresses #1404.

title: perf(sync): skip unchanged OpenCode sessions within a changed container
body:
Active OpenCode streaming advances the shared SQLite container's write markers on each dispatch interval. Discovery then runs the full `ForEachOpenCodeSessionMeta` query, which aggregates every `message` and `part` row to build per-session child identities, even when one session changed and 122 did not. The measured 1.2 GB production container repeats that archive-sized scan every five-second cycle.

This widens the container listing predicate so a recently digest-verified container uses `ForEachOpenCodeSessionWatermarkMeta` (session and project rows only, no child aggregation) while its verification age remains within a five-minute interval. Changed members resolve their composite fingerprint through the indexed per-session path. The reconciliation spool carries a compact discovery-state payload so watermark fidelity survives source rehydration across pages. Full digest verification runs on process start, after the interval expires, and when a container's file identity changes; it is stamped only after a complete successful pass.

Force parsing, resync, cancellation, failed passes, container replacement, legacy schemas, and non-OpenCode providers retain existing behavior. No database schema, archive, or frontend change.

Closes #1557

title: fix(frontend): keep concurrency tooltip on screen and ignore future buckets
body: ## TL;DR Hovering a concurrency bucket near a window edge cut off part of the tooltip, and hovering the not-yet-elapsed part of the range highlighted it and popped an all-zero tooltip that reads as "nothing happened" instead of "has not happened yet". The tooltip now clamps itself inside the viewport, and buckets that start at or after the report's effective end get no hover target. ## How The tooltip drops its fixed CSS transform. An effect measures the rendered box and clamps its left and top to the viewport with an 8px pad, keeping the centered-above placement when there is room. The API returns buckets for the whole requested range, including ones that have not started. A `liveBars` prefix now feeds the hover hit targets, so future buckets cannot be hovered, focused, or selected, and keyboard navigation and drag selection clamp to the last live bucket. Their bar geometry and the shaded future region still render. Review from `ConcurrencyTimeline.svelte`; the new tests pin the clamped tooltip positions and the live hit-target count.

title: fix(docker): fail over between Debian mirrors
body:
AgentsView OCI builds depended on one Debian CDN. When that endpoint stopped responding, `apt-get` could stall the build for several minutes.

This keeps the existing Debian Bookworm build and runtime images, but gives Apt an ordered mirror list. GitHub-hosted runners prefer Microsoft's Azure-hosted Debian mirror, then Debian's official endpoints, then independent US mirrors. A stalled HTTP request fails over after 10 seconds, and each Apt command has a 90-second final deadline.

A cold ARM64 Bake build completed with the new mirror setup, and kenn-dist accepted the resulting OCI archive.

title: fix(docker): distribute Apt requests across mirrors
body: Apt kept using the highest-priority Debian mirror when it responded partially, so a slow mirror could consume the entire command timeout without reaching the remaining entries. This gives the existing Bookworm mirrors equal priority, allowing each file request to select a working mirror while preserving the existing request and command deadlines.

title: Let config.toml choose how much of each session the archive keeps
body:
Adds `archive_content` to `config.toml` with three storage modes:

- `full` keeps the complete archive and remains the default.
- `transcripts` keeps conversations and tool metadata while dropping tool inputs and outputs.
- `usage` keeps token and cost accounting, model attribution, and automation classifications without conversation text.

`AGENTSVIEW_ARCHIVE_CONTENT` can set the same policy for a separate reporting archive. To apply a stricter policy to existing data, restart the daemon and run `agentsview sync --full`. Removed content requires the original source files to recover.

Writes, archive copies, and signal recomputation apply the policy consistently. Transcript-only copies conservatively remove text when older parser rows cannot separate tool output from prose. This may remove adjacent prose; it is a storage policy, not a guarantee that ordinary conversation text contains no secrets. Restricted Codex archives omit parser checkpoints whose resumable hash state can contain source bytes.

Usage-only mode also disables insights, recall, and vector operations. Opening the writable archive clears existing local vector indexes; PostgreSQL pushes remove indexed content for owned sessions while preserving other sessions. PostgreSQL automation audits preserve classifications only when a persisted marker says the prompt evidence was discarded. Tool-result rows remain part of the transcript totals but do not count as user prompts or prompt-quality evidence across SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB.

title: recall query --mode hybrid 500s with a project/cwd filter: knn k escalates to 8000 past sqlite-vec's 4096 limit
body:
### Summary

`recall query --mode hybrid` combined with a context filter (`--project`, `--cwd`, `--current-cwd`) returns HTTP 500 whenever the filter selects a small fraction of the accepted corpus:

```
fatal: POST /api/v1/recall/query: HTTP 500:
{"error":"search: k value in knn query too large, provided 8000 and the limit is 4096"}
```

The same filter works fine in `--mode vector` and `--mode lexical`, and `--mode hybrid` works unfiltered. So the fault looks specific to the hybrid path's candidate-oversampling when a filter is applied.

### Version

`agentsview v0.41.1+candidate-findings (commit 5338e09, built 2026-08-31T09:25:16Z)` — a local build carrying only the `candidate_findings` config key from #1559; nothing in that patch touches recall retrieval.

Linux, SQLite backend, embeddings generated locally (Ollama over a tunnel), 4966 accepted recall entries.

### Repro

```
$ agentsview recall query "status" --project <small-project> --mode hybrid --limit 3
fatal: POST /api/v1/recall/query: HTTP 500: {"error":"search: k value in knn query too large, provided 8000 and the limit is 4096"}

$ agentsview recall query "status" --project <small-project> --mode vector  --limit 3   # fine
$ agentsview recall query "status" --project <small-project> --mode lexical --limit 3   # fine
$ agentsview recall query "status"                          --mode hybrid  --limit 3   # fine
```

### Observed threshold

Same query, same corpus (4966 accepted entries), varying only `--project`:

| project | accepted entries | share of corpus | hybrid + filter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dh` | 2793 | 56% | ok |
| `Work` | 1026 | 21% | ok |
| `local_inference` | 457 | 9% | **500** |
| `Mini_PM_docs` | 346 | 7% | **500** |
| `miniboard` | 128 | 3% | **500** |

`--cwd /home/dh/Work/Mini_PM_docs` fails identically. The reported `k` is **8000 regardless of `--limit`** (tested 1, 3, 5, 30), so it is not derived from the requested result count.

That pattern reads as: the hybrid path widens `k` until enough candidates survive the post-filter, doubling up to a fixed ceiling of 8000, and never clamps to the sqlite-vec `k` limit of 4096 — nor to the corpus size, which is 4966 here, so `k=8000` could not return more rows even if sqlite-vec accepted it. A filter matching a small share of the corpus reaches the last escalation step and hard-fails.

### Expected

Either clamp the escalated `k` to `min(sqlite-vec limit, corpus size)` and return whatever the filter yields, or push the context filter into the knn query so oversampling isn't needed. A narrow filter returning a short list is a normal outcome; it shouldn't 500.

### Impact / workaround

Hybrid is the mode the docs recommend for recall, and filtering to the current project is the natural way to use it from inside a session — so on any archive with more than a couple of projects, the recommended combination is the one that breaks. Everything narrower than roughly a fifth of the corpus is affected, which in practice means every project except the largest one or two.

Workaround is `--mode vector` (loses the lexical half of the fusion) or dropping the filter and relying on content ranking.

title: test(capture): synchronize source removal after persistence
body:
The Windows Go job failed because the source-disappearance integration test
renamed the provider root as soon as `SourceObserved` reached the manifest.
Capture records that marker before it finishes enumerating, snapshotting, and
copying the live source, so the test could remove the directory during those
operations instead of during final live-source verification.

The test now pauses at the existing post-persistence hook, removes the live
provider root after its copy is durable, and resumes finalization. This keeps
the test focused on the `source_unavailable` contract and includes the
underlying capture error if the classification fails again. Production capture
behavior is unchanged.

title: Use stepped area chart for Cost Over Time
body:
### Problem / motivation

The "Cost Over Time" chart under the Usage view currently uses a stacked area chart with linear interpolation between dates. The sloped lines that connect data points presentan inaccurate view of the total - the area under the line isn't mathematically proportionate to spend. 


### Proposed solution

A stepped area chart would accurately reflect usage:

https://developers.google.com/chart/interactive/docs/gallery/steppedareachart

### Alternatives considered

A stacked bar chart would also be sufficient, but might not present continuity as well as a stepped area chart.

title: docs: rebuild agentsview.io as a tiered marketing and documentation site
body:
Rebuilds agentsview.io as a three-tier site: a hand-written marketing landing page at `/`, a nine-stop guided tour at `/guide/`, and the Zensical documentation moved under `/docs/`. The goal is to pitch AgentsView as the system of record for agent session intelligence — an always-on daemon with monitoring, cost accounting, search, recall, and agent-facing interfaces — rather than a desktop session browser.

## What the site does now

- **Marketing tier** (`docs/website/`): landing page with a two-column hero (headline, install command, and a framed dashboard screenshot), nine numbered sections (record, observe, account, understand, remember, feed back, share, own, start), 56 agent-harness chips, live GitHub stars/version via the API with a cached fallback, and a lightbox for screenshots. `/guide/` walks the session intelligence loop across nine stops. Dark blue theme with vendored Inter and JetBrains Mono (OFL licenses included), a custom AV favicon, and a 404 page.
- **Docs tier**: Zensical builds under `/docs/` via `site_url`, with `docs/index.md` rewritten as a docs landing page (mental model, architecture, privacy). All 28 doc pages' absolute links are rewritten with the `/docs/` prefix. The `docs/agents/` contributor guides are no longer published (they were accidentally reachable before).
- **Machine-readable tier**: every route ships a Markdown twin (`/index.md`, `/guide.md`, `/docs/<page>.md`) advertised by a `rel="alternate" type="text/markdown"` head link and footer links, and `/llms.txt` lists the full twin set.

## Redirects and contracts

`docs/vercel.json` carries 61 permanent redirects covering every legacy route: 28 old root pages (both `/<page>/` and `/<page>.md`) to their `/docs/` locations, asset wildcards, and the pre-existing `/postgresql/`, `/insights/`, and `/architecture/` aliases. The two temporary install-script redirects are unchanged.

The validators enforce the new structure: `check_built_site.py` verifies every route's Markdown twin, alternate link, metadata, and bidirectional `llms.txt` coverage; `check_vercel_redirects.py` now also rejects unexpected redirect entries; `scripts/docs_assets_test.go` covers the assembled three-tier output, including the sitemap shipping at both `/sitemap.xml` and `/docs/sitemap.xml` (Zensical's instant navigation fetches the latter and silently degrades if it 404s).

## Tradeoffs and limits

- The marketing tier is plain HTML/CSS/JS assembled by `zensical-docs.sh` — no new build toolchain or Node dependency.
- Vercel configuration is untouched: the root directory stays `docs/`, output stays `site/`, and deploys remain manual via `make docs-deploy`.
- The docs tier still uses the Zensical default favicon; only the marketing tier has the AV mark.

## Where to look

- `docs/zensical-docs.sh` — the site assembly: docs build into `site/docs/`, then the website tier, `llms.txt`, and sitemap copies are placed at the root.
- `docs/website/index.html` and `docs/website/styles/site.css` — the landing page and theme.
- `docs/scripts/check_built_site.py` — the contracts that keep the twin/llms.txt/redirect structure honest.

Preview locally with `make docs-build && make docs-preview`.

title: fix(search): exclude live sessions and bake remote skill flags
body:
## Summary

Content search can now drop specific sessions before `--limit`, and `skills install` can bake `--server` / `--server-token-file` into the finding-history examples.

Identifier hunts no longer have to lose the real history to the live conversation, and remote-daemon installs no longer teach commands that silently query local SQLite.

`--exclude-session` is repeatable on the CLI and `exclude_session` on HTTP; SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB apply it in SQL. For substring, regex, and FTS the excluded rows are gone before `LIMIT`, so they cannot consume the page. Semantic and hybrid still filter after the vector overfetch, so an excluded session can occupy top-k slots there.

`skills install --server` records the remote in an `# install-remote:` comment so a flagless reinstall stays current. Precedence is explicit flags, then the installed file, then `AGENTSVIEW_SKILLS_SERVER` / `AGENTSVIEW_SKILLS_SERVER_TOKEN_FILE` — an installed file decides even when it bakes no remote, so an exported variable cannot report existing skills as stale. `--server ""` un-bakes a remote. The variables are skills-only and named apart from `AGENTSVIEW_SERVER_TOKEN` so they cannot be read as a default read path for `session` commands, which have none.

Reviewers should look at two places. The `exclude_session` query tag in `internal/server/huma_routes_search.go`: Huma disables query-param explode by default and then splits a single value on commas, while the HTTP backend sends one param per ID, so without the `explode` tag every ID after the first was silently dropped on remote searches. And `skillRemoteSource.resolve` in `cmd/agentsview/skills.go`, which carries the precedence rule described above.

Baked values are shell-quoted, since the examples are meant to be run verbatim, and control characters are rejected because they would break the single-line `install-remote` comment.

Closes #1511

title: fix(frontend): keep Codex answers in focused transcripts
body:
Focused transcript mode shows user prompts and final answers. It treats an
assistant message as mid-turn narration when tool work follows it before the
next user turn. That fits Claude, whose closing text ends a turn. Codex and its
fork TraeX can emit an answer and then keep calling tools, so the same rule
discarded an answer the user had received.

On a local archive, the suppression fired for 16.7% of Codex turns (168 of
1009) against 0.2% of Claude turns (4 of 1970). In one long Codex session, it
hid the response for 20 of 48 turns and left runs of consecutive user prompts
with nothing between them.

Agents now declare post-answer tool work as a provider capability. The settings
API publishes that capability through the generated OpenAPI client, and the
frontend uses it when filtering focused transcripts. HTML export reads the
same provider declaration, so exports and the viewer stay aligned without
separate agent lists. Providers without the capability, including responses
from older servers where the optional field is absent, keep the existing
behavior. Turns that produced no assistant text remain empty for every agent.

Closes #1581

title: Docs logo link mangles marketing homepage via instant navigation
body:
Clicking the AgentsView logo from any `/docs/` page loads the marketing homepage (`/`) through Zensical's `navigation.instant` XHR fetch instead of a full page navigation. The marketing homepage is plain HTML outside Zensical's scope, so the instant-navigation intercept injects raw marketing HTML into the Zensical shell, producing a mangled page.

A full page load (Ctrl+click or typing the URL directly) renders the homepage correctly.

The logo link at `/` needs to force a full navigation to bypass the instant-navigation intercept. MkDocs Material documents a `data-preview` attribute that can be set to disable instant loading for specific links, or the link could use an absolute URL with a different origin/scheme to break out of the SPA routing.

Introduced in #1568.

title: Retire inactive usage-cache generations safely
body:
Usage-cache format or archive database-ID changes leave obsolete sibling databases on disk indefinitely because SQLite transaction locks cannot prove that another process has released an idle handle.

Introduce a format-gated cross-process retirement lease. Lease-aware openers hold a shared lease for the lifetime of the SQLite pool. Retirement takes the exclusive lease without waiting, revalidates application ID, cache kind, retirement protocol, format, source database ID, and exact generation path, then removes the database and its WAL/SHM sidecars. Preserve the current generation, active generations, pre-protocol generations, and any mismatched or unrecognized file. Keep the lease inode so racing openers remain coordinated.

title: Retire inactive usage-cache generations safely
body:
## What changed

- Adds a version 8 lease that every open usage-cache connection holds for its full lifetime.
- Retires an old version 8 cache only after an exclusive lease succeeds and the cache identity matches the expected source database, format, protocol, and filename.
- Removes the retired database and its SQLite sidecars. The current cache, active caches, older pre-protocol caches, caches written by a newer format, symlinks, and unknown files remain untouched. Skipping newer formats keeps a downgraded or older side-by-side binary from forcing the newer cache to rebuild.
- Closes every lease handle after success, contention, and errors.
- Removes the unused cache manager Reset method so no untested path can delete persistent cache files.
- Lets the first cache build finish while active session files keep changing. It publishes the stable snapshot and leaves changing sessions to the existing incremental updater.

## Why

Old cache generations could consume hundreds of megabytes after upgrades. Live testing with 40,951 sessions found a second failure: a continuously changing session could invalidate every publication attempt, so the 28-day usage query timed out.

Closes #1572

title: fix(command-palette): dismiss only when a drag starts and ends on the overlay
body:
This fixes the undesirable behavior where the search overlay closes early, which happens whenever a drag starts inside the search input and is released outside it. This PR changes that behavior to match established conventions in OS and app dialogs, so that releasing the mouse button does not cancel the search or close the overlay.

The palette dismisses early due to the `click` handler on `.palette-overlay` firing on click events that target the common ancestor of its mousedown and mouseup elements. A drag that starts inside the palette and releases past its edge therefore reports `.palette-overlay` as the click target, so the palette closes even though the press began inside it. The search input sits flush with the palette border, so selecting the current query to replace it puts the release outside the input on most attempts and the palette disappears mid-gesture.

This replaces the overlay click handler with paired `mousedown` and `mouseup` handlers that dismiss only when both ends of the gesture land on the overlay itself. A press inside the palette released on the overlay leaves the palette open, and so does the mirror case of a press on the overlay released inside the palette, which would otherwise close the palette out from under a cursor that is back over the results. A plain click on the backdrop still dismisses.

title: fix(docs): bypass instant navigation on logo link to marketing homepage
body:
Adds `data-preview=""` to the logo anchor to opt it out of Zensical's `navigation.instant`, which otherwise intercepts the logo link and fetches the marketing homepage via XHR, producing a mangled page when the home icon is clicked from the docs.

Fixes #1571

title: fix(codex): resolve forks of turnless parents instead of retrying forever
body:
Codex Desktop writes a rollout the moment a thread opens, so a fork taken before the first prompt names a parent that holds only `session_meta` and settings events. The fork gate treated a parent with no turn ids the same way as a parent it could not find: the child was stamped `DataVersionNeedsRetry`, re-parsed on every pass, and never reached the current data version. Because a retry counts as a failure in `collectAndBatch`, one such fork on a reconciliation page aborted that page and every page behind it. A local archive carried six of these forks in one chain, every parent present and readable, and logged the identical abort every fifteen seconds for a day; the deferred-source work in #1490 stops the abort from spreading but leaves those forks permanently deferred.

`codexParentResolution` now treats any parent that can be read as resolved, whether or not it holds turn ids. A turnless parent never opened a turn, so the fork replayed nothing and the gate has nothing to drop; with an empty parent turn set the gate suppresses nothing either way, so parsing the child as current is the only change. A parent that cannot be read still defers the child, exactly as before.

An earlier revision of this PR kept a turnless parent blocking when the child carried a copied parent `session_meta`, on the theory that a replay prefix always begins with that copied meta. A survey of a large local Codex archive disproved it: about half of the forks there, including many written by Codex 0.147.0, replay parent turns with no copied parent meta at all. That gate and its test are gone, which is why the net diff is small.

Reviewers should look at `codexParentResolution` in `internal/parser/codex.go` and `TestCodexProviderTurnlessParentResolvesWithoutRetry`, which parses a fork of a meta-only parent and expects a current result with only the child's messages.

Closes #1582

title: fix(sync): stop SQLite-backed containers from re-syncing on their own -shm writes
body:
Opening a WAL-mode SQLite database as a reader rewrites its `-shm` index. Several providers treated that rewrite as a source change: they resolved a bare `-shm` event to the whole container, folded the `-shm` mtime into the container fingerprint, or both, while each of them opens its own read connection during a scan. Together those made each scan schedule the next. On one archive the ZCode container had not changed for half an hour while its 22 sessions were rewritten every five seconds, and the usage-cache backfill and `/api/v1/usage/summary` failed continuously with "source archive changed during rollup build" because the archive never held still long enough.

Every SQLite-backed provider that opens its own read connection now ignores bare `-shm` events and leaves the `-shm` mtime out of its fingerprint:

- The db-backed containers (Forge, Piebald, Warp, Goose, ZCode) through the shared `dbPathForEvent`, plus the ZCode fingerprint.
- Zed and Shelley through the shared container classifier, the same flag Omnigent already passed.
- Kiro and Devin through their own event mapping.
- The shared journal suffix list is now main file plus `-wal`, so Omnigent and Cursor IDE use it instead of private copies.

Real changes always land in the main file or its `-wal` sibling, and every path still honors those. Existing tests that used a `-shm` event as an example database sibling now use `-wal`.

Two limits remain. The first read-only open after an agent closes its database cleanly re-creates an empty `-wal`, so a provider whose fingerprint reads the `-wal` mtime re-parses its container once per app close. That is one bounded pass, not a loop; the OpenCode provider already guards it by checking whether the WAL has frames, and the same check could be extended later. Stored ZCode mtimes from older builds included the `-shm` mtime, so the first scan after upgrading rewrites the ZCode archive once.

Reviewers should look at `dbPathForEvent` in `internal/parser/db_backed_provider.go`, `zcodeSessionFileMtime` in `internal/parser/zcode.go`, and `sqliteDBJournalSuffixes` in `internal/parser/zed_provider.go`.

Closes #1583

title: Focused transcript mode drops Codex answers that are followed by tool work
body:
### agentsview version

v0.41.1 (commit 55646d64); the same code is present on `main` at d0395b50.

### Install method

Built from source

### OS / platform

Linux x86_64 (Debian-based)

### Which agent and version

Codex Desktop / CLI 0.147.0 (also applies to TraeX, which shares the transcript shape)

### Which model(s)

gpt-5.6-sol; the bug is model-independent

### What happened, and what did you expect

## What happened

Focused transcript mode ("user prompts and final answers only") shows runs of consecutive user prompts for Codex sessions with no assistant answer between them. In one long Codex session, 20 of 48 turns lost their answer; measured across a local archive the suppression fires for 16.7% of Codex turns (168 of 1009) against 0.2% of Claude turns (4 of 1970).

`filterDisplayItemsByTranscriptMode` treats an assistant message as mid-turn narration, not the answer, whenever a tool group follows it before the next user turn. That matches Claude, whose closing text ends a turn. Codex reports a result and then keeps calling tools, and the next user prompt frequently lands while that work is still running, so the rule discards the answer the user actually received. `focusedExportOrdinals` in `internal/server/export.go` carries the same rule, so the HTML export drops the same answers.

## Expected behavior

For Codex-format transcripts, the last assistant text of a turn should stay visible even when tool work follows it. Turns that produced no assistant text at all should still show nothing.

### Sample session file or snippet

```text
5165 user       22:09:01  <prompt>
5166 assistant  22:09:16  <answer>            <- dropped by focused mode
5167 assistant  22:09:18  [Bash] exec_command <- tool group after the answer
5168 user       22:10:38  <next prompt>
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any Codex session where the assistant answers and then continues with tool calls before the next prompt.
2. Switch the transcript to Focused mode.
3. Observe that the answer between the two prompts is missing; Normal mode shows it.

Fix in #1570.

title: Codex fork of a turnless parent is marked NeedsRetry forever
body:
### agentsview version

v0.41.1 (commit 55646d64); still present on `main` at d0395b50.

### Install method

Built from source

### OS / platform

Linux x86_64 (Debian-based)

### Which agent and version

Codex Desktop 0.147.0 (source `vscode`)

### Which model(s)

gpt-5.6-sol; the bug is model-independent

### What happened, and what did you expect

## What happened

Codex Desktop writes a rollout the moment a thread opens. Forking before the first prompt therefore produces a parent rollout that holds only `session_meta` and a `thread_settings_applied` event, with no `turn_context` at all. A chain of such forks (six sessions, three of them empty, one 221 MB) is sitting in a local archive.

`codexParentResolution` returns `resolved && len(turnIDs) > 0`, so a parent that exists and is fully readable but has no turn ids is treated exactly like a parent that cannot be found: the child is stamped `DataVersionNeedsRetry` with reason "codex parent turns unresolved" on every parse, and never reaches the current data version. Each pass re-parses the 221 MB rollout in full.

Before #1490 the retry also counted as a hard failure in `collectAndBatch`, which aborted every reconciliation page behind it; the archive logged `watch root reconciliation failed processing page: 6 failures` 7,977 times in one day. #1490 stops the abort from spreading, but the six forks stay permanently deferred and their fork lineage (`parent_session_id`) is never recorded, because `linkSubagentSessions` is gated on a clean pass.

This is distinct from #1476, whose parent transcript was genuinely missing. Here every parent is present.

## Expected behavior

A parent that was read but never opened a turn has nothing to replay, so the fork should parse as current unless the child itself carries the copied parent `session_meta` (the positive sign that replayed history exists and the parent file is simply behind). Only an unreadable parent should defer the child.

### Sample session file or snippet

Parent rollout (complete file, two lines):

```text
{"type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":"<parent-id>","forked_from_id":null,"cli_version":"0.147.0","originator":"Codex Desktop", ...}}
{"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"thread_settings_applied", ...}}
```

Child rollout head:

```text
{"type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":"<child-id>","forked_from_id":"<parent-id>", ...}}
{"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"thread_settings_applied", ...}}
{"type":"turn_context","payload":{"turn_id":"<child-turn>", ...}}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Codex Desktop, open a new thread and fork it before sending a prompt; send prompts in the fork.
2. Sync the Codex root.
3. Observe the fork stays below the current data version with `RetryReason` "codex parent turns unresolved" on every pass, while `doctor sync` shows the parent present.

Fix in #1578.

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: db-backed SQLite containers re-sync every interval on their own -shm writes
body:
### agentsview version

`main` at f64e22e8 (v0.42.0 era); not reproducible on v0.41.1 commit 55646d64 from 2026-08-22.

### Install method

Built from source

### OS / platform

Linux x86_64 (Debian-based)

### Which agent and version

zcode CLI (db-backed provider, `~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite`); goose shares the same `dbBackedSourceSet`

### Which model(s)

Not applicable

### What happened, and what did you expect

## What happened

After upgrading a daemon to current `main`, the watcher fired every five seconds with "1 file(s) changed" and each cycle rewrote all 22 zcode sessions (`sync: 22 file(s) updated`), although `db.sqlite` and `db.sqlite-wal` had not changed for over half an hour and no zcode process was running. The only file moving was `db.sqlite-shm`, whose mtime advanced by exactly one dispatch interval each cycle.

The loop is self-inflicted. Opening a WAL-mode database as a reader rewrites its `-shm` index. `dbBackedSourceSet.dbPathForEvent` resolves a bare `-shm` event to the whole container, and `zcodeSessionFileMtime` folds the `-shm` mtime into every member's fingerprint. So the sync opens the database, the watcher sees the `-shm` write, every fingerprint moves, every member is rewritten, and the next interval repeats it.

Downstream, the archive never held still: `usage cache backfill could not stabilize after 3 attempts` on every start, and `/api/v1/usage/summary` returned 500 with "usage cache source archive changed during rollup build" continuously.

Omnigent and Cursor IDE already guard against exactly this through `rejectShmSiblingEvents` in `classifySQLiteContainerPath`; the db-backed providers do not.

## Expected behavior

A bare `-shm` event should not resolve to a db-backed container, and the `-shm` mtime should not participate in the zcode fingerprint. Real writes always land in the main file or the `-wal` sibling, which should keep triggering syncs as before.

### Sample session file or snippet

```text
19:43:00 watcher: 1 file(s) changed, triggering sync
19:43:01 sync: 22 file(s) updated
19:43:05 watcher: 1 file(s) changed, triggering sync
19:43:06 sync: 22 file(s) updated
...
db.sqlite      mtime 19:16:54   (unchanged)
db.sqlite-wal  mtime 19:16:54   (unchanged)
db.sqlite-shm  mtime 19:45:25 -> 19:45:30 -> ...  (advances every cycle)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a zcode (or goose) database with several sessions under its default root, with the CLI not running.
2. Start `agentsview serve` from current `main` and watch the log.
3. Observe a sync every dispatch interval that rewrites every session in the container, and `stat` showing only `db.sqlite-shm` changing.

Fix in #1580.
