title: fix(capture): reuse test helper executables
body:
The capture integration suite copied its 44 MB test binary for every helper
invocation. On Windows, launching 50 identical binaries from unique paths took
48.9 seconds, versus 1.6 seconds when reusing one path, so executable scanning
could exhaust the finalization budget under concurrent CI load.

The suite now creates one helper copy per required invocation name and reuses
it for the test process. This preserves the executable-name coverage while
removing about 2.1 GB of redundant writes and restores the malformed-record
test's normal 15-second finalization budget. On native Windows, the full capture
package fell from 71.7 seconds to 32.7 seconds.

title: Malformed token_usage panics GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages: blank transcript in UI while HTML export renders
body:
## Environment

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| agentsview version | v0.42.0 |
| OS / platform | Windows 10.0.22631.7517 (Windows 11 Enterprise, Build 22631) |
| Install method | not recorded |
| Agent | believed Claude Code — unconfirmed; the unguarded raw-usage write is in the Claude parser (see root cause) |
| Model | not recorded |

## What happened, and what did you expect

Selecting a session in the web UI (via `duckdb serve`) shows the session in the list, but the
transcript pane stays **blank**. Exporting that same session to HTML renders all
of its content correctly, so the messages are present and correctly linked in
the database.

The messages request fails at the network level — Chrome reports
`ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE`, not an empty result set. The server log shows the handler
panicking while **encoding the response**:

```
2026/09/03 18:55:33 GET /api/v1/sessions/<redacted>/messages
2026/09/03 18:55:33 http: panic serving 127.0.0.1:61982: error marshaling response for GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages 200: json: cannot marshal from Go jsontext.Value: unexpected EOF within "/messages/0/token_usage" after offset 396
goroutine 166 [running]:
net/http.(*conn).serve.func1()
    net/http/server.go:1939 +0xbb
panic({0x7ff71ae718b0?, 0x3c125c1822c0?})
    runtime/panic.go:859 +0x125
net/http.(*timeoutHandler).ServeHTTP(0x3c125c5561c0, ...)
    net/http/server.go:4061 +0x76c
go.kenn.io/agentsview/internal/server.(*Server).humaTimeout.func1.1(...)
    go.kenn.io/agentsview/internal/server/huma_routes.go:426 +0x2aa
github.com/danielgtaylor/huma/v2/wrap.func1(...)
    github.com/danielgtaylor/huma/v2@v2.39.1/chain.go:16 +0x25
go.kenn.io/agentsview/internal/server.humaRequestInfoMiddleware(...)
    go.kenn.io/agentsview/internal/server/huma_routes.go:176 +0x108
...
```

Expected: a session whose stored usage metadata is malformed should still render
its transcript. A single unusable metadata field should not take down the
endpoint.

## Root cause

One message row has a **truncated `token_usage` blob**. `jsontext.Value` defers
parsing until marshal time, so the bad value is stored without complaint and
only fails when the API encodes the response. Four things combine:

1. **`internal/parser/claude.go:2671`** stores gjson's raw slice with no validity
   check:
   ```go
   msg.TokenUsage = jsontext.Value(usageResult.Raw)
   ```
   A torn read of a JSONL line still being written yields a truncated `.Raw`.
   `IsValid()` is already used for exactly this purpose in
   `internal/parser/hermes.go:899` and `internal/parser/piebald.go:713`, but not
   here.

2. **`internal/db/validate.go`** — the centralized sanitize pass every write flows
   through explicitly excludes the field: *"Message.TokenUsage (jsontext.Value)
   and transient ToolResults.ContentRaw are intentionally not run through this
   pass."*

3. **`internal/db/messages.go:2143` and `:2748`** — the read path only checks for
   non-empty, never for validity:
   ```go
   if tokenUsage != "" { m.TokenUsage = jsontext.Value(tokenUsage) }
   ```

4. **`internal/server`** contains no `recover()`, so the marshal error becomes an
   unrecovered handler panic and `net/http` drops the connection.

HTML export escapes all of this because `humaExportSession` →
`db.GetAllMessages` → `generateExportHTML` renders server-side and never
marshals `token_usage`. That asymmetry is what makes the symptom look like a
frontend rendering bug.

The Windows correlation appears incidental to *how the row got truncated* (a
torn read during concurrent writes); the crash itself is platform-independent
and reproduces anywhere with the same data.

## Steps to reproduce

Store a truncated usage object on any message, then request that session's
messages:

```sql
-- against %USERPROFILE%\.agentsview\sessions.db
UPDATE messages
SET token_usage = '{"input_tokens":4,"cache_read_input_tokens":123'
WHERE session_id = '<some-session>' AND ordinal = 0;
```

```
GET /api/v1/sessions/<some-session>/messages   -> connection dropped, panic in log
GET /api/v1/sessions/<some-session>/export     -> renders fine
```

A Go-level reproduction, which fails on `main`:

```go
_, err := json.Marshal(struct {
    Messages []Message `json:"messages"`
}{Messages: []Message{{
    TokenUsage: jsontext.Value(`{"input_tokens":4,"cache_read_input_tokens":123`),
}}})
// json: cannot marshal from Go jsontext.Value: unexpected EOF within "/messages/0/token_usage"
```

## Workaround for affected users

```sql
-- back up sessions.db first
SELECT session_id, ordinal FROM messages
WHERE token_usage != '' AND json_valid(token_usage) = 0;

UPDATE messages SET token_usage = ''
WHERE token_usage != '' AND json_valid(token_usage) = 0;
```

Non-destructive: it blanks only unparseable metadata and touches no transcript
content.

## Suggested fix

Guarding one end is not enough. A write-side fix leaves already-corrupted
databases broken until a resync; a read-side fix alone leaves invalid blobs
being persisted and pushed to PG. Both:

- **Write seam** — have `ValidateAndSanitize` blank invalid `TokenUsage`,
  following the file's stated sanitize-don't-drop policy. Covers every agent and
  every write path (sync, upload, import) rather than only the Claude extraction
  site.
- **Read path** — drop an invalid stored value in `scanMessages` and
  `GetMessageByOrdinal`, so existing databases render without a resync.

Worth reporting the blanked count alongside the other sanitize counters
(`SanitizeStats`) so the drop is visible in the sync summary instead of silent.

One deliberate behavior change falls out of this: invalid usage no longer
rejects a session from artifact export, because the value can no longer reach
the segment encoder (`internal/db/artifact_export_load.go:118` loads through
`scanMessages`). Previously a single truncated blob cost the whole session its
export — `TestExportContinuesPastInvalidTokenUsage` asserts the old behavior and
needs updating. Export continuing past a genuinely un-encodable session stays
covered by `TestExportContinuesPastInvalidManifestValue` and
`TestExportContinuesPastDeterministicRejection`.

I have this implemented with tests at both layers plus a server-level regression
test asserting the endpoint returns 200 rather than panicking, and can open a PR
if useful.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: fix: blank invalid token_usage instead of panicking the messages API on every backend
body:
Fixes #1614.

A malformed `token_usage` blob takes down `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages`
entirely. `jsontext.Value` defers parsing to marshal time, so an invalid value
is stored without complaint and only fails when the API encodes the response:

```
json: cannot marshal from Go jsontext.Value: unexpected EOF within
"/messages/0/token_usage" after offset 396
```

`internal/server` installs no `recover()`, so `net/http` closes the connection
without a response. The session list still renders, the transcript comes back
blank, and exporting the same session to HTML still shows its content because
`humaExportSession` -> `GetAllMessages` -> `generateExportHTML` never marshals
the field. That asymmetry makes it look like a frontend rendering bug.

### Scope correction vs. the issue

Issue #1614 describes this as a SQLite-path bug. It is not — **all three
backends are affected**. The reporter was running `duckdb serve`, and
`internal/duckdb/messages.go` had no guard at all (it assigned
`[]byte(tokenUsage)` unconditionally, not even checking for empty).
`internal/postgres/messages.go` checked only for non-empty. Any mirror pushed or
built before this change still reproduces the panic through `pg serve` and
`duckdb serve`.

### Changes

**Write seam** — `ValidateAndSanitize` now blanks invalid `TokenUsage`. This is
the single path every session write passes through, so it covers every agent and
every write path (sync, upload, import) rather than only the Claude extraction
site at `internal/parser/claude.go:2671`, which stores gjson's `.Raw` verbatim.
A torn read of a JSONL line still being written yields a truncated `.Raw`;
`IsValid()` is already used for exactly this purpose in `hermes.go:899` and
`piebald.go:713`. Follows the file's stated sanitize-don't-drop policy: the
message keeps its content, only the unusable metadata is cleared.

**Read path** — `db.DecodeStoredTokenUsage` is exported and used by all three
scanners (`internal/db`, `internal/postgres`, `internal/duckdb`), so databases
and mirrors populated before the write guard render without a resync, and the
backends cannot drift again. This is the backend-parity rule in AGENTS.md.

**Observability** — `TokenUsageBlanked` is reported alongside the other
sanitize counters, so the drop shows up in the sync summary instead of being
silent. Silence is what made this hard to trace.

**Generated client** — regenerated after `token_usage_blanked` was added to
`SanitizeStats`; `npm run check:api` was failing the consistency gate.

### Behavior change worth a reviewer's attention

Invalid usage no longer rejects a session from artifact export, because the
value can no longer reach the segment encoder (`artifact_export_load.go:118`
loads through `scanMessages`). Previously one truncated blob cost the whole
session its export.

`TestExportContinuesPastInvalidTokenUsage` asserted that old behavior, so it now
describes an unreachable scenario. **I rewrote it rather than deleting it** —
it is now `TestExportSanitizesInvalidTokenUsage` and asserts the new outcome.
Export continuing past a genuinely un-encodable session remains covered by
`TestExportContinuesPastInvalidManifestValue` and
`TestExportContinuesPastDeterministicRejection`, both untouched and passing.
This is the one change here that flips an existing assertion, so it deserves
the closest look.

### Tests

Regression coverage at all three backends, each seeding the store directly
because the write seam now sanitizes the value before it could reach a mirror:

- `internal/db` — sanitize, idempotency, read-path, and `DecodeStoredTokenUsage`
  contract tests
- `internal/server` — endpoint returns 200 instead of panicking
- `internal/duckdb` — corrupts the mirror after push
- `internal/postgres` — writes the row directly (`pgtest` tag)

Every one of them was confirmed to **fail with its guard reverted**, reproducing
`cannot marshal from Go jsontext.Value: unexpected EOF`, so none are tautological.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go vet` | clean |
| `make test-short` | 48 packages passing |
| `make test-postgres` | passing against a real PostgreSQL instance |
| frontend `vitest` | 159 files / 2457 tests passing |
| `npm run check:api` | exit 0 |

One pre-existing failure is unrelated and untouched by this change:
`cmd/agentsview TestRunDaemonArtifactExchangeConnectsToIPv6LocalhostListener`.
It is environmental — the test listens on `[::1]` but rewrites the endpoint host
to `localhost`, and on hosts whose `/etc/hosts` maps `localhost` to `127.0.0.1`
only (the Debian/Ubuntu default, where `::1` is named `ip6-localhost`) the dial
lands where nothing is listening. Its skip guard covers IPv6 *listening* being
unavailable, not resolution. It fails identically at tag `v0.41.1`.

### Workaround for affected users on an existing install

The read-side guard means no data surgery is needed — but for anyone pinned to a
released build, blank the unparseable rows in whichever store is being served
(`sessions.db` for `serve`, `sessions.duckdb` for `duckdb serve`):

```sql
UPDATE messages SET token_usage = ''
WHERE token_usage != '' AND json_valid(token_usage) = 0;
```

title: feat(config): register alternate Claude and Codex homes
body:
Closes #1611.

Register alternate Claude and Codex homes through `claude_homes`, `codex_homes`, or Settings. AgentsView derives their native session directories and adds them to existing roots. `CODEX_HOME` controls Codex defaults, matching Claude's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Settings changes take effect after restart.

Configuration loading resolves local paths to absolute destinations and deduplicates transcript roots. Providers receive their metadata directories explicitly and use the same configuration for parsing, discovery, watching, freshness checks, and capture. There is no process-wide alias registry or import registration lifecycle.

Shared transcripts can read title indexes from several configured homes; the newest index wins. Sharing a sessions directory does not associate separate archive directories. HTTP remote exports carry title indexes and their root associations, and imports configure independent provider instances with the remapped paths.

HTTP mirror imports reconsider sessions named by an index before that index is removed or replaced. Remaining configured indexes supply titles; when none names a session, its last known title is retained. Protocol version 2 requires upgrading both HTTP sync peers together so older collectors cannot silently discard index associations.

title: duckdb serve renders no session transcripts in v0.42.0: empty token_usage fails response marshaling
body:
Supersedes #1614, which misdiagnosed this as a rare data-corruption bug. The
real defect is far broader: **`duckdb serve` cannot render any session
transcript in v0.42.0.** Every session, every user, every request. No corrupt
data is involved.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| agentsview version | v0.42.0 |
| OS / platform | Windows 10.0.22631.7517 (Windows 11 Enterprise, Build 22631) — not platform-specific, see below |
| Install method | not recorded |
| Agent | n/a — affects every agent |
| Model | n/a |

## What happens

Under `agentsview duckdb serve`, the session list renders normally but selecting
any session leaves the transcript pane blank. The request fails at the network
level (`ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` in Chrome), and the server log shows the handler
panicking while encoding the response:

```
http: panic serving 127.0.0.1:61982: error marshaling response for
GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages 200: json: cannot marshal from Go
jsontext.Value: unexpected EOF within "/messages/0/token_usage" after offset 396
```

`internal/server` installs no `recover()`, so `net/http` closes the connection
without a response.

Exporting the same session to HTML renders its content correctly, which makes
this look like a frontend rendering bug. It is not — `humaExportSession` ->
`GetAllMessages` -> `generateExportHTML` renders server-side and never marshals
`token_usage`.

`agentsview serve` (SQLite) and `pg serve` are unaffected.

## Root cause

`token_usage` is declared `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, so nearly every message row
holds `''`. The DuckDB scanner assigns it **unconditionally**, while the SQLite
and PostgreSQL scanners guard for the empty case:

```go
// internal/duckdb/messages.go:296  -> non-nil, ZERO-LENGTH jsontext.Value
m.TokenUsage = []byte(tokenUsage)

// internal/db/messages.go, internal/postgres/messages.go -> stays nil
if tokenUsage != "" { m.TokenUsage = ... }
```

A zero-length `jsontext.Value` is not valid JSON, and `omitempty` does **not**
skip it, so marshaling fails for the very first message of every response.

The truncated-blob theory in #1614 was wrong. A zero-length value produces a
byte-identical error message to a truncated one, which is what misled the
original diagnosis. Both stores on the reporting machine were queried and
contained **zero** rows with invalid `token_usage`:

```sql
-- 0 rows in sessions.db AND in sessions.duckdb
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages
WHERE token_usage <> '' AND NOT json_valid(token_usage);
```

## This is a regression, and it is datable

The DuckDB scanner line is unchanged since `ac7cef31` (#609, the original DuckDB
backend). It was harmless for two releases. What broke it is `b85eae5a`
("feat: adopt Go 1.27 JSON v2 semantics", #1475, 2026-08-21), which changed the
field type:

```go
- TokenUsage json.RawMessage `json:"token_usage,omitempty"`
+ TokenUsage jsontext.Value  `json:"token_usage,omitempty"`
```

v1's `omitempty` dropped a zero-length slice; v2's does not. Verified directly:

```
v1 json.RawMessage("") + omitempty -> [{}]           err=<nil>
v2 jsontext.Value("")  + omitempty -> err=json: cannot marshal from Go
                                          jsontext.Value: unexpected EOF
```

`b85eae5a` first shipped in **v0.42.0**, which is the first affected release.

## Why CI did not catch it

`frontend/e2e/duckdb-backend.spec.ts` is the entire DuckDB end-to-end suite. It
checks `/api/v1/version` and counts sessions in the list — it never opens a
session, so the one broken endpoint is never requested. With the bug present
that test still passes.

The Go side has the same shape of gap: `runDuckDBServe`, `openDuckDBServeStore`,
and `loadDuckDBServeConfig` are all at 0% statement coverage.

## Reproduction

```
agentsview duckdb push
agentsview duckdb serve
# open any session in the UI -> blank transcript
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/sessions/<any-id>/messages   # connection dropped
```

No special data required. A mirror built from a healthy SQLite archive is enough.

## Fix

PR to follow, from `tlmaloney:fix/duckdb-serve-blank-transcripts`:

- Export `db.DecodeStoredTokenUsage` and use it in all three scanners, so empty
  yields `nil` and invalid is dropped, and the backends cannot drift again
  (the backend-parity rule in AGENTS.md).
- Blank invalid `TokenUsage` in `ValidateAndSanitize` — defensive hardening for
  genuinely malformed provider payloads, which is a real but separate concern
  from this bug.
- Regression coverage that asserts on a **clean** mirror, plus two e2e tests
  that open a session and hit the messages endpoint. With the guard reverted the
  pre-existing e2e test still passes while all three new tests fail.

Severity note: this makes `duckdb serve` unusable for its primary purpose in
v0.42.0, so it may warrant a patch release rather than waiting on the next
minor.

title: fix(duckdb): restore session transcripts under duckdb serve (empty token_usage fails response marshaling)
body:
Fixes #1617. Supersedes #1614 (closed as misdiagnosed) and PR #1615, whose
description was written against that wrong diagnosis.

**`duckdb serve` cannot render any session transcript in v0.42.0.** Every
session, every user, every request. No corrupt data is involved.

## The bug

`token_usage` is declared `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, so nearly every message row
holds `''`. The DuckDB scanner assigned it **unconditionally**, while the SQLite
and PostgreSQL scanners guard the empty case:

```go
// internal/duckdb/messages.go:296  -> non-nil, ZERO-LENGTH jsontext.Value
m.TokenUsage = []byte(tokenUsage)

// internal/db/messages.go, internal/postgres/messages.go -> stays nil
if tokenUsage != "" { m.TokenUsage = ... }
```

A zero-length `jsontext.Value` is not valid JSON, and `omitempty` does **not**
skip it, so the very first message of every response fails to marshal:

```
json: cannot marshal from Go jsontext.Value: unexpected EOF within
"/messages/0/token_usage"
```

`internal/server` installs no `recover()`, so `net/http` drops the connection —
`ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE`, blank transcript. HTML export of the same session still
works because `humaExportSession` -> `GetAllMessages` -> `generateExportHTML`
never marshals the field, which is what makes it look like a frontend bug.

## A datable regression

The scanner line is unchanged since `ac7cef31` (#609) and was harmless for two
releases. `b85eae5a` ("adopt Go 1.27 JSON v2 semantics", #1475) changed the field
type:

```go
- TokenUsage json.RawMessage `json:"token_usage,omitempty"`
+ TokenUsage jsontext.Value  `json:"token_usage,omitempty"`
```

v1's `omitempty` dropped a zero-length slice; v2's does not:

```
v1 json.RawMessage("") + omitempty -> [{}]           err=<nil>
v2 jsontext.Value("")  + omitempty -> err=cannot marshal ... unexpected EOF
```

First affected release is **v0.42.0**.

## The change

`db.DecodeStoredTokenUsage` is exported and used by all three scanners: `""`
yields `nil`, invalid JSON is dropped, valid values pass through. One
implementation means the backends cannot drift again, per the backend-parity
rule in AGENTS.md.

That is the whole fix. The net diff against `main` touches three scanners, one
existing test, and adds test files — no schema changes, no new API fields.

Dropping invalid values (as opposed to empty ones) is defense at the point of
consequence: reaching the response encoder with one panics the handler, and
there is no `recover()` to catch it.

### On the write side: deliberately not included

Earlier revisions of this branch also validated `TokenUsage` in
`ValidateAndSanitize`. That has been reverted in `6ca8f5be`, because it defends a
path that does not exist:

- `internal/parser/claude.go:168` validates every line with `gjson.ValidBytes`
  and **skips invalid ones**, so a torn read never reaches
  `extractClaudeTokenFields`. gjson would return an invalid `.Raw` for a
  truncated line, but that line is discarded first.
- Every other parser builds usage through `json.Marshal` (devin) or derives it
  from an already-valid value (`claude_websearch`).

`TokenUsage` is valid by construction at every write site, so the counter that
change added could never increment — and it cost a public API schema field
(`token_usage_blanked` on `SanitizeStats`) plus its generated client entry for
no reachable benefit. Happy to revisit it as its own PR if you consider
"never persist known-bad data" worth the schema surface.

## Tests

The read-path tests plant corrupt data, so **none of them could catch this bug.**
The coverage that matters asserts on a pristine mirror:

- `TestDuckCleanMirrorMessagesMarshal` — an absent usage value must be `nil`
  rather than zero-length, and a clean mirror must marshal.
- Two e2e tests in `duckdb-backend.spec.ts` — open a session and assert the
  transcript renders; hit the messages endpoint directly, taking the session id
  from `GET /api/v1/sessions` so the assertion is not coupled to UI rendering.

Plus corruption-based coverage at all three backends, an endpoint-level
regression test, and a contract test for `DecodeStoredTokenUsage`.

**Every new test was confirmed to fail with the guard reverted**, so none are
tautological. Most tellingly, with the bug present the pre-existing e2e test
still passes while both new ones fail:

```
✓ DuckDB backend › serves fixture sessions in read-only mode
✘ DuckDB backend › renders a session transcript
✘ DuckDB backend › serves session messages over the API
      apiRequestContext.get: socket hang up
```

`socket hang up` is the dropped connection — the Node-level form of the
`ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` users see.

## Why CI missed it

`duckdb-backend.spec.ts` was the entire DuckDB e2e suite: it checked
`/api/v1/version` and counted sessions in the list, and never opened a session,
so the one broken endpoint was never requested. `runDuckDBServe`,
`openDuckDBServeStore`, and `loadDuckDBServeConfig` are also all at 0% statement
coverage on the Go side — worth a follow-up beyond this PR.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go vet` | clean |
| `make test-short` | 48 packages passing |
| `make test-postgres` | passing against a real PostgreSQL instance |
| `make e2e-duckdb` | 18 passed, 2 skipped |
| frontend `vitest` | 159 files / 2457 tests passing |
| `npm run check:api` | exit 0 |

One pre-existing failure is unrelated and untouched:
`cmd/agentsview TestRunDaemonArtifactExchangeConnectsToIPv6LocalhostListener`.
It listens on `[::1]` but rewrites the endpoint host to `localhost`, so it fails
on hosts whose `/etc/hosts` maps `localhost` to `127.0.0.1` only (the
Debian/Ubuntu default). Its skip guard covers IPv6 *listening* being
unavailable, not resolution. Fails identically at tag `v0.41.1`.

## One behavior change worth review

Invalid usage no longer rejects a session from artifact export, since the value
can no longer reach the segment encoder (`artifact_export_load.go:118` loads
through `scanMessages`). Previously one bad blob cost the whole session its
export. `TestExportContinuesPastInvalidTokenUsage` asserted that, so it now
describes an unreachable scenario; I rewrote it as
`TestExportSanitizesInvalidTokenUsage` rather than deleting it. Export
continuing past a genuinely un-encodable session stays covered by
`TestExportContinuesPastInvalidManifestValue` and
`TestExportContinuesPastDeterministicRejection`, both untouched and passing.

This follows from the read guard, not the reverted write-side change — verified
by disabling the write seam alone and confirming the rewritten test still
passes. It is the one change here that flips an existing assertion.

## Severity

This makes `duckdb serve` unusable for its primary purpose in v0.42.0, so it may
warrant a patch release rather than waiting on the next minor.

https://claude.ai/code/session_016BtS7hmmCDXSXvLRDxmkFx

title: usage daily fails on Windows: localTimezone returns non-IANA zone name
body:
`agentsview usage daily` fails with HTTP 500 on Windows because `localTimezone()` returns the Windows timezone name (e.g. `Eastern Standard Time`) instead of an IANA name (`America/New_York`).

The server rejects it:

```
> agentsview usage daily
error: usage summary: HTTP 500: {"error":"internal error"}
```

Hitting the endpoint directly with the Windows name confirms it:

```
GET /api/v1/usage/summary?timezone=Eastern+Standard+Time
400: {"error":"invalid timezone: Eastern Standard Time"}
```

Passing an IANA name works fine:

```
GET /api/v1/usage/summary?timezone=America/New_York
200
```

## Source trace

`localTimezone()` at `cmd/agentsview/usage.go:655` calls `time.Now().Location().String()`. On Windows, Go's `time.Local` resolves to the Windows zone name, not IANA. Every caller of `localTimezone()` sends this to the server or to `time.LoadLocation()`, which rejects it:

- `cmd/agentsview/usage.go:135` — `runUsageDaily`
- `cmd/agentsview/usage.go:245` — `runUsageStatusline`
- `cmd/agentsview/usage_cursor.go:85`
- `cmd/agentsview/activity.go:445`
- `cmd/agentsview/archive_query_backend.go:181`

`internal/timeutil/timeutil.go:85` has `BestEffortLocalTimezone()` which validates via `time.LoadLocation` before returning, so it would return `""` instead of the bad name. But `localTimezone()` doesn't use it, and `BestEffortLocalTimezone()` itself doesn't map Windows names to IANA either — it just falls back to empty string, which callers treat as UTC.

## Possible fix

Map the Windows zone name to IANA. Go doesn't expose a mapping, but the registry at `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Time Zones\<name>` has metadata, and the CLDR `windowsZones.xml` provides the canonical mapping. Alternatively, checking `$env:TZ` first (as `BestEffortLocalTimezone` does) and documenting the workaround would cover users who set it.

## Workaround

```
set TZ=America/New_York
agentsview usage daily
```

## Environment

- Windows 11 (build 26100)
- agentsview v0.42.0-9-ga5e1348cc-dirty
- Go embeds tzdata (`_ "time/tzdata"` at `cmd/agentsview/main.go:21`)

title: fix(cli): resolve Windows local timezone to IANA
body:
CLI usage and activity defaults now resolve the host timezone to a loadable IANA name, so Windows local-day reports reach the daemon with the correct calendar rules. Statusline date bounds use the same resolved timezone. Explicit timezone values and valid TZ overrides remain unchanged.

The shared time utility now uses an OS-aware resolver for Windows identities, including Eastern Standard Time, while retaining safe fallbacks for environments that cannot provide a named zone. This adds `github.com/thlib/go-timezone-local` for the Windows-to-IANA zone mapping. Daily usage, statusline usage, Cursor usage windows, direct activity reports, daemon activity requests, and stats metadata use one timezone decision.

This also allows `agentsview usage daily` to work on Windows; currently it returns `HTTP 500: {"error":"internal error"}`

Closes #1619

title: daemon stop cannot recover from a daemon that already died — leaves a permanent stale runtime lock blocking all writes
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.41.1 (commit a902515a2f8256ffb95716a2ca860c1887d35da5, built 2026-08-18T13:32:18Z)

### Install method

GitHub release binary

### OS / platform

Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 (x86_64)

### Which agent and version

n/a — bug is in agentsview's own daemon lifecycle management, not tied to any specific coding agent's session format

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened, and what did you expect

What happened: after running agentsview daemon stop, any command that touches the DB (agentsview view, agentsview sync) still fails with:

fatal: opening writable database: local daemon owns the SQLite archive but is not responding; refusing to write directly. Retry through the daemon or run `agentsview daemon stop` first

Running agentsview daemon stop again — following the error's own suggestion — fails too:

fatal: cannot confirm every writable agentsview daemon: pid <PID> (runtime record C:\Users\<user>\.agentsview\daemon.<PID>.json); no process was signalled; verify each process and terminate it manually before retrying

agentsview daemon status reports "agentsview daemon process is running but not responding to health checks" and still lists the same pid, even though tasklist confirms no such process exists on the machine anymore. The runtime record (daemon.<PID>.json) and the .lock files under ~/.agentsview/ are never cleaned up, because daemon stop's cleanup path requires successfully signalling the pid first — and a pid that's already dead can't be signalled, so cleanup is skipped instead of being treated as "already stopped."

Net effect: once the daemon process ends without a clean shutdown (crash, killed by OS/another tool, etc.), the tool gets permanently stuck. Neither the error's own suggested fix (daemon stop) nor retrying it resolves the state — only manually deleting the stale files under ~/.agentsview/ (daemon.<pid>.json, daemon.lock, db.write.lock, serve.background.lock) unblocks it.

What I expected: when the recorded pid no longer exists on the system, daemon stop (or the write-path ownership check) should treat that as "no daemon currently holds the archive" and clean up the stale runtime record automatically, instead of requiring the user to hand-delete files.

### Sample session file or snippet

```text
n/a — not a parse/render bug, no session file needed to reproduce.
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have the agentsview daemon running normally.
2. Cause the daemon process to end without a clean agentsview daemon stop (crash, OS-killed, etc.) — the runtime record file stays on disk pointing at the now-dead pid.
3. Run agentsview daemon stop → fails with "no process was signalled; verify each process and terminate it manually before retrying"; stale runtime record is not removed.
4. Run any command touching the DB (agentsview view, agentsview sync) → fails with "local daemon owns the SQLite archive but is not responding; refusing to write directly."
5. Repeat step 3 → same failure again, no way out short of manually deleting the stale files.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: Feature request: remove archived tool images and keep them excluded on future syncs
body:
### Problem / motivation

I use AgentsView to review conversations with coding agents. Image-heavy tool results can take far more disk space than the text I want to keep. I would like to remove images from the AgentsView archive while preserving conversation text and textual tool output, without changing the original agent transcripts or standalone image files.

A read-only inspection of my macOS desktop installation, AgentsView v0.41.1 (a902515a), found:

- `sessions.db`: 19.96 GB (decimal).
- Inline `data:image/...;base64,...` payloads in `tool_calls.result_content`: 9.57 GB.
- The same aggregate image payload size in `tool_result_events.content`: another 9.57 GB. Combined, these account for about 96% of the database file size.
- 2,239 image-bearing tool-result rows in each table, across 151 sessions. Most image bytes came from `exec` calls categorized as `Bash`.
- SQLite reported zero freelist pages, so reclaiming free pages alone would not address the main storage cost.

These measurements describe v0.41.1, not a claim that the latest development branch still duplicates tool results. Related: #1375 (storage maintenance/compression) and #1586 (duplicate tool-result storage). This request specifically concerns selective image retention, including after synchronization.

### Proposed solution

Please add an opt-in way to remove inline image payloads from existing tool results and persist that retention policy for future ingestion.

Desired behavior:

1. Let users select sessions, or the whole archive, and preview how many tool images and bytes would be removed before applying cleanup.
2. Preserve user/assistant text, textual tool-result blocks, tool-call metadata, and the order of the conversation. Replace image blocks with a small readable placeholder if needed.
3. Change only AgentsView's stored content. Leave original Codex/other agent transcripts and standalone image files untouched.
4. Apply the policy during incremental ingestion and full resync/rebuild, so images are not silently imported again from the original transcripts. A restart or upgrade should preserve the preference.
5. Support cleanup of existing archived content even when its original transcript file is no longer available; do not require deleting or reconstructing those sessions.
6. Provide a supported space-reclamation step and report the actual disk space recovered. A desktop setting/action and a CLI or API equivalent would make this accessible without manual SQLite edits.

The initial scope could be tool-result images only, leaving user-uploaded images separately controllable. Keeping image data remains useful for other users, so this should be opt-in.

### Alternatives considered

- `result_content_blocked_categories`: blocking `Bash` would also discard textual command output that is valuable for reviewing conversations. An image-only policy would be more precise.
- Session deletion / `agentsview prune`: removes more than the image payloads; in v0.41.1, `prune` also removes original session files.
- `db compact`: useful for reclaiming free pages, but the storage-maintenance documentation correctly distinguishes it from filtering live payloads.
- Manually editing the database once: does not establish a supported retention policy, so a later full reparse could restore images from source transcripts.
- Compression or deduplication: complementary improvements, but users should also be able to choose not to retain bulky tool images at all.

No transcript contents, screenshots, session identifiers, or private paths are attached.

title: fix(api): generate frontend client with Orval
body:
The frontend now generates its OpenAPI client with Orval 8 and splits endpoint
code by API tag while keeping each schema in its own file. This makes the
generated contracts easier to inspect, preserves concrete collection element
types, and removes the duplicate handwritten response types and unchecked
response casts that compensated for the previous generator.

Huma now describes ordinary Go slices as non-null arrays, matching the server's
JSON v2 encoding. A small fetch boundary retains server URL selection, bearer
authentication, structured API errors, cancellation, text responses, and
raw-sync response-header handling. Binary upload bodies pass through directly
as `Blob`.

Frontend development now requires Node 24.11 or newer. TypeScript remains on
6.0.3, and generation continues through the repository's `vp` workflow.

Closes #1610

title: fix(bench): stop the bench gate failing PRs on log noise and pooled-buffer noise
body:
The bench gate has been failing PRs that didn't touch anything it measures. Two reasons.

First, some benchmarks were logging straight to stderr while the testing package was halfway through printing a result line. When fixture seeding was slow enough to trigger the db package's "slow InsertMessages" warning, that line got wedged between the benchmark name and its numbers, and benchgate couldn't parse the result. A few benchmarks had been hand-silencing the logger to avoid this. The ones added in #1589 hadn't, so it started biting.

The fix is to stop writing output that bypasses the test. Benchmarks now send the global logger through `b.Output()`, and the two db test helpers that wrote to `os.Stderr` use `tb.Logf`. `testDB` handles it for every db benchmark, so there's nothing to remember when you add one. The testing package prints that output under the result line instead of inside it. Same rule now applies to all the gated packages, and the old `io.Discard` workarounds are gone.

Second, benchgate assumed bytes-per-op is deterministic and failed a PR if any single run came in 1.35x over the baseline. It isn't deterministic on the recall window path: `encoding/json` pools its encoder buffers per processor, so the same code swings between roughly 3.6 and 7.9 MiB per op depending on scheduling. That noise was tripping the gate on unrelated PRs. B/op now uses the same rule as sec/op: compare medians, and only fail when the difference is statistically significant. allocs/op keeps the strict worst-run check because that one really is stable.

I ran the full `make bench-gate` locally on this branch: 46 benchmarks, 5 samples each, every line parsed, no regressions.

Until this lands, the merge-base side of the comparison still runs the old code, so it can still produce a broken baseline. benchgate already treats that as partial and only gates what parsed on both sides. The Windows sync test failure on this PR is a pre-existing 20-minute timeout that also fails on main.

title: fix(copilot): report usage without shutdown summaries
body:
Resolves #1625

Copilot CLI sessions now report known token usage even when no usable shutdown summary exists. The parser reads richer per-call usage from the local session store. Later transcript responses supply per-message output fallback; within the overlapping time range, only positive per-model transcript output remainders are added as aggregate estimates. Known output remains in session totals when the model is unknown, without inventing a model-priced usage row.

Session-store rows use request-level pricing bands without requiring a transcript message ordinal. A trace through GitHub's published CLI confirms that separate model calls remain separate database rows even within one turn. The primary-source pricing research and producer trace are recorded in `docs/internal/copilot-pricing-research-2026-09-07.md`.

Store tokens remain catalog estimates. Transcript shutdown billing totals retain the existing authoritative-cost treatment; estimates are not claims about plan allowances, discounts, or invoice charges. Existing Copilot sessions reparse, and the usage cache rebuilds facts with the corrected request classification.

Copilot shared-store updates now use the same general strategy as OpenCode: scan lightweight session metadata, then read payloads and refresh the archive only for changed sessions. Transcript hashes are cached and restored across engine restarts after validating current file-change metadata. Per-session usage fingerprints use the producer's indexed latest usage-row ID because usage appends do not advance `sessions.updated_at`. One append among either 8 or 800 sessions refreshes one session, rereads no unchanged transcript payloads, and reads only that session's usage rows. Candidate enumeration still grows with session count.

Startup and the first sync after each five-minute interval verify all usage rows. Copilot also joins the daemon's 15-minute scheduled reconciliation, so edits or deletions below an unchanged latest row ID do not need another filesystem event to be detected. The threshold and scheduled cadence are separate; with regular ticks, deferred edits can wait up to 20 minutes. Shared-store timestamps no longer become transcript timestamps, and missing transcripts remain in the persistent archive. The freshness logic is in `internal/parser/copilot_store_freshness.go`.

The official CLI writer can lose a usage insert under SQLite write contention and still persist later calls. Producer experiments now establish that gap and confirm native assistant events generate timestamps. The parser no longer treats the latest store timestamp as proof that all earlier output was captured. If missing rows later appear, they replace the aggregate remainder rather than adding to it. This remains a conservative lower bound: extra store-only calls can mask missing output for the same model, and the remainder cannot recover a call's input count or pricing band. The research note and usage documentation record the evidence and limits.

title: Cursor CLI transcript fidelity: subagent linking, legacy tool results, turn timestamps, and richer local stores
body:
## TL;DR
agentsview currently omits some Cursor CLI data that exists locally, including subagent transcripts and legacy tool results, and presents inferred timestamps as exact.

The roadmap addresses these gaps in independent stages, starting with discovery and parent linking for `subagents/` transcripts. Existing archives gain child sessions on their next sync.

## Problem / motivation

agentsview imports Cursor CLI sessions from `~/.cursor/projects/<project>/agent-transcripts/`, but several gaps have different causes.

- Cursor writes delegated transcripts to `agent-transcripts/<parent>/subagents/<child>.jsonl`. Batch and streaming walks, watcher classification, find-by-ID, and the S3 layout filter currently reject this path, so parents show a `Subagent` call without the child session.
- One macOS sample held 814 parent transcripts, 109 of them delegating, and 967 children. 933 children still had a parent file on disk, and every child sat exactly one level deep.
- The legacy text parser discards parsed `[Tool result]` blocks.
- Parent and child user messages begin with a `<timestamp>` tag, but the parser discards it and uses file mtime as the exact session start and end. The sample contained tags in 810 of 814 parents and 964 of 967 children.
- Cursor names the delegation tool `Subagent`, while the taxonomy matches lowercase `subagent`, so these calls appear as `Other`.

A Cursor forum thread reports tool inputs present but outputs absent in CLI JSONL: https://forum.cursor.com/t/accessing-the-full-agent-transcript-in-cursor/157311. In the inspected transcripts, no `tool_result` blocks were present and every `tool_use` block had `"id": null`; JSONL alone therefore cannot join results to calls, and parent-child relationships must come from the file layout.

Cursor also stores data in the CLI `store.db`, IDE `state.vscdb`, protobuf `toolCallBinary` payloads, SDK databases, and `agent-tools/*.txt` sidecars. The IDE parser already reads `toolFormerData.result` and real timestamps, but it does not decode `toolCallBinary` or model subagent relationships.

Since #1589, blank `tool_calls.result_content` can indicate deduplication. The text remains in `tool_result_events`, and the API reconstructs it.

## Proposed solution

Implement the work as independently reviewable changes:

1. Accept `agent-transcripts/<parent>/subagents/<child>.jsonl` and `.txt` in every discovery route, including S3. Derive the parent from the path, mark the child as a `subagent`, retain the parent's project and cwd, and map the `Subagent` tool to the `Task` category.
2. Convert legacy `[Tool result]` blocks into tool-result events attached to the preceding call.
3. Parse each `<timestamp>` as a minute-precision turn timestamp with an explicit source marker. Stop presenting file mtime as exact session boundaries, and never fabricate seconds.
4. Link a parent's `Subagent` call to its child as a display hint only. Prompt equality is the only available signal: 835 of the 933 children with a parent file had an opening `<user_query>` that matched a parent `prompt` byte for byte. It cannot establish identity, and 34 children had no parent transcript file.
5. Add a Cursor CLI `store.db` provider. Read a WAL-consistent snapshot copy, traverse only the tree under `latestRootBlobId`, join results by native tool-call ID, and record timestamp sources.
6. Reconcile JSONL, `store.db`, `state.vscdb`, and SDK data by native IDs. Preserve source and confidence for each timestamp instead of silently choosing one value.
7. Decode `toolCallBinary` with a bounded protobuf reader and retain the raw blob while the decoder remains provisional.
8. Document result reconstruction so blank `result_content` is understood as possible deduplication.
9. Capture future runs with Cursor `postToolUse`, `afterShellExecution`, and `subagentStart` hooks. Hooks cannot restore older JSONL, so the earlier stages remain necessary.

All stages must treat live Cursor stores as read-only, retain unknown data while decoders are provisional, and avoid presenting inferred timestamps as exact.

## Alternatives considered

- Use hooks only. This is the cheapest option but leaves existing transcripts unchanged.
- Start with `store.db`. It contains more data but requires snapshot handling and a new provider before users see any improvement. Subagent discovery can use files agentsview already walks.
- Treat children with missing parent files as root sessions. This simplifies the sidebar but hides a real delegation. A later `store.db` provider may recover the parent.

## Evidence and references

- Counts above come from read-only inspection of one live `~/.cursor/projects` tree on macOS on 2026-09-04.
- agent-sessions derives parentage from the same path shape in `AgentSessions/Services/CursorSessionParser.swift` at `7a3f1f4`.
- cc_transcript_viewer does the same in `cursor_parser.py` at `4157ac3` and also strips the `<timestamp>` tag.
- vibe-replay at `f9d205d` reports zero Cursor delegations until it maps `Subagent` and reads `subagent_type`. It reconciles JSONL, `store.db`, `state.vscdb`, SDK data, and sidecars field by field.
- cursor-history at `aa0d469` traverses `store.db` from `latestRootBlobId`, joins by tool-call ID, and records that bubbles have no per-message timestamps.
- Related issues: #1515 for Cursor IDE discovery, #1418 for Cursor cwd, and #1589 for tool-result deduplication.

title: feat(parser): discover and link Cursor CLI subagent transcripts
body:
Cursor CLI subagent transcripts now appear under the session that launched
them. Agentsview imports `.jsonl` and `.txt` files from each session's
`subagents` directory, including files from S3 sources.

When several files share a session ID, full scans and file-change events now
choose the same copy within a project. A session's own transcript wins over a
copy under another parent. Otherwise, JSONL wins over text, with alphabetical
parent order breaking ties. Updating another copy no longer changes the
selected child's content or parent link. Review this selection logic in
`internal/parser/cursor_provider.go`.

Cursor's `Subagent` calls now count as Task calls. Existing archives re-parse
on the next sync; installations that only run `agentsview usage` need one
`agentsview sync` to import existing children. Discovery supports one
`subagents` level and links sessions rather than individual tool calls. A
child whose parent transcript is missing remains visible on its own.

title: perf: reduce recurring sync work and retain performance simulators
body:
Reduce recurring sidebar and session-sync work as archives grow. SQLite and PostgreSQL now compute sidebar totals in one filtered session scan. Claude duplicate lookup probes the requested session IDs, Codex discovery reuses directory-entry metadata, and unchanged skip caches avoid another database rewrite.

OpenCode active-session events no longer trigger container-wide source-existence checks for successfully resolved virtual members. Removed WAL/SHM sidecars also avoid those checks when the database still exists. Actual source removal continues to preserve archived messages and mark their sources missing. The retained missing-WAL regression drops from 188,690 allocations to 89. Coverage compares 8 and 800 OpenCode sessions for both WAL and SHM events; small deletion cases cover OpenCode, Kilo, MiMoCode, and Icodemate. Deleted members inside a surviving database become source-missing after the next successful authoritative reconciliation; an ordinary sidecar event does not promise immediate detection.

Includes the reusable `cmd/perfsim` simulator, available through `make perf-sim`: synthetic Claude/Codex JSONL and OpenCode SQLite/WAL sources pass through the real parsers, sync engine, archive, usage cache, and analytical queries. It covers cold ingest, steady appends, long sessions, reconciliation, child-only edits, and writer-close recovery; records profiles and build provenance; and supports source-only generation for isolated server experiments.

The investigation and sanitized daemon measurements are in `docs/internal/performance-investigation.md`; workload instructions are in `docs/internal/performance-simulator.md`. Earlier component timings are marked historical because their original temporary captures were lost. This PR does not claim a demonstrated idle-CPU reduction or optimize the remaining usage/search query hotspots.


The retained daemon capture is exploratory and has incomplete generator provenance: its exact uncommitted generator cannot be reconstructed. It must not be used as a reproducible benchmark or release gate.

title: Expose stable archive identity in session exports
body:
Session-export consumers can now distinguish a rebuilt database from a new
logical archive. Full resync changes `database_id`, so using it alone to scope
session IDs can make previously exported sessions appear new. AgentsView
already preserves a stable `archive_id`; this change publishes it in JSON
exports and the NDJSON metadata line.

Both IDs come from the same read snapshot as the session rows, including empty
results. The field is an additive extension to schema v6: existing session IDs,
usage, pricing, ordering, and cursor-reset behavior remain unchanged. Consumers
can use `(archive_id, session.id)` to recognize sessions across rebuilds while
keeping pagination tied to the database generation.

Synthetic tests cover rebuild preservation, pagination, empty exports, and
snapshot consistency. This does not add transcript content, revision ordering,
incremental change feeds, or deletion signals.

Focused export checks pass. The broader CLI suite encountered an IPv6-localhost
artifact-exchange test failure also reproduced on the unchanged main checkout.

title: fix(ci): allow PostgreSQL integration tests twenty minutes
body: Give PostgreSQL integration tests an explicit 20-minute timeout in both Makefile targets. CI run #5056 exhausted Go's default 10-minute package limit while tests were still progressing. This is a stopgap while the second PR in the stack reduces integration-test runtime.

title: perf(ci): keep the disposable PostgreSQL cluster in memory
body:
Run the CI PostgreSQL 18 service on a 4 GiB memory-backed filesystem to remove disk I/O from its repeated schema creation and teardown. The mount covers PG18's data directory and keeps normal PostgreSQL durability settings. The full suite used about 1.8 GiB locally, so a 1 GiB mount is insufficient.

Local PostgreSQL suite times varied from 64 to 76 seconds on tmpfs versus 68 seconds on disk; this does not establish a reliable end-to-end speedup. CI timing remains to be measured. Stacked on #1631, which raises the timeout as a stopgap.

title: Expose transcript revision and modification time in session exports
body:
Session exports now expose the existing `transcript_revision` and `local_modified_at` fields, so consumers can distinguish transcript corrections from session activity. Both are read alongside the session rows in the same transaction and appear in JSON and NDJSON. The counter is a decimal string to preserve integer precision; a missing local timestamp remains `null`.

This is additive to session-summary schema **v6**, with no database migration, writer changes, or cursor changes. Full-resync coverage verifies that identical transcripts preserve their counter and corrected message usage advances it even when activity time stays unchanged.

The contract describes a tuple of independent version evidence: transcript revision, project identity or its digest, and pricing timestamp plus digest, with local modification time retained for metadata and standalone usage-event changes. It is not a single total order: a usage-event rewrite need not advance the transcript counter, and a pricing change need not advance the maximum pricing timestamp. Modified-since discovery, tombstones, and journal-reset reconciliation remain follow-up work.

Export-focused checks, the database short suite, and lint pass. The full short suite encounters an IPv6-localhost artifact-exchange failure also reproduced with unchanged main sources.

Windows CI runs capture in the existing isolated SQLite-package matrix, removing competition from the bulk package suite while keeping all tests and deadlines unchanged. Two capture timeouts passed on an unchanged retry; isolation addresses package contention but does not establish it as the sole cause. The matrix supplies per-test timing diagnostics for any recurrence. This workflow change takes effect after merge because the PR dispatcher calls the workflow on `main`.

title: Codex gpt-reserve usage is unpriced despite being Luna Reserve
body:
### agentsview version

Current main (pricing catalogs already include `gpt-5.6-luna`; this is a reported-name miss, not a missing Luna row).

### Install method

Built from source

### OS / platform

macOS 27.0 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

Codex (ChatGPT / Codex app sessions that enter Luna Reserve)

### Which model(s)

`gpt-reserve` (producer id) / GPT-5.6 Luna

### What happened, and what did you expect

Codex rollouts that continue under Luna Reserve persist `turn_context.payload.model` as `gpt-reserve`. Agentsview copies that string onto later messages and usage rows.

`gpt-5.6-luna` is already in the Pydantic and LiteLLM-backed catalogs. `gpt-reserve` does not match that row, so Reserve turns show as unpriced / `$0` even when token counts are present.

This is expected Codex identity, not a parser bug. OpenAI documents Luna Reserve as extra GPT-5.6 Luna usage after regular allowance is exhausted, with internal model id `gpt-reserve`. It is a separately metered fallback mode, not a distinct list-price SKU.

Expected: keep the stored / reported model as `gpt-reserve` (do not rename it in the UI or merge it into `gpt-5.6-luna` in breakdowns). Resolve it for pricing the same way `k2d6-agent` maps to K2.6 in #1337, using the existing `gpt-5.6-luna` catalog rates across SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB.

These estimates would be Luna list rates, not an OpenAI invoice. Luna Reserve is a Plus/Pro allowance, not API credits. That is the same class of catalog estimate Agentsview already applies to ordinary Codex Luna turns.

Out of scope: display aliases, collapsing Reserve and Luna into one usage series, or asking Codex to stop writing `gpt-reserve`.

Local workaround until this lands: a `[custom_model_pricing."gpt-reserve"]` row keyed to the producer string.

### Sample session file or snippet

```json
{"type":"turn_context","payload":{"model":"gpt-reserve"}}
```

Agentsview then stores that model on subsequent messages. `internal/parser/codex.go` reads `payload.model` from each `turn_context` line.

First-party description: [Luna Reserve in Codex and ChatGPT Work](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001499-luna-reserve-in-codex-and-chatgpt-work).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Codex until regular usage is exhausted and Luna Reserve is active.
2. Continue a turn so the rollout writes `turn_context` with `model: "gpt-reserve"`.
3. Sync the session and open Usage (or `agentsview usage daily --agent codex --breakdown`).
4. Observe `gpt-reserve` listed as unpriced while `gpt-5.6-luna` rows in the same archive price normally.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: fix(pricing): price Codex gpt-reserve as GPT-5.6 Luna
body:
## Summary
- Codex Luna Reserve turns persist `gpt-reserve`. Usage reports kept that name unpriced even though `gpt-5.6-luna` is already in the catalog.
- Pricing now resolves `gpt-reserve` to the Luna catalog row at query time on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB. The archived model string is unchanged, and an exact custom `gpt-reserve` rate still wins.
- SQLite usage caches rebuild (format version 8) because the pricing digest only hashes catalog rows and would otherwise keep the old zero costs.

Fixes #1636.

Review focus: `internal/pricing/supplemental.go` for the fixed alias, `duckPriceModelCaseSQL` for DuckDB CASE parity, and the usage-cache generation bump in `internal/db/usage_cache_schema.go`.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: feat: add native Evener v2 session support
body:
Adds Evener as a native file provider, with local discovery, configuration, session names, reasoning, tools, model and token usage, and fork/subagent relationships in the existing AgentsView UI. Reads semantic transcript v2 and optional metadata without requiring a running Evener hub.

Reuses existing source, capture, and remote-sync mechanisms. Composite freshness covers metadata and the immediate fork parent; incomplete transcript writes preserve archived content. Verified copied fork history is omitted using the existing Codex policy. When the parent cannot be verified, child history is retained and shared usage can appear in both sessions.

Structured model-switch facts from [Evener #889](https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/evener/pull/889) update model context when available; older prose-only switches do not invent billing identities. Per-response identities take precedence. Older transcript formats are unsupported, and unsupported media is represented by a placeholder. Provider code, synthetic lifecycle fixtures, and pinned producer provenance are included; no storage migration or new transport is introduced.

title: perf(analytics): filter tool and skill calls before aggregation
body:
Filter candidate sessions and message rows by a padded UTC date window before aggregating tool and skill calls in SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB. Keep the existing resolver as the final date and hour filter, including session timestamp fallback for calls without a message timestamp. SQLite skill rows retain raw timestamp grouping so mixed fractional-second precision keeps the chronological last-used value.

Group tool rows by minute where the response carries no raw timestamp, and retain native timestamp maxima in PostgreSQL and DuckDB where their timestamp types preserve chronological order. The scaled benchmark measures reduced tools query work; dashboard request ordering remains separate.

Refs #1592

title: fix(frontend): defer analytics burst until sidebar hydration starts
body:
Defer the dashboard's initial analytics burst while the sidebar loads its index, then release it on the next task or after two seconds. The activity timeline changes long ranges to week granularity without starting an extra request during that deferral. Explicit refresh runs immediately, and unmount cancels the pending load.

AnalyticsPage and ActivityTimeline own the initial scheduling. The analytics store invokes the cancellation hook only when a full fetchAll refresh starts, so panel-specific controls leave the pending dashboard load eligible for release. Browser coverage confirms that visible-session hydration starts before analytics on head. The existing fixture paints within the visibility budget on both base and head, so it does not establish a first-paint latency improvement.

Refs #1592

title: OpenCode 2.0 parser fails because of new event-sourced SQLite schema
body:
## Environment

- AgentsView: `v0.42.0`
- Platform: macOS 26.6 on Arm64
- Agent: OpenCode CLI 2.0.0-beta.7 (and later)

## Problem

OpenCode 2.0 updates the SQLite storage layout.

The new schema replaces the `session` table with `session_v2`.
The new schema replaces the `message` table with `session_message`.

The `session_message` table uses an event-sourcing design.
Each record stores message deltas with an incremental `seq` integer.

AgentsView currently expects the legacy `session` and `message` tables.
Because of this schema change, AgentsView cannot find or parse OpenCode 2.0 conversations.

## Evidence

The OpenCode 2.0 SQLite schema contains these tables and columns:

- Metadata table: `session_v2`
  Key columns: `id`, `directory`, `title`, `model`, `cost`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Message stream table: `session_message`
  Key columns: `id`, `session_id`, `seq`, `role`, `content`, `parts`, `created_at`

The legacy tables (`session`, `message`, `part`) do not exist in fresh OpenCode 2.0 installations.

## Expected behavior

1. AgentsView checks the database schema.
2. If `session_v2` exists, AgentsView parses records from `session_v2`.
3. AgentsView reconstructs messages from `session_message` in ascending order of `seq`.
4. AgentsView keeps the existing parser for legacy OpenCode 1.0 databases that contain the `session` table.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched the existing issues.
- [x] I removed secrets and private data.

title: fix(search): derive snippet spans from the matched bytes
body:
The three content-search snippet paths end a match at `start+len(pattern)`. The start offset is already computed the careful way, rune by rune over the body, so a case mapping that changes UTF-8 length cannot shift it, but the end is taken from the pattern. Simple folding maps U+212A KELVIN SIGN, three bytes, to `k`, one byte, so a body holding the long form ends the span two bytes inside that rune, and a pattern holding it ends the span two bytes past the match.

`snippetBounds` and its PostgreSQL and DuckDB twins pad the span by 60 bytes and snap only the padding edges back to a rune boundary. Their loops stop when they reach the span, so none of them can repair a span that is not aligned. The 60-byte radius means no snippet is visibly wrong today, but rune alignment is the precondition those helpers and `secrets.RedactWindow` are written against, and the three copies of the same end expression are the kind of thing that drifts.

`CaseInsensitiveIndex` becomes `CaseInsensitiveSpan`: it returns the byte range the match actually covers in the body plus whether one was found, and each backend windows that range instead of recomputing an end from the pattern. Everything ASCII, which is nearly every query, gets the identical span it got before.

One behavior change comes with it. A miss now yields an empty span at the start of the body rather than a pattern-length one, so the fallback window is up to `len(pattern)` bytes shorter on its right edge. The substring paths reach that branch only if SQL `LIKE`/`ILIKE` matched where the Go search did not, and the Go fold is the wider of the two, so it is unreachable there; `FTSSnippetRange` already returned `0, 0` for its own start fallback.

Reviewer attention is best spent on `CaseInsensitiveSpan` and `foldPrefixEnd` in `internal/db/search_content.go`. The PostgreSQL and DuckDB call sites are the same two-line substitution, and I could not exercise their suites locally since both need services I do not have set up.

title: Codex guardian review threads indexed as root sessions since Codex switched thread_source to guardian_review
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.42.0 (commit ff8fb4e8, built 2026-09-01T19:37:06Z)

### Install method

Homebrew cask

### OS / platform

macOS 26.6 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

Codex CLI 0.153.x via Codex Desktop (any Codex ≥ 0.151 that writes `thread_source: "guardian_review"`)

### Which model(s)

n/a (parser lineage bug, model-independent)

### What happened, and what did you expect

Codex "guardian" auto-review threads are indexed as **root** sessions (`parent_session_id` and `relationship_type` empty) instead of as subagent children of the user thread that spawned them. They then appear as unrelated top-level sessions in the sidebar and in `session list`/`session search` results. On one archive this was 260 root rows out of 1,305 guardian rollouts; the older 971 (written by Codex ≤ 0.149) link correctly.

Cause: Codex changed the label it writes for guardian threads. Since openai/codex#40221 (2026-08-23, "Distinguish Guardian review threads from subagents") guardian rollouts carry `"thread_source":"guardian_review"` instead of `"thread_source":"subagent"`. Their `source` is unchanged: `{"subagent":{"other":"guardian"}}`, and the parent is in the top-level `parent_thread_id`. `codexSubagentParentThreadID` (`internal/parser/codex.go:140-148`) only reads the top-level `parent_thread_id` when `thread_source == "subagent"`:

```go
parentID := strings.TrimSpace(payload.Get("source.subagent.thread_spawn.parent_thread_id").Str)
if parentID == "" && payload.Get("thread_source").Str == "subagent" {
    parentID = strings.TrimSpace(payload.Get("parent_thread_id").Str)
}
```

Expected: a rollout whose `source` is a `subagent` object (any variant: `thread_spawn`, `review`, `compact`, `other`) and that carries a top-level `parent_thread_id` links to that parent regardless of the `thread_source` string. `thread_source` is a free-form label on the Codex side (unknown values are legal), so gating on one literal will break again on the next rename. Codex's own session listing never consults `thread_source`; it allowlists interactive `source` values (`codex-rs/rollout/src/lib.rs`, `INTERACTIVE_SESSION_SOURCES`).

Suggested fix: in `codexSubagentParentThreadID`, fall back to the top-level `parent_thread_id` whenever `payload.Get("source.subagent").Exists()` (or `thread_source` is any non-empty value other than `"user"`). Add the guardian shape to `internal/parser/codex_parser_test.go` (which today covers `thread_spawn`, the legacy `thread_source:"subagent"` top-level form, and a root) and to `internal/testjsonl`. A `dataVersion` bump is needed so already-indexed guardian rows relink on resync. Note `payload.session_id` on these rollouts is the root/tree id (equals the parent only at depth 1), so it must not be used as the parent edge.

Prior art in other Codex viewers that hit the same rename: deadeye636/switchboard#492 (fixed by keying on the presence of `source.subagent`), vladar107/claudescope (their `thread_source === "subagent"` check broke on the rename and was re-keyed on the structural marker), jazzyalex/agent-sessions.

### Sample session file or snippet

Three synthetic 5-line rollouts (no real ids, paths, or content). Place them under `<sessions>/2026/09/07/` with these names. Only the `session_meta` lines matter; the rest gives each rollout one user and one assistant message.

`rollout-2026-09-07T10-00-00-01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001.jsonl` (parent P, a normal user thread):
```jsonl
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:00:00.000Z","type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001","timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:00:00.000Z","cwd":"/home/user/project","originator":"Codex Desktop","cli_version":"0.153.1","source":"vscode","thread_source":"user","instructions":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:00:01.000Z","type":"turn_context","payload":{"cwd":"/home/user/project","model":"gpt-5.3-codex","turn_id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:00:02.000Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"add a retry to the fetch helper"}]}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:00:03.000Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Added a bounded retry loop to the fetch helper."}]}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:00:04.000Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"task_complete","last_agent_message":"Added a bounded retry loop to the fetch helper."}}
```

`rollout-2026-09-07T10-05-00-01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002.jsonl` (G1, guardian thread as written by Codex ≥ 0.151 — **the bug**):
```jsonl
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:05:00.000Z","type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002","timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:05:00.000Z","cwd":"/home/user/project","originator":"Codex Desktop","cli_version":"0.153.1","session_id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001","parent_thread_id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001","thread_source":"guardian_review","source":{"subagent":{"other":"guardian"}},"base_instructions":{"text":"<redacted guardian instructions>"}}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:05:01.000Z","type":"turn_context","payload":{"cwd":"/home/user/project","model":"gpt-5.3-codex","turn_id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b1"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:05:02.000Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"review the retry change for safety"}]}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:05:03.000Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"No blocking issues found in the retry change."}]}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:05:04.000Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"task_complete","last_agent_message":"No blocking issues found in the retry change."}}
```

`rollout-2026-09-07T10-10-00-01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000003.jsonl` (G2, control: identical except `thread_source:"subagent"` as written by Codex ≤ 0.149 — links correctly):
```jsonl
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:10:00.000Z","type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000003","timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:10:00.000Z","cwd":"/home/user/project","originator":"Codex Desktop","cli_version":"0.149.0","session_id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001","parent_thread_id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001","thread_source":"subagent","source":{"subagent":{"other":"guardian"}},"base_instructions":{"text":"<redacted guardian instructions>"}}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:10:01.000Z","type":"turn_context","payload":{"cwd":"/home/user/project","model":"gpt-5.3-codex","turn_id":"01a00000-0000-7000-8000-0000000000c1"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:10:02.000Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"review the retry change for safety"}]}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:10:03.000Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"No blocking issues found in the retry change."}]}}
{"timestamp":"2026-09-07T10:10:04.000Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"task_complete","last_agent_message":"No blocking issues found in the retry change."}}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Put the three files above under an empty Codex sessions tree, e.g. `/tmp/repro/codex-home/sessions/2026/09/07/`.
2. Use an isolated data dir so nothing else is indexed: `export AGENTSVIEW_DATA_DIR=/tmp/repro/data`, and in `/tmp/repro/data/config.toml` set `codex_sessions_dirs = ["/tmp/repro/codex-home/sessions"]` plus `disabled_agents = [...]` listing every other provider.
3. `agentsview sync` → `Sync complete: 3 sessions synced`.
4. `sqlite3 "file:/tmp/repro/data/sessions.db?mode=ro" "select id, parent_session_id, relationship_type from sessions order by id;"`

Result on v0.42.0:

| id | parent_session_id | relationship_type |
|---|---|---|
| codex:01a00000-…-000000000001 (P) | | |
| **codex:01a00000-…-000000000002 (G1)** | **(empty)** | **(empty)** |
| codex:01a00000-…-000000000003 (G2) | codex:01a00000-…-000000000001 | subagent |

G1 and G2 differ only in `thread_source`.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (no issue mentions guardian, `guardian_review`, or `thread_source`; nearest are #1246 and #1381, which added the current gate)
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files (all ids, paths, and text are synthetic)

title: sync writes in-place progress (CR + ESC[K) to non-TTY stdout; no quiet/summary mode
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.42.0 (commit ff8fb4e8, built 2026-09-01T19:37:06Z)

### Install method

Homebrew cask

### OS / platform

macOS 26.6 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

n/a for the bug itself. Observed when coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) run `agentsview sync` from their shell tool, where stdout is a pipe.

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened, and what did you expect

`agentsview sync` writes its in-place progress line with a carriage return and an erase-to-end-of-line escape on every refresh, unconditionally, even when stdout is not a terminal. In a pipe or a captured buffer nothing is overwritten, so every refresh is retained. On a large archive the captured output scales with the number of sessions: one sync captured by a coding agent's shell tool on a ~6,600-session archive came back as ~700 KB of `\r  N/6639 sessions (x%) …\x1b[K` refreshes, which the agent's context window then had to absorb or truncate. The final `Sync complete` summary is at the very end, after the flood.

Source: `cmd/agentsview/sync.go:315` and `:325` both do

```go
fmt.Fprintf(p.w, "\r  %s\x1b[K", formatSyncProgress(progress))
```

with no terminal check. The codebase already gates interactive output on `term.IsTerminal` elsewhere (`cmd/agentsview/session_search.go:243`). `sync` has no `--quiet`, `--format json`, or summary-only flag (`cli.go` registers only `--full/--host/--target/--user/--port`).

Expected: when stdout is not a terminal, either print line-oriented progress at a coarse cadence (or nothing) and the final summary, or provide a flag such as `--quiet` / `--format json` that emits only the summary. The `\r…\x1b[K` in-place refresh should be reserved for a TTY.

### Sample session file or snippet

Not session-specific. Captured output of `agentsview sync > out 2>&1` against a 3-rollout corpus, shown with `cat -v`:

```
Preparing sync...
Running sync via daemon...
^M  Discovering sessions^[[K^M  0/3 sessions (0%) · 0 messages^[[K^M  1/3 sessions (33%) · 0 messages^[[K^M  2/3 sessions (67%) · 0 messages^[[K^M  3/3 sessions (100%) · 0 messages^[[K^M  3/3 sessions (100%) · 6 messages^[[K
Sync complete: 3 sessions synced in 99ms
```

304 bytes, 6 refreshes for 3 sessions. `sync --full` adds a second progress printer for the resync phases (2,447 bytes on the same corpus).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Any archive; a daemon may or may not be running (the CLI proxies to it either way).
2. `agentsview sync > /tmp/sync.out 2>&1`
3. `cat -v /tmp/sync.out | head -c 400` shows the `^M … ^[[K` refreshes; `wc -c /tmp/sync.out` grows with session count.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (no open issue on non-TTY progress output or a quiet mode for `sync`)
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: Show the Codex config profile used by each session
body:
## Problem / motivation

Codex can be started with `-p, --profile <CONFIG_PROFILE_V2>`, which layers `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` over the base config. When several profiles are used for different providers, models, permissions, or workflows, agentsview currently gives no way to tell which profile produced a session.

The current normalized session model has no profile field, and the Codex parser does not extract one. More importantly, current Codex rollout `session_meta` does not persist the selected config profile name. It records fields such as cwd, originator, cli_version, source, and model_provider, so agentsview cannot reliably recover the profile from the transcript alone.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional normalized session profile field and expose it for Codex sessions in the session sidebar/detail view and through the session HTTP/CLI JSON contract.

When Codex provides an authoritative profile name in persisted session metadata, import it directly. Existing sessions and sessions whose source format does not provide a profile should leave the field empty or show Unknown.

Please also document the provenance and compatibility boundary for this metadata. If implementation depends on an upstream Codex format change, track that dependency rather than inferring a profile.

Useful UI follow-ups would be filtering or grouping sessions by profile once the metadata is available.

## Alternatives considered

Inferring the profile from model/provider/settings is not reliable because multiple profiles can resolve to identical effective settings, command-line `-c` overrides can change them, and profile files can change after a session was created.

Reading the currently selected config file is also insufficient: agentsview observes historical rollout files and generally does not know the original process arguments. A capture-only solution would not cover normal background discovery or existing sessions.

Until Codex persists the selected profile name, the only dependable workaround is to encode the profile manually in a session title or keep separate Codex homes/session roots.

title: fix(parser): preserve OpenCode v2 tool-result file payloads

OpenCode v2 tool results now retain embedded file payloads. Inline images use Agentsview's existing image format and keep/drop policy. PDFs and other files retain their complete URI, MIME type, and optional filename in raw result JSON. External references are retained without fetching them.

File-bearing results preserve text and files in order, including output attached to failed tools. Text-only results keep their existing format. This extends the v2 reader from #1687; data version 108 makes existing imports eligible to recover omitted files. PDF payloads are retained in raw results; this change does not add a PDF preview.

title: feat(mcp): add session search date filters and contextual search guidance
