title: fix(deps): complete the Mermaid 12 upgrade
body:
Upgrade Mermaid to 12.0.0 and pin Kit UI to the merged update in https://github.com/kenn-io/kit-ui/pull/64. Both packages require that exact Mermaid release. The regenerated lockfile fixes clean installs. Kit UI leaves layout and look unset, allowing Mermaid's native defaults and author-selected settings.

Adopt the newer Kit UI control state tokens and update tests for selector labels that now include their selected value. The Kit UI update also fixes false disabled-style findings for hover selectors.

Fix the Windows Pi resume test by allowing tildes in directory names. The test still checks the complete command and now exercises a tilde-containing path on every platform.

title: feat(timing): separate measured tool time from unattributed turn time (#1753)
body:
Session timing now shows where a turn's time went. Session Vitals separates measured tool execution from the time the archive cannot assign to a phase.

The payload comes from one reducer shared by SQLite, PostgreSQL and DuckDB. It clips and merges paired execution intervals, removes the old whole-turn call fallback, and carries the remainder as unattributed time. Existing transcript and navigation behavior stays intact.

The timing route and live session updates carry the same fields. The UI links each activity row to its transcript ordinal. Claude rows without stored phase endpoints remain unattributed, so the view does not infer model time from content flags.

Paired `tool_execution` events currently come from the Copilot, Grok and OpenCode Review parser paths. Closed child session boundaries also measure linked Task calls. Calls without either boundary remain unknown, and their unresolved turn time stays unattributed.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Session Vitals before timing activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rodboev/agentsview/f0d9734f6/agentsview-1753-before.png) | ![Session Vitals with timing activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rodboev/agentsview/f0d9734f6/agentsview-1753-after.png) |

Screenshots show the previous completed-turn and timeline view beside the new Turn activity section with measured tool time and unattributed time.

Refs #1753

title: feat(server): add bounded image byte cache with age eviction
body:
AgentsView keeps recently served image bytes in memory for up to seven days. Reopening a stored image can reuse bytes already read by the asset route, while the durable copy stays under dataDir/assets.

Entries expire seven days after creation. The cache holds 64 entries and 64 MiB, clears with the daemon, and falls back to the durable file after expiry or a source change. Asset validation and response headers stay the same. The cache is built on jellydator/ttlcache/v3, the same library Forge uses, which owns the expiry, the entry cap, and the byte bound; a one-minute sweep releases expired bytes.

The browser owns its HTTP cache and Blob URLs, so hit rates and visible latency remain unmeasured. Builds on PR 1696 (https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/1696) and PR 1729 (https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/1729).

Refs #1718


Also carried on this branch: the roborev review guidelines gain a rule against recommending gates in front of reads of user-owned files.

title: docs: update 0.43.0 release notes and screenshots
body:
Document the published 0.43.0 release with source-checked notes and contributor acknowledgements. Rewrite the past two months of release notes in plain language, update the feature guides, README, and website, and record the documentation style in AGENTS.md. The changelog identifies 0.43.0 as released on September 14, 2026; the documentation index explains that main may contain newer changes.

Refresh all 89 screenshots, including image retention and cleanup, additional agent homes, in-session search results, and remote resume commands. The images live on the orphan [docs-generated-assets branch](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/commit/2be5bf38a69825afdd2a8ed9166fee675536c2e6). The release workflow requires fresh screenshots and a local website review before opening a documentation PR.

title: feat(frontend): separate provider and UUID path segments in session links
body:
Session links now put the provider and UUID in separate path segments, which gives the UUID its own replaceable URL segment.

The frontend RouterStore writes the new format, reads existing encoded links, and keeps bare IDs in one segment. Existing link consumers continue using its URL builder, with no backend or configuration changes.

The current workaround removes %3A before pasting. This slice covers URL serialization and parsing. Ctrl/Cmd+G remains a separate change.

Refs #1768

title: feat(frontend): add ctrl/cmd+g session navigation
body:
Ctrl/Cmd+G opens a "Go to session" dialog where you can paste a session ID or UUID and press Enter to open it. This gives session navigation a direct keyboard path.

The frontend resolves an exact opaque session ID or a bare UUID through the existing endpoint, then routes the stored ID through the session and router stores. The input follows the shared find field focus treatment, and open-find G keeps next and previous match behavior.

The dialog uses shared controls and the session-ID resolver from PR https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/933. URL formatting stays with slice 1.

![Go to session dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rodboev/agentsview/screenshots/agentsview-1768-2-after.png)

Refs #1768

title: fix(sync): replicate archived sessions despite ingestion failures
body:
Healthy archived sessions now continue to PostgreSQL when a daemon-owned incremental push encounters a local ingestion failure. Previously, one broken source could leave the entire mirror stale despite successful imports from other sources.

The push returns its actual result, including row failures and deferred vector work, while local ingestion errors remain logged and retryable. A completed copy no longer repeats at the watcher debounce interval solely because ingestion was incomplete. Full resyncs and scoped watcher batches retain their existing completion requirements. The shared coordinator also applies to daemon-owned DuckDB pushes.

title: fix(kilo): import projections without a sequence column
body:
Kilo sessions now import when their database has a `session_message` table without `seq`. Previously, discovery queried that missing column and rejected the entire database, even when its conversations used the legacy message and part tables.

The shared OpenCode parser detects the projection ordering format. It reads older projections in the producer’s `time_created`, `id` order, retains unmatched legacy messages, and includes the ordering key in change detection. Databases with `seq` keep their existing behavior. The provider evidence entry links the released reader and migration that establish the two formats. No source database or archive migration is needed.

title: feat: add Augure CLI/Desktop agents, agent remap rules, and duplicate-session suppression
body:
## Background: the Augure agents

[Augure](https://augureai.ca) ("the sovereign Canadian coding agent") ships
three clients, and each stores its sessions in a different place:

- **Augure CLI** — a rebranded fork of codex-rs (the same situation as
  TraeX, which agentsview already supports). It writes byte-compatible
  Codex rollout JSONL under `~/.augure/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/`. Adding it is a
  registry entry plus a relabel of the shared Codex-format provider onto an
  `augure:` ID namespace, mirroring `internal/parser/traex.go`.
- **Augure Desktop v2** (goose-based, pre-beta) — an Electron shell whose
  conversations land in the **standard Goose store**
  (`~/.local/share/goose/sessions/sessions.db`). Nothing new to parse: the
  existing `goose` agent already ingests them. The only decision is labeling.
- **Augure Desktop v3** (current beta) — replaced the goose core with a fork
  of Hermes Agent (Nous Research). The runtime renames Hermes's `~/.hermes`
  to `~/.augure-desktop` and writes a Hermes-schema `state.db`
  (`schema_version` 26 on an independent version line). The existing Hermes
  state-DB parser already handles the shape, so this reuses the Hermes
  provider through a spec seam, relabeling onto `augure-desktop:`.

All three findings were verified against live installs (CLI 1.0.6, Desktop
2.x, Desktop 3.0.0-beta.7) on 2026-09-11; details are recorded in
`docs/internal/session-format-sources.md`.

## Why the enhancements are needed

**Agent support alone is not enough — the stores overlap.** Desktop v3
migrates conversations out of the shared Goose store without deleting them,
and early Augure CLI releases wrote Codex-format rollouts into the stock
Codex store. Measured against a live archive on 2026-09-14:

- 113 of 114 `goose` sessions have an `augure-desktop:` twin with the same
  `started_at` second — the same conversation ingested twice from two
  stores.
- 24 of those `goose` sessions carry Augure-hosted model slugs
  (`ossington-*`, `rosedale-*`, `tofino-*`); 90 have none and are genuine
  Goose.
- 5 archived `codex` sessions carry Augure model slugs.
- The twins are **partial duplicates**: the old-store copy of
  `goose:20251023_10` has 5 messages / 3,067 output tokens; its
  `augure-desktop:` twin has 4 messages / 0 tokens — migration copied the
  transcript but not the usage. The inverse also exists: a session resumed
  in the new client after migration makes the new copy a prefix plus
  continuation.

Investigation proved **no schema-level discriminator exists** in
the Goose store, so the parser cannot separate Augure-hosted sessions from
genuine Goose ones. The user can: message model slugs are a reliable
post-parse signal. Hence the three enhancements on this branch:

1. **Agent remap rules** (`feat(data): add agent remap rules…`) —
   user-defined rules (source agent + optional model GLOB + optional ID
   prefix) → target agent, applied to archived sessions with preview/apply
   and a consistency token, mirroring the existing worktree project-mapping
   feature. The parser phase stays untouched; users tune classification to
   their own setups (e.g. `goose` + `ossington-*|rosedale-*|tofino-*` →
   `augure-desktop`). Rules are stored in a new `agent_remap_rules` table,
   served through settings routes, applied incrementally on new sessions,
   and mirrored to PostgreSQL/DuckDB.
2. **Duplicate-session groups** (`feat(data): … duplicate-session
   suppression`) — client migrations duplicate sessions across stores, so
   the same interaction can be counted twice. This adds deterministic
   duplicate-group detection (same machine + started second + first-message
   prefix), a **presence-aware suppression** rule in the usage cache so a
   duplicate is only suppressed when its canonical copy actually carries
   usage (never losing usage that exists on only one side), UI indicators
   (sidebar badge `⧉2`, detail banner, Data-page review card), and PG/DuckDB
   parity. Nothing is ever deleted — the archive's hard rule — roles are
   re-derived on every rebuild.
3. **Typeahead selectors on the remap form** (`feat(data): add typeahead
   selectors…`, `fix(data): show raw slug case…`) — the remap form
   originally asked for raw slugs (`goose`, `augure-desktop:`, ID prefixes)
   as free text; a typo silently creates a rule that matches nothing. The
   source/target/prefix fields are now searchable dropdowns fed by the
   archive's agents (`/api/v1/agents`) merged with the built-in catalog,
   sorted by session count, with free-text preserved for agents outside the
   catalog and prefix rows displayed in the actual ID-prefix case
   (`goose:`), matching what the matcher compares against.

## Reviewer notes

- The remap and duplicate-group work is agent-agnostic — nothing in
  `internal/db`, `internal/sync`, or `internal/server` reads Augure code;
  the Augure agents merely motivated it.
- Parser behavior for existing agents is unchanged; the Codex/Hermes
  providers are reused via relabel seams, following the established TraeX
  pattern.
- The usage-cache format version was bumped (v12 → v13) for the suppression
  change, per the divergence contract in `docs/agents/storage.md`.
- Commit `502dc3f2` is large because the remap rules and duplicate-group
  features landed together.

## Verification

- `go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean; full db suite green with `fts5`
  tags; server/sync suites green.
- Frontend: `npm run check` 0 errors / 0 warnings; `npx vitest run` 164
  files / 2,733 tests pass, 0 unhandled errors; `npm run check:api` clean.

title: Expose date and project scope in search
body:
Search now shows its project scope and date range in the command palette. Users can broaden an inherited project filter to All Projects without changing the sidebar, or narrow Full text, Semantic, and Hybrid searches to relative, calendar, or custom dates.

The date range survives retries and mode changes and resets when the palette closes. Dates filter overlapping session activity; Semantic and Hybrid use the browser timezone, while Full text retains UTC behavior. Escape closes an open picker before closing the search palette.

title: fix(sync): ignore transient lock file events
body:
## Summary

Transient lock-file replacement events are now ignored by the filesystem watcher. The default watch exclusions include `*.lock*`, and fsnotify events are checked against exclusions during translation for create, write, remove, and rename operations.

This covers lock staging files such as `session.jsonl.events.lock` and `session.jsonl.events.lock.<uuid>.pending`. It prevents agentsview from treating another process's lock-file replacement as a session change while the lock is active, without suppressing normal session-file events.

The change is intentionally generic watcher/configuration behavior. It does not introduce or modify Factory/Droid CLI integration, provider parsing, or session-format code, so those changes can land separately.

This is a prerequisite for the correct implementation of #1358; it references the issue without closing it.

> Note: Yes, this was generated by OpenAI Luna, however it referenced real issues that I am seeing from the linked ticket above. I do believe that ignoring the `.lock` files from tool's like Droid (My use case) and others would be beneficial, as it would prevent breakages to active sessions that are trying to run in those TUI's.

Thanks

title: fix(daemon): show database upgrade progress before syncing
body:
Daemon startup now reports database opening, schema and index updates, and column migrations before each stage runs. Previously, an upgrade could spend minutes showing only “initial sync” before any session counters appeared.

Both worker and in-process startup publish these stages immediately and record their elapsed times in `serve.log`. A required full resync is announced as soon as the database check detects it. This makes the wait explainable; it does not shorten migrations or change when the server becomes ready.

title: Cannot push model and token data into message table with "pg push" when using vscode copilot as AI asistant
body: ### agentsview version agentsview v0.42.0 ### Install method install.sh / install.ps1 ### OS / platform windows11 ### Which agent and version VSCode-win32-x64-1.137.0 （GitHub Copilot Chat） ### Which model(s) glm5/qwen3.7/deepseek4pro ### What happened, and what did you expect After using VSCode Copilot for Q&A, I tried to push data to PostgreSQL using pg push, but found that both the model and token fields in the message table were empty. However, using OpenCode CLI, I was able to successfully store values in the model and token fields ### Sample session file or snippet ```text ``` ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Checklist - [x] I searched existing issues - [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: fix(parser): record the model on vscode-copilot assistant messages
body:
VS Code Copilot chat sessions persist the serving model per request, in `modelId` and in `result.metadata.resolvedModel`, but only the per-turn usage event read it. Assistant messages were appended without a `Model` even though the provider advertises per-message model support, so mirrored message rows carried an empty model column.

Both consumers now resolve the model through one helper: `result.metadata.resolvedModel` when the request carries metadata, otherwise the request's prefixed `modelId`, normalized the same way the usage event already normalized it. The token columns are unaffected and stay empty by design for this format: it records only per-turn token totals, which the parser emits as usage events rather than per-message values.

The test covers a turn whose model comes from metadata, a turn whose model falls back to `modelId`, and a per-turn switch between two models, which is why the value belongs on the message and not on the session.

Locally, one unrelated parser test fails on the branch base in this sandbox (`TestParseWorkBuddySessionUsesCwdProjectAndFileSessionID`).

Fixes #1777

title: fix(parser): restore parent links for native Pi sessions
body:
Native Pi branches whose headers contain only a `parentSession` path appear disconnected because the parser ignores that field.

This reuses Prime Agent's resolver to read the parent file's session ID. `branchedFrom` keeps priority, and OMP/Prime Agent handling remains unchanged. Regression tests cover discovery through parsing, filename/header-ID mismatches, POSIX/Windows paths, and precedence. Pi's format evidence has been reverified.

Review `internal/parser/pi.go` for parent resolution and `internal/db/db.go` for reparsing. The version bump applies across providers without deleting the archive, increasing work on the next sync. If the parent file cannot be read, filename fallback may still leave the link unresolved.

The short test suite has three failures also reproduced on the upstream base: IPv6 artifact exchange and two OpenCode sync tests.

title: MCP search by session UUID
body:
MCP search cannot look up a session by its UUID. The current search filters are provider, project, model, and time range. Finding a specific session requires paging through results and matching manually.

Session UUIDs are how coordinator sessions reference other sessions. A Claude Code session managing several Codex sub-sessions identifies each by UUID. Looking one up through AgentsView MCP today costs multiple round-trips and full result payloads. Reading the JSONL from disk is cheaper, which defeats the purpose of the MCP search layer.

Add a UUID filter to the MCP search endpoint. A query with a UUID returns that session directly, no pagination. This is the most specific lookup possible and should be the cheapest.

title: feat(cli): include browser links in session results
body:
Session list, detail, sync, and search JSON now include `web_url`, and MCP preserves it in session results. Discovered connections use the running daemon’s effective browser URL, computed from its final startup config. Explicit HTTP connections use the selected server. Links preserve the existing provider/session route and base path and omit credentials while API requests keep their authentication.

The field is derived for output and is excluded from archive content and manifest identity. Direct database reads omit it when no browser server is selected.

title: Export reporting history and conversation changes
body:
Adds two commands for reports built from the local AgentsView database:

- `export range` finds the earliest recorded activity and the latest complete reporting hour.
- `export conversations` lists new, edited, and deleted user and assistant messages, then lets you fetch only the text you need.

Conversation export reads normalized database records for every agent, including imported archives and sessions whose source files are gone. It preserves stored message text and omits separate tool and reasoning fields.

Readers can save their progress and fetch changes next time. Archive rebuilds tell readers to refresh their saved state. Storage policies apply, and the export keeps only the latest message version.

The Codex parser also corrects prompts mixed with injected context. Existing archives undergo the normal startup resync to update stored text, previews, and message counts. Sessions whose source files are gone retain their archived content.

title: Support resuming pi sessions
body: ### Problem / motivation Resume a session for a pi agent ### Proposed solution In the same way as other agents, eg: codex ### Alternatives considered _No response_

title: feat(mcp): look up sessions by UUID
body:
A session UUID passed to `search_sessions` returns one metadata row, including active sessions. Full stored IDs use exact lookup. Bare UUIDs resolve through literal agent `:` or host `~` suffixes; ambiguous or missing IDs return errors.

An optional server lookup mode resolves those suffixes before limiting results. The ID takes precedence over search filters and pagination. `get_session_overview` remains available for full-ID message previews, while keyword search keeps its existing behavior.

Closes #1780

title: Fix discovery and API requests for servers mounted below a base path
body:
PostgreSQL and DuckDB servers mounted with `--base-path` publish correct browser links but remain undiscoverable because probes and API requests omit the prefix. Use the mount path from the effective runtime browser URL for discovery and API requests while retaining the local API host and port.

Follow-up to #1781, which merged while this approved fix was in progress. A real prefixed-server test verifies discovery and API requests with and without authentication.

title: test(e2e): leave runner capacity for WebKit
body:
The self-hosted end-to-end job could start eight Playwright workers on its eight-CPU runner. The Go server and browser processes then had no reserved capacity. Under load, WebKit crossed five-second readiness windows across unrelated tests and stretched the suite from 1.9 to 5.1 minutes.

This caps self-hosted CI at four workers and gives CI assertions 15 seconds to observe asynchronous UI state. Message-content tests now open their known fixture by direct route, so responsive sidebar visibility cannot block coverage of message rendering. Recent Edits also drops an unrelated sidebar wait, and the virtualizer readiness check uses the shared CI timeout.

title: CLI support for activity insights
body:
Today the Activity Insights are exposed via the HTTP API, but not through the CLI. This has come up before: #67, which was closed by #860 with the CLI portion explicitly deferred.

I'd love if there was CLI support for generating and inspecting insights so I could fold it into my own automated tooling.

title: fix(quality): keep signal excerpts on rune boundaries
body:
On the Quality page, a signal example whose excerpt runs past 180 bytes can render with a black diamond replacement character at the end instead of its last whole character. A message like "Fix this: 这个函数返回错误的结果..." comes back with the final character destroyed. The excerpt has one consumer, the signal sessions panel in `frontend/src/lib/components/quality/QualityPage.svelte`.

`truncateExcerpt` in `internal/db/analytics.go` cuts with a plain byte slice, `s[:max-3] + "..."`. Its only caller is `BuildSignalExamples`, which passes 180, so the cut always lands on byte 177. When byte 177 is a continuation byte the returned string is invalid UTF-8, and `encoding/json` rewrites the split character into U+FFFD on the way to the API. 177 is a multiple of three, so a pure Han excerpt happens to survive; a ten-byte ASCII lead such as "Fix this: " shifts the alignment and breaks it, four-byte emoji break on a different lead, and two-byte Cyrillic on a third. The content arriving here is already valid UTF-8 through `db.SanitizeUTF8`, so the invalid bytes are introduced at this one line.

Both slices now back up to the nearest rune start. That walk already existed inline in `ClampModel`, so it moves into a `runeBoundaryAtOrBefore` helper in `internal/db/validate.go` beside the `utf8RuneStart` predicate it uses, and `ClampModel` calls it too. The excerpt cut reuses that walk instead of adding a second copy of it. ASCII excerpts keep byte-identical output and the 180-byte budget stays an upper bound.

One behavior change worth naming: on the degenerate `max <= 3` branch a multibyte string now yields an empty string rather than a broken fragment. The only caller passes 180, so that branch is unreachable in production; it is kept correct rather than removed. Backend parity holds by construction, since `internal/postgres/analytics.go` and `internal/duckdb/analytics_usage.go` both build their examples by calling `db.BuildSignalExamples`.

Reviewer attention is best spent on the `ClampModel` hunk in `internal/db/validate.go`, the one existing caller this change reshapes. `truncateLogLine` in `internal/insight/generate.go` has the same defect against a 16 KiB stdout budget; I left it out to keep this change to one concern. I did not run the PostgreSQL or DuckDB suites locally.

title: refactor(api): adopt huma-check and generated clients
body:
Adopts every huma-check rule in prek and CI, moves production JSON to v2, and commits the Huma OpenAPI contract as YAML. Orval and DoorDash generate the clients, with generation drift checks.

The CLI and browser execute generated operations, including daemon startup probes, progress streams, imports, assets, and downloads. The Go service, CLI JSON, and raw-sync clients consume generated results and reuse existing application models. The HTTP service adapter lives in servicehttp to avoid an import cycle. Removed the old timing client, duplicate frontend wire models, handwritten SSE framing, unused raw upload wrapper, and redundant Go response decoders and model copies. Deleted the Recall client wrapper and the callGenerated forwarding layer; consumers now use generated operations and query/page types directly. Stats also uses the daemon API when the discovered daemon is read-only, reporting its error instead of opening a separate local archive.

Most added code is the OpenAPI document and generated clients. Review the JSON migration behavior, service adapters, stream consumers, and native transfer contracts. Embeddings build now documents its actual 202 response; JSON consumers reject empty successes, and Markdown downloads return readable Responses.

Raw uploads call the generated operation with the released runtime’s request-editor hook to supply binary bytes and the upload-offset header. No fork or upstream merge is required. Task 58fz remains open for archive and bounded-response adapters; the runtime still buffers archive downloads.

<sup>generated by a clanker</sup>

title: usage: sum tokens per agent home (source root) over a time window without one /usage call per session
body:
We run 16 Claude Code homes on one Mac (12 pool seats under `~/.claude-pool/profiles/seat-NN` plus four context profiles) through `[agents.claude] homes`, collected to one archive. A seat scorer needs the token use of one home over rolling 5-hour and 7-day windows, across every machine the collector covers.

What works in 0.43.0: `GET /api/v1/sessions?agent=claude&active_since=…&include_children=true&include_source=true` returns `file_path`, so a session can be attributed to a home by path prefix, and `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/usage?breakdown=true` returns timestamped token rows. That is one request per session. The busiest seat has about 1,000 sessions in 7 days, and a loaded daemon answers about 20 usage calls a second, so one pass takes around 50 s. We cache rows per session on the client to make it usable.

What would remove the N calls: a home (source root) dimension on the usage surface. Either of these would do:

1. A `source_root` (or `home`) filter on `/api/v1/usage/summary` and `/api/v1/usage/top-sessions`, matching the configured home the session was read from (the remote's own path for collected machines), plus a time bound finer than a day so a 5-hour window is expressible.
2. A bulk per-session usage endpoint, e.g. `/api/v1/usage/sessions?active_since=…&include_source=true`, returning the four token counters and first/last usage timestamps per session in one page.

Two smaller things noticed on the way:

- `include_source` is HTTP-only. `session list` has no `--include-source` flag, and the docs mention it in one table row. A `home` field on the session DTO (the configured root, not the transcript path) would be the cleanest attribution and would survive path differences between machines.
- A daemon started before homes are added to config keeps discovering only the home it started with until restarted. `doctor sync` shows the right roots, so this is expected, but a line in the homes docs saying "restart the daemon after editing homes" would have saved us an hour.

Version: agentsview v0.43.0 (commit 9be7745), macOS, one machine so far.

title: Content search matches carry no machine or title, so a multi-machine search needs one GET per session
body:
agentsview v0.43.0 (commit 9be7745), macOS.

`GET /api/v1/search/content?pattern=...` (and `agentsview session search --json`) returns matches with `session_id`, `project`, `agent`, `location`, `role`, `ordinal`, `timestamp`, `snippet` and `ordinal_range`. There is no `machine` and no `display_name`. On a collector that pulls several machines over HTTP remote sync, a search result cannot say which machine a hit came from without a second request per session (`GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}`). A page of 50 matches over 30 sessions costs 30 extra requests to render a list.

`GET /api/v1/search?q=...` has `name` (the title) but also no `machine`.

Repro on any archive with a session:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/search/content?pattern=kwt&limit=1' | jq '.matches[0] | keys'
```

Ask: add `machine` (the key, as `/api/v1/sessions/{id}` reports it) and `display_name` to content-search matches, or accept a batch filter on `/api/v1/sessions` (`ids=a,b,c`) so a client can resolve a page in one call. Either would let a fleet search print "date, machine, title" per hit without the N+1.

Smaller, related: `agentsview sync --help` still describes `--host` as "SSH hostname for deprecated remote sync", while the configuration docs say `sync --host <name>` selects a configured `[[remote_hosts]]` HTTP entry by name. The help text could say both.

title: feat(parser): support DeepSeek Harness v3 sessions
body:
## What changed

agentsview now recognizes the generation-addressed DeepSeek Harness session
logs written by current releases (`session.vN.jsonl` / `session.vN.jsonl.zstd`)
and selects the newest generation when one session directory retains several
immutable files. Header validation accepts generations 0 through 3.

The parser also understands the event vocabulary those generations added:
`system/message`, `assistant/attempt`, `model/selection`, embedded
`assistant/message` streams, `tool/ptc-dispatch*`, `deliverables/presented`, and
`subagent/catalog`. It reads embedded stream usage and finish reasons, supports
the `{op, startSeq, endSeq}` replacement spelling, accepts `file` content
blocks, and applies the last `session/end-seed {inherited: true}` marker as the
inherited cut so seeded child sessions do not import their parent transcript.

Version-0 behavior is preserved, including packed assistant rows, compressed
`sourceEventSeqs` ranges, and surface replacements spelled with `start`/`end`.

## Limits

- agentsview reads each on-disk generation directly and does not run DeepSeek
  Harness's own migrations.
- Generation-2 request-header system prompts are not imported as transcript
  rows, and a failed assistant attempt with no final `assistant/message` is not
  reconstructed.
- A generation newer than 3 is passed over during discovery, so a session
  that also retains a readable generation still indexes from that log.
  Opening such a log directly reports an unsupported-version error.

Reviewers should start with `internal/parser/deepseek_harness_provider.go` for
discovery and generation selection, then `deepseek_harness_format.go` for
header, envelope, and filename handling, and `deepseek_harness.go` for event
folding, embedded streams, and the inherited seed cut.

title: serve: an explicit --port should refuse a taken port (or take --strict-port) instead of moving to the next free one
body:
## What happens

`agentsview serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080` on a Mac where another
process already listens on 8080 does not fail. It prints

```
Port 8080 in use, using 8081
agentsview v0.43.0 listening at http://127.0.0.1:8081 (started in 1.2s)
```

and runs on 8081. In v0.43.0 this is `prepareServeRuntimeConfig` in
`cmd/agentsview/serve_runtime.go`: `server.FindAvailablePort(cfg.Host,
cfg.Port)` picks the next free port whether `cfg.Port` came from the config
default or from an explicit `--port`.

## Why it hurts under a supervisor

I run the daemon under launchd with `KeepAlive`, pinned to `--host 127.0.0.1
--port 8080`, and expose it to my tailnet with `tailscale serve --tcp=8080
tcp://127.0.0.1:8080`. A collector on another machine pulls the archive from
`http://<tailnet-ip>:8080`, and the config lists that origin in
`public_origins`.

On one machine a different service held 8080. The daemon came up healthy on
8081 and the whole chain around it kept pointing at 8080: the `tailscale
serve` forwarder, the collector's `[[remote_hosts]]` url, the install
script's health probe (which waited 15 minutes on 8080 and then rolled the
install back), and `public_origins`, which `rewriteConfiguredPublicURLPort`
only adjusts when `public_url` is set. Nothing was down, but nothing
reachable either, and the only evidence was one stdout line.

For an interactive `agentsview` that opens a browser, picking a free port is
the right default. For a supervised `serve` with an explicit `--port`, a
moved port is a silent misconfiguration.

## Ask

One of:

- an explicit `--port` refuses to start when the port is taken (exit
  non-zero with the holder in the message), and only the default or `port =
  0` falls back to `FindAvailablePort`; or
- a `--strict-port` flag (or `strict_port = true` in config) with that
  behaviour, leaving the current default alone.

Either lets a supervisor see the failure instead of a working daemon on the
wrong port. I have worked around it on my side by checking the daemon log
for the `listening at` line and failing the install when the port differs,
but the daemon knows first.

v0.43.0, macOS, brew cask.

title: feat(sessions): support Pi session resume
body:
Pi sessions now expose the existing resume actions. You can launch or copy a self-contained `pi --session <session>` command from AgentsView instead of finding the session target and assembling the command by hand.

Adds Pi to the backend and frontend resume registries. The server includes the selected working directory and uses the session file path without its archive host prefix, which covers local and synced older sessions without a header ID. The browser avoids an incomplete fallback when server context is unavailable.

Closes #1783

title: feat(insights): generate and inspect insights from the CLI
body:
Adds agentsview insight list, get, and generate so scripts can inspect saved insights and create new Activity Insights without discovering daemon URLs, bearer tokens, or SSE details by hand.

The commands call the existing insight API through current daemon discovery and explicit-server credentials. Generation keeps validation, configured agents or endpoints, caching, and persistence on the server. cmd/agentsview owns the client, and docs/commands.md documents the interface.

The current workaround is a hand-built HTTP client. CLI access was raised in #67 and deferred when #860 added export and publish.

Closes #1787

title: fix(search): match sessions by identifier
body:
## What changed

Global full-text search now also matches canonical session IDs and provider
source session IDs, alongside the existing display-name and first-message
matches. Pasting either the AgentsView ID or the provider's original session ID
into the command palette resolves to the owning session, including child
sessions that are intentionally hidden from the default session list.

The match is implemented in all three read backends (SQLite, PostgreSQL, and
DuckDB) so a mirrored or PostgreSQL-backed deployment behaves the same. An
identifier match returns the session result with ordinal `-1`, which the
command palette already uses for name-only matches and navigates without
scrolling to a message.

## Why

DeepSeek Harness exposes sessions by their provider ID (for example
`session-<provider-id>`), while AgentsView stores them as
`deepseek-harness:session-<provider-id>`. Before this change the command
palette only searched message content, display names, and first messages, so
searching by a provider ID could miss the owning session entirely.

## Limits

- Identifier matching is a substring match over the canonical and source IDs.
  It does not normalize away hyphens or other provider-specific formatting.
- Semantic and hybrid palette modes still rank message content only; the new
  matching applies to full-text mode.

Reviewers should start with `internal/db/search.go`, then check the matching
name-branch predicates in `internal/postgres/messages.go` and
`internal/duckdb/store.go` for parity.

title: Cursor IDE bubble with object-typed toolFormerData.result permanently blocks sync (and therefore pg push --watch)
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.43.0 (commit 9be7745ad1906ee24e04eb05bb86c872ef0939a1, built 2026-09-14T02:30:01Z)

### Install method

install.sh / install.ps1

### OS / platform

Windows 11 24H2 (amd64), build 26100.1

### Which agent and version

Cursor IDE (built-in chat panel / state.vscdb). Cursor version not confirmed, but the offending tool is Cursor's internal `todo_write` (tool id 35 in its own schema) — see reproduction sample below.

### Which model(s)

n/a — this is a storage/parsing bug independent of which model the session used.

### What happened, and what did you expect

A Cursor IDE bubble whose assistant turn called Cursor's built-in `todo_write` tool has `toolFormerData.result` stored as a JSON *object* (with fields like `success`, `finalTodos`, `initialTodos`, `wasMerge`, ...), not a string. `cursorIDEToolFormerData.Result` is typed as a plain Go `string`, so decoding fails every time this composer is touched:

sync error: decoding cursor IDE bubble <composerID>:<bubbleID>: json: cannot unmarshal JSON object into Go string within "/toolFormerData/result"

Expected: agentsview to accept a structured result for tools like `todo_write` (or degrade that one tool result to raw/truncated text) and move on.

What actually happens is much worse than one bad session: the decode error aborts the *entire* sync worker pass, not just this composer, so `SyncStats.ProcessingComplete()` never becomes true again on this machine:

fatal: sync worker startup: failed
ERROR: startup sync worker ran but did not complete: startup worker pass reported failed (surfacing incomplete pass; not re-syncing in process)

Which in turn means `pg push` / `pg push --watch` refuse to push anything, forever, on every retry:

pg watch: initial daemon push failed: local sync processing incomplete
pg watch: push (change) failed: local sync processing incomplete
pg watch: push (interval) failed: local sync processing incomplete

Confirmed this isn't a stale-process/lock artifact: killed all `agentsview.exe` processes and restarted `serve` clean — identical composer/bubble ID fails identically on the fresh process too.

Root cause: `internal/parser/cursor_ide.go`'s `cursorIDEToolFormerData.Result` is `string`-typed with no object/string normalization, unlike `RawArgs`, which (per PR #168's description) already has `normalizeCursorParamsJSON` to handle "params stored as either a JSON object or a JSON-encoded string." That same normalization was apparently never extended to `result`, and at least the `todo_write` tool writes `result` as a structured object.

### Sample session file or snippet

```text
{
  "type": 2,
  "toolFormerData": {
    "toolCallId": "<uuid>",
    "name": "todo_write",
    "tool": 35,
    "rawArgs": "{\"todos\":[{\"id\":\"<redacted>\",\"content\":\"<redacted>\",\"status\":\"TODO_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS\",\"createdAt\":\"<epoch-ms>\",\"updatedAt\":\"<epoch-ms>\",\"dependencies\":[]}],\"merge\":true}",
    "params": "{\"todos\":[{\"content\":\"<redacted>\",\"status\":\"in_progress\",\"id\":\"<redacted>\"}],\"merge\":true}",
    "result": {
      "success": true,
      "readyTaskIds": [],
      "needsInProgressTodos": false,
      "finalTodos": [
        {"content": "<redacted>", "status": "in_progress", "id": "<redacted>", "dependencies": []}
      ],
      "initialTodos": [
        {"content": "<redacted>", "status": "completed", "id": "<redacted>", "dependencies": []}
      ],
      "wasMerge": true
    }
  }
}

Note that `rawArgs` and `params` are JSON-encoded strings here and decode
into `RawArgs string` without issue — it's specifically `result` that comes
back as a raw JSON object instead of a string, which is what
`cursorIDEToolFormerData.Result string` fails to unmarshal.
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Cursor IDE, have the assistant call the built-in todo_write tool at least once in a chat session (this is Cursor's own internal to-do list tracker, invoked automatically during agentic work — not something the user calls directly).
2. Run `agentsview serve` (or trigger any sync) so the archive parses that composer's bubbles.
3. Observe the decode error above on every sync attempt, and that the overall sync pass never completes.
4. Optionally run `agentsview pg push --watch` and observe it fails indefinitely with `local sync processing incomplete`.

Suggested fix:
- Accept `result` as either a JSON string or a raw JSON object (reuse/extend the existing object-or-string normalization already used for `rawArgs`), falling back to storing the raw JSON text when it isn't a simple string.
- And/or don't let one bad bubble abort the whole sync worker pass — flag that composer as truncated/failed (as already done for a missing bubble row) and let the rest of the archive sync and push normally.

Workaround: setting `cursor_ide_dirs = []` in config.toml disables Cursor IDE discovery entirely, unblocking local sync and pg push for all other sources.

title: feat(cli): add session list --include-source

title: fix(sync): describe configured HTTP hosts in flag help
body:
`agentsview sync --help` now describes `--host` as a configured HTTP host name or deprecated SSH hostname. The old line named SSH as the flag's only transport.

The flag usage and command reference now match the routing already described in the long help. `--user` and `--port` keep their SSH wording because they configure that transport only. The stale line was reported in #1791.

Refs #1791

title: fix(serve): reject collisions on an explicit port
body:
An explicit nonzero `--port` now fails when occupied, so supervisors see a failure instead of a daemon running on the wrong port. Default and config-file ports retain automatic fallback; `--port 0` still chooses an available port. The shared runtime check covers `serve`, `pg serve`, and `duckdb serve`, including background launches.

Replacement checks an explicit port before stopping the running daemon. Its bind address can be reused, including aliases and narrowing a wildcard bind. Widening on the same explicit port requires stopping the daemon first because other interfaces may have unrelated listeners.

The daemon records the original `--port` value so `agentsview update` preserves that choice, including `0`. Explicit ports remain strict after restart, and a configured `public_url` for a forwarder stays unchanged when it differs from the CLI port. Without a recorded explicit port, update uses the hidden `--restart-port` flag to retry the previous listening port while retaining fallback and the configured public URL's port rewrite. Older runtime records cannot recover the original CLI choice.

Review the runtime metadata in `daemon_runtime.go`, restart arguments in `update.go`, port selection and URL rewriting in `serve_runtime.go`, and replacement preflight in `serve_lifecycle.go` together.

CI and local hooks use the same available Huma checker revision. CI prepares the SQLite headers before loading the API packages.

Refs #1793

title: fix(cli): include machine labels in JSON reports
body:
`session list --json` and `usage daily --json --breakdown` now include a top-level `machine_labels` map, so scripts can resolve machine keys without a second authenticated request. Existing row keys stay unchanged.

Direct reads use the selected store's label catalog. Daemon-backed reads use the existing `/api/v1/machines` route. Each document includes labels only for machine keys in its rows. Label failures leave a complete document with an empty map and write the reason to stderr. The CLI gap was reported in #1794.

The change stays in the Cursor IDE parser. Malformed bubbles still return errors; missing and empty rows keep their existing gap behavior. title: fix: reduce background CPU during sync and usage backfill

Reduce sustained background CPU during startup sync and usage-cache backfill.

When a Codex checkpoint is rejected, a matching non-empty source hash and stored metadata can still skip an unchanged transcript. The rejected cursor cannot authorize incremental parsing. A missing hash, changed source, or explicit reparse takes the full-parse path.

Usage rollup queries keep the selected session batch outermost in SQLite's join order. This avoids scanning complete identity indexes for every batch. On a production-scale cache snapshot, the combined identity queries for 256 sessions fell from about 1.05 seconds to 35 milliseconds with identical results. This measures those queries, not total backfill time.

title: Devin usage undercounted: per-session node_id used as SourceUUID collides across all Devin sessions in usage-rollup dedup
body:
### agentsview version

v0.42.1-0.20260902150422-6070f2aaaf16 (relevant code paths verified unchanged on `main` @ `490a230f`, 2026-09-17)

### Install method

Built from source

### OS / platform

macOS

### Which agent and version

Devin CLI (local store `~/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db`). Devin Desktop sessions are equally affected — the desktop app runs `devin acp` and writes to the same store.

### Which model(s)

all

### What happened, and what did you expect

Usage view counts only ~48% of Devin tokens on my database; several recent sessions contribute 0 tokens even though their per-message token facts were extracted and stored. Sessions still appear in the session list, projects, and health views — only Usage is wrong.

**Root cause:** `internal/parser/devin.go:640` sets

```go
SourceUUID: fmt.Sprintf("%d", row.NodeID),
```

but `node_id` is only unique *within* a session. Devin's own DDL (`sessions.db`):

```sql
CREATE TABLE message_nodes (
  row_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  node_id INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- node_id within this session's forest
  parent_node_id INTEGER,
  chat_message TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, metadata TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES sessions(id),
  UNIQUE(session_id, node_id)
)
```

On my database: 36,394 rows / 36,394 distinct `(session_id, node_id)` pairs but only **8,155** distinct `node_id` values; **71/71** sessions start at `node_id = 0`.

The usage-rollup "general" dedup key omits session scope (`internal/db/usage_rollup_build.go:531`):

```go
return fmt.Sprintf("source:%d:%s%s", len(fact.Agent), fact.Agent, fact.Fact.SourceUUID)
// → "source:5:devin10" for the 10th message node of *every* Devin session
```

Then:

- `usageRollupCrossSourceUUIDSQL` (`usage_rollup_classify.go`) flags every `source_uuid` that appears in more than one cached session as a cross-session identity → the whole group is diverted to `usage_rollup_exceptions`.
- At read time `deduplicateUsageRollupGeneral` (`usage_rollup_query.go:638`) keeps exactly one winner per key; `compareUsageGeneralWinner` picks the minimum `DedupTimestamp`.

Net effect: **the earliest Devin session wins each node_id; every later session's same-numbered messages are discarded from Usage.** This is correct for globally-unique ids (Claude `uuid`, opencode `messageID`, …) but `node_id` is a small per-session integer, so unrelated messages across sessions are treated as duplicate observations of a single event.

The transcript path has the same flaw: `SourceUUID = devinStepID(step_id)` and Devin transcript `step_id`s are also per-session `1..N`.

### Evidence

**1. Dedup eats 38.5% of all Devin facts.** In my `usage-cache-v7` DB, 51 Devin sessions produced 964 token-eligible facts; grouping by `agent + source_uuid` yields 593 keys → 371 facts dropped.

**2. Re-implementing the dedup rule reproduces the API exactly.** ~30 lines of Python (group by `source:5:devin<uuid>`, keep min-timestamp member, bucket by local date) against the raw `usage_facts` table reproduces `/api/v1/usage/summary?from=…&to=…` **on every day, for both input and output tokens**:

title: fix(parser): scope Devin message source identities by session
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1812.

Devin numbers `message_nodes.node_id` and transcript `step_id` per session (`UNIQUE(session_id, node_id)` in Devin's own DDL), but the parser emitted them as bare `SourceUUID` values. The usage rollup treats `SourceUUID` as a global identity: `usageRollupGeneralKey` builds `source:5:devin<id>` with no session scope, cross-session sharers are diverted to the exception tier, and `deduplicateUsageRollupGeneral` keeps one earliest-timestamp winner per key. Every later Devin session therefore lost the messages whose node ids had already appeared in an earlier session. On a real archive only 47.6% of Devin output tokens were counted, with recent sessions at 0%.

The parser now prefixes both identities with the raw session id (`<session>:<node_id>`, `<session>:<step_id>`), and `SourceParentUUID` uses the same prefix so parent links stay intra-session. A step without a usable `step_id` still yields an empty identity rather than a bare prefix.

Because the source bytes are unchanged, a fingerprint change cannot trigger re-parse, so `dataVersion` is bumped to 110; `usageCacheFormatVersion` is bumped to 13 so facts and rollups are rebuilt under the new identities, per the deduplication rule in `docs/agents/storage.md`.

Where to look: `internal/parser/devin.go` (`devinNodeSourceUUID`, `devinStepSourceUUID`, the two threaded `rawSessionID` parameters), the two new parser tests, and the Devin entry in `docs/internal/session-format-sources.md`.

Tradeoff: this widens `SourceUUID` for Devin rows only; no consumer parses it numerically, and other parsers already use `id:suffix` forms.

title: feat(parser): add Tencent CodeBuddy CN agent support
body:
Add Tencent CodeBuddy CN sessions stored by CodeBuddyExtension under `Data/history`, using session manifests and companion message files. The provider reconstructs user and assistant messages, explicit thinking/reasoning blocks, tool calls and results, model metadata, and recorded usage. It registers CodeBuddy in discovery, configuration, CLI help, and the frontend.

Projects use the recorded working directory with the workspace identifier as a fallback. User source blocks are preserved together, Windows defaults honor `LOCALAPPDATA`, and `CODEBUDDY_DIR` overrides discovery roots. Composite fingerprints include workspace metadata and message files, and their content hashes are required for freshness and skip-cache identity so equal-size rewrites with unchanged modification times still refresh the archive. Workspace index events refresh that workspace's sessions, while message writes and deletions resolve directly to their owning session without scanning unrelated workspaces. Valid manifests with no readable messages replace the stored transcript with an empty session; invalid JSON or a missing/non-array messages field produces a parse error and preserves existing archive content.

Usage normalization retains explicit zero values and excludes missing, null, and negative counters. Thinking-only and usage-only assistant messages are preserved. The parser currently interprets input tokens as including cache reads; producer-version coverage and whether thinking snapshots are cumulative remain unverified. The format inventory records these limits rather than claiming audited billing parity.

title: fix(cli): hint at restarting stale clients on daemon data-version mismatch
body:
## Summary

Archive-write commands (`pg push --watch`, `duckdb push --watch`, resync, etc.) returned a bare `daemon data version N is incompatible with client data version M` error when a live daemon could not be safely replaced, unlike the read path, which already appends actionable restart guidance for this exact class of mismatch (added for issue #929). This left a long-running client stuck on an old binary — for example an `agentsview pg service` (`pg push --watch`) still running from before an upgrade, discovering that the daemon it talks to has since been restarted onto a newer data version — with no indication of what to do about it.

`ensureTransportContext`'s archive-write branch falls through to a generic block that builds the error straight from `tr.DirectReason` instead of wrapping it with `appendDaemonRestartUpgradeHint` like the read-intent branch does. This change closes that parity gap.

Separately, the shared restart hint only ever said "this database was written by an older version, restart the daemon". That is the wrong advice when the daemon is the newer side, which is exactly the stale-writer case above: restarting the daemon changes nothing. The transport now records whether the live daemon is ahead of the client, and the error picks its guidance by direction. An older daemon or archive keeps the existing daemon-restart wording. A daemon that is ahead tells the operator to upgrade this agentsview install and restart the stale command or background service (`pg push --watch`, `duckdb push --watch`, or a service installed with `agentsview pg service`), matching the guidance already in `docs/configuration.md`.

Where reviewer attention is most valuable: the wording of the two hints, and whether `DirectDaemonAhead` on the transport is the right place to carry the direction.

With `AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1` the CLI never replaces a live daemon, so a writer that finds a daemon on a newer data version cannot proceed and still fails. That failure previously said the daemon was "not responding", which is false in this case. It now reports the real data-version mismatch. No restart hint is added there, because the operator has opted out of daemon management on that path and the combination is not a supported setup.

title: fix(activity): dismiss concurrency hover box on date change
body:
## TL;DR

Hovering a late concurrency bar, then switching to a day that has not reached that hour, left yesterday's data box sitting on the new chart. The chart now clears that box when the report is replaced.

## How

Activity keeps this chart mounted across report loads so a date change does not flash a blank chart. Hover targets are keyed by bucket index, so they can disappear or get reused without a pointer-leave. The hover box is local state, so it survived.

Remounting on date change would also drop the box. It would bring back the blank flash that in-place report updates exist to avoid.

## Reviewer notes

- **Look at `ConcurrencyTimeline` hover state.** ActivityPage already clears the selected-range chip on `reportGeneration`. This is the hover box, not that chip.
- Replacing the report also dismisses a still-valid hover on a same-day refresh. That is a little broader than the date-switch bug, and it matches "the data under the pointer just changed."

title: test: fix go-to-session URL and Windows tilde assertions
body:
Fixes the two CI failures that every pull request currently inherits from `main`.

The go-to-session end-to-end spec expected a session id as one encoded path segment. The router now puts the provider prefix and the UUID in separate segments (#1769), and the spec from #1770 was written before that change. The spec builds its expected paths the same way the router does.

The Pi resume test (#1795) rejected any tilde in the resume command to catch an unexpanded home directory. Windows runners use a temp path containing an 8.3 short name such as `RUNNER~1`, so the working directory itself tripped the check. The test now strips the working directory before looking for a tilde.

No application code changes. Reviewers should look at the path helper at the top of `frontend/e2e/go-to-session.spec.ts` and the assertion near the end of the Pi resume subtest in `internal/server/resume_handler_test.go`.

title: Piebald parser requires chats.current_directory; older app.db has worktree_path only and retries forever
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.43.0 (commit 9be7745ad1906ee24e04eb05bb86c872ef0939a1, built 2026-09-14T02:30:01Z)

### Install method

GitHub release binary

### OS / platform

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64)

### Which agent and version

Piebald v0.5.1 (Web). Data dir: `~/.local/share/piebald/app.db` (default Linux path). Last Diesel migration in that DB: `202606250000000000` applied 2026-07-14.

### Which model(s)

n/a — parse/schema bug, not model-specific

### What happened, and what did you expect

`agentsview serve` repeatedly failed to load every non-empty Piebald chat:

```
sync error: loading piebald chat 10: no such column: c.current_directory
sync error: loading piebald chat 11: no such column: c.current_directory
… (same for chats 14, 15, 16, 19, 20, 21, 22, 48, 56, 57)
watcher callback: watch root reconciliation failed processing page: 12 failures
```

Those 12 chats are the full set of non-deleted Piebald chats with `message_count > 0`. The failure did not settle: the watcher retried the same 12 chats about every 20 seconds (`watcher: N file(s) changed, triggering sync` → same 12 `current_directory` errors → `watch root reconciliation failed processing page: 12 failures`).

**Cause:** `internal/parser/piebald.go` `piebaldChatSelect` unconditionally selects `c.current_directory`:

```go
SELECT c.id,
       COALESCE(c.title, ''),
       c.created_at,
       COALESCE(c.updated_at, c.created_at),
       c.message_count,
       COALESCE(c.current_directory, ''),
       COALESCE(c.worktree_path, ''),
       COALESCE(c.branch_name, ''),
       COALESCE(p.directory, ''),
       COALESCE(p.name, '')
FROM chats c
LEFT JOIN projects p ON p.id = c.project_id
```

This Piebald `chats` table (v0.5.1 / last written 2026-07-14) has `worktree_path`, `branch_name`, and `project_id`, but **no `current_directory` column**. Relevant columns:

```
id, title, …, message_count, permission_mode, …, project_id, branch_name, worktree_path, is_read_only, …
```

The in-repo Piebald test fixtures create `current_directory TEXT`, so they do not cover this older/real schema.

**Expected:**
- Load chats from a Piebald `app.db` that has `worktree_path` but not `current_directory` (treat the missing column as empty).
- Schema/parse failures should not be retried every watcher tick. Sticky-fail until the source DB identity (path + mtime/size) changes, otherwise a leftover unused Piebald install keeps the daemon busy forever.

I no longer use Piebald, so I deleted `~/.local/share/piebald/` locally. Filing this so the parser does not assume a column that older `app.db` files do not have.

### Sample session file or snippet

Cannot attach `app.db` (private chats). Repro schema for `chats` is: include `worktree_path`, `branch_name`, `project_id`; omit `current_directory`. The existing test helper in `internal/parser/piebald_test.go` / `internal/sync/piebald_integration_test.go` currently creates `current_directory TEXT` — dropping that column from a fixture should reproduce `no such column: c.current_directory` on `loadOnePiebaldChat`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Piebald v0.5.1 (or any build whose `chats` table has `worktree_path` but not `current_directory`).
2. Have at least one non-deleted chat with `message_count > 0` in `~/.local/share/piebald/app.db`.
3. Run `agentsview serve` (or `agentsview sync`).
4. Watch `~/.agentsview/debug.log`: the same N chats fail on `c.current_directory` every watcher cycle.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (`piebald`, `current_directory`, `no such column`) — no match
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: Idle daemon burns ~1 core on large archive: 4k-file watcher loop, 46 TiB rchar in 6.5 days (v0.42.0; still ~1 core on v0.43.0)
body:
### agentsview version

- **v0.42.0** for the 6.5-day idle observation (binary that had been running since boot)
- **v0.43.0** (`9be7745ad1906ee24e04eb05bb86c872ef0939a1`, built 2026-09-14T02:30:01Z) after a restart/upgrade — high CPU is reduced in the 4k-file stampede sense, but the daemon still sits at about **one full core** on this archive

### Install method

GitHub release binary, run as a systemd user service:

```
agentsview serve --host <ip> --port 4092 --public-url http://seamus:4092 --no-browser
```

### OS / platform

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64), 8 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM. Host load was ~15–16 while otherwise idle.

### Which agent and version

n/a as a single-agent parse bug. Archive mixes Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok, and (until deleted) Piebald. ~**14.5k sessions**, `~/.agentsview/sessions.db` **~5 GB**. Extra config is only custom OpenCode dirs:

```toml
[agents.opencode]
  dirs = ["~/.local/share/opencode", "~/.config/seamus/opencode"]
```

Related parser failure that fed the same retry loop: #1819 (Piebald `chats.current_directory`).

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened, and what did you expect

Idle `agentsview serve` was the machine's baseline CPU hog. Nobody was using the UI.

#### v0.42.0, 6.5 days uptime (PID lived the whole boot)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Live CPU (`top`) | **~90% of one core** continuously |
| CPU time | **94 hours** in **158 hours** uptime (~60% of one core for the entire uptime) |
| RSS | 1.1 GiB |
| `rchar` | **~46 TiB** |
| `syscr` | **~11.4 billion** |
| `read_bytes` / `write_bytes` | ~171 GiB / ~757 GiB |
| `debug.log` | **96 MB** of repeating sync errors |

FDs: `sessions.db` + WAL, `usage-cache-v7-*.db`, inotify.

Watcher log, **every ~5 seconds, forever**:

```
watcher: 4229 file(s) changed, triggering sync
sync: 3 file(s) updated
watcher callback: changed-path sync incomplete: 130 source or archive failures
```

4,229 paths treated as changed, **3** actually updated, **130** failures, then the next 5s batch is 4,229 again.

Repeating failure classes in that loop:

1. Missing Grok sidecars, same paths every cycle:
   ```
   sync error: stat ~/.grok/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/<id>/summary.json: no such file or directory
   ```
2. Piebald schema mismatch (now #1819):
   ```
   sync error: loading piebald chat N: no such column: c.current_directory
   ```

This looks like a **failure-driven resync loop** plus **over-broad change detection**: failed paths never get a backoff / “don't retry until identity changes” bit, and the watcher reports thousands of changes when only a handful of files need work. v0.43.0 notes “SQLite-backed sessions stop resyncing in a loop because of AgentsView's own database reads” — the 4,229 stampede matches that class of bug, and it was still happening on **v0.42.0**.

#### After restart onto v0.43.0 (same archive)

- Startup did a **full resync** (`Data version changed, running full resync...`) of **14503 sessions**. HTTP stayed closed for ~10 minutes.
- The 4,229-file stampede stopped. Watcher batches dropped to **~40–55 files / 5s** while the Piebald failures were still present, then quieter after those files were removed.
- It did **not** become idle. Same process, ~38 minutes after start (mostly post-resync, serving HTTP 200):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| `ps` `%CPU` (lifetime) | **90.9%** |
| 5s `/proc/<pid>/stat` sample | **~101% of one core** (incl. children; none at sample time) |
| `rchar` | **621 GiB** in 38 minutes |
| `read_bytes` / `write_bytes` | ~26 GiB / ~39 GiB |
| RSS | ~360 MiB |

It also logs `polling 3 unwatched root(s)` about every two minutes. I do not know which roots those are.

**Expected:** an idle daemon on a large but quiet archive should be near 0% CPU. Stat/schema failures should be sticky until the source path's identity (mtime/size/inode) changes. A watcher tick should not claim thousands of changed files when only 3 need updates. `debug.log` should not grow at tens of MB/day from the same errors.

### Sample session file or snippet

No session transcript needed. Representative watcher cycle from v0.42.0 (redacted paths):

```
watcher: 4229 file(s) changed, triggering sync
sync: 3 file(s) updated
watcher callback: changed-path sync incomplete: 130 source or archive failures
sync error: stat /home/…/.grok/sessions/…/summary.json: no such file or directory
sync error: loading piebald chat 10: no such column: c.current_directory
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a large local archive (~10k+ sessions, multi-GB `sessions.db`) with several agent roots, including some that 404/stat-fail (Grok sessions without `summary.json` is enough).
2. Run `agentsview serve` as a long-lived daemon. Do not open the UI.
3. Watch `top` and `~/.agentsview/debug.log`.
4. On v0.42.0: watcher reports thousands of changed files every 5s, CPU stays ~1 core, `rchar` grows without bound.
5. On v0.43.0: the thousand-file batches are gone, but CPU and `rchar` on this 5 GB / 14.5k-session archive still look like a tight loop rather than an idle watcher.

### Suggested direction

- Treat parser/stat failures as sticky until the source file's identity changes.
- Keep AgentsView's own `sessions.db` / WAL / usage-cache out of watch roots (v0.43.0 may already do this; v0.42.0 did not behave that way).
- Cap or coalesce changed-path batches so a noisy tree cannot schedule a 4k-file sync every 5s.
- Log *which* unwatched roots are being polled, and how expensive that poll is.

Happy to attach more `debug.log` excerpts or `agentsview doctor sync` output.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (`high CPU`, `idle CPU`, `busy loop`, `watcher`) — no match besides the related Piebald schema issue #1819
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: Digest export reloads all source data 30 times instead of once
body:
The 30-day digest export reloads all source data from the database 30 times, once per day. Each call to `ExportReportingDay` opens its own read transaction, queries all active sessions, loads their full message histories (with no timestamp bound), loads usage rows with 14-hour padding on each side, and loads standalone usage. Across 30 days this means:

- 30 independent read transactions
- 150 source-loading function calls (5 per day)
- Sessions spanning multiple days have their full message history loaded repeatedly
- Adjacent days' 14-hour usage padding overlaps by 28 hours, reading 2.09x the combined window

On a 4.5 GB archive the digest takes 22.8 seconds. The per-day cost averages 0.76 seconds, with the heaviest day at 1.55 seconds. At benchmark scale (15.7 GB corpus, 6 runs of two digest workloads) this is roughly 16 minutes.

The digest command (`cmd/agentsview/export_reporting.go:185-206`) calls `ExportReportingDay` in a loop. `ExportReportingDay` (`internal/db/reporting_export.go:33-99`) opens a transaction, calls `reportingHoursFromSnapshot`, and commits. `reportingHoursFromSnapshot` (lines 102-270) loads five source tables, then loops over 24 hours calling `PairActivityEvents` and `AggregateCandidatesWithJointActivity` per hour.

A shared read transaction across all 30 days would load source data once and slice it per day. The source-loading functions (`activityReportSessionsFrom`, `activityReportActivityFrom`, `reportingUsageSessionsFrom`, `activityReportUsageCandidatesFrom`, `reportingStandaloneUsageCandidatesFrom`) are at `reporting_export.go:128-167` and `activityreport.go:507-655,1196-1340`.

Constraints: daily boundaries must survive the change. Session eligibility, first-seen counts, usage survivor selection, and cost allocation currently use daily boundaries. A multi-day source load must preserve those daily decisions. Model inheritance across adjacent messages within a day must not cross day boundaries. Usage deduplication across the whole month could suppress rows that daily exports retain.

Estimated saving: ~85% of digest time (loading dominates processing). At benchmark scale, ~14 minutes per run.

Related: #1821 fixed the session export path. The digest path has the same class of problem (redundant database work on each iteration) at a different scale.

title: MCP search_content: expose include_one_shot so single-prompt autonomous sessions are searchable
body:
### Problem / motivation

The MCP `search_content` tool excludes one-shot sessions (`user_message_count <= 1`) by default and offers no way to opt back in. `TestSearchContent_ExcludesOneShotByDefault` in internal/mcp/tools_test.go documents this as deliberate and notes "Tracked as a possible follow-up: expose an include_one_shot opt-in so single-exchange sessions can be searched." I could not find that follow-up in the tracker, so this is it.

The gate bites hardest on exactly the sessions agents most need to find later: long unattended runs driven by a single prompt. Concrete case: a Pi session with 1 user message, 598 assistant turns and 834 tool results moved a secrets file and hand-edited a systemd unit. Days later, an agent investigating the resulting breakage searched for the distinctive strings (`secure_env_mode`, a file path) with `search_content` in substring mode, including with `agent: "pi"`, and got `{"matches": []}`. The tool description only mentions the active-session exclusion, so the agent concluded the text existed nowhere and fell back to grepping transcript files on disk. `search_sessions` with the same phrase, and the CLI with `--include-one-shot`, both find the session immediately.

Every other surface already has the opt-in: `agentsview session search --include-one-shot`, the REST `include_one_shot` query parameter, and the web UI's search store, which sends `include_one_shot: true` unconditionally. `search_sessions` in the MCP server applies no one-shot gate at all. The MCP `search_content` tool is the only caller with neither the opt-in nor an inclusive default, and the one with the least visibility into why a result set is empty.

Environment: agentsview v0.41.1-42-g4ba3ad4f built from source; the relevant code is unchanged on main at 44c8ed0f.


### Proposed solution

Add `include_one_shot` (and, for symmetry with the REST API and web UI, `include_automated`) to `searchContentIn` and thread them through to `ContentSearchFilter`. Update the tool description to say that one-shot sessions are excluded unless `include_one_shot` is set, so an empty result is interpretable. Optionally consider whether the MCP default should match `search_sessions` (no gate) rather than the REST list default, since content search is a needle-in-haystack operation where a silent exclusion costs more than a noisy inclusion.

### Alternatives considered

- Use `search_sessions` first and treat an empty `search_content` result as inconclusive. Works, but only if the agent already knows about the gate, which the tool description does not reveal.
- Grep transcript directories on disk. Defeats the point of the index.
- Route MCP callers through the REST API. Loses the MCP tool's context windows and citations.

title: fix(sync): cache source failures to stop retrying unchanged broken files
body:
An idle daemon no longer repeats the same failed work on every watcher cycle. Before this change, sync parsed a broken source file again on each pass, and a failed watcher batch retried at once whenever an unrelated file event arrived. The change bounds that repeated work; it does not claim a fixed CPU result for every archive.

## Failure cache

Sync now remembers a source whose content is malformed or whose file is missing, and skips it until the file's mtime changes. The records live in a small `internal/sync/failurecache` package backed by a new `source_failures` table. The cached identity is `{mtime, missing}` and the cache owns the comparison, so the ordinary skip cache and its readers are unchanged. The table is created with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and needs no data-version bump.

- Timeouts, permission errors, I/O errors and canceled passes are never cached. `sourceParseFailureCacheable` decides this from the error text. It is the most fragile part of the change and the first place to look.
- Aider, composite, multi-file and hash-aware sources never use the cache, because one mtime does not describe their freshness. S3 and virtual paths are excluded too.
- Failures reach the archive even when the pass that found them did not complete, without promoting that pass's ordinary skip entries.
- A forced parse, a session row with a stale data version, a full resync, a watcher overflow and a per-path skip clear all forget the failure, so the source is parsed again.
- A resync build that fails in the worker process does not pass its failures back to the daemon. Each broken file is parsed once more on the next pass and cached again. An in-process resync that aborts flushes them to the live archive.
- Entries have no maximum age, and entries for missing sources are not pruned.

## Watcher backoff

A retained retry keeps its backoff delay when unrelated file events arrive. Explicit retries through `QueueRetryBatch`, authoritative reconciliation and `OpenDispatch` still dispatch at once. An `immediate` flag travels with the pending batch to carry that urgency; the wake handling in the `watcher.go` loop is where the two cases split.

## Poll logs

Unwatched-root polling now logs the roots it checked for each agent and how long the poll took.

This can be split if desired, see https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/1833#issuecomment-5722539204. Closes #1820

title: fix(desktop): restore the main window on macOS reopen
