title: Add StepCode session support (Pi-family harness with its own agent root)
body:
### Agent name and link

**StepCode** — the open-source (MIT) terminal coding agent from **StepFun**
(阶跃星辰), a Shanghai foundation-model company and one of China's "AI six
tigers". StepFun builds the Step model family and runs the Step Platform
(`platform.stepfun.com` for China, `platform.stepfun.ai` overseas), which offers
both a Step Plan subscription and pay-per-use API keys.

- StepCode: <https://github.com/stepfun-ai/Step-Code> (public, MIT)
- Upstream harness it is derived from: [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
  (also MIT)

### Why not just use Pi?

StepCode is a vendor-branded distribution of Pi, the same way a Linux
distribution packages a kernel. Its own notices state it is derived from Pi, and
its integration page states that the entrypoint is an adapter over the Pi
coding-agent runtime that keeps Pi's `SessionManager` class, JSONL format, and
tree operations unchanged — the session files are byte-compatible with Pi's.

What StepFun adds on top is integration, not a different format:

- a built-in **Step** provider with browser OAuth and the Step Plan / Step
  Platform billing profiles
- prompt and context tuning claimed against its own Step models
- built-in static-site publishing (StepPage)
- long-running task delegation via `/goal` and scheduled runs via `/cron`

So the interesting consequence for agentsview is that **no new parser is
needed** — only discovery. Listing StepCode separately (rather than folding it
into Pi) is what makes its sessions visible at all, and keeping a distinct
session-ID prefix keeps them from being mislabeled as Pi's.

### Where does it store sessions?

`~/.stepcode/agent/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/<timestamp>_<session-id>.jsonl`

Same on macOS and Linux. Two native overrides, mirroring Pi's:

- `STEP_CODING_AGENT_DIR` replaces `~/.stepcode/agent`, so sessions land under
  `<value>/sessions`
- `STEP_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` supplies the session directory directly and
  takes precedence

Filenames are timestamp-prefixed (`2026-10-01T12-07-49-281Z_<uuid>.jsonl`), so
the filename does not contain the session's header UUID.

### File format

Identical to Pi's, and deliberately so — a v3 tree-structured JSONL log:

- line 1: `{"type":"session","version":3,"id":...,"timestamp":...,"cwd":...}`
- then entries linked by `id`/`parentId`, including `message`, `model_change`,
  `thinking_level_change`, `compaction`, `branch_summary`, `custom`,
  `custom_message`, `label`, and `session_info`
- `compaction` entries written by current versions embed a `retainedTail`
  `AgentMessage[]` and act as self-contained checkpoints
- `parentSession` records the parent transcript as a file path, and
  `/fork`/`/clone` write it that way

StepCode also ships the pi-subagents extension, so subagent transcripts appear
at `<project>/<parent-transcript-stem>/<runId>/run-N/session.jsonl` — the same
nesting Pi already handles.

### What is missing

There is no `stepcode` provider or agent root, so StepCode sessions are never
discovered:

- `agentsview doctor sync` on v0.44.0 lists 134 agent roots; none is
  `.stepcode`
- the v0.44.0 binary contains no occurrence of `stepcode`, `.stepcode`, or
  `step-harness`
- a local archive holding 2031 sessions across 15 agents has zero sessions
  whose file path is under `.stepcode`

`[agents.pi] dirs` is a partial stopgap, but it records StepCode sessions under
Pi's agent name and, because the array overrides rather than extends, it drops
`~/.pi` unless both paths are listed.

### Sample session file

Below is a hand-written file in the exact shape StepCode writes, not a verbatim
capture.

```jsonl
{"type":"model_change","id":"f742ba79","parentId":null,"timestamp":"2026-10-01T12:07:54.725Z","provider":"step","modelId":"step-5-preview"}
{"type":"thinking_level_change","id":"56031da1","parentId":"f742ba79","timestamp":"2026-10-01T12:07:54.725Z","thinkingLevel":"medium"}
{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"01a0f75d-1b21-7216-be47-e09208deb630","timestamp":"2026-10-01T12:08:49.281Z","cwd":"/repos/example"}
{"type":"message","id":"d1c7d96a","parentId":"56031da1","timestamp":"2026-10-01T12:08:46.960Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"List the files here."}],"timestamp":1790856526956}}
{"type":"message","id":"df220c3e","parentId":"d1c7d96a","timestamp":"2026-10-01T12:08:52.727Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll list the files."}],"provider":"step","model":"step-5-preview","usage":{"input":1024,"output":12,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":1036,"cost":{"input":0.001024,"output":0.0000324,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0.0010564}},"stopReason":"toolUse","timestamp":1790856532727}}
{"type":"message","id":"e3f4a5b6","parentId":"df220c3e","timestamp":"2026-10-01T12:08:52.900Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_1","toolName":"list_files","content":[{"type":"text","text":"README.md\nsrc/"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1790856532900}}
```

### Can you help?

- I can share a sample session file
- I use this agent and can test a PR or build a parser

A pull request implementing this is open: #2063.

title: feat(parser): add StepCode session ingestion
body:
StepCode (https://github.com/stepfun-ai/Step-Code) is StepFun's packaged Pi, with byte-compatible session files under `~/.stepcode/agent/sessions`. Agentsview already parses that format but never looked in StepCode's folder, so StepCode users saw none of their sessions. This registers StepCode like OMO: the shared Pi provider, its own `stepcode:` prefix so sessions never merge into Pi's, and `STEPCODE_DIR`, `STEP_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and `STEP_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` for custom locations. Closes #2062.

StepCode runs subagents and workflow agents as separate sessions named `subagent-<uuid>` and `workflow-<run>-<agent>`, saved beside the parent with no parent link. Those IDs are tagged as subagents so they stay out of the session list, the same rule StepCode's resume picker uses. They stay unlinked because the parent transcript never records the child's ID, and guessing from timestamps would attach children to the wrong parent when two sessions overlap in the same project.

`/fork` and `/clone` sessions carry a `parentSession` header and are classified as forks, the same as Pi.

title: Fix two intermittent Windows sync test failures
body:
## TL;DR

Two tests failed now and then on Windows CI. Both failures came from real sync bugs that only show up with a coarse clock or a slow watcher setup. Both bugs are fixed, and two DuckDB tests now skip on Windows ARM, where DuckDB can't run.

## How

- **Same-size replacements were skipped.** Claude, Codex, Copilot, and Evener store a digest of size, modification time, and change time, so a restarted daemon can skip unchanged files. The default Windows clock ticks every 15.6 ms. A file replaced through write-then-rename can get the original's exact times, and the sync kept the old messages. The digest now also covers the inode, which is the file index on Windows. It leaves out the device number, because some filesystems renumber devices after a reboot or remount, and every source would then be read again. Fixes `TestIncrementalSync_ClaudeSameSize*FileReplaceUsesFullParse`.
- **Sessions written during a settings reload were missed.** The daemon switched the engine to the new roots and only then registered a watcher for them. That gap took about 50 ms on CI, and a session written in it waited for the next full sync. The watcher now registers first and sends changes once the switch is done. Fixes `TestDaemonIngestionReloadAppliesProviderSettings`.
- **DuckDB tests skip on windows/arm64.** DuckDB ships no library for that platform. The two tests that open a real mirror moved to a file with the same build constraint `internal/duckdb` already uses.

## Reviewer notes

- **One extra content check after upgrade.** Digests stored by older versions won't match, so each source gets checked against its content once.
- **Known gap.** An in-place rewrite that keeps the size and all timestamps within one clock tick still matches the digest, since its inode doesn't change. Codebuff computes its own digest without the inode, so a same-tick replacement there can still be missed.

title: fix(telemetry): tag reports with install age
body:
agentsview's telemetry now carries each install's age, so reports can filter out agent sandboxes and test harnesses that start from an empty data directory while first-day activity from real installs stays visible.

New installation IDs record their creation time in a telemetry-install-created file beside the ID, tagged with that ID, and the daemon passes it to kit, which tags every report with `install_age_hours`. IDs without a record report without the tag. The time lives in its own file because copying the data directory resets modification times, which would make an old ID look new.

title: refactor: use backoff/v7 for archive recovery retries
body:
Use backoff/v7 for archive restoration, write-owner lock reacquisition, vector startup lock acquisition, artifact folder lock contention, and SQLite WAL checkpoint retries. Archive recovery and write-owner reacquisition use the library default exponential jitter. Each call keeps its existing intervals, attempt budget, cancellation behavior, and operation errors. Vector startup retains the deadline checked after failed lock attempts and disables serving when contention lasts too long.

HTTP retry policies remain unchanged because their Retry-After overrides preserve exponential progression, while the library resets it. Linear rename retries, incremental backup progress, and background scheduling also retain their existing behavior.

The existing isolated JSON/SQLite fixture test now runs with the non-race sandbox limit tests. CI exposed intermittent ThreadSanitizer trace-memory allocation failures when the test re-executed its race-instrumented binary under production limits. The fixture remains in normal CI; production limits and the remaining race coverage are unchanged.

<sup>generated by a clanker</sup>

title: perf(sync): use 16 KiB fsnotify watch buffers on Windows
body:
At the 8,192-watch limit, Windows AgentsView uses 128 MiB for change buffers instead of 512 MiB, easing pressure on the daemon's 256 MiB soft memory limit.

A single native watch adapter uses 16 KiB for initial, runtime, and reinstated watches. Linux ignores the fsnotify buffer option; macOS uses FSEvents.

Smaller buffers can overflow sooner during event bursts; existing full-sync and polling recovery repairs missed changes. The [issue report](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/2059#issue-5657491189) also tracks the separate Cursor reparse loop.

Refs #2059

title: fix(sync): ignore empty SQLite WAL files when detecting changes
body:
With Cursor closed, AgentsView re-read the whole Cursor IDE database in a loop. Opening `state.vscdb` read-only makes SQLite create an empty `state.vscdb-wal` and delete it when the connection closes, and AgentsView counted that file appearing, its size and its timestamp as a change. On a 5 GB database with about 540 chats, that kept roughly one core busy indefinitely. With this change the daemon idles at about 0.05 cores.

A WAL of 32 bytes or less holds only the header and no committed data, so it now counts as absent everywhere AgentsView checks for changes: the shared event routing and timestamps used by every agent that keeps sessions in one SQLite file, plus the Cursor IDE, Antigravity, Trae, Windsurf and Hermes fingerprints. No real change is lost, because a commit writes past the header and a checkpoint rewrites the database file. A WAL event for a deleted database still resolves so its sessions get cleaned up, and a WAL that can't be read for a reason other than being missing still counts as a change.

The empty WAL still appears and disappears on every scan. Opening with `immutable=1` would avoid creating it, but that's unsafe while Cursor is writing.

Refs #2059

title: fix(sync): continue when remote host names cannot resolve
body:
AgentsView now skips configured remotes whose hostnames cannot resolve, allowing local sessions and reachable remotes to keep syncing when a private network is disconnected. Previously, that DNS failure could abort an archive upgrade or full rebuild before importing any local sessions.

DNS failures use the existing unavailable-host handling, which preserves the skipped host's archived sessions. Authentication, protocol, import, and cleanup failures retain their existing behavior.

title: fix(layout): make each pane divider one 4px kit-ui resize handle
body:
Both pane dividers in the session view, between the sidebar and the content and between the content and the vitals panel, are now one 4px kit-ui resize handle. Before, each pane drew its own 1px border right beside the 4px handle, so each divider was 5px.

This adopts the single split-handle size from kenn-io/kit-ui#82. kit-ui now owns the handle thickness through one brand token (`--split-handle-size`, 4px). Apps may not restyle the handle, and a pane beside a handle must not draw its own edge.

- **Pane borders removed.** The desktop sidebar loses its `border-right` and the vitals panel loses its `border-left`. The mobile sidebar drawer keeps its right border because it has no handle.
- **Layout math reads the token.** `SPLIT_HANDLE_SIZE` in `sidebar-width.ts` comes from `layout.splitHandleSize` in kit-ui's `brand.json`. It replaces a hard-coded 4 and a separate 1px border term. Without the borders, the sidebar can grow 2px wider before the content column reaches its 480px minimum, so two clamp expectations move from 510 to 512.
- **Modal backdrop test.** The new kit-ui closes a modal only on the click that follows a press which starts and ends on the backdrop, not on `pointerdown` alone. The Go to Session test now sends that full press (`pointerdown`, `pointerup`, `click`) and still checks that the modal closes.

In Chromium, with the vitals panel open, both handles and both dividers measure exactly 4px and the adjacent pane borders are 0px.

The `@kenn-io/kit-ui` pin is kit-ui#82's merge commit (`ceff715`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<sup>generated by a clanker</sup>

title: feat(import): return a reason for each conversation an import refuses
body:
Claude.ai and ChatGPT imports now list each conversation they couldn't write, with its session ID and a reason: diverged, shorter_export, trashed, or transient. A script can drop the first three from its retry queue. The CLI summary splits its error count by the same reasons.

Until now every failure only raised `errors`, so a capture tool couldn't tell an export the archive will always refuse from a write that failed once. In #2054 that meant about 800 import calls over two days.

Existing counts keep their meaning, and a trashed ChatGPT conversation is still a skip. Progress events carry only counts; the final result carries the full `refusals` list with no cap, since a cap would hide IDs a caller needs.

Refs #2054

title: fix(import): restore truncated ChatGPT message text on re-import
body:
Re-importing a ChatGPT export now restores archived messages whose text was cut short. When an archived message's text is the start of the export's text for the same turn, the import writes the full text into the same row, so message IDs, order, pins, and renames stay as they were, and search finds the restored text.

Before, any text difference made the import refuse the whole conversation, so a session archived from a truncating export could never take a later capture. Role, timestamp, and the archived tool calls must still match (completed tool results stay as archived), empty archived text never counts as a cut copy, and any other difference is refused as before.

The repair updates rows in place inside the write that already fills tool results and appends new turns. Replacing the session's messages would reinsert rows when most of them change and give them new IDs.

Refs #2054

title: feat(usage): add a total input card and label uncached input
body:
The Usage page now shows a Total Input card that adds uncached input, cache writes, and cache reads. The old Input Tokens count is relabeled Uncached Input on the summary card, the Top Sessions title, the pairwise comparison, and the Activity timeline tooltip, matching the name the Cache Efficiency panel already uses. With heavy prompt caching, the card read 248.6M while the models read 7.9B prompt tokens, so the page looked like it was missing data. The "+7.6B cached" note under the card was easy to miss. Renaming reuses an existing translated label, so the only new string is Total Input. The browser sums totals it already receives, so costs and the API stay the same. At 1280px the ten cards now wrap to a second row, as they already do when the Copilot credits card shows.
Before
After
In the after version, Total Input shows 7.9B, and the old Input Tokens card reads Uncached Input. Closes #2042

title: feat(import): replace listed sessions and keep the old version in trash
body:
Imports can now replace the archived messages of sessions you list. Pass `--replace <session-id>` to `agentsview import`, or `replace=<session-id>` to the ChatGPT or Claude.ai import route, once per session. The old version moves to the trash as a copy with its messages, name, and pins. Imports that list nothing behave as before.

Until now a ChatGPT session whose export no longer matched the archive, or a Claude.ai session whose export had fewer messages, could never be updated. Every later import refused it, and deleting and re-importing lost pins and renames.

A listed session is replaced only when the normal import would refuse it, so appends keep their message IDs. The live session keeps its name, and pins stay on messages that still match. The copy and the replacement save together, and the copy restores from Trash like any deleted session. Each copy takes the space of the old transcript until the trash is emptied.

Refs #2054

title: Usage on gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol and gpt-6.1-sol stays unpriced without a pricing refresh: the embedded LiteLLM snapshot predates them
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.44.0 (commit 413a87f7bfbd67b2815b1119ac51abc1efbeeaba, built 2026-09-21T12:48:49Z)

Current `main` (`d3764220`) pins the same LiteLLM snapshot and has the same supplemental rows for these models.

### Install method

GitHub release binary (wrapped by a Nix package for NixOS)

### OS / platform

NixOS, Linux x86_64

### Which agent and version

Pi coding agent 0.87.1. agentsview reads the model names and token counts correctly; only the price lookup fails. So I expect any agent that records these plain model names to be affected.

### Which model(s)

`gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` (OpenAI), recorded under those plain names.

### What happened, and what did you expect

When agentsview prices usage from its built-in prices, these three models cost $0. The token counts are correct. I expected them to get a price from the built-in list, the same way `gpt-5.6-sol` does.

This happens when `model_pricing` has never been filled. In my case, a nightly job runs `agentsview sync` and `agentsview export sessions` with `AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1` against its own data directory. The daemon never runs there, so `model_pricing` stays empty, and the export falls back to the embedded prices (`ensureExportSessionsPricing`). `usage --offline` should hit the same gap, because its help says it uses fallback pricing only. I have not tested daemon mode. Going by the code, its pricing refresh should price these models, because current LiteLLM lists them.

Why the built-in prices miss them:

- The embedded LiteLLM snapshot is pinned to LiteLLM `418c7c6012d7c39a9d4a28c72cabe1995595ad2b` (2026-08-21). It has none of the three names.
- The embedded GenAI snapshot (`83a49e8b`) has none of them either.
- `supplemental.go` has a temporary Astra row, but only as `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-6-astra`, reached through the exact alias `openai.gpt-6-astra`. The plain name `gpt-6-astra` doesn't match it. `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` have no row.

LiteLLM `main` (`7d50a31eb5`, 2026-10-02) lists all three under their plain names. Prices are in USD per million tokens:

| Model | Input | Output | Cache read | Above 272k input tokens (input / output / cache read) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6-astra` | 10 | 50 | 1.00 | 20 / 75 / 2.00 |
| `gpt-6-sol` | 2 | 10 | 0.20 | 4 / 15 / 0.40 |
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | 2 | 10 | 0.10 | 4 / 15 / 0.20 |

It now also lists `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-6-astra` (11 / 55 / 1.10), so the temporary supplemental Astra row may not be needed after a snapshot update.

Expected: update the pinned LiteLLM snapshot to a ref that includes these models. That would also bring in their above-272k rates, which a `[custom_model_pricing]` entry can't express.

Workaround until then: add flat rates to `config.toml`. This prices the three models correctly below 272k input tokens:

```toml
[custom_model_pricing."gpt-6-astra"]
input_microdollars_per_mtok = 10000000
output_microdollars_per_mtok = 50000000
cache_read_microdollars_per_mtok = 1000000

[custom_model_pricing."gpt-6-sol"]
input_microdollars_per_mtok = 2000000
output_microdollars_per_mtok = 10000000
cache_read_microdollars_per_mtok = 200000

[custom_model_pricing."gpt-6.1-sol"]
input_microdollars_per_mtok = 2000000
output_microdollars_per_mtok = 10000000
cache_read_microdollars_per_mtok = 100000
```

Related: #1862 and #1636 were the same kind of gap for other model names.

### Sample session file or snippet

The script below writes one minimal Pi session per model. Each has one assistant message with 100,000 input and 10,000 output tokens. The content is made up.

### Steps to reproduce

Run this with agentsview v0.44.0 and `jq` on PATH. It uses a temporary HOME and data directory, and deletes them at the end.

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Needs agentsview v0.44.0 and jq. Uses a throwaway HOME and data dir.
set -eu
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
export HOME="$tmp" AGENTSVIEW_DATA_DIR="$tmp/data" AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1
dir="$HOME/.pi/agent/sessions/--tmp-demo--"
mkdir -p "$dir"
i=0
for model in gpt-6-astra gpt-6-sol gpt-6.1-sol gpt-5.6-sol openai.gpt-6-astra; do
  i=$((i + 1))
  id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000000$i"
  ts="2026-10-01T10:0$i:00.000Z"
  cat > "$dir/2026-10-01T10-0$i-00-000Z_$id.jsonl" <<EOF
{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"$id","timestamp":"$ts","cwd":"/tmp/demo"}
{"type":"message","id":"u1","parentId":null,"timestamp":"$ts","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"hello"}]}}
{"type":"message","id":"a1","parentId":"u1","timestamp":"$ts","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"hi"}],"model":"$model","usage":{"input":100000,"output":10000,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":110000}}}
EOF
done
agentsview sync >/dev/null
agentsview export sessions --all --include-one-shot --format ndjson \
    --date-from 2026-09-30 --date-to 2026-10-02 |
  jq -r 'select(.model_usage) | .model_usage.by_model | to_entries[]
         | "\(.key)\t$\(.value.cost.microdollars / 1e6)"'
```

Output:

```text
openai.gpt-6-astra	$1.65
gpt-5.6-sol	$0.6
gpt-6.1-sol	$0
gpt-6-sol	$0
gpt-6-astra	$0
```

The two control rows are correct: `gpt-5.6-sol` at $4 / $20, and `openai.gpt-6-astra` at the supplemental Bedrock rate of $11 / $55. At LiteLLM's current rates, the other three should be $1.50 (`gpt-6-astra`), $0.30 (`gpt-6-sol`) and $0.30 (`gpt-6.1-sol`). With the workaround block appended to `$AGENTSVIEW_DATA_DIR/config.toml` after the sync, the export returns exactly those amounts.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: feat(api): add fleet search metadata and batch session lookup
body:
## What changed

- Search hits include the machine key and effective session title across supported backends and search modes.
- Session lists accept a batch of IDs and expand raw IDs to host copies. Explicit filters and pagination still apply; hosted reads keep their public-ID boundary.
- `include_source=true` returns available file size and archive update time alongside the source path. PostgreSQL still omits fields it does not store.

## Why

Fleet clients had to resolve each hit and fetch each copy before showing its host or choosing the longest transcript. The response now carries the display metadata, and one list request can retrieve the copies for comparison.

## Usage

`GET /api/v1/sessions?ids=codex:abc,codex:def&include_source=true` accepts up to 100 comma-separated IDs. Tilde-qualified IDs match exactly. Raw IDs include host copies; empty members return 400.

Closes #1791

title: Codex auto-review tokens are priced at $0 because `codex-auto-review` has no pricing row
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.44.0 (commit 413a87f7, built 2026-09-21T12:48:49Z)

### Install method

Desktop app, plus the CLI installed via `agentsview update`

### OS / platform

macOS 14.8 (arm64)

### Which agent and version

Codex CLI 0.159.2, with auto-review enabled

### Which model(s)

`codex-auto-review`

### What happened, and what did you expect

Codex writes each auto-review (guardian) thread with `"model": "codex-auto-review"` in its `turn_context`. The pricing table has no row for that name, so the tokens are counted but priced at $0. In `usage daily --json --breakdown`, the model resolves like this:

```json
"codex-auto-review": {
  "cost_source": "computed",
  "resolutions": [
    {
      "priced_model": "codex-auto-review",
      "matched_pattern": null,
      "input_cost_per_mtok": { "microdollars": 0 },
      "output_cost_per_mtok": { "microdollars": 0 },
      "cache_read_cost_per_mtok": { "microdollars": 0 }
    }
  ]
}
```

Two things look wrong:

1. The cost is under-reported. Auto-review runs on every approval prompt, so its token volume adds up. Most of it is cache reads.
2. The $0 is silent. The token-usage docs describe `matched_pattern: null` with zero rates for reported costs. Here, `cost_source` is `computed` and `pricing.fallback.used` is `false`, so the output does not identify the model as unpriced.

I'd expect one of these:

- Price `codex-auto-review` by default as an alias for a known model.
- Flag it as unpriced, for example under `pricing.fallback.models`, instead of reporting a computed $0.

The `[custom_model_pricing."codex-auto-review"]` setting works around this locally. The rates have to be guessed because OpenAI does not say which model backs auto-review.

Prior art: attn fixed the same gap in SolenesInc/attn#462. It prices `codex-auto-review` at another model's rates, defaulting to gpt-6-luna, through a `billed_as` setting. That PR also notes that Codex now writes `cache_write_input_tokens` separately, which may need the same check here.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Codex CLI with auto-review enabled and trigger an approval prompt.
2. Run `agentsview usage daily --json --breakdown --agent codex`.
3. Find `codex-auto-review` in `modelBreakdowns`. Its tokens are non-zero and its `cost` is 0.
4. Find it in `pricing.models`. Its `matched_pattern` is `null`, its `cost_source` is `computed`, and `pricing.fallback.used` is `false`.

Related: #1644 covers guardian threads indexed as root sessions. That issue is about lineage; this one is about pricing.

title: fix(pricing): refresh embedded LiteLLM rates for GPT-6 models
body:
Refreshes the pinned LiteLLM catalog so session exports from unseeded archives and offline usage reports price `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, and `gpt-6.1-sol`. Cache rates and the above-272k tier apply per request.

The generator retains retired model keys from the previous immutable catalog, with current rows taking precedence. The snapshot now supplies Bedrock Astra directly while preserving its existing namespaced alias. Custom pricing and historical pricing still take precedence.

Closes #2076

title: fix(usage): let summary cards grow for wrapped text
body: Usage summary cards now grow when localized labels or cache notes wrap, so longer text stays inside the cards. English layout tests still require equal heights; the Azerbaijani case allows taller cards while retaining the overflow checks.

title: test(usage): measure cards after comparison text arrives
body:
Usage card layout checks now include the comparison text that arrives after the initial totals. That text overflowed the fixed-height cards in Azerbaijani, as seen in [CI](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/37019779744), but the previous test could measure before it appeared.

#2081 landed the card height fix while this PR was running. This PR keeps that layout and adds a fixed comparison response, waits for its text, and checks Azerbaijani labels at 1280px, 768px, and 400px.

title: fix(parser): price Codex cache writes at the cache-write rate
body:
Codex sessions on GPT-5.6 and later models now bill prompt-cache writes at the model's cache-write rate. Codex counts them as `cache_write_input_tokens` inside its input total, and AgentsView billed them as plain input, so each write came out 20% below what OpenAI charges.

The parser moves those tokens into the cache-write bucket every backend already prices. Context size stays the same, rollouts without the field parse as before, and existing Codex sessions are re-read once after upgrading. One-shot capture still counts writes inside `input_tokens`, since older Codex releases don't record them.

Refs #2078

title: fix(pricing): price Codex auto-review at GPT-5.6 Luna rates
body:
Usage reports now price Codex auto-review turns, recorded under the model name `codex-auto-review`, at GPT-5.6 Luna catalog rates. Before this, their tokens added $0 to every cost total.

OpenAI doesn't publish a rate for `codex-auto-review`. Codex runs the same review role on GPT-5.6 Luna under an API key or Bedrock ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ca466061d64f0b44f416135c7fd06aa7af850bbc/codex-rs/model-provider/src/provider.rs#L122-L126)), so Luna's rates make the estimate. A custom pricing row for the name still wins.

Closes #2078

title: feat(telemetry): count app opens from the web UI
body:
The web UI now reports `app_opened` to its server on load and on the first window focus of each later UTC day, so an open tab counts at most once a day. The browser posts to a new route, `POST /api/v1/telemetry/events`, behind the API's token and origin checks, and the server checks the event against its allowlist before sending it with the heartbeat's install ID and opt-out.

Until now the daemon heartbeat was the only event, so usage counts included installs nobody looked at. This builds on kenn-io/kit#144 and pins kit to its head until a release includes it.

title: Startup sync hangs under launchd when a session cwd is on /Volumes (removable-volume consent prompt not covered by protected-path gating)
body:
### agentsview version

agentsview v0.44.0 (commit 413a87f7bfbd67b2815b1119ac51abc1efbeeaba, built 2026-09-21T12:48:49Z)

### Install method

Other / not sure: the PyPI wheel, run through `uvx agentsview@0.44.0`

### OS / platform

macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), headless Mac mini (nobody at the console)

### Which agent and version

Codex CLI, sessions whose recorded `cwd` is a git repository on an external APFS drive under `/Volumes/`

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened, and what did you expect

With `agentsview serve` running as a launchd LaunchAgent, startup sync never finishes. The log stops at `Running initial sync...`, the `sync-worker` process stays at 0% CPU indefinitely, and the daemon never starts listening. Every restart reproduces it, including with an empty data directory.

The same command, with the same flags and the same data, completes in about 2.4 s when started from an SSH session. It also completes from SSH under `env -i` with the launchd `PATH`, so the environment is not the difference.

A goroutine dump of the stuck worker (`kill -QUIT`) shows it blocked in `os.ReadFile`, called from `readGitRemotes` ← `discoverLocalGitIdentity` (`internal/sync/engine.go:19203` and `:19020` in v0.44.0). The file being read is `<cwd>/.git/config` for sessions whose `cwd` is on the external volume. Granting agentsview access to removable volumes on that Mac (Privacy & Security → Files and Folders) made the same LaunchAgent start in 2.6 s.

My reading is that the read waits on the macOS consent prompt for removable volumes, which a launchd-started process raises and nobody answers on a headless machine.

`mayProbeLocalPath` / `ClassifyLocalPathProbe` exist to avoid exactly this ("Working directories inside macOS TCC-protected locations stay untouched unless the user set scan_protected_paths"). But `protectedUserDataDirs` in `internal/export/project_identity.go` only lists home-relative folders (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Library/CloudStorage, Library/Mobile Documents). A `cwd` under `/Volumes/<name>` is classified as safe, so the probe runs and blocks. `main` appears to have the same list.

Expected: on darwin, a `cwd` under `/Volumes/<name>` (removable or network volumes, not the boot volume's `/System/Volumes/Data` spelling) is classified like the other protected locations and only probed when `scan_protected_paths` is set, so startup sync never waits on a consent prompt.

Two things made this hard to find:

- The hang is silent. There is no timeout and no log line after the discovery count; the daemon simply never listens.
- With `uvx`, a version bump changes the binary path, so a permission granted to the previous binary no longer applies and the hang returns on the next upgrade.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, have a Codex session whose recorded `cwd` is a git repository on an external drive, for example `/Volumes/External/project`.
2. Run `agentsview serve --host 0.0.0.0 --require-auth` as a launchd LaunchAgent (`RunAtLoad`, `KeepAlive`), not from a terminal, and do not answer any prompt.
3. The log stops at `Running initial sync...`. `ps` shows the `sync-worker` at 0% CPU, and `kill -QUIT <sync-worker pid>` shows the goroutine in `os.ReadFile` under `readGitRemotes`.
4. Run the same command from an SSH session: startup sync completes.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: feat(telemetry): report core UI actions through the server
body:
The web UI now reports five actions through the server's telemetry route: `search_run`, `session_viewed`, `export_run`, `insight_generated` and `analytics_viewed`. App opens alone can't show which features people use.

Each event carries one property whose value must come from a fixed list. The server drops other values and still sends the event. Startup builds the agent and insight lists from their registries and passes them to telemetry, so new agents and templates count without adding application dependencies to the telemetry package.

Searches count once per mode used during each command palette visit; typing pauses and setup retries do not add events. Downloads and Gist publishes count attempts, while Markdown links count successful copies. Insights count when generation finishes, excluding cache hits.

title: Docs logo link still breaks the marketing homepage after #1575
body:
### agentsview version

n/a (documentation website, agentsview.io)

### Install method

n/a (website)

### OS / platform

macOS (arm64), Chrome

### Which agent and version

n/a

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened, and what did you expect

Clicking the "AV" logo in the header of any docs page (for example `/docs/usage/`) shows a broken page: the URL changes to `/`, but the browser keeps the docs markup (the "Skip to content" link, the two drawer and search checkboxes, the docs header) with the marketing site's stylesheet applied. The result is unstyled text and two oversized shapes. Reloading shows the correct homepage.

Expected: the logo opens the marketing homepage, fully rendered, without a reload.

This is the same symptom as #1571. The fix for it (#1575) added `data-preview=""` to the logo link, and that attribute is still in the deployed docs header, but the bug still reproduces with a real click.

Cause: `data-preview` enables Zensical's page-preview feature. It does not opt a link out of `navigation.instant`. The instant-navigation click handler skips a link only when it has a `target` attribute or the click uses ctrl/cmd. Otherwise it intercepts the link if the URL is in the docs sitemap. `docs/overrides/sitemap.xml` lists `/` and `/guide/` on purpose, so the marketing pages count as docs pages. The handler fetches `/` and swaps it into the docs document instead of doing a full page load.

Other links that point at the marketing pages hit the same path, such as "product overview" and "five-minute guide" in `docs/index.md`.

Tested on the live site: adding `target="_self"` to the logo link makes the click a normal full page load, and the homepage renders correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open https://agentsview.io/docs/usage/ (any docs page works).
2. Click the "AV" logo at the top left of the header.
3. Observe the unstyled page at `/`. Reload to see the intended homepage.

title: fix(docs): load the marketing homepage with a full page load from docs links
body:
Clicking the AV logo in the docs header now opens the marketing homepage with a normal page load. Before, it showed the docs page with the homepage's stylesheet applied, which rendered as unstyled text and two oversized shapes until a reload.

Fixes #2090. This is the same symptom as #1571, which #1575 tried to fix.

## Why it happened

Zensical's instant navigation intercepts a link when its URL is in the docs sitemap. The only ways to make it skip a link are a `target` attribute or a ctrl/cmd click. `docs/overrides/sitemap.xml` lists `/` and `/guide/` on purpose, so the marketing pages count as docs pages. The handler fetched the homepage and swapped it into the docs document.

#1575 added `data-preview=""`. That attribute turns on page previews and does not opt a link out of instant navigation, so the bug stayed.

## What changed

- The header logo, the sidebar logo, and the two homepage links in `docs/index.md` now carry `target="_self"`. The handler skips them, and the browser does a full page load.
- `docs/overrides/partials/nav.html` is a copy of Zensical's `nav.html` with that one attribute added. The sidebar logo is only rendered by that template, so the copy is the only way to set the attribute. This follows what `header.html` already does.
- `docs/scripts/check_built_site.py` fails the build when a docs page links to `/` or `/guide/` without a `target`. It fails on the previous output and passes on this one.

## Tradeoffs and limits

- `nav.html` can drift from Zensical's template when Zensical updates (pinned at 0.0.45). The comment at the top of the file says why it exists.
- The check covers relative and root-relative links. Absolute links to `https://agentsview.io/` are not covered.
- Links inside the docs pages that point at other docs pages still use instant navigation.

## Where to look

- `docs/scripts/check_built_site.py`: the rule and which links it covers.
- `docs/overrides/partials/nav.html`: confirm the only difference from upstream is the `target` attribute and the header comment.

title: fix(vector): drop permanently deleted sessions on incremental refresh
body:
Permanently deleting a session now removes its vectors from semantic search on the next embedding build. A session that sync removes and later imports again gets embedded again, even when it ended before the index's last refresh point.

Until now only the full backstop scan, which runs every 24 hours by default, removed deleted sessions. Their vectors kept taking search's candidate slots, so live sessions dropped out of semantic and hybrid results. Incremental builds now read the archive's existing session deletion journal. The first build after upgrading, and the first after a resync, runs one full pass.

Split from @salmonumbrella's work in #2080.

title: docs: standardize Markdown frontmatter with root exemptions
body:
Standardize title, description, and last_edited as the first three YAML fields across 103 nonexempt tracked Markdown documents, including hidden guides, historical notes, fixtures, and skill docs. Update two Markdown generation templates to match the generated documents. Preserve existing values and dates; derive missing dates from complete Git body history through renames while skipping metadata-only edits.

Exempt root README.md and AGENTS.md, including the CLAUDE.md symlink alias. Keep their original frontmatter, leave README.md unchanged, and add the exemption-aware maintenance rule to AGENTS.md. Preserve document bodies and other metadata, with two generated ownership hashes refreshed by the production package generator.

The agent guide requires `title`, `description`, and `last_edited` when creating Markdown files, and a body-edit date update when editing any nonexempt Markdown body. Root `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` remain YAML-exempt; metadata-only edits preserve the date.

title: A pricing change makes the next usage page load rebuild every session's rollup
body:
After the daily pricing refresh changes any model's rate, the next dashboard load rebuilds the usage rollups for every session and blocks until it finishes. On my archive the first load after the refresh took 2 minutes 9 seconds. Loads a few hours earlier, on the same server, took about 5 seconds.

Each session's rollup should depend only on the prices of the models that session used, and any rebuild after a pricing refresh should run in the background before someone opens the page.

**Environment.** v0.44.0-73-gf8ba7b1c9 on Windows 11. `sessions.db` is 8.2 GB with about 10,000 sessions. The behavior is still on `main` at be0730d41.

**What happened.** The server started at 19:14 on 10/02. The pricing refresh runs at startup and then every 24 hours ([`pricing_schedule.go:14`](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/be0730d41/cmd/agentsview/pricing_schedule.go#L14)), so the next run landed around 19:16 on 10/03 and updated 34 `model_pricing` rows. When I opened the dashboard at 19:26, `/usage/summary` and `/usage/top-sessions` waited on this:

```
16:26:49 usage rollup read took 5.233s: ... rollup build 760ms ... (9716 candidate sessions; built 494 daily rows, 16 exception rows in 2 groups)
19:28:45 usage rollup read took 2m9.347s: ... rollup build 1m47.624s, rollup install 13.264s ... (10166 candidate sessions; built 65670 daily rows, 16152 exception rows in 13554 groups)
```

The same thing happened at 20:37 on 10/02, about an hour after startup, when a rebuild took 1 minute. Both slow loads came right after a pricing change.

**Why every session goes stale.** The rollup check marks a session stale when its stored pricing hash differs from the current one ([`usage_rollup.go:514`](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/be0730d41/internal/db/usage_rollup.go#L514)). That hash covers the whole pricing catalog, every model's rates plus its `updated_at` ([`canonical_json.go:22`](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/be0730d41/internal/export/canonical_json.go#L22)). A price change for one model I've never used still invalidates sessions that only used other models. In the usage cache afterward, 12,029 `America/New_York` rollups carry the new hash, 8 carry the one from the 10/02 20:37 rebuild, and 4,261 still carry the startup hash.

**Why it shows up as a slow page.** The usage endpoints skip the 30-second request timeout on purpose ([`huma_routes_usage.go:25`](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/be0730d41/internal/server/huma_routes_usage.go#L25)), and the request waits for the rebuild ([`usage_rollup.go:247`](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/be0730d41/internal/db/usage_rollup.go#L247)). Concurrent requests share one build, so this is one rebuild that everyone waits on. The only background builder is the backfill that runs when the archive opens ([`usage_cache_background.go:28`](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/be0730d41/internal/db/usage_cache_background.go#L28)), so nothing rebuilds after a pricing refresh. Whoever opens the page first after the refresh waits for the whole rebuild.

**Windows doubles the work.** The cache holds two rollup sets for the same zone: 15,502 under `Local` and 16,298 under `America/New_York`. On Windows, `usageLocationName` can't resolve `Local` to a zone name because there's no `/etc/localtime`, so the same rollups get built twice under two keys.

To reproduce, run `agentsview serve` on a large archive and load `/usage` once to warm the rollups. Then change the rate on any `model_pricing` row, or wait for the daily refresh to change one, and load `/usage` again. The debug log shows a `usage rollup read took` line that rebuilds every session in the window.

Related: #2093 covers the dashboard requests that hit the 30-second timeout after a day of uptime.

title: fix(usage): share one rollup set between local and named zones
body:
On Windows, the background usage backfill now does half the work: it builds your time zone's totals once instead of twice.

It used to build a second copy under an unnamed "Local" zone that the `/usage` page never reads. That copy doubled the time the backfill held the database while you loaded pages, and doubled the cache: 15,502 rollups under `Local` plus 16,298 under `America/New_York` on an 8 GB archive. The next backfill deletes it.

Part of #2100.

title: fix(usage): scope rollup pricing staleness to each session's models
body:
The first `/usage` load after the daily price update no longer waits minutes for a full rebuild. A price change now rebuilds only the sessions that used the changed model, and the rebuild starts in the background as soon as the update lands.

A price change for any one model used to throw out every session's cached totals, and the next page load paid for all of them. On an 8 GB archive, a 34-row price update made the next `/usage` load rebuild 65,670 daily totals in 2 minutes 9 seconds. The same load a few hours earlier took 5 seconds.

Tradeoff: the usage cache format changes, so the first start after upgrading rebuilds the cache once.

Closes #2100 together with #2101.

title: fix(ci): use canonical roots in macOS backfill test
body:
Fix the overlapping-root backfill test that failed in [macOS CI](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/37149529604). Its manually constructed configuration kept the temporary-directory symlink, while backfill resolved it, producing different source keys for the same transcript. The fixture now uses canonical roots, matching the configuration loader used by both CLI commands, and retains the assertions that watch reuses the completed backfill.

Include the CLI package in macOS pull request checks so this regression is caught before merge.

title: fix(sync): refresh positron projects when timestamps match

Positron project changes now sync even when the workspace file keeps the same size and effective modification time. Sync checks the content hash it already computes. This fixes one of the Windows failures in [CI run #5371](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/37217577170).

The Codex rewrite test also establishes a changed native change time before syncing. Rapid Windows writes can share a clock tick, so the fixture previously failed to create the condition it meant to test.

title: fix(parser): stop counting Claude cross-session peer messages as user prompts
body:
Claude Code can deliver a message from one local session to another. The receiving transcript stores it as a `queued_command` attachment, the same record type AgentsView already turns into a user message for prompts typed while a tool runs:

```json
{"type":"attachment","attachment":{"type":"queued_command","commandMode":"prompt","isMeta":true,
 "prompt":"<cross-session-message from=\"uds:/tmp/example.sock\" from-name=\"peer\" from-mode=\"bypass\">\nBODY\n</cross-session-message>",
 "origin":{"kind":"peer","from":"uds:/tmp/example.sock","name":"peer","fromMode":"bypass","msg_id":"...","body":"BODY"}}}
```

`queue-operation` `enqueue` and `remove` records surround it. Today the parser re-inserts the prompt as an ordinary user message. A message written by another agent therefore raises `user_message_count`, can become the session's first message and sidebar title, and skews any analysis of what people typed. This is the same problem #1131 fixed for queued task notifications.

**What changes**

- `classifyClaudeSystemMessage` recognizes a prompt that starts with `<cross-session-message` and returns a new `peer_message` subtype. Queued commands and plain user records both go through this classifier, so the message is stored as `is_system: true`, `role: user`, `source_type: system`, `source_subtype: peer_message`. That is the same treatment `task_notification` gets, so every backend's existing `is_system = 0` filters exclude it from user counts, first message, and one-shot classification without new schema.
- The stored content keeps the `<cross-session-message>` wrapper, so the sender's `from-name` stays visible and the full text is still there.
- The web UI adds `peer_message` to the promoted system subtypes and labels it "Message from another session" (all eight locales). Without this, the SPA would hide the row as an unknown system message.
- Data version 126 reparses Claude sources once so existing sessions pick up the classification.

**Related records checked**

- Task notifications in the same Claude Code release are `type:"user"` records with `origin:{"kind":"task-notification"}` and a `<task-notification>` body. The existing prefix rule already classifies them. No change.
- Harness notices such as a cross-session delivery notice are `type:"user"`, `isMeta:true`, `promptSource:"system"`. The parser already drops `isMeta` user records. No change.

**Tradeoffs and limits**

- Detection uses the content prefix, which matches how the parser already identifies task notifications and stop-hook feedback. It does not read `origin.kind`. A user who literally types a prompt that starts with `<cross-session-message` would be classified as a peer message. That seems unlikely enough not to justify a second detection path.
- Like task notifications, peer messages are excluded from full-text search, which filters out system rows. Substring, regex, and semantic search still find them.
- A session driven mostly by peer messages, with at most one human prompt, now counts as one-shot and is hidden by default where one-shot sessions are filtered out. That follows from not counting agent input as human input, and matches #1131.

**Where to look**

- `internal/parser/claude.go`: the new classifier case.
- `internal/parser/claude_parser_test.go` with the synthetic fixture `internal/parser/testdata/claude/queued_peer_messages.jsonl`. The fixture covers a peer message that opens a session, a typed queued command, a `type:"user"` task notification, and an `isMeta` notice, and runs both the full and the incremental parser.
- `frontend/src/lib/utils/messages.ts` and `SystemBoundaryCard.svelte`, plus their tests.
- `docs/internal/session-format-sources.md` has the format evidence entry. `docs/session-api.md` and the changelog are updated.

**Screenshots** (synthetic fixture)

Before (v0.44.0): the peer message is a User turn and becomes the session title.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pb3975/agentsview/pr-assets-peer-messages/before.png)

After: the peer message is a collapsible "Message from another session" card, and the typed follow-up becomes the first message.

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pb3975/agentsview/pr-assets-peer-messages/after.png)

![after, expanded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pb3975/agentsview/pr-assets-peer-messages/after-expanded.png)

title: test(rawderive): finish sandbox helper input before exit
body: Linux sandbox tests now wait for the parent's input before exiting, so a fast helper can't turn a successful isolation check into a cancellation error. This fixes the race behind [CI run #5372](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/37231722774) while keeping every security assertion.

title: feat(db): log WAL stalls, reader pool waits, and write lock waits
body:
The dashboard stall in #2093 left nothing in the log to show where the time went. This adds the missing log lines so the next occurrence can be diagnosed. It does not fix the stall, and the cause is still unknown.

On the existing five-minute maintenance pass, the server now logs:

- **A WAL that is not draining.** Each pass runs a passive checkpoint and logs when three in a row leave pages unmoved, which means a long-running reader is holding the WAL. Before, the periodic checkpoint only ran once the WAL passed 512 MB, and a busy result was dropped silently.
- **Requests queueing for a reader connection.** It logs the request count and total wait when requests waited a second or more for one of the four reader connections during the interval.
- **A busy truncate checkpoint**, like any other checkpoint failure.

Slow `InsertMessages`, `WriteSessionIncremental`, and `ReplaceSessionMessages` lines now end with `(lock wait Ns)`. Their timer starts before the write lock is taken, so a slow line could not previously be split into waiting and writing.

Nothing here changes how readers or the WAL behave. The passive checkpoint moves no pages that the writer's automatic checkpoint would not already move. It does take the write lock for its duration, the same as the existing truncate checkpoint.

The stall counter and the pool-wait arithmetic are in `internal/db/wal_diagnostics.go`. The log lines themselves and the lock-wait suffix have no automated test.

Refs #2093

title: fix(sync): skip Git probes on macOS volumes under /Volumes
body:
Closes #2087.

On macOS, `agentsview serve` started by launchd could stop at `Running initial sync...` and never listen. The sync worker was blocked reading `<cwd>/.git/config` for a session whose working directory is on an external drive. macOS asks for Removable Volumes access on that read, and on a Mac with nobody at the console the prompt is never answered.

The protected-path classifier only knew the guarded folders under home (Documents, Downloads, cloud folders), so a cwd under `/Volumes/<name>` counted as safe to probe.

## What changes

- `ClassifyLocalPathProbe` now treats `/Volumes/<name>` and everything below it as a protected location on darwin. The engine and parser gates already consult the classifier, so Git discovery leaves those directories untouched, including when a cwd only reaches the volume through a symlink.
- `scan_protected_paths = true` lifts the restriction, as it does for the home folders.
- The match is lexical and needs no home directory, so it also applies when the home directory cannot be resolved. It folds case and accepts the `/System/Volumes/Data/Volumes/...` spelling.

## Tradeoffs and limits

- Sessions recorded on external or network volumes now get path-only project identity (no Git remote, worktree, or branch) unless the user opts in. This affects people who ran from a terminal that already had volume access and saw Git detail before.
- `/Volumes/<startup volume name>` is a symlink to `/` and is matched too. Telling it apart would need an `Lstat` on the entry; a session recorded under that spelling only loses Git detail.
- This does not add a timeout or a log line around Git probes. With `scan_protected_paths = true` under launchd and no volume grant, the read can still block.

## Where to look

`internal/export/project_identity.go`: `IsMountedVolumePath` and `consentGatedPath` (renamed from `protectedUnderAnyHome`).

title: fix(raw-sync): keep hosted sessions when their source leaves the device
body:
Closes #2112.

Hosted sessions now stay listed, searchable, and curated after their source file disappears from the uploading device, matching the local archive (#1505). Before, a tombstone from `raw-sync watch` deactivated every session the source supplied.

A tombstone now records the source as gone and leaves its sessions alone. If the file returns, its next snapshot updates the same session. Sessions are still removed by user deletion, parser exclusion, or omission from a later full snapshot.

Limits:

- Sessions hidden by earlier tombstones stay hidden until their source returns.
- `pg raw-reparse` cannot reparse a departed source, so its sessions keep the last parser's output.
- The UI cannot mark a session whose source is gone.
- A departed device's copy stays as a variant. A conflicting copy keeps the session ID ambiguous until the user deletes one.

title: fix(ci): restore Antigravity fuzz coverage
body:
Weekly fuzzing can search for parser bugs again after a missing pricing catalog stopped all five targets in [the scheduled run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/37268903906).

The workflow restores the catalog before compilation, and its assertions now account for roles encoded in the payload and messages containing only tool calls, with the failing input retained as a regression seed and all five targets exercised in [this branch run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/37271314097).

title: Hosted raw sync hides a session when its source file leaves the device
body:
### agentsview version

Built from `main` at `1c2b14cf` (after v0.44.0).

### Install method

Built from source

### OS / platform

macOS (arm64) client; hosted PostgreSQL server

### Which agent and version

n/a. The behavior is in the hosted projection and applies to every provider that `raw-sync watch` uploads.

### Which model(s)

n/a

### What happened, and what did you expect

**What happened.** A hosted instance stops showing a session once its source file is gone from the device that uploaded it. When a complete `raw-sync watch` audit finds a captured file missing, it uploads a tombstone, and the hosted projection then removes every session that source supplied. The session:

- leaves the session list and search;
- leaves the trash, if the user had trashed it;
- loses its star and pins from view until the file returns;
- is replaced by a shorter copy when another device holds an earlier prefix of the same transcript.

The raw files and manifests stay in custody. Only the derived session is removed.

**What I expected.** The session stays browsable, as it does in the local archive. #1505 made that the rule for local sync: a missing source sets `source_missing_at` and leaves the session visible, and only the user sets `deleted_at`. It also removed the `preserve_missing_sources` setting because keeping archived data is unconditional. #1470 and #1471 are the reports behind it: agents and users clean up old session files and do not expect to lose history as a side effect.

I found no statement of the intended hosted behavior. #1352 says a disappearing source produces a tombstone and that raw history is retained; it does not say whether the session stays browsable. So this is a report of a difference between local and hosted behavior, and hiding may be deliberate.

**Proposed fix.** #2110 makes a tombstone record that the source left without removing what it supplied. A session is still removed when the user deletes it, when the parser excludes it, or when a later snapshot of a source that reports its full contents omits it.

**Not covered by #2110.**

- Sessions already hidden stay hidden until their source returns. Their branches are deactivated, not deleted, so a repair looks possible, but it is separate work.
- `pg raw-reparse` schedules each source's current head. For a departed source that is the tombstone, so its retained sessions keep the output of the parser version that last saw the file.

### Sample session file or snippet

None needed. Any session reproduces it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Provision a hosted instance and enroll a device (see `docs/hosted-raw-sync.md`).
2. On the device, create one session file under a supported provider root.
3. Run `agentsview raw-sync watch` until the session appears in the hosted session list.
4. Delete or move the session file and wait for the next complete audit (15 minutes by default).
5. Reload the hosted session list and search for text from the session.

Observed: the session is gone from the list and from search. Expected: it is still there.

I derived these steps from the code and have not run them against a deployed instance. What I ran is the projection against a disposable PostgreSQL: accept a snapshot, project it, accept and project a tombstone, then read through the hosted store.

Two existing tests assert the current behavior:

- `TestRawProjectionTombstoneHidesEveryPhysicalInventoryAndReactivationRestoresCuration` in `internal/postgres/raw_projection_provenance_pgtest_test.go`: after a tombstone, the session list, trash, stars, and search are empty.
- `TestHostedRuntimeSubprocessTombstoneRemovesPublicSource` in `internal/postgres/raw_runtime_pgtest_test.go`: the same through the worker and the sandboxed parser.

Relevant code at `1c2b14cf`:

- `internal/rawwatch/auditor.go`, `finishDiscoveryScan`: queues a tombstone for a known source missing from a complete discovery.
- `internal/postgres/raw_projection.go`, `Project`: `replaceMembership := complete && (parsed.Tombstone || parsed.Outcome.ForceReplace)` deactivates the source's branches.
- `internal/postgres/raw_projection_rows.go`, `materializeGroup`: deletes the `sessions` row when no active branch remains.

### Related

- #2110: proposed fix
- #1505: local sync keeps sessions browsable when sources disappear
- #1470, #1471: reports that motivated #1505
- #1352: hosted raw sync roadmap

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues
- [x] I removed secrets and private data from any attached session files

title: Let duckdb push replace a served mirror on Windows
body:
## TL;DR

On Windows, `duckdb push` fails with "Access is denied" while `duckdb serve` has the mirror open, and it tells the user to stop the server. The mirror swap now uses `atomicfile.Replace` from kit, so the push succeeds and serve picks up the new file, as it already does on macOS and Linux.

## How

`os.Rename` on Windows calls `MoveFileEx`, which fails while another handle has the target open. DuckDB opens files with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, and that sharing mode allows a rename with POSIX semantics. `atomicfile.Replace` does that rename. The server keeps reading the old file until its watcher reopens the new one. On Unix `Replace` is `os.Rename`, so nothing changes there. The pinned kit version already has it.

## Reviewer notes

- **The retry loop stays.** A program that opens the mirror without delete sharing still blocks the rename. The error now asks the user to close that program.
- **Eight tests now run on Windows.** They skipped there because of this failure. The reopen tests swap the mirror through `swapMirrorFile` instead of `os.Rename`.
- **I checked the other file-replacing renames.** They already move the old file aside or use `os.Root.Rename`, or their readers use `os.Open`, which blocks `Replace` too.

### [`v0.3.2`](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/releases/tag/v0.3.2): vite-plus v0.3.2: independent package-manager versions and Oxlint plugin APIs

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2)

`vp env use` now sets each package manager's version independently. This release also adds Oxlint plugin APIs and fixes migration, installation, and template extraction.

##### Breaking Changes

##### Package-manager overrides

Direct package-manager commands no longer use `VP_PACKAGE_MANAGER`. Use the matching version variable in shell profiles, CI jobs, and Dockerfiles:

| Previous override for a direct command | New override                |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `VP_PACKAGE_MANAGER=npm@<version>`     | `VP_NPM_VERSION=<version>`  |
| `VP_PACKAGE_MANAGER=pnpm@<version>`    | `VP_PNPM_VERSION=<version>` |
| `VP_PACKAGE_MANAGER=yarn@<version>`    | `VP_YARN_VERSION=<version>` |
| `VP_PACKAGE_MANAGER=bun@<version>`     | `VP_BUN_VERSION=<version>`  |

`VP_PACKAGE_MANAGER` still selects the manager and version for `vp install` and related commands. `vp env use pnpm@10` now changes only the direct pnpm commands. To override `vp install`, set `VP_PACKAGE_MANAGER` explicitly.

The old `.session-package-manager` file is no longer read or migrated. Run `vp env use` again to create the new session files. Projects that use only project pins or global defaults need no changes. See the [environment guide](https://viteplus.dev/guide/env) ([#​2658](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2658), [#​2659](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2659)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ).

##### Installer preferences

`VP_NODE_MANAGER` now controls only Node.js. Existing installations retain saved preferences during upgrades, so `vp upgrade` needs no configuration changes. For scripted installations, set `VP_PM_MANAGER` to apply the same choice to package managers:

| Previous combined setting | New combined setting                    |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `VP_NODE_MANAGER=no`      | `VP_NODE_MANAGER=no VP_PM_MANAGER=no`   |
| `VP_NODE_MANAGER=yes`     | `VP_NODE_MANAGER=yes VP_PM_MANAGER=yes` |

Update installer commands in CI jobs and Dockerfiles. Use `VP_NPM_MANAGER`, `VP_PNPM_MANAGER`, `VP_YARN_MANAGER`, or `VP_BUN_MANAGER` for individual preferences. The interactive prompt retains its combined choice. See the [installer variables guide](https://viteplus.dev/guide/installer-env-vars) ([#​2681](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2681)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ).

##### Vite DevTools

Projects that install `@vitejs/devtools` must update its dependency range from `^0.4.0 || ^0.5.0` to `^0.7.1`. Projects without this optional dependency need no changes. This requirement comes with the Vite upgrade listed below.

##### Highlights

- Installers and `vp upgrade` share setup behavior across platforms, which simplifies maintenance. The installers retain support for older releases ([#​2611](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2611)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ).
- Custom Oxlint rules can import their APIs from `vite-plus/lint/plugins` and `vite-plus/lint/plugins-dev`. `vp migrate` updates supported existing imports ([#​2328](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2328)), by [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2).
- `vp install` and `vp add` now honor `--ignore-scripts` for named packages and managed global installations ([#​2682](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2682)), by [@​jong-kyung](https://redirect.github.com/jong-kyung).

title: Hybrid recall refuses whenever the vector index lags the corpus by one revision — the normal state during extraction
body:
### Summary

`recall query` / `recall brief` in `--mode hybrid` (and `vector`) refuse whenever the recall vector index is **one or more revisions behind** the recall corpus:

```
fatal: … semantic search not available: … recall index is stale: run 'agentsview embeddings build --store recall'
fatal: … semantic search not available: … recall corpus changed during search; retry after the recall index refreshes
```

While an extraction pass is writing entries the index is almost always behind, so hybrid quietly turns into "keyword only" for every caller that falls back. The cause is an exact-equality test. Most refusals guard against nothing: the only thing missing from the index is the few newest entries, and the keyword half of hybrid still finds those.

### Version / platform

- `agentsview v0.43.0 (commit 9be7745, built 2026-09-14)`, installed with `agentsview update`; the gate is unchanged on `main` (`9bfe867`)
- Linux (Arch), SQLite backend, recall extraction enabled, embeddings from a remote Ollama (`nomic-embed-text`)
- About 38,700 accepted recall entries

### What happens

1. Each insert, delete or title/body/trigger change of an **accepted** `recall_entries` row increments `recall_corpus_state.revision` (`trg_recall_corpus_insert/update/delete`, `internal/db/schema.sql:507–540`).
2. `Index.StaleActive` treats the index as stale unless `completed_corpus_revision:<gen>` **equals** that revision exactly (`internal/vector/search.go:521`: `return !ok || completed != wantRevision`).
3. Even when the index is fresh at the start of a search, `recallSearcherAdapter.ValidateRecallSnapshot` (`cmd/agentsview/embed_scheduler.go:438–462`) fails the query if the corpus revision moved **during** the search.

The extraction scheduler writes accepted entries continuously while it distils sessions, so either check trips within seconds:

- Measured on 2026-09-05: a freshly built index went stale in **40 s** with one live session. A drift of one revision is enough to refuse.
- Today (2026-10-05), 06:00–16:00 UTC: 1,065 accepted entries were written, in 21 of the 60 ten-minute slots. Each one is a revision bump. Outside those stretches the index matched the corpus exactly (sampled for 2 minutes while idle). So refusals cluster whenever a pass is distilling, which on a working day is a large share of the time.
- Running `agentsview embeddings build --store recall` immediately before the query does not fix it: the build finishes, an entry lands during the search, and step 3 refuses ("corpus changed during search").

### What I expected

Hybrid and vector should serve from an index that is slightly behind the corpus. The missing entries are the few newest ones, and they stay reachable through the keyword ranking that hybrid already fuses in. Refusing is right when the embedding space or generation does not match (model or config change), or when the lag is large. It is not right for a lag of a handful of revisions.

### Possible fix (happy to send a PR if this direction is acceptable)

- `StaleActive`: keep the strict check for a generation/space mismatch. For the revision, parse the `counter-v1:N` values and call the index stale only when the lag exceeds a bound. The bound could be a revision count, an age, or a config key such as `[vector] recall_max_revision_lag`. The default could be generous, with `0` keeping today's behaviour.
- `ValidateRecallSnapshot`: still fail on a `GenerationFingerprint` change during the search, but accept a corpus revision that only moved forward within the same bound.
- Optionally report the lag (for example `"index_lag": N` in the query JSON, or a note in `recall brief`), so callers know the newest entries were matched by keyword only.

### Workaround in use

Every caller runs `agentsview embeddings build --store recall` before a hybrid query, retries once after a drift refusal, and falls back to lexical after that. That costs about 2 s and a remote embedding round trip per query. It still loses whenever drift hits twice in a row. It also cannot cover agents that call the MCP `query_recall` tool directly, because there is no hook point in front of it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable recall extraction and recall embeddings, and leave the daemon distilling sessions (any active agent session will do).
2. `agentsview embeddings build --store recall`
3. Wait about a minute, then run `agentsview recall query "anything" --mode hybrid --json`. It refuses with "recall index is stale".
4. Repeat step 2 and query immediately in a loop. Some attempts still fail with "recall corpus changed during search".

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (nothing on the recall staleness gate; #1565 was a different hybrid bug)
- [x] No session files attached

title: fix(recall): serve vector and hybrid recall within a revision lag bound
body:
`recall query` and `recall brief` in vector or hybrid mode now keep answering while extraction writes new entries. Before, each new entry left the index one step behind, and every query refused until the next build. Closes #2117.

The index may now trail by up to `[vector] recall_max_revision_lag` changes, 256 by default, or about 50 minutes of steady extraction. Entries newer than the index drop out of the vector ranking only, and hybrid still finds them by keyword. Setting it to 0 restores the exact match.

Hybrid now runs its keyword search after the vector search, so entries written while a query is prepared still match by keyword. It then checks the merged page against the current entries once, so an entry rejected between the two searches drops out instead of the query refusing.

title: chore(hooks): run whole-repo lint, huma-check, and timing budgets at pre-push
body:
Commits now take about 3s instead of 2m because golangci-lint, huma-check, and the timing budget check run on push instead of on every commit, next to NilAway.

Nothing reaches CI unchecked: push still runs all three, and golangci-lint runs there without `--fix` so it fails on issues instead of silently editing the tree after the commit exists.

title: docs(agents): require a user or developer benefit for pull requests
body: Agents now open a pull request only when it has a user-facing benefit or improves the developer experience, and the body names which. Maintainers spend less time reviewing and closing changes that help no one.

title: build(lint): ban raw os.Rename in production code
body: Developers can't reintroduce the Windows failure where replacing a file fails while a reader that opened it with share-delete holds it open, because the linter now rejects `os.Rename` in production code and points at kit's `atomicfile.Replace`. Every production `os.Rename` now uses `atomicfile.Replace`.

title: fix(sync): preserve startup fallback result during polling
body: The startup fallback test now keeps its result for the final assertion, preventing the false timeout in [CI run #5386](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/37376542159). A late `assert.Never` poll could consume that result after the foreground sync resumed; the poll now watches a separate completion signal.

title: feat(sessions): let an orchestrator record a session's parent
body:
An orchestrator that starts workers as separate `claude` processes can now record each worker's manager with `PUT /api/v1/sessions/{id}/parent`. The worker then shows up under its manager in the sidebar tree, the breadcrumb, and the children list. Part of #2115.

`relationship_type` defaults to `subagent` and also accepts `fork` or `continuation`; `delegated` from the issue returns 400. Ids include any remote host prefix. A link can be set before the worker syncs and survives rebuilds, but a parent named in the transcript wins. Remote and read-only serving return 501.

A link that would form a loop returns 400. A later transcript can still contradict a link into a loop that hides both sessions, as two transcripts pointing at each other already do on main; setting the parent to `null` breaks it. A `subagent` worker in another project drops out of that project's list unless its worktree maps to the manager's project.

title: fix(friction): require corrective wording for coding corrections
body:
The Friction Log now counts a short coding reply as a correction only when it reads like one ("no, keep the old name"), so "now run the tests" stops showing up as a correction. It reuses the chat wording check, so "revert that change" alone goes uncounted.

Refs #1924, #1933

title: build(lint): replace the timing budget script with kit's deadline check
body: A test that waits on the wall clock with a sub-second budget now fails lint before it flakes in CI. The copied timing script goes, because kit's shared `deadlinetest` analyzer replaces it and also catches `time.After`, timers, and context deadlines.

title: feat(sync): push one archived session to a remote instance
body:
`agentsview push` shares one exact archived session with a remote instance. It reads local SQLite without syncing source files or following session references. Tokens come from an environment variable or file; JSON output confirms the accepted ID, agent and status.

The receiver must opt in, require bearer authentication and use writable SQLite. Its first accepted snapshot stays immutable: retries with the same transcript content are unchanged, while changed transcripts and existing unowned IDs conflict. Transfers reuse the normalized artifact format with a 64 MiB limit. Restricted signed ingress is unsupported in this version.

The push preserves launcher parent links and allows bounded uploads over slower connections. The archive version stops older binaries from writing over accepted snapshots. A receiver awaiting an earlier archive rebuild refuses pushes until it finishes, and rejects sessions from a newer parser.
