title: fix(import): import Gemini Apps Takeout exports instead of rejecting them
body:
`agentsview source import --type gemini-apps` rejected every real Google Takeout export with `input does not contain a Gemini Apps My Activity HTML document`. Fixes #2947. **Why it failed.** The parser was written against an assumed layout: an `

Gemini Apps

` heading plus `

Prompted

` and timestamp paragraphs in the header. Real Takeout My Activity cells look like this instead: ```html

Gemini Apps

Prompted 
Nov 9, 2026, 9:15:42 PM PST

response…

``` No cell matched, so no file was admitted. The zip and the bare `MyActivity.html` both reach the same parser, so both failed. **What it does now.** - Reads the product name from the header and splits the body cell at the timestamp line. Each `Prompted` record becomes a session with the prompt as the user message and Gemini's response as an assistant message. Session names are now the prompt alone, not the prompt plus the whole reply. Other activity (such as feedback, Canvas creation, `Cleared`, or `Used`) is counted as skipped, as before. - Resolves zone abbreviations through the importing machine's zone (`timeutil.LocalLocation`, which honors `TZ` on every platform). Takeout labels each timestamp with the account's zone abbreviation, which is ambiguous: `IST` means India, Ireland, or Israel, and `CST` means US Central or China. When the local zone uses the same abbreviation in the record's year, its offset wins. Otherwise the existing US/UTC/`GMT±HH:MM` table applies. Unknown zones still fail the whole import before anything is written, and the error says to rerun with `TZ` set. - Counts a record as an error when more than one of its lines matches the timestamp format. A prompt can contain such a line, for example a pasted log, and the markup does not mark which line is metadata. Guessing would give the session the wrong date and split the prompt. - Keeps authored whitespace and boundary newlines in `
` blocks in both prompts and responses.
- Session IDs, the locale and title checks, and the preflight that rejects an unsupported file before any write are unchanged.

**Evidence and limits.** Google publishes no schema for this HTML. The layout matches two independent parsers of real exports, `purarue/google_takeout_parser` and `spookyrunt/split-gemini-activities-by-chats`, and was confirmed on real `Takeout/My Activity/Gemini Apps/MyActivity.html` exports reported in #2947 (including ` ` after `Prompted` and `\u202f` before `AM`/`PM`). Pinned links are in `docs/internal/session-format-sources.md`. This change has not been run locally on a private Takeout export; the scrubbed fixture `internal/parser/testdata/gemini-apps/MyActivity.html` follows the real layout. Activity labels other than `Prompted` are not documented anywhere, and non-English exports remain unsupported. Records are not grouped into multi-turn chats.

**Where to look.** `planGeminiAppsCell`, `geminiAppsPromptText`, and `parseGeminiAppsTimestamp` in `internal/parser/gemini_apps_takeout.go`. The parser tests were rewritten around the real cell shape, keeping the rendering, locale, preflight, identity, and zone cases, and the unused Gemini fixture was removed from `ordinaryImportInputs` in `cmd/agentsview/archive_only_test.go`.

This fixes a user-facing bug: Gemini Apps Takeout imports did not work at all. It does not touch Chrome-based Gemini Sync.

title: hermes: compacted sessions include archived rows, report 0 compactions, and misorder rows near turn end
body:
## Summary
When opening a compacted Hermes Agent session in AgentsView, the session looks much larger, noisier, and slightly out of order compared to Hermes itself:

- Archived pre-compaction messages still show up in the transcript instead of being excluded.
- Compactions aren't detected (`CompactionCount` stays `0`) because Hermes writes the boundary header with an em-dash (`—`), which the parser doesn't recognize.
- Hermes's internal `[STILL IN PROGRESS — ...]` compaction replay prompt shows up as a regular user message.
- Rows near the end of a turn can render out of order (e.g. an assistant reply before the prompt that triggered it), and `EndedAt` uses the wrong last message when row timestamps differ by a few milliseconds.

## Observed example (`local-755c...` session)

| Item in `state.db` | Actual Hermes state | Current AgentsView (`v0.46.1` / `main` `fc988a80`) |
|---|---|---|
| Total vs active messages | `183` rows total, **`43` active** (`140` marked `active = 0` by compaction) | Imports all `183` rows (no `active` filter) |
| `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]` (`id=14404`) | `1` compaction (`—`, `U+2014`) | Compaction not detected (`CompactionCount = 0`) |
| `[STILL IN PROGRESS — ...]` (`id=14426`, `compaction_inflight_task_restatement: true`) | Internal compaction scaffold, not a user turn | Shown as a normal `user` message |
| End of turn (`id=14441` user `steer` vs `id=14442` assistant reply) | `14441` precedes `14442` by `display_order` | Sorted by `timestamp ASC, id ASC`; `14441` had a timestamp 2 ms later than `14442`, so the reply shows before the prompt and `EndedAt` picks `14441` |

## Parser pointers (`internal/parser/hermes.go` at `fc988a80`)
1. **Archived rows included (`readHermesStateMessages` / `hermesStateMessagesQuery`, lines 799-803 & 849-853):** queries `FROM messages` without `WHERE COALESCE(active, 1) = 1`.
2. **Row order & `EndedAt` (`hermesStateMessagesQuery` lines 849-853, `sess.EndedAt` lines 1158-1161):** sorts by `ORDER BY timestamp ASC, id ASC` instead of `display_order ASC, id ASC`, and sets `sess.EndedAt` from the last timestamp-sorted row.
3. **Em-dash compaction boundary (`isHermesCompactBoundary`, lines 1471-1475):** matches `-` and en-dash (`–`, `U+2013`), missing Hermes's em-dash `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]` (`U+2014`).
4. **In-flight restatement leak (`convertHermesStateMessages`, lines 1328-1345):** doesn't check `display_metadata` for `"compaction_inflight_task_restatement": true` (or `display_kind`).

## Environment
- AgentsView `v0.46.1` (verified unchanged in `kenn-io/agentsview` `main` `fc988a80`)
- Hermes Agent local SQLite `state.db`

title: fix(cursor): Make cursor sync-usage retry on 429 instead of aborting
body:
## Why

`agentsview source cursor sync-usage` gives up on the whole sync when Cursor rate-limits it. Users whose sync touches the limit lose the run and have to retry by hand, or wrap the command in their own retry loop.

[Cursor limits](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/admin-api) `/teams/filtered-usage-events` to 60 requests per minute per team, and every tool using the team's admin keys shares that budget. The command requested pages back to back and treated any non-2xx response as fatal. Events are only stored after every page is fetched, so one `429 Too Many Requests` on a long sync, or on a sync running alongside other tools on the same team, stored nothing.

## What it does now

- Requests start at least one second apart, retries included.
- A page that gets a 429 or a 5xx is requested again, up to 5 attempts:
  - It waits for `Retry-After`, capped at 60s. [Cursor's API docs](https://cursor.com/docs/api) say Admin API rate-limit responses carry `Retry-After: 60`.
  - Without that header, it backs off from about 2s, randomized so callers sharing a team don't retry in lockstep.
- Any other failure still ends the run at once: a 400/401/403, a transport error, or a timeout.
- The CLI prints each wait on stderr with the page number, so a 60s pause doesn't look like a hang.

This extends the retry approach the Claude.ai importer already uses (`internal/importer/claude_ai_sync.go`): `cenkalti/backoff/v7`, `httputil.ParseRetryAfter`, 429 and 5xx retried, Retry-After capped at 60s. `fetchClaudeAI` is tied to the Claude.ai response type and its own status rules (401 means log in again, 413 means the response is too large), so this uses the same pieces rather than calling it.

## On real data

I ran the change on my own team's data. The archive and schema were v0.47.0, with this change applied, since the client code is identical on `main`. It synced the last 30 days for one member, filtered by `cursor_admin_email`:

- 32,450 events over 325 pages, in 9.5 minutes, exit 0.
- 1,540 new rows were stored; the rest were already in the archive.
- Requests ran at about 1.8s each, which is Cursor's response time, so the one-second pacing never had to wait. Cursor returned no 429s on this run.

To exercise the retry path for real, I deliberately exhausted my team's budget with 75 minimal concurrent requests. Exactly 60 succeeded. The rest got `429` with `retry-after: 60` and `{"code":"error","message":"Rate limit exceeded"}`. Then, while the limit was still in force, I synced one day:

- **v0.47.0:** `fatal: cursor admin API returned 429 Too Many Requests` after 1s. Nothing stored.
- **This change:** printed `Cursor usage page 1: cursor admin API returned 429 Too Many Requests; retrying in 1m0s`, waited out the window, then fetched and stored all 1,452 events (76s, exit 0).

## Where to look

- `listUsageEventsWithRetry` in `internal/cursorusage/client.go`. Every attempt waits for its request slot inside the retry operation, so the page after a retried page is paced from the retry, not from that page's first attempt.
- `WithMaxElapsedTime(0)`. Backoff's default 15-minute limit would cut off a run of honored 60s waits. Attempts and the context bound the loop instead.

## Limitations

- Transport errors and the 30s client timeout are not retried. They still abort a sync with nothing stored. That's the same outcome from a different cause, but this change is scoped to rate limits and server errors.
- Pacing is per process. Two syncs on the same team at once can still exceed the limit together; the retries absorb that.
- The command holds the archive write lock while it fetches, as before. With waits, a heavily rate-limited sync now holds it longer, up to 4 minutes per page in the worst case.

Model used: Opus 5.5

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: feat(markdown): render KaTeX math in session messages
body:
Session messages now render KaTeX math in both the desktop app and web viewer. Inline dollar and parenthesis delimiters, display dollar and bracket delimiters, supported bare equation environments, and math/latex/tex fences use the same renderer. In a real Codex conversation opened with an isolated macOS desktop build, Euler's identity, integrals, summations, and aligned Maxwell equations changed from literal source into readable equations with both delimiter styles.

Multiline equations containing standalone equals signs also remain intact, including inside numbered lists. The renderer respects display-math boundaries before Markdown can interpret those lines as heading underlines. Rendering another real Codex reply through the message pipeline preserved all eight formulas, all three display equations, and its numbered list.

This extends the existing Marked and DOMPurify pipeline and promotes the already-pinned KaTeX dependency to a direct dependency. Fonts are bundled for offline use. Inline code and ordinary code fences stay literal; unsupported expressions remain readable source, and full LaTeX documents retain their code-block controls. Single-dollar boundaries avoid ordinary currency, trusted TeX HTML commands stay disabled, and macro expansion is bounded.

The tokenizer lives in `frontend/src/lib/utils/math.ts`. Bare environments consume nested matrices through the matching outer closing command, respecting comments and escapes. Message segmentation lets valid math fences reach it, while search text and highlight mapping skip KaTeX's duplicate accessibility tree. Display equations scroll horizontally when wider than the transcript. This supports KaTeX's math vocabulary, not arbitrary LaTeX packages or document compilation.

title: feat(parser): add Factory Droid session provider
body:
Adds a `factory` provider that imports Factory Droid sessions from `~/.factory/sessions/` (override with `FACTORY_DIR` or `factory_dirs`). Closes #1358.

## What it reads

Droid writes one `<uuid>.jsonl` transcript per session in a directory named after the working directory, plus a `<uuid>.settings.json` sidecar. The provider is a `DirectoryJSONLSourceSet` with the sidecar registered as an optional companion: a sidecar write re-parses its transcript, and a missing or unreadable sidecar only drops usage. Freshness requires the content hash, so a sidecar rewrite with the same size and mtime still resyncs. Every parse replaces the stored messages, because a `tool_result` appended after a sync folds into an earlier tool call that an append-only write would never update.

- **Transcript:** The session ID is the file name. `session_start` supplies the title, cwd, and, for subagent sessions, a validated `callingSessionId` that becomes a subagent link to the parent. `message` records use Anthropic-shaped content blocks and go through `ExtractTextContent`. Bookkeeping records only extend the session time bounds. Reading honors cancellation, oversized lines count as malformed, and project lookup follows the remote-import filesystem discovery policy.
- **Visibility:** `llm_only` user rows are injected `<system-reminder>` context and are dropped. `user_only` user text (provider errors, MCP status, skill notices) is kept as a system row and does not count as a prompt. `user_only` tool_use/tool_result pairs are nested Script tool calls and stay as ordinary rows. A prompt with pasted images opens with an "Attached image local file paths" reminder; it is stripped, and each image is marked `[image]`, so image-only prompts are kept.
- **Usage:** Droid records no per-message usage. The sidecar's `tokenUsage` becomes one aggregate event per session, and each entry in `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId` becomes one more event on the same session. Provider identity comes from `providerLock` (older releases wrote `apiProviderLock`). The sidecar is read only when it is a regular file, capped at 16 MiB, and negative counters are floored at zero.

## Usage accounting

- **Session source:** Every Factory event uses the `session` source. These are cumulative totals covering many requests, so they are not clamped to the per-request token bound and stay out of the per-turn rollups.
- **Subagents counted on the parent only:** A session with `callingSessionId` emits no usage events. The parent lists every child whether or not the child has a transcript, so each child is counted exactly once regardless of which child transcripts exist, appear later, or are removed.
- **No peak context:** Sessions set total output tokens from the events but leave peak context unknown, because the sidecar has no per-request measurements.
- **One session per transcript:** Every transcript parses to exactly one session, even with no visible messages or usage, so each sync replaces the stored messages and usage. The sidebar already hides zero-message sessions.

## Tradeoffs and limits

- The format is not published (Droid is closed source). It was recorded from local `version: 2` transcripts, and the evidence entry in `docs/internal/session-format-sources.md` lists what was checked.
- Subagent events are priced as the parent session's model, because the sidecar does not record the child's model.
- A persisted subagent session shows its messages but no usage of its own; its usage appears on the parent.
- Bring-your-own-key models are recorded as `custom:<name>-<index>` and stay unpriced unless the user maps them with `price_as` in custom model pricing.
- Images are shown as `[image]` markers, not rendered.

## Where to look

- `internal/parser/factory.go`: transcript and sidecar parsing, including `factoryUsageEvents` and `readFactorySettings`.
- `internal/parser/factory_provider.go`: source set wiring and capabilities.
- `internal/parser/capabilities_sync_test.go`: Factory's hash-required freshness declaration.
- `internal/parser/testdata/data-version-corpus/factory/` and the new `182-*.json` digest record: first digest for the new provider at the current data version, with no bump.
- Docs: README and configuration discovery tables, env var references, token-usage coverage, changelog, and the website agent list.

The original provider commit is by @sra. The follow-up commits rebase it onto current `main` and update it for current Droid output.EOF

title: Feature request: Add "Match device" appearance mode
body:
## Problem / motivation

Currently, the appearance (light / dark) has to be selected manually. If I use agentsview on multiple devices, or my OS switches between light and dark during the day (e.g. macOS / Windows automatic appearance), agentsview does not follow along, so I have to change the setting by hand each time.

## Proposed solution

Add a third appearance option, **"Match device"** (also commonly called "System"), alongside Light and Dark:

- When "Match device" is selected, agentsview follows the device / OS / browser color scheme (`prefers-color-scheme` for the web UI, and the OS appearance setting for the desktop app).
- It should update automatically and live when the device appearance changes, without a reload or restart.
- Ideally, make "Match device" the default for new installs, while keeping Light and Dark as explicit overrides for users who prefer a fixed appearance.

## Alternatives considered

Manually toggling light / dark in settings whenever the device appearance changes — this works, but it is repetitive and easy to forget, especially across multiple devices.

title: perf(sync): stop re-checking Claude subagents on each tool-result write
body:
A tool result that Claude Code writes during an active session now makes sync re-check only the session that owns it. Since #3131, a result from a root session also re-checked every subagent transcript under that session. Each one was hashed and then skipped, on every local watcher batch that held a new tool result.

**User-facing benefit:** less disk I/O and CPU while a Claude session with subagents is running, with no change to what gets imported or uploaded.

#3131 made `claudeSourceSet.sourcesForToolResultPath` run for Claude so that a remote mirror journal listing a tool-result file maps to its session rather than falling back to the whole provider. The local watcher calls the same mapping. It delivers every file under the Claude projects directory, because the engine drops watch globs. So the subagent fan-out that ICodeMate uses reached local Claude watching too.

For Claude sync, the fan-out cannot import anything. Claude fingerprints hash only the transcript. A subagent whose transcript is unchanged is always skipped, and a changed subagent transcript arrives as its own changed path. Sync now fans out only behind `sidecarSources`, which ICodeMate sets because its composite fingerprints include the parent session's tool results.

Raw capture keeps the fan-out for Claude. A subagent's capture plan uploads its parent session's tool results, so `claudeProvider.RawCaptureSourcesForChangedPath` still recaptures each subagent when a parent result changes. The split lives in `claudeSourceSet`: `SourcesForChangedPath` and `RawCaptureSourcesForChangedPath` share one mapping and differ only in whether a root result includes subagents.

On my Claude projects directory, the 1,343 root-session tool results selected 25,834 transcripts for sync before this change and 1,343 after, one each. The largest single fan-out was 134 transcripts.

**Known limit, unchanged from `main`:** a tool result that arrives after its transcript was imported leaves the missing-result placeholder in place, for the owning session and its subagents alike. Selecting a session for sync does not re-parse an unchanged transcript, because Claude fingerprints hash only the transcript. On `main`, a late parent result selects the subagent too, and its placeholder still stays. Closing this gap needs composite Claude fingerprints, which would force a full Claude reparse on every archive.

Model used: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(cursor): support multiple authenticated accounts for usage tracking
body:
### Problem / motivation

Currently, the agentsview cursor integration only supports a single authenticated account. As a result, users who utilize multiple Cursor accounts cannot accurately track their total usage or aggregate their activity data within the tool, leading to incomplete insights.

### Proposed solution

Update the Cursor integration to support multiple accounts. This could involve allowing users to add or link multiple credentials within the configuration, ensuring that usage reports and session data are correctly synced and attributed across all user accounts.

### Alternatives considered

- Manually switching between profiles (impractical for daily use).
- Consolidating data externally (breaks the seamless integration provided by agentsview).

title: Sessions that work on a PR they didn't open aren't linked to it
body:
The `pr` filter in `list_sessions`, along with the PR links on a session, misses most sessions that work on a pull request. A PR link only gets recorded when Claude Code writes its own `pr-link` entry, which happens when that session opens the PR. A Codex session started with a prompt like `$pr https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123` and running for a day of fixes on that PR has no link to it, so `list_sessions` with `pr: owner/repo#123` returns nothing. A Claude session that picks up a PR someone else opened has the same gap.

Proposal: link a session to every pull request URL in its user prompts, for every agent, using the same normalization and deduplication as `pr-link` records. Codex sessions could also link through the `git_branch` they already store when it matches a PR's head branch, but the prompt URL covers the common case without calling GitHub.

This breaks the "is another agent already working on this PR?" check. An agent looking for a running session on a PR got zero results while one was mid-run, concluded nobody owned the PR, and started pushing to the same branch. A full-text search for the PR URL returned the right session first.

title: feat(search): link sessions to pull requests named in their prompts
body:
You can find a session by a pull request its prompt names, even when the session didn't open it. A Codex session started with `$pr https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123` now matches `owner/repo#123` in the PR filter.

Prompt mentions use the same identity as structured `pr-link` records, and a session shows one link per pull request. A prompt-derived match means the prompt named the pull request, not that the session changed it.

Local archives backfill from retained prompt text when AgentsView opens after an upgrade. For hosted sessions, run the explicit raw reparse rollout:

```bash
agentsview replica pg raw-reparse hosted --run-id <id> --batch-size 64
```

Closes #3195

title: perf(postgres): restore finished activity reports after restart
body:
After a restart, a finished PostgreSQL Activity month took 1.8 seconds to reopen instead of 5.6, and a year took 2.2 instead of 7.6.

| Range | Restart page load (s) |
| --- | --- |
| Past month | 5.6 → 1.8 (3.1×) |
| Past year | 7.6 → 2.2 (3.5×) |

On the long-lived PostgreSQL fixture, an empty first visit cost 4.0 seconds more for a month and 4.5 seconds more for a year. After a write, a year took 4.3 seconds longer. Those regressions left too little consistent benefit to continue this PR.

Reuse requires matching database identity, prices, timezone rules, and history; after 128 unvalidated updates, the report rebuilds. The cache holds up to eight reports or 128 MiB, whichever fills first, and expires unopened files after 30 days. Larger reports use the full read.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/1451

title: Agent content searches starve homepage panels until they time out
body:
AgentsView's homepage times out while agents run content searches through MCP: every analytics panel fails with "request timed out" after 30 s, while lighter requests such as the session list still answer in about 20 ms. Agent searches and page panels share the same three bulk reader connections, so a few slow all-history searches leave the panels waiting in line until the request limit cuts them off.

The proposal is to keep reader capacity for page requests that agent searches can't take, default MCP `search_content` and `search_sessions` to a recent window (for example the last 30 days) when the caller gives no date or session, saying so in the response along with how to search further back, and stop a search after a time limit so it frees its connection. Each change ships with a measurement of homepage waits under a replayed search load.

This happened on Nov 19, 2026, on a local SQLite server (build `a0c95ef21`, Linux, 256 cores, `GOMAXPROCS=16`) with a 139 GB database holding 4.9 million messages. From about 10:05 to 13:00 ET, a batch of agent sessions sent 300–750 content searches every 10 minutes, peaking around 70 a minute. CPU wasn't the limit: the server used about 2.8 cores.

What was measured on that server:

| Request | Alone | During 4 concurrent searches |
|---|---|---|
| `analytics/summary`, last 30 days | 2.2 s | 18 s, finishing only after the searches did |
| `sessions?limit=1` | 0.02 s | 0.02 s |
| Substring `search/content`, all history | 18.7 s | |
| The same search with `date_from` 30 days back | 5.2 s | |

The homepage fires its panel requests together, so at that search rate each panel queued behind ~19 s searches and crossed the 30 s request limit.

Main still sets `readerMaxOpenConns = 4`, with `bulkReadSlots = readerMaxOpenConns - 1` keeping one reader for quick reads (https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/main/internal/db/db.go#L714-L715). Analytics panels count as bulk reads, which is why the session list stayed fast while the panels timed out.

To reproduce: on a large archive, start four all-history substring searches through `/api/v1/search/content` at once, then request `/api/v1/analytics/summary` for the last 30 days. The summary waits for the searches to finish.

title: perf(postgres): refresh finished activity ranges by changed session
body:
After syncing a few sessions, you can reopen a past-month or past-year Activity report and see current runs and totals while the report refreshes changed sessions and affected snapshot peers. Today, one sync makes a finished report rebuild all of its inputs, including unchanged transcripts.

The path reuses session inputs and bounds retained message times to the selected range. The target needs about one second saved on both pages and at most 256 MiB retained. Three-pair medians vs main:

| Archive | Past month (s) | Past year (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Archive 1 | 5.6 → 5.2 (1.1×) | 7.1 → 6.4 (1.1×) |
| Archive 2 | 5.6 → 5.7 | 7.2 → 6.9 (1.0×) |

Archive 2's month regressed 56 ms; the best gain was 0.779 s. Reports matched, and other visits stayed within drift. The gate left live retained bytes unmeasured, so the candidate is dropped.

title: fix(services): clean up test databases after each run
body:
Developers can run `make test-postgres`, `make test-clickhouse`, and `make bench-pg-usage` at the same time, each with its own database container. Before, each run left a container up on port 5433 or 19000.

Each run gets its own Compose project on a free local port. After tests finish or receive Ctrl-C, `SIGHUP`, or `SIGTERM`, the wrapper waits for every test process to release the lease, then tries to remove the project, its volumes, and labelled test containers. If Docker cleanup fails, the lease stays and a labelled container may remain.

A `kill -9` skips cleanup and leaves the lease file and any container. The lock releases when the last process exits, so a future cleaner can identify the run.

title: perf(postgres): fill Dashboard frustration counts at startup
body:
The first Dashboard visit after AgentsView starts on PostgreSQL loads in about 6 seconds instead of 20. Today that visit waits while the server scans every prompt to count frustration signals; on a 30,946-session archive that scan holds the page for about 19 seconds. Startup now prepares those counts after the Usage warm-up, so the first visit reads them.

| First Dashboard visit after startup, 30,946 sessions | Seconds |
|---|---|
| Run 1 | 19 → 6.4 (3.0x) |
| Run 2 | 20 → 5.8 (3.4x) |

Later visits on main already reuse the counts the first visit saved, at 3.1 to 3.3 seconds. The Usage warm-up takes the same time as before (683 → 672 s, then 746 → 748 s in reverse order). A visit that arrives before preparation finishes, or right after new sessions sync, has no measured gain yet.

title: refactor(postgres): store hosted and pg push vectors through Kit
body:
A fix to Kit's Postgres vector code now reaches AgentsView with a version bump. Before, a Kit change to how vectors are batched or how the nearest chunks are searched used to need a matching hand edit in AgentsView's own copy of that SQL. Here, AgentsView drops about 270 of those lines and uses Kit's shared chunks code.

If a local index holds an all-zero vector, `pg push` used to store it, and that chunk could never match a search. It now stops and says to run `agentsview index embeddings build --repair-invalid`. Semantic search now needs pgvector 0.8; on 0.7 it reports unavailable until you upgrade, with no rebuild.

The branch pins Kit [v0.58.1](https://github.com/kenn-io/kit/releases/tag/v0.58.1), which includes the Chunks API this PR uses.
Related: [agentsview#1352](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/1352)

title: feat(frontend): show injected <skill> blocks as skill disclosures
body: Some harnesses inject a skill into the user's message as `...`, sometimes followed directly by the user's own text after the closing tag. AgentsView showed these as a long block of raw text. Now they show as the existing collapsible skill row, with the skill name in the label and any trailing user text below it, the same way `[Skill: name]` blocks already do. ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## What changed - `content-parser.ts` finds `...` blocks next to the existing `[Skill: name]` rule. The `name` must be double-quoted; the body can span lines and the tags need not be on their own lines, so text before or after stays normal text. Tags inside inline code or fenced code blocks (backtick or tilde) are ignored. Other attributes, such as `location`, are dropped. - The skill body now gets the same prose styling as a normal message. The `.markdown` rules in `MessageContent.svelte` are scoped to that component, so the `.markdown` div inside `SkillBlock` never matched them and headings, lists, and tables rendered unstyled. This was already true for `[Skill: name]` blocks. I wrapped `SkillBlock` in a `.markdown` element in `MessageContent`, and aligned the body padding with the header. - Tests in `content-parser.test.ts` cover multiline bodies, surrounding text, extra attributes, code spans and fences, and an unclosed tag. ## Limits This change is display only. Markdown export, server-side search text, and stored message content still contain the raw `` tags. Claude Code and Codex skill bodies are dropped by their Go parsers before they reach the UI, so this change does not affect them. ## Trying it on my data I ran the change in the dev server against two of my own Pi sessions that contain injected skills. Both rendered as collapsed skill rows that expand to styled Markdown. The screenshots above use a synthetic session instead of my own. Model used: Claude Sonnet 5.5

title: feat(settings): add a Match device theme option
body:
Closes #3179.

Settings > Appearance > Theme is now a three-way choice: **Match device**, Light, or Dark. With Match device, AgentsView follows the OS or browser color scheme and switches live when it changes. No reload is needed.

**Why:** the kit-ui theme store already supports this mode, and it is the default when no theme is saved. But the old Settings button only switched between Light and Dark, and every click saved a fixed theme. After one click, no control could return the app to following the device. Also, the theme store from before #957 saved `light` on first load. So most people who installed before #957 are fixed to Light and could not get out. This change gives them a way back.

**What changed:**
- `ui.themeMode` exposes kit-ui's `getThemeMode` and `setThemeMode`, including `system`.
- The Theme row uses the shared `SegmentedControl`, the same control as Chart colors and Message layout.
- A new `appearance_match_device` string, added in all 8 locales.

**Limits:**
- The header sun/moon icon still toggles Light and Dark. A quick one-click override is useful there, and Match device is a setting you choose once.
- Saved `light` and `dark` values are not changed. People who installed before #957 still start on Light until they choose Match device.
- In the Tauri desktop build, this depends on the webview reporting `prefers-color-scheme`. The macOS and Windows webviews follow the OS setting.

I tried it on my own archive in Chromium. With a saved `light` theme and the OS set to dark, choosing Match device turned the page dark. With the OS set to light, it stayed light. In both cases it saved `system`.

Model used: Opus 5.5

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Update Huma to v2.41.0 to use its upstream schema and request-validation fixes. The published OpenAPI document and generated Go and TypeScript clients remain unchanged. No nullable UUID workaround tags were present to remove.

AgentsView already uses JSON v2 decoding, so the release's default JSON decoder changes need no adapter.

The API and client tests pass. The local short suite has capture-permission failures; two focused cases pass under `umask 077`. Its IPv6-loopback failure also reproduces with the original dependency graph.

title: fix(parser): show Pi /skill: invocations as a skill row and the typed prompt
body: When a user sends `/skill:NAME some text` in Pi, Pi's terminal shows a collapsed skill entry followed by the user's text as a normal message. AgentsView showed one user message that held the raw `` block, so the skill's markdown ran into the prompt and the session title and sidebar preview were the opening tag. AgentsView now matches Pi: a collapsed skill disclosure, then the user's own prompt. ## What changed - The Pi parser (`internal/parser/pi.go`) splits a user message that is a skill expansion into two rows. The skill row is a system row with the subtype `skill_invocation` and the content `[Skill: NAME]...[/Skill]`. The user row is the text typed after the skill, or `/skill:NAME` when there was none. The match is a Go port of the regex Pi uses in `parseSkillBlock`, so only the exact expansion format is split. Any other text, including a `` tag that appears mid-message or in an assistant reply, is untouched. - The skill row is a system row on purpose. Ingest counts user messages as `role=user AND NOT is_system`, so the skill body does not inflate user message counts, the prompt picker, one-shot detection, or automation detection. It stays out of in-session search for the same reason. A bare `/skill:NAME` still gets a user row, so counts and titles are the same as before. - In the transcript, the skill disclosure attaches to the top of the user prompt that follows it, so the pair reads as one turn. A skill row with no following prompt, or when only the System block is shown, renders as its own card labelled "Skill". The System toggle owns the row. - Data version 188 reparses existing Pi sessions in place. The scope entry covers the six providers that share the Pi parser: Pi, OMP, OMO, StepCode, Direct API, and Prime Agent. Session ids do not change. - The `.markdown` wrapper in `MessageContent.svelte` is there because that component's prose styles are scoped to it, so `SkillBlock`'s own markdown would otherwise render unstyled. - `docs/internal/session-format-sources.md` records the Pi format evidence, as the provider provenance rule requires. ## Why the parser and not the frontend This redoes #3279, which I closed. That attempt parsed `` blocks in the frontend. Each review round found another Markdown edge case: inline code, fences, CRLF, shell output. Codex, Copilot, Zencoder, and Hermes already handle their skill formats in their Go parsers. The Pi format comes from Pi core, not an extension (`AgentSession._expandSkillCommand` and `parseSkillBlock` in `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.5.2). ## Running it on real data I ran it against 3,473 Pi session files from my own machine. All 101 `/skill:` expansions match the regex, and there is no other injection format. I also served the branch against a copy of a real session that runs a skill with arguments. Before, it was one user message with the raw tag and the skill body. After, it is a collapsed skill disclosure on the user prompt, and the sidebar title is the prompt. ## Limits - OhMyPi adds its `/skill:` invocations as custom-message entries from a prompt template, which the Pi parser does not read. They probably do not appear at all today. I have not verified that, and this PR does not change it. - Codex, Claude, and Posit Assistant skill use is unchanged. Co-authored-by: pi Model used: Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5

title: test(e2e): wait for auth settings to save before checking access
body:
The Playwright test `retries a lost restart request against the real daemon` failed once and passed on retry in the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/44804647552/attempts/1). The recorded CI assertion is unavailable. On current `main`, delaying the authentication settings save reproduces `Expected: 401, Received: 200` in that test.

The browser marks the authentication switch checked as soon as it is clicked. The server still accepts unauthenticated requests until it processes the save. The test races that save by sending its unauthenticated ping after checking only the switch's appearance.

Wait for the switch to re-enable, which happens after the save completes, before asserting that the server rejects the request. Both the original test and a reproduction with a delayed save pass against an isolated real daemon. The same brief interval can occur during normal use while a save is pending; this change corrects the test's ordering and leaves application behavior unchanged. The lost-request retry, restart, saved settings, and authentication assertions remain in place.

Model used: GPT-6

title: fix(postgres): keep page reads working at role limits
body:
Pages served by `pg serve` stay fast while agents search sessions through `agentsview mcp --server`. At 228 searches a minute on main, the dashboard's median load was 6.3 s and the slowest 5% of searches took 9.7 s, because searches and page reads waited on the same few database connections.

| Measurement | Before → after (speedup) |
| --- | ---: |
| Dashboard median at 228 searches/min, s | 6.3 → 3.2 (1.9×) |
| Search p95 at 228 searches/min, s | 9.7 → 0.31 (31×) |
| Search p95 at 456 searches/min, s | 12 → 0.32 (38×) |

`pg serve` and hosted serving now open up to 15 connections, never more than the login role allows, and a page read waits for a free connection when all are busy. On a role limited to five connections, pages load instead of failing. These numbers come from a prototype with the 15-connection pool alone. The role-limit cap came after it and wasn't re-measured.

A burst can still use every connection a role allows, so another client on that role, such as `replica pg push`, can fail to connect, as it can on main today.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3260

title: Roadmap: Link sessions to pull requests they act on
body:
Asking AgentsView "which session is working on this PR?" misses sessions that drive a PR through commands rather than prompts. An orchestrator can select a PR, launch a worker for it, and check, edit, or merge it with `gh` without naming the PR in its own prompts.

Link a session to a PR when a `gh pr` command names it, a push updates its head branch, or a child-agent prompt names its URL. Use the existing PR identity and deduplication. This covers the same ownership check described in https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3195.

### Outcomes

PR-scoped search finds sessions that select, update, or delegate work on a PR. A prompt mention identifies a reference; it doesn't prove the session acted on that PR.

### Delivery sequence

1. Link sessions from `gh pr` commands and child-agent prompts.
   PR: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3303
2. Link sessions from pushes to an existing PR head branch.

### Design constraints

Older transcript-only and usage-only archives that dropped tool inputs can't recover past command or child-prompt links.

title: MCP lookups often fail, and nothing records it
body:
Agents using the AgentsView MCP tools hit an error, an empty result, or a result too large to read in most lookups, and nothing records when that happens. In 30 days of one heavy user's sessions, a quarter of lookups gave up on the tools and read raw transcript files or queried `sessions.db` instead. Many of the failures come from inputs the tools could accept, such as a plain Codex session ID, or from defaults that return more than a client can read.

Proposal: record the outcome of every MCP call so failures can be counted, then fix the tool arguments, output, and descriptions behind the failures below. Once outcomes are recorded, a benchmark of common questions can measure how many calls each takes, and the tools can be tuned to answer in fewer steps.

## How lookups fail

A lookup is one question an agent answered with AgentsView, from its prompt until the next one. Over 30 days: 4,491 lookups, about 59,000 MCP calls (89% from Codex), and about 1,200 `agentsview` CLI calls. Result text survives for 2,043 lookups. AgentsView doesn't store MCP results, and older Codex transcripts were already pruned from disk, so the counts below come from the raw transcripts still on disk.

| What happened | Lookups | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fell back off the MCP tools | 1,096 | 24% of all |
| …read raw transcript files | 1,010 | 22% of all |
| …queried `sessions.db` | 134 | 3% of all |
| …used the `agentsview` CLI | 46 | 1% of all |
| …parsed an oversized result the client saved to a file | 70 | 2% of all |
| Result too large to read whole | 802 | 39% |
| Came back empty | 627 | 31% |
| Searched again after an empty result or error | 421 | 21% |
| Codex printed the tool descriptions before calling a tool | 414 | 20% |
| Tool returned an error | 390 | 19% |
| "session not found" | 298 | 15% |
| A `get_messages` page came back with every message filtered out | 248 | 12% |
| Arguments rejected | 196 | 10% |
| No visible trouble | 637 | 31% |

Shares without "of all" are of the 2,043 lookups with results. A lookup takes a median of 4 MCP calls; 1 in 10 takes 25 or more. Most lookups load context for PR or issue work (about half), read a named earlier session, or audit how earlier agent runs behaved.

## Causes and fixes

**Session IDs.** `get_session_overview`, `get_child_sessions`, and `get_messages` reject a plain Codex UUID with "session not found" and only accept `codex:<uuid>`, while `search_sessions` accepts both. 281 lookups passed a plain UUID, and most recovered by retrying with the prefix. Every tool that takes a session ID should resolve the same forms `search_sessions` does, and report an unknown ID as an error rather than an empty page. The web app has the same seam: `/sessions/<uuid>` works but redirects to `/sessions/codex/<uuid>`, so the address bar shows a storage key. The prefix exists for copies of one session under two tools or machines, so a plain UUID can resolve to its only copy and ask only when there are two.

**Arguments.** Agents pass arguments one tool takes to another:

- `include_one_shot` on `search_sessions`: 129 lookups. `list_sessions` takes it.
- `concepts` with `mode` other than `semantic` on `search_content`: 87. The schema says concepts imply semantic, but the call fails instead of switching.
- `search_content` paging without `activity_cutoff`: 24. The cursor could carry the cutoff.
- `query` instead of `pattern` on `search_content`: 13. `git_branch` on `list_sessions`: 16.

Accepting the obvious alias, or naming the accepted fields in the validation error, ends the retry.

**Output size.** Codex cuts any tool output over about 10,000 tokens down to its start and end, and 69% of Codex lookups hit that (760 of 1,096). Those outputs had a median of 15,500 tokens and a 90th percentile of 35,700. `search_content` and `get_messages` cause most of it. Claude saves oversized results to a file, which 4% of Claude lookups hit. A server-side size budget per response, with a cursor to continue and a total count, keeps each result readable.

**Empty results.** Agents get nothing back and search again in 21% of lookups. Default multi-word substring search comes back empty far more often than hybrid search. Sessions active in the last 10 minutes are hidden by default, which is wrong for "who is working on this right now," and a retry with `include_active` found results in dozens of lookups. `search_content` returns retry hints on an empty result; `search_sessions` and `list_sessions` don't.

**Descriptions and server instructions.** The server's only instruction is "Use returned web_url values when linking to recorded sessions." Codex agents can't see tool descriptions up front, so 20% of Codex lookups spend a call printing them. Short server instructions should name the tool for each common question: a session by topic, a named session, who owns a PR or task, what a session did, and what is running now. They should also cover the ID forms and the filters that hide sessions.

**Missing data.** The fallbacks show what agents can't get from the tools: thinking text alone, per-message timing, regex matches with wide context across a session, whether a session is still running, subagent transcripts, tool result bodies (`get_tool_calls` returns only their size), and cost joins across sessions. Each needs a tool option or a pointer to the tool that already has it.

**Slow search.** 1 in 10 Codex scripts that call `search_content` run 30 seconds or more, and 751 returned before the search finished. A default date window or partial results would bound this.

## Delivery sequence

1. Record each MCP call's tool, argument names, outcome (ok, error, empty, or truncated), result size, and duration, so failure rates are measurable going forward instead of rebuilt from transcripts.
    Slice 1: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3297
2. Resolve session IDs the same way in every tool, and error on unknown IDs.
    Slice 2: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3304
    Slice 3: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3290
3. Accept or redirect the mismatched arguments above, and name accepted fields in validation errors.
    Slice 4: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3292
    Slice 5: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3295
4. Add a response size budget with continuation and totals to `search_content`, `get_messages`, and `get_tool_calls`.
    Slice 6: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3301
5. Write the server instructions, and add empty-result hints to `search_sessions` and `list_sessions`.
    Slice 7: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3291
    Slice 8: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3323
6. Add the missing data in the order the fallbacks rank it.
    Slice 9: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3298
7. Build a benchmark from common questions, measure calls-to-answer and failure rate per question, and tune search ranking and defaults until common questions take one or two calls.

## Adjacent

https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3286 links sessions to PRs they act on through commands; `list_sessions` with `pr` came back empty in 21 of 49 lookups that used it. https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/2789 serves the bundled conversation-history skill through MCP, which helps agents that load it; server instructions reach every agent.

title: Open AgentsView tabs use up the browser's connections, so new tabs stall
body:
With a few AgentsView tabs open, a new tab's requests wait in the browser until earlier ones finish, so Go to session (Ctrl+G) can't open a session until the sidebar finishes loading, and a fourth tab doesn't load at all. Every tab holds the `/api/v1/events` stream open, and a tab showing a session also holds its `/watch` stream. Over plain HTTP, Chrome allows six open connections per host, shared across tabs, so two streams per tab use up the pool after three tabs.

Proposal: share one live-update stream across all tabs of an origin, through a `SharedWorker` or a `BroadcastChannel` leader tab, and carry session watch events on that same stream. Closing streams in hidden tabs and reopening them on focus also works, but it leaves a burst of reconnects on each tab switch.

Measured on v0.46.1-300-ga0c95ef21 served over HTTP on a tailnet host (`main` still opens both streams per tab), in headless Chromium, pasting a Codex session ID into Go to session right after the page loads. The server answers the ID lookup in about 110 ms every time:

| Other AgentsView tabs open | Lookup waiting in the browser | Session opened after Enter |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0 ms | 0.2 s |
| 1 | 250 ms | 0.35 s |
| 2 | 700 ms | 0.86 s |
| 3 | page never loads | — |

With one or two other tabs open, the lookup waits behind the sidebar index, which takes about 3 seconds on a large archive, so the delay grows with archive size. Serving over HTTP/2 lifts the per-host limit, but browsers only speak HTTP/2 over TLS, which most local installs don't use.

title: test: clear chart fixtures before testing checklist dismissal
body:
The dashboard checklist test, `shows the checklist and hides it after dismissal`, repeatedly fails on its first CI attempt and passes on retry. The saved report for the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/44839107717/attempts/1) does not include its assertion error. On unchanged main, limiting the test process to half a CPU reproduces a failure in that same test with `Test timed out in 5000ms`.

An earlier chart-selection test leaves its sample activity data in the shared dashboard store. Later tests reset the date window but keep that data, so mounting the dashboard for the checklist also renders an unrelated chart across the restored window. The chart-selection test also leaves every element reporting a width of 600 pixels. This is test-state leakage, not a production race: production does not run these test fixtures or mocked loads.

Clear the activity fixture during the existing cleanup and make the width override a spy, which the existing mock cleanup restores. The chart-selection test still renders and exercises its chart, and the checklist still checks both visibility and dismissal. Under the same half-CPU limit, all 37 tests pass and the checklist takes about 0.2 seconds instead of 7.3 seconds. Product behavior and test timeouts are unchanged.

title: fix(mcp): list accepted arguments when a tool call has unknown ones
body:
Agents can correct a rejected MCP argument in one retry.

Passing `include_one_shot` to `search_sessions` appeared in 129 lookups over 30 days, the most common specific argument mismatch. The error now lists that tool’s accepted arguments.

When another argument has the wrong type, the middleware still finds the unknown name by comparing the call with the tool’s schema. Other errors keep their existing content.

title: fix: synchronize file cache setup with reads
body:
The Go race detector job failed in the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/44852220243/attempts/1) with a reported race between cache opening and checking whether the cache is enabled. This is an intermittent failure; a focused reproduction triggers the same race locally. The original job log could not be retrieved, so the exact failing test names and frequency remain unverified.

`kept.Disk` is the shared file cache for saved analytics and search results. Its opening method writes the directory, file format, and size limits before taking the mutex used by reads, writes, and cleanup. Meanwhile, another goroutine can read that state, and the enabled-status method takes no lock at all. This is a race in application code and can occur whenever cache setup overlaps a request or other cache user; it does not depend on test-only mocks.

Hold the existing cache mutex throughout opening and when reading enabled status. All cache operations then see initialization in order, with no changes to file formats, limits, or retention. The regression reproduces the race without the patch and passes with it, alongside the full cache package under the race detector.

The related [Activity report optimization PR](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3264) also moves the opening lock, but leaves enabled-status reads unlocked. This repair covers both sides of the race independently.

Model used: GPT-6 (Codex)

title: test(db): wait for canceled usage requests before checking batch limits
body:
`TestUsageRollupInstallsInBoundedBatches/cancel_first=true` intermittently fails on macOS with batch sizes `[256, 1]` instead of `[256]` and 257 installed sessions instead of 256. The [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/44852208904/attempts/1) recorded one failure followed by a passing retry.

The test cancels a usage request just before its first batch commits. Cancellation wakes the request's waiting goroutine, which must unregister itself from the shared worker. Meanwhile, the worker can finish that batch and check for remaining callers before the waiting goroutine runs. It then sees a caller and installs the last session too. This scheduling can happen in production, where finishing work while a caller remains registered is allowed. The flaky assumption is in the test.

Run the request in a goroutine and hold the first install callback until that request returns. Returning confirms that the canceled caller has unregistered, so the worker can reliably drop later batches. The existing checks still cover the 256-session limit, completion of the active batch, reuse by the next request, and final usage totals. Production behavior stays unchanged.

On fetched `main`, a temporary scheduling probe delayed caller removal by 100 ms and reproduced both reported mismatches. The repaired rollup tests passed 10 repetitions, and forcing the worker to ignore abandoned callers still made the repaired test fail.

Model used: GPT-6

title: fix(mcp): accept concepts with any mode and list session messages by ID
body:
Agents can now run semantic searches with `concepts` and `mode: "hybrid"`, and list a session's messages in order by passing `session_id` without `pattern` or `concepts`. Before this change, those combinations failed in 87 concept lookups and 43 session-listing lookups; listings also retain the other filters.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3287, slice 5 (Content search stops rejecting fixable calls)

title: test: accept either order of watcher failure and wake flush
body:
`TestDaemonIngestionFailedCatchupClearsPending` failed once and passed on retry in the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/44855741754/attempts/1). The original assertion output is unavailable. On fetched `main`, delaying the test's flush call by 100 ms reproduces a missing `archive catch-up incomplete` log message in five out of five attempts.

The test makes a session file unreadable, then wakes the daemon through a search request. Waking resumes the file watcher, which imports changed files in the background. That watcher can fail the file before the request's catch-up flush asks for unfinished work. The watcher logs the error and retains the file for a later retry; the flush then finds no fresh work and has no error to log again. The test requires that second log message, so its result depends on which side runs first.

Assert the watcher's failure report, which appears in either order. Keep the existing checks that the unreadable session is absent, the response has no stale-data header, and the daemon clears its pending flag. This ordering can occur in production when a file is unreadable; the watcher already retains the failure for retry. Only the test's log expectation changes.

With the same temporary delay, the repaired test passes ten repetitions. The scheduling probe is not included in the patch.

Model used: GPT-6 (Codex)

title: feat(mcp): report tool call outcomes
body:
AgentsView can now report MCP error and truncation rates per tool, plus empty-result rates for supported first-page searches. Each call records `ok`, `error`, `empty`, or `truncated`.

To reach one or two calls per common question, measure outcomes. [The 30-day sample](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3287) found errors in 390 of 2,043 lookups and empty results in 627.

`agentsview mcp calls` shows:

- Call count and error rate
- Empty-result rate across first-page attempts to `search_sessions`, `list_sessions`, `search_content`, `search_docs`, and `query_recall`; errors stay in the denominator
- Rate of server-marked truncated results
- Top three unknown argument names in failed calls
- Median text-result bytes and duration
- Daily UTC records under `mcp/calls/` retain tool and argument names, outcome, rejected names, text bytes, and duration until removed; logging failures warn while calls continue

| State | Dark |
|---|---|
| Summary of recorded calls | ![MCP call summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b26fab45-5ef5-4e7f-bca7-4fccdbd1c107#gh-dark-mode-only) |
| Config prevents logging | ![MCP recording warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ad5c6e7-2d47-4851-83d6-c363dabbf449#gh-dark-mode-only) |

```sh
agentsview mcp calls --since 7d --format json
```



Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3287, slice 1 (MCP call outcomes)

title: feat(mcp): return saved tool results from get_tool_calls
body:
Agents using MCP can now read the result text saved in the archive for a tool call. Before, `get_tool_calls` reported only `result_length`. In a real session in a read-only scratch archive, the tool returned the call's saved event and its 7,878-byte stored length. It also returned a 32-character first chunk and the next 32 characters through `result_cursor`.

`include_results` adds `result` and `result_events` to the `get_tool_calls` response, with secret-shaped values masked. Each event stays separate, and `max_result_chars` caps each text field. With results on, a page defaults to one call. There is no response-wide cap yet, so a call with many saved events can still exceed a client's output limit.

A `result_cursor` reads the next chunk of a single summary or event. It stores a digest of the text it pages through. New messages in the session leave it valid. A changed result fails with `source_changed`. Continuation responses leave out `category`, `input`, and `total`. Without `include_results`, the response keeps its current shape.

The new fields bring the full MCP tool list to 96,068 bytes, so the size limit in `TestNewServer_CatalogFitsBudget` goes from 96,000 to 97,000 bytes. The `get_tool_calls` text is already short, and further cuts would drop the unit hints agents use to page results.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3287, slice 9 (tool results are readable)

title: Support native session titles for Antigravity CLI
body:
### Problem / motivation

AgentsView does not show or update the title I set in Antigravity for an Antigravity CLI session. This makes renamed sessions harder to identify in AgentsView.

My Antigravity CLI version is 1.5.12 or later.

### Proposed solution

Support reading and syncing native titles for Antigravity CLI sessions, including subsequent renames, so the title shown in AgentsView follows the title set in Antigravity.

The existing native title sync handles the Antigravity app/IDE provider, but does not register the Antigravity CLI provider. The repository's format notes document a CLI `conversation_summaries.db` store; please verify where CLI 1.5.12+ stores renamed titles before choosing the implementation.

Related: #2086 addressed Antigravity app/IDE and Qoder titles.

title: feat(reporting): report Cursor usage by account
body:
Admins can count Cursor account-hours once after the server accepts schema 6 `--by-machine` rows with `polled_at`. Until then, two archives syncing a team count its hour twice; this PR adds the rows.

```
agentsview export hour --schema-version 6 --by-machine 2026-07-28-13
```

The field records when the unfiltered poll finishes. Only closed-hour events in that poll returned by exactly one numeric member query get account IDs; unmatched events stay archive-billed.

Schema 5 remains supported, but mixing schemas 5 and 6 may count the same Cursor usage under both an account and a machine ID.

- Roster lookups cover only 30-day windows with closed-hour events or stored account-hours.
- Each client leaves 3 seconds between roster requests and 1 second between member queries.
- Cursor's [Admin API](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/admin-api) limits filtered-event requests to 60 per minute per team.

title: feat(mcp): return large results in pages that fit the response budget
body:
Agents that read your session history through AgentsView MCP now see all of a large result, rather than its start and end. Codex trims any tool output over about 10,000 tokens down to its start and end, so an agent reading a long message, a tool call's output, or a big set of search matches used to answer without the middle.

Now pattern searches, message reads, and tool-call results stay under 12,000 bytes per response. A response that holds something back says how much it left out and returns a cursor to read the rest. Semantic and hybrid searches can't resume, so they report what they left out and ask for a smaller `limit`.

Responses add `omitted`, cursors including `body_cursor` and `result_cursor`, `total` and `total_capped` on cut search pages, and `message_count` on cut `get_messages` pages. A call returns an error if its required fields can't fit.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3287, slice 6 (large results in readable pages)

title: fix(sync): share live updates across tabs
body:
AgentsView users can keep session tabs open over HTTP/1.1 without blocking new pages. Three tabs used six connections and stalled the fourth; now archive and session updates share one stream.

API 27 archives stay available, but selected-session live updates need API 28. Settings warns; reload shows new messages.

A transient read error keeps the session ID watched until recovery. Absent or unresolved sessions get `session_missing`, while archive and healthy-session updates continue.

title: feat(sessions): find sessions by pull request
body:
Developers can find sessions that selected a PR with `gh` or gave its URL to a child agent. Before, `gh pr view 42 -R example/repo` or a full PR URL in a child prompt left no searchable `example/repo#42` reference.

Data-version 190 backfills full-content local archives from retained tool inputs. New writes with retained tool inputs also index supported `gh pr` commands and child-agent prompts. Full URLs and explicit `-R` or `--repo` selectors link a PR; a child-prompt URL records a reference, not proof of work.

Archives that discard tool inputs can't index command or child-prompt references, and discarded inputs can't be backfilled. Bare-number commands stay unlinked. Bash inputs over 256 KiB stay unlinked.

title: fix(mcp): accept plain session UUIDs in every session tool
body:
MCP agents can pass a plain UUID to `get_session_overview`, `get_messages`, and other session tools. Before, `get_session_overview` returned `session not found` for that same ID.

Session tools resolve a plain UUID to one match; ambiguous UUIDs list up to five candidates. Required unknown or trashed IDs error; optional filters pass unknown or trashed IDs through.

Older remote servers (API before 29) need full stored IDs for required lookups.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3287, slice 2 (Every session tool takes a plain ID)

Needed by https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3323

title: fix(db): repair upgraded image-text archives
body:
An archive upgraded from an older nightly now opens, syncs, and serves again. Before, the upgrade could leave its image-text tables without an `id` column, and every later startup and sync failed with `no such column: id`.

Startup now replaces those tables with the current schema and marks the affected sessions for sync. When image-text processing is on, its job rebuilds search text from images kept in tool results.

title: fix(hermes): filter archived rows, order by display_order, and detect em-dash compaction
body:
Fixes #3113

### Why
When Hermes Agent compacts a session in `state.db`, archived pre-compaction messages remain in the `messages` table with `active = 0`, compaction boundaries are written with an em-dash (`[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]`), internal task restatement scaffolds carry `display_metadata` (`compaction_inflight_task_restatement`), and rows near the end of a turn can carry slightly out-of-order wall-clock timestamps relative to `display_order`. AgentsView previously queried all rows ordered by `timestamp ASC, id ASC` and checked only ASCII hyphen and en-dash boundaries, causing archived noise, `CompactionCount = 0`, leaked restatement prompts, out-of-order turns, and `EndedAt` picking the wrong final row.

### What changed
- **Schema-aware `messages` queries (`internal/parser/hermes.go`, `internal/parser/hermes_provider.go`)**: `readHermesMessageColumns` inspects `PRAGMA table_info(messages)` so older `state.db` files without `active`, `display_order`, or `display_metadata` continue to work unchanged, while databases that have them:
  - exclude archived rows via `COALESCE(active, 1) = 1` across `readHermesStateMessages`, `readHermesStateMessagesForSession`, and `hermesStateDBHasReadableSession` (keeping timestamp readability checks aligned with full message reads);
  - sort rows by `(display_order IS NULL) ASC, display_order ASC, timestamp ASC, id ASC` so display order wins over millisecond timestamp skew and `EndedAt` resolves from the final non-scaffold message (`lastHermesStateTimestamp`);
  - select `COALESCE(display_metadata, '')` and skip `compaction_inflight_task_restatement` scaffold messages in `convertHermesStateMessages` and `hermesStateQuality`.
- **Em-dash compaction boundary (`internal/parser/hermes.go`)**: `isHermesCompactBoundary` now recognizes `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]` (`U+2014`) alongside `-` and `–` (`U+2013`), covering `state.db`, JSON, and JSONL paths.
- **Tests (`internal/parser/hermes_test.go`)**: Added `TestIsHermesCompactBoundary` and `TestHermesCompactedStateDBExcludesArchivedOrdersByDisplayOrderAndFiltersRestatement` covering both container (`parseArchive`) and member (`parseStateMember`) paths.

### Design notes & tradeoffs
- Inspecting `PRAGMA table_info(messages)` adds one metadata query per DB open/read path, avoiding breakage on pre-compaction schemas and legacy fixtures while keeping all columns explicitly projected and scanned.
- Filtering `compaction_inflight_task_restatement` in `convertHermesStateMessages` and `lastHermesStateTimestamp` (rather than SQL `json_extract`) keeps `stateMessages` pure-Go/SQLite-extension-independent and avoids scanning unindexed JSON inside SQLite queries.

Model used: Gemini 4
Co-authored-by: Antigravity <noreply@antigravity.dev>

title: perf(dashboard): reuse per-session analytics across filters
body:
AgentsView users with long histories see the Dashboard and its agent filter finish sooner after the first load, most of all right after new messages sync. On a synthetic archive of 91,711 sessions and 2,897,301 messages, the Dashboard finished in 7.5 s instead of 13 s after a message write.

| View, seconds | Warm | After a message write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard | 7.9 → 5.1 (1.5×) | 13 → 7.5 (1.7×) |
| Agent filter | 3.5 → 2.1 (1.7×) | 3.9 → 2.3 (1.7×) |

The table shows medians of five paired runs, timed until every panel finished. Cold loads and the date filter stay within run-to-run noise. A cold Dashboard still takes about 19 s, but its first summary shows at 6 s instead of 11 s. Warm first summaries show about 0.2 s later.

The activity, hour-of-week, and velocity panels now reuse each session's cached results across filters. Two new triggers on `messages` clear a session's cached results when a message is added or its length changes. A 4,000-row content update takes 46 ms longer, or 11.5 µs per row.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/2093, slice 2 (Faster remaining dashboard analytics)

title: fix(pricing): price decorated Gemini display names and bare Gemini 4 ids
body:
Antigravity sessions using Gemini 4 models (such as `Gemini 4 Neon (High)`) and bare `gemini-4-*` model IDs now resolve to Google's catalog rates (previously `$0`). Older Antigravity display names (such as `Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)`) now match Pydantic GenAI Prices v2 directly.

User-facing benefit: Gemini 4 and Antigravity sessions show accurate token spend in `agentsview report usage daily`, the Usage dashboard, and downstream consumers such as VibePulse.

Two gaps in the pricing resolver caused these models to come back unpriced:

- `genAICandidatesFor` in `internal/export/pricing.go` passed reported names verbatim to Pydantic GenAI Prices. Display names with spaces and trailing effort suffixes (`Gemini 4 Neon (High)`) never matched catalog rules expecting hyphenated lowercase slugs (`gemini-4-neon`).
- LiteLLM publishes Gemini 4 models only under provider-qualified prefixes (`gemini/`, `vertex_ai/`, `github_copilot/`). When flat or untimestamped lookup ran on either a bare `gemini-4-*` ID or a display name, `resolveCanonicalMatch` saw multiple competing provider keys with no unqualified row and treated the lookup as ambiguous.

This change extends the existing pricing normalization and fixed-alias machinery so rates follow future catalog refreshes:

- `pricing.DisplayNameModelID` strips one trailing parenthesized or bracketed suffix and converts whitespace-separated tokens to lowercase hyphenated slugs (`Gemini 4 Neon (High)` -> `gemini-4-neon`), leaving bare slugs unchanged. `genAICandidatesFor` adds that candidate when it differs from the reported name, so timestamped usage resolves through GenAI Prices v2 and picks up date-window rate changes (such as Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon).
- `fixedPricingAliases` maps bare `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-4-hydrogen`, and `gemini-4-neon` to `gemini/gemini-4-*` (`Exact: true`), matching the existing `muse-spark-*` pattern. `PricingResolver.resolveFlat` also checks `FixedCanonicalModel(DisplayNameModelID(pricedModel))` when the direct flat lookup misses, so both decorated display names and uncanonicalized bare IDs (including saved pre-upgrade cache inputs) resolve cleanly when untimestamped or when GenAI Prices lacks matching rates. Exact custom rates for the reported name, slug, or fixed alias target keep precedence.
- SQLite adds `usageZonePricingIdentityVersion` (`usage-zone-pricing-v2`) to the zone-level pricing identity (`usagePricingIdentityWithDigest`) while keeping `usageSessionPricingIdentityVersion` unchanged. Upgraded databases with an unchanged catalog fall out of the stale zone fast-path during both usage reads and startup backfill, re-check per-session `DependencyFingerprint` hashes, and rebuild only sessions whose resolution changed. ClickHouse bumps `chUsagePriceFormatVersion` from `3` to `4` to reprice stored mirrors and extends `chUsagePriceContext.customPriced` to detect custom overrides on the display-name slug or alias target.

Running a branch build against an isolated copy of a real archive with 174 `antigravity-cli` usage events for `Gemini 4 Neon (High)` across three days resolved `google/gemini-4-neon` ($3 input, $15 output, $0.15 cache read per MTok) and reported `$21.92` total spend across those days where `main` reported `$0.00`.

Reviewers should focus on `internal/export/pricing.go` (`resolveFlat` and `genAICandidatesFor`), `internal/pricing/normalize.go` (`DisplayNameModelID`), `internal/pricing/supplemental.go` (`fixedPricingAliases`), `internal/db/usage_rollup_pricing.go` and `internal/db/usage_rollup.go` (`usageZonePricingIdentityVersion`), and `internal/clickhouse/usage_prices.go` (`chUsagePriceFormatVersion` and `customPriced`).

Model used: Gemini 4 Neon

Co-authored-by: Antigravity <noreply@google.com>

title: Restarts spend minutes setting up search indexes that are already current
body:
AgentsView takes about three minutes to start serving pages after a plain restart, even when there is nothing to upgrade, because it spends most of that time setting up full-text search on an index that is already current.

Startup should check the search indexes cheaply and skip work they don't need, so a restart with nothing to upgrade serves its first page in about two seconds. Any repair or rebuild that has to happen can run after the server is listening.

On a 148 GB archive running v0.47.1-nightly.2413 (9145e48964), the log for a restart with no schema changes shows:

| Startup step | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| Initializing full-text search | 2m 25s |
| Everything else before listening | about 45 s |
| Started in | 3m 10s |

The other database steps took under half a second each, so search setup alone holds back the first page. On November 10, a restart of the same archive took about 150 ms.

title: Usage page takes minutes when its cache is cold
body:
Usage can take minutes to load when cached totals are missing or out of date. On a 148 GB archive, a cold 7-day request took 2 min 16 s and a warm request took 2.8 s; the Sessions page timed out during the cold request. The reader capacity that protects other pages during bulk work is tracked separately in https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3272.

Usage should return totals for days already built as soon as they are available, then update the page as missing days rebuild. This work must preserve session changes that arrive during the rebuild.

On a 6.4 GB test archive (30,946 sessions), at commit `9145e48964`:

| Usage range | Cold cache, median / slowest of 4 | Cached, median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 30 days | 42.8 s / 56.2 s | 5.6 s |
| Six months | 54.7 s / 93.4 s | 8.5 s |

CPU profiles of the cold 30-day requests spend most of their time loading and building per-day rollups, and extracting and pricing message facts. The archive-wide usage backfill that starts at launch runs alongside these requests and competes for resources.

title: First sync shows nothing until every session is imported
body:
A new AgentsView install shows nothing useful until its first sync finishes, which takes minutes for a few hundred sessions and much longer for a large history, because sessions are imported in no particular order.

The first sync should import the newest sessions first and serve pages while it continues, so a new user sees their recent work within seconds and older history fills in behind it.

On a 500-session sample on main, the first page appeared after a median 170 s with 8 sync workers and 138 s with 32, importing 3 to 4 sessions per second. Syncing only the newest 100 session files first returned a first page in 27 s. Profiles put most sync CPU in SQLite writes, then parsing.

title: perf(db): check the search index without reading message content
body:
Restarting AgentsView on a large archive no longer spends minutes checking the search index before the first page loads: on a 148 GB archive the check took over 200 s and now takes 0.07 s, because it looks up the index instead of reading message content.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3327
