title: test(e2e): keep live reloads out of manual history retry tests
body:
The session-find regression test `recovers a failed forward page with earlyHit=false` intermittently times out after 45 seconds. It failed and passed on retry in the [earlier failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/44885883066/attempts/1) and the [latest failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45037135609/attempts/1). On current main, five repetitions of the regression file reproduced four timeouts out of 45 tests, including the exact reported case. Playwright reports that the retry button detached during its click.

The fixture supplies simulated messages and failed history requests, but still receives real live-update notifications. A late notification that the live connection is ready starts a background transcript reload. That reload encounters the fixture's temporary server error and schedules another attempt. The test then allows successful responses just before clicking Retry loading history. The background attempt can finish first, completing history and removing the button while Playwright waits to click it.

For the two manual-retry cases, end live event streams with HTTP 204, which tells the event-stream client to stop reconnecting. Disable the browser's shared worker in those cases so stream requests stay in the page where Playwright can intercept them, following the existing live-refresh test fixture. All failure responses and assertions about incomplete results, retry, match counts, and the visible match remain. Live-refresh coverage continues in its separate tests. Background reloads also happen in production, but this race depends on the fixture switching its simulated failure off before a manual click; no application behavior changes.

The same 45 Chromium tests passed with the change and retries disabled. The full file also passed three times on both Chromium and WebKit through the pinned CI browser container, 54 tests with no retries.

Model used: GPT-6

title: test: keep session usage wait deadlines independent of HTTP scheduling
body:
`TestSessionUsageArchiveOnlyWaitIncomplete/own_only_status_error` intermittently fails with `waiting for session usage: context deadline exceeded` while checking sync status. It failed once and passed on retry in the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45044084698/attempts/1).

The test gives the command 100 ms to look up a saved session and wait for ingestion. The deadline timer races the HTTP client's session lookup and the fixture server's response. If lookup loses, the command has no saved session ID when it checks sync status, so it returns an error instead of the saved totals the test expects. A temporary 150 ms delay in the lookup fixture reproduced the exact error on fetched main. Production uses a 30-second wait budget and can also time out before identifying a session; returning an error then is expected. This test intends to cover a known session whose ingestion wait expires.

Run all four cases with Go's virtual clock and the existing in-memory HTTP fixture used by `TestSessionUsageWait`, the neighboring ingestion-wait test. Requests complete before virtual time advances to the polling deadline. Keep the existing warning and incomplete-result assertions, and also check the saved token total and elapsed virtual time. This changes only the test, preserves the command's real polling and response parsing, and passed 100 repetitions of all four cases plus the session-usage test group locally.

Model used: GPT-6.1-sol

title: Declarative worktree mappings: rules in config.toml and a <repo>.<suffix> sibling layout
body:
### Problem / motivation

We run `agentsview pg push --watch` in a container on each machine. Only the session roots are mounted, not the source checkouts, so the Git-root walk finds nothing and the project falls back to the folder name.

Our worktrees use worktrunk's default sibling layout, `~/code/<repo>.<suffix>`. #2968 (merged after v0.47.0) groups these under `<repo>` when the recorded branch matches the suffix. That leaves cases where it does not match. In our archive about a third of the worktree sessions are like this:

```text
cwd: /home/user/code/sample-app.abc1      branch: feat/abc1-retry-logic
cwd: /home/user/code/sample-app.envrc     branch: chore/sample-app-mise-activate
```

Worktree mapping rules fix this, but they are hard to provision:

- They live only in each machine's archive and are created through the UI or the HTTP API (`/api/v1/settings/worktree-mappings`). Config management (Ansible, Nix, dotfiles) cannot declare them.
- A prefix matches on a directory boundary, so `/home/user/code/sample-app` does not cover `/home/user/code/sample-app.abc1`. With the `explicit` layout that means one rule per worktree.
- `repo_dot_worktrees` only fits `<repo>.worktrees/<branch>`, not `<repo>.<suffix>` siblings.

### Proposed solution

Either or both:

1. **Mapping rules from `config.toml`.** They would be applied like enabled rules, after parser inference, and never stored in the archive:

   ```toml
   [[worktree_mappings]]
   path_prefix = "~/code/sample-app/.claude/worktrees"
   project = "sample-app"
   ```

2. **A sibling layout for the `<repo>.<suffix>` convention.** For a cwd under the prefix, the first path segment `<repo>.<anything>` would resolve to project `<repo>` (split at the first `.`). It is opt-in per prefix, so a user with dotted repository names simply does not enable it there:

   ```toml
   [[worktree_mappings]]
   path_prefix = "~/code"
   layout = "repo_dot_suffix"
   ```

Together these give one declarative rule per machine for every repository, with no per-worktree state.

### Alternatives considered

- **Mount the checkouts into the push container** so the Git walk works. This works, but it gives a third-party image read access to every repository, including local secret files. We would rather not.
- **A worktree-manager hook** (for example worktrunk `post-start`) that POSTs an `explicit` rule for each new worktree to the local API. This works, but it covers only worktrees created by that tool. It also has to reach an API that listens on loopback inside the container's network namespace, and it requires an `Origin` header.
- **Rewriting `sessions.project` with SQL** in the archive. This works once, but it repeats for every new worktree and bypasses the identity bookkeeping.

title: fix(ci): recognize boolean flags in released command examples
body:
The Released commands CI job fails on every check of the v0.48.0 README with the old locked action. It reports 15 valid examples as unsupported, including `agentsview serve --background: v0.48.0 unknown flag: --background`. See the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45082233172).

The released binary prints boolean options as `--flag[=true|false]`. The command checker reads its help output, skips that format, then rejects README examples that use those flags. The action lockfile selects a checker revision from before the [upstream boolean flag parser repair](https://github.com/kenn-io/actions/pull/33), even though the workflow names the action's `main` branch.

Refresh the shared action's locked revision to include that repair. This keeps the README examples and validation intact and changes no application behavior. The update also advances the shared path-filter and sibling-pin actions; their existing workflow inputs remain supported. The page-rendering checks use the same locked reference as the other shared actions, preserving their exact commit and letting the lockfile generator record all nested dependencies together. The old checker reproduced all 15 failures against the published v0.48.0 archive; the updated checker accepted the same README and both installers on Linux amd64. The PR checks exercise the updated action through the repository's existing Released commands job.

Model used: GPT-6 (Codex)

title: fix(ci): split Windows database tests across two runners
body:
The scheduled MSYS2 Update Check, which tests Windows with newly updated compiler packages, failed once on the current main revision with `panic: test timed out after 20m0s` in the database package. See the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45144731274/attempts/1).

The database suite runs its sequential tests before starting tests marked to run in parallel. In this run, completed database tests consumed over 19 minutes, including 215 seconds for the large-session activity-report test. The package timer expired during a test that had started only one second earlier, while parallel tests still waited to start. Compiler setup and the other five jobs succeeded. This is a CI workload limit; the application's database operations do not run under Go's test-package timer.

Split the database suite across two Windows runners using complementary test-name filters, following the existing CLI and sync test partitions. Separate parser tests from the database workload and use the same database partitions in regular Windows CI. Keep every test, assertion, compiler setup, and the 20-minute package timeout. The tradeoff is two additional Windows jobs per workflow. Changes to the update-check workflow now run it as a pull request check, so the updated compiler setup is exercised before merging.

The compiled database test list contains 2,651 entries, covered by 1,313 entries in the first partition and 1,338 in the second, with no overlap. The saved failing-run output supplies the workload measurements. In the [Successful Windows update-check run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45153398076), the two database partitions completed in 151 and 147 seconds, and all eight jobs passed.

The x86-64-v2 startup check timed out at its 15-minute limit on this branch and on main. Inside the plain Ubuntu container, apt downloaded gcc from archive.ubuntu.com at 40 to 84 kB/s; a passing run fetched the same files in seconds. The container now tries the Azure mirror the runner host already uses, falls back to archive.ubuntu.com, and reads only the main component, which holds every package the build installs. That also skips a 20 MB package index the job never used.

title: Embedding re-sends unchanged text when a message grows
body:
AgentsView embeds the whole message again each time an agent's reply grows, so text it already embedded goes back to the embedder. On a busy archive, 41% of the text sent for embedding in one hour had been embedded before.

AgentsView should keep each chunk's embedding and reuse it when the chunk's text is unchanged, embedding only the chunks that changed. Chunks are cut at fixed positions from the start of a message, so when a reply grows, its earlier chunks stay identical. Stored documents keep their current shape, search results stay the same, and no existing embedding needs a rebuild.

Measured on a live 148 GB archive over 62 minutes, with the vector mirror snapshotted every 2 minutes:

| Over 62 minutes | Characters embedded |
| --- | --- |
| Today | 1.46M |
| With chunk reuse (estimate) | 1.00M (31% less) |

76 growing messages caused the repeats; 165 new documents arrived in the same window, and none shrank. The estimate still embeds the chunk that held each message's old end, plus new chunks. The 15% overlap between chunks stays.

On machines where the local embedder is the main background cost, this cuts that cost by about a third and lets new replies reach meaning search sooner.

title: fix(antigravity): discover Antigravity ACP sessions in meta-harness containers
body:
User-facing benefit: Antigravity sessions run through T3 Code's ACP harness (including Gemini 4 Neon sessions) now appear in AgentsView automatically with no extra configuration, and sessions isolated by other meta-harnesses can be discovered by pointing `agents.antigravity-cli.dirs` or `ANTIGRAVITY_CLI_DIR` at the harness's container directory.

## Why it changed

T3 Code launches `agy acp` with an isolated per-instance `--gemini-dir` and `--app-data-dir antigravity-acp` under `~/.t3/userdata/providers/antigravity/<sha256(instanceId)>/antigravity-acp` (or `$T3CODE_HOME/userdata/providers/antigravity`). Because AgentsView only scanned `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` by default, every Antigravity ACP session created through T3 Code was invisible.

Running this branch against an isolated copy of a real local T3 Code Antigravity ACP profile with default discovery (no overrides) discovered and synced all 23 conversations (plus 22 `implicit/*.pb` entries), 575 messages, workspace projects/CWDs from `conversation_summaries.db`, and 182 `Gemini 4 Neon (High)` usage events (2.1M input, 15.4M cache-read, 263K output tokens).

## How it works

This extends the dynamic container-root pattern already used for Hermes profiles (`~/.hermes/profiles` in `internal/config/config.go` and `internal/parser/hermes_provider.go`) into two reusable pieces:

- **Meta-harness default root registry (`internal/config/meta_harnesses.go`, `internal/config/config.go`):** Registers default meta-harness container roots per agent, starting with T3 Code's `T3CODE_HOME` / `~/.t3` + `userdata/providers/antigravity` container for `antigravity-cli`. Explicit `ANTIGRAVITY_CLI_DIR` or `agents.antigravity-cli.dirs` overrides still replace all default roots, matching Hermes. `MetaHarnessEnvVars()` exposes the override variables to `serviceRuntimeEnvVars` in `cmd/agentsview/pg_service_manager.go` so service installation warns when shell overrides diverge.
- **Generic instance-container expansion (`internal/parser/instance_container.go`, `internal/parser/antigravity_cli_provider.go`):** `InstanceContainerSpec` expands a configured container root across direct roots (`<root>/conversations`), single-profile `--gemini-dir` roots (`<root>/antigravity-{acp,cli}`), direct-instance containers (`<root>/<instance>/conversations`), and nested-instance containers (`<root>/<instance>/antigravity-{acp,cli}`).
  - Discovery (`Discover`, `DiscoverEach`, `FindSource`) expands instances dynamically on every pass so instances created after startup become visible without restarting, skips symlinks, enables `Sync.PartialDiscovery`, and collects unreadable container/instance filesystem errors across siblings while surfacing `DiscoveryIncompleteError` at the end (preserving immediate context cancellation and `yield` callback error propagation) so healthy standalone and sibling-instance sessions still sync without tombstoning.
  - `WatchPlan` watches container roots with `MaxDepth: 1` plus explicit `ExtraDirectories` for `*/antigravity-{acp,cli}`, `conversations`, `implicit`, `cache`, `brain/*` (Markdown artifacts and metadata), and `brain/*/.system_generated/logs` (`transcript.jsonl`) so newly created instances and live edits sync immediately while keeping unlisted intermediate (`brain/`, `.system_generated/`) and high-churn trees (`scratch`, `.system_generated/steps`, `logs/chunks`, `log`, `builtin`, `config`) quiet across all layouts.
  - Shared watch-depth filtering (`internal/sync/watch_depth.go`, `internal/sync/watch_backend_fsnotify.go`, `internal/sync/watch_backend_factory_darwin.go`): both non-macOS (`fsnotify`) and macOS (`FSEvents` `consumeFSEvents` and `includeCreatedSubtreePath`) enforce `MaxDepth` and `ExtraDirectories` consistently without filesystem I/O in native callbacks, and `extraCoversFiles` reports direct files for every explicitly listed extra directory even when another pattern descends further beneath it.
  - `SourcesForChangedPath` and `ChangedPathRelevance` map changed paths to their owning instance root in O(1) without scanning sibling instances, matching `ExpandRoot`'s `DirectMarkers` check so instances named `cache` or `brain` route cleanly, and classify both `conversations/<id>.db-shm` and `conversation_summaries.db-shm` as non-data.
  - `antigravityRemoteRoot` checks containment so expanded instances under a foreign-machine container root keep `SourceCwdRemote`.
- **Remote sync (`internal/remotesync/resolve.go`):** Expands `antigravity-cli` container roots into concrete instance directories (failing closed on unreadable containers) so each instance's `conversation_summaries.db` is snapshotted cleanly and sibling `config/` directories stay out of remote archives.

## Tradeoffs and limits

- Only T3 Code's production `userdata/providers/antigravity` container is added by default; dev-mode T3 Code profiles (`~/.t3/dev/providers/antigravity`) and other meta-harnesses are opt-in via `agents.antigravity-cli.dirs` or `ANTIGRAVITY_CLI_DIR` to avoid adding speculative missing watch roots for most users.
- An arbitrary user-configured container path that does not match `providers/antigravity` is recognized as a container once at least one instance subdirectory exists under it; if configured while completely empty, it starts with direct watches until the next startup or full sync discovers its instances.
- `antigravity-cli` still does not import `conversation_summaries.db` titles (`display_name`); that remains separate work since it requires a data-version bump and title-reconciliation wiring.

## Where reviewers should look

- `internal/config/meta_harnesses.go` and `internal/config/config.go` for default meta-harness root resolution and `T3CODE_HOME` handling.
- `internal/parser/instance_container.go` and `internal/parser/antigravity_cli_provider.go` for container expansion, partial streaming discovery, bounded watch planning, and O(1) changed-path routing.
- `internal/sync/watch_depth.go`, `internal/sync/watch_backend_fsnotify.go`, and `internal/sync/watch_backend_factory_darwin.go` for shared `MaxDepth`/`ExtraDirectories` enforcement across both `fsnotify` and macOS `FSEvents`.
- `internal/remotesync/resolve.go` for remote archive target expansion and per-instance `conversation_summaries.db` snapshotting.

Model used: Gemini 4 Neon (High) in Antigravity

title: Daemon burns ~1 core forever when a Codex fork's parent rollout is missing (retry loop + unwatched-root polling)
body:
## What happens

A handful of Codex sessions whose `forked_from_id` parent rollout no longer exists on disk stay in "needs retry" permanently. Two loops follow, and together they keep the writable daemon at roughly 0.7–1.4 cores around the clock:

1. **Every watcher-triggered sync re-reads all of the affected files.** With other agents writing sessions continuously, a sync fires about every 8 seconds, and each pass re-reads and re-parses the same eight files (44 MiB).
2. **Codex root reconciliation never completes, so the daemon falls back to polling unwatched roots.** A poll starts 2 minutes after the previous one ends, takes about a minute (up to 5 minutes), and re-reads Codex rollouts one after another (I saw a 295 MB `.jsonl.zst` open during a poll). Every poll ends `failed`.

Removing the eight orphaned rollouts from the Codex sessions directory stops both loops immediately.

## Environment

- AgentsView v0.48.0 (commit 14ab8dd), macOS 27.2.1, arm64. Also present on v0.47.0.
- SQLite archive about 22 GB, about 40,000 sessions. PostgreSQL replica via `replica pg push --watch`.
- Codex sessions directory: about 2,100 rollouts, 1.4 GB, mostly `.jsonl.zst`.
- The affected rollouts: eight files from one day, written by Codex Desktop (`cli_version` 0.142.5, `history_mode: "paginated"`, `multi_agent_version: "v1"`). Each `session_meta.payload.forked_from_id` is a UUIDv4 that matches no rollout under `sessions/` or `archived_sessions/`.

## Log evidence

Repeated on every sync pass (ids shortened):

```
sync: session needs retry: codex:019f41aa-… (~/.codex/sessions/2026/07/08/rollout-…jsonl.zst): could not read the Codex session it was forked from (3f7746a2-…)
Fork parent unavailable. Messages remain visible; unverified history may include parent replay, and its token usage is withheld until reconciliation.
sync: 8 sessions need retry: codex:019f41aa-… 
sync: changed paths: 8 path(s) matched 8 source(s): 8 updated, 0 unchanged, 0 with errors; 8 source(s) read to check their content (44.2 MiB); took 2.095s
watcher callback: watch root reconciliation deferred: 8 provider results need retry: codex:019f41aa-…
```

Repeated about every 3 minutes:

```
polling 7 unwatched root(s): antigravity=[…] antigravity-cli=[…] codex=[~/.codex/archived_sessions ~/.codex/sessions] cursor-ide=[…] gemini=[…]
polling unwatched roots failed after 1m25.178s: reconcile codex roots: watch root reconciliation deferred: 8 provider results need retry: …
polled 7 unwatched root(s) in 1m25.178s
```

## Measurements

| Measure | With the 8 orphaned forks | After moving them out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Daemon CPU, average | about 73% of a core (688 CPU-minutes in 15 h 40 min) | 9% (39 CPU-seconds in 7 min) |
| CPU during a poll | about 140% | no polls |
| CPU between polls | about 67% | — |
| `session needs retry` lines | about 390 per 10 minutes | 0 |
| `polling unwatched roots` | 378 polls in the log window, all `failed`, mean 57 s, max 323 s | 0 |

A second machine on the same version, with more Codex data (2.9 GB) and no orphaned forks, logs no retries and no unwatched-root polls and averages about 3% of a core.

A 10-second stack sample of the busy daemon is dominated by `sqlite3_step`, with `sync.(*Engine).processProviderFile`, `verifiedProviderSourceFreshInDB`, `db.GetSourceRepairStateByAgentPath` and zstd decoding on the Go side.

## Expected

- A fork whose parent is permanently unavailable should stop being retried on every pass: for example retry with backoff, or settle after N attempts as "parent unavailable" (the session is already stored and visible, with usage withheld).
- A per-session retry should not mark the whole Codex root as unreconciled, and should not switch the daemon into polling every unwatched root.
- If polling is still needed, it should not re-read rollouts whose size and mtime are unchanged.

## Workaround

Move the orphaned rollouts out of `~/.codex/sessions` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions`. The archived sessions stay intact in AgentsView (not marked deleted or source-missing).

## Possibly related

- #2911 (closed): resync-build aborts forever when a Codex parent-inventory source stays deferred.
- #1820 (closed): idle daemon burns about 1 core on a large archive.

## Can provide

A `session_meta` header from one of the affected rollouts (keys and ids only), `agentsview doctor` output, or a longer stack sample.

title: docs(clickhouse): list every system-table grant push and serve need
body:
Operator benefit: the ClickHouse docs now list every grant the push and serve roles need, including the `SELECT ON system.data_skipping_indices` grant that 0.48.0 started requiring and the docs never mentioned.

## What happened

0.48.0 added a schema-step read of `system.data_skipping_indices` (`readSkipIndexes` in `internal/clickhouse/schema.go`), so the schema step can drop a retired skipping index. With the server's default `select_from_system_db_requires_grant`, `GRANT ALL ON <db>.*` does not cover that table. A push user set up from the current docs (`ALL` on the mirror database, plus `system.parts` and `system.projections`) fails every push after upgrading from 0.47.0:

```
schema: reading clickhouse skipping indexes: code: 497 ... Not enough privileges.
To execute this query, it's necessary to have the grant SELECT ON system.data_skipping_indices
```

The schema upgrade never finishes. `clickhouse serve` then fails its compatibility check with `clickhouse model_pricing comes from an older agentsview version; run agentsview replica clickhouse push to upgrade it`, which sends the operator back to the push that is failing. Adding the grant to the XML-managed user and reloading users fixes it.

## Changes

- `docs/clickhouse-sync.md` gets a **Required grants** section under Configuration. It has one table of the database and system-table grants for each role, the SQL and XML `<query>` forms, and the error each missing grant produces. The quick start links to it.
- The compaction section and the serve "Required system-table permissions" section now point to that table instead of each listing their own grants. The serve section still says that a table-creating serve role without a schema grant skips the upgrade silently.
- `docs/changelog.md` adds a 0.48.0 upgrade note: grant `system.data_skipping_indices` before upgrading, or pushes fail and serve won't start.

## Where to look

I checked every `system.` table that `internal/clickhouse` queries, using a stock ClickHouse 26.8 user that had only `GRANT ALL ON <db>.*`. That user can read `system.tables` and `system.columns`. It is denied `system.parts`, `system.projections`, and `system.data_skipping_indices`, and the table covers those three. One change from the old text: `system.parts` is now listed as required for every push, not only for compaction. Since 0.48.0, every push reads it to price Cursor usage (`readCursorPricingParts`) and returns an error without it.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

When `EnsureSchema` fails with a permission error, `OpenServeStore` (`internal/clickhouse/backend.go`) drops the error and carries on as if the role were read-only. The compatibility error that follows only says to run a push. Serve could log the swallowed permission error, or add it to the compatibility error, so an operator sees which grant is missing instead of being sent to a push that fails for the same reason.

title: fix(usage): make the treemap Linear/Sqrt/Log scale resize tiles
body:
On the Usage page, the Linear, Sqrt, and Log buttons on the cost attribution treemap changed only the label font size. Tile areas always stayed proportional to cost. When one agent or project dominates, the small ones become slivers too thin to see or click, and none of the buttons changed that. The scale now sets tile area, so Sqrt and Log let the small items take visible space.

Tile shares by scale for one cost breakdown by agent ($14,867, $1,365, $199, $39.57, $5.50, $1.44, $1.42, $0.17, $0.14):

| Scale | Largest tile | Smallest tile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linear | 90.2% | under 0.1% |
| Sqrt | 66.0% | 0.2% |
| Log | 24.6% | 2.0% |

What changed for users:

- Tile values, percentages, and hover titles still show real costs or token counts. Only the area is scaled.
- Label size now follows each tile's drawn area, so it stays consistent with the tile.
- The button group's tooltip and accessible name say "Tile size scale" instead of "Label size scale", in all eight locales.

title: First broad search takes 8–10 s on a laptop-sized archive
body:
AgentsView's first search for a common word takes 8 to 10 seconds, even on a laptop-sized archive, and it's the longest wait left in the app on that kind of machine.

Searching should return the first page of results within a couple of seconds and keep looking past that page only when someone asks for more. A broad first search should no longer scan every matching message before anything appears.

Measured on origin/main (`ff834278`), with a 1.74 GB archive of 12,000 sessions and 1.2 million messages, three runs each:

| Operation | 4 CPUs, 8 GB (laptop proxy) | Uncapped |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First broad search (`code`, matches every message) | 9.8 s | 7.7 s |
| Search, median | 1.4 s | 1.2 s |
| Dashboard, median | 1.5 s | 1.2 s |
| Sessions page | 0.71 s | 0.70 s |

Every other page stayed under about 1.5 s. On the 148 GB live archive, a search limited to the last 30 days took 5.2 s against 18.7 s for the whole archive. That came from https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3272, which closed for a separate homepage change and took the search change with it.

Related: https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3260 covers searches holding up homepage panels.

title: feat(export): write one whole session's conversation as JSON lines
body:
A program that copies conversations out of AgentsView today walks the archive-wide changes listing and then reads each message with its own `export conversations message` process. On a large archive that walk takes days. The listing orders changes across every session, so until it ends, the copy holds part of most sessions, and one session can have its replies without its prompts.

`agentsview export conversations session SESSION_ID` writes one session from one archive snapshot, in one process: a header, the session and message changes with their text in bounded chunks, an optional tool summary, and a trailer. A consumer can copy the newest sessions first and store each one whole.

- The header carries the archive revision the snapshot was read at. A consumer that stored a stream can skip session and message changes for that session at or below that revision when it resumes the changes walk. The tool summary keeps its own revision sequence, so a consumer compares it only with the summary it stored.
- The trailer repeats the message count, so a consumer can tell a complete stream from one cut short.
- The command masks secrets the same way `export conversations message` does, and `--reveal` writes stored text unchanged.
- The command exits with the new code 6 when a session is not found, so a consumer can tell a session that left the archive from a failed read.

The Conversation Export guide describes the record format under "Read one whole session".

title: fix(ci): retry API tool downloads and split long macOS command tests
body:
The frontend CI job failed once during `npm run check` with `github.com/go-playground/validator/v10@v10.30.4: verifying module` and `stream error: stream ID 77; INTERNAL_ERROR; received from peer` from the Go checksum service. See the [Failing frontend CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45251877432/attempts/1). While checking this repair, the macOS command-line tests also failed once with `panic: test timed out after 10m0s` in the [Failing macOS CI job](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45263394476/job/138005014109).

Before checking Svelte types, the frontend command regenerates the API clients and rejects stale generated files. The Go client generator ran with a version suffix, which makes Go ignore the project's dependency versions. It fetched its own validator v10.30.4 even though this project already uses v10.30.6. That extra checksum request failed, stopping the job before the type checker ran.

Register the generator as a Go tool in `go.mod`, the project's Go dependency list, and run it with `go tool`. Keep the same generator version while recording its command-only dependencies and checksums. Download those dependencies first through `kit-retry`, the existing helper that retries a command up to three times with a five-second delay. Generation, stale-file detection, and type checking remain outside the retry. Regenerating from the real API specification left all checked-in clients unchanged, and the corrected frontend CI job passed.

The macOS failure exhausted the ten-minute timer for the whole command-line test package. Completed sequential tests consumed about 599 seconds, while the test active at the timeout had run for less than a second and parallel tests still waited to start. Run the command-line tests in the same two complementary name groups already used on Windows, on the existing macOS runner. Keep every test, assertion, retry setting, and the ten-minute package limit, and save both groups' test reports. This adds two test invocations but no runners. The package timer applies only to tests; production commands do not share it.

title: Embedding can't be limited to chosen agents
body:
Embedding can't be limited to the agents a person actually searches by meaning, so a machine running many unattended Codex sessions spends most of its local embedding CPU on transcripts nobody looks up that way. The only filter today is `include_automated`, which drops review-bot sessions but keeps every other agent.

AgentsView gains an `agents` list under `[vector]`. When it's set, only sessions from those agents are embedded, for both the after-sync pass and the backstop rescan; when it's empty, every agent is embedded as today. Keyword search is unchanged, and semantic search simply has no vectors for the excluded agents.

On one devbox over the last day, Codex sessions held 286,065 messages and Claude sessions 83,250, so `agents = ["claude"]` would skip about three quarters of the embedding work there.

body:

On one live archive, 41% of text sent to the embedder in an hour had already been embedded. On 300 synthetic messages with a local nomic embedder, vectors and a sample search result match main's:

title: fix(sync): settle unresolved Codex forks and stop polling loops
body:
User-facing benefit: the daemon no longer burns ~1 CPU core indefinitely or loops over every watched root when a Codex forked rollout references a missing parent rollout on disk.

## What happened

A Codex fork whose `forked_from_id` parent rollout is absent (deleted, expired, or never present on this machine) triggered three compounding loops:

1. **Unbounded re-parse and rewrite loop:** Unresolved forks stay at `data_version = CurrentDataVersion() - 1` so they remain eligible for replay reconciliation when the parent appears. Because that stale version bypassed both `verifiedSources` and `skip_cache`, every watcher retry and poll decompressed the `.jsonl.zst` rollout, re-parsed it, invalidated `codexThreadFileCache`, reconciled against SQLite, rewrote the session, and emitted a `"sessions"` SSE event.
2. **Watch lifecycle stalled in fallback polling:** `Watcher.loop()` only acknowledged `backendLifecycleToken`s when a watch callback returned `nil`. Returning a defer-only `watchBatchApplyError` kept native watch recovery from releasing fallback polling on macOS (`darwinWatchBackend`).
3. **Every poll turned into a full reconciliation:** `PollProviderRootsGrouped` discarded `afterRecon` metadata snapshots for every provider group whenever any group returned an error, including a defer-only Codex fork retry. Every scheduled poll therefore ran a full `ReconcileProviderRootsGrouped` across all configured roots.

## What changed

- **Settle unchanged unresolved forks in background sync (`internal/sync/codex_unresolved_forks.go`, `internal/sync/engine_process_file.go`, `internal/sync/engine.go`):** After writing an unresolved Codex fork, `Engine` records its verified file signature (including `session_index.jsonl`), missing `parentID`, and DB repair state in `unresolvedCodexForkTracker`. On later passes, `unresolvedCodexForkSkip` checks that the file stat and SQLite repair state still match and asks `codexProvider.HasCodexParentRollout` (`internal/parser/codex_provider.go`) whether the original parent rollout exists without invalidating `codexThreadFileCache`. Background watcher and reconciliation passes (`withSettleUnresolvedCodexForks`) settle the fork with zero reads, writes, emits, or deferred errors; explicit `SyncAll` passes keep reporting `stats.Deferred` while still skipping redundant re-reads and SQLite rewrites.
- **Wake waiting forks when the parent arrives, including across roots and restarts (`internal/db/codex_fork.go`, `internal/sync/codex_unresolved_forks.go`, `internal/sync/engine.go`):** `ListUnresolvedCodexForkSources` loads active unresolved fork paths and parent IDs from `codex_fork_state` on demand. When a parent rollout arrives in a changed-path batch (`appendWaitingCodexForkPaths`) or is discovered in another root during a scoped reconciliation (`collectCrossRootWaitingCodexForks`), waiting child forks immediately re-parse, strip inherited turns, restore child usage, and upgrade to `CurrentDataVersion()`. Editing a settled fork file still updates its visible transcript; deleting or tombstoning it clears its tracker entry.
- **Acknowledge lifecycle tokens on defer-only watch batches (`internal/sync/watch_batch_sync.go`, `internal/sync/watcher.go`):** `watchBatchApplyError` propagates `deferOnly` strictly across composed batch phases, and `watchBatchDeferOnlyError` walks single-error and multi-error wrappers so mixed `errors.Join` failures never classify as defer-only. When a watch callback returns a defer-only error, `Watcher` acknowledges `lifecycleTokens` immediately and omits them from the path-scoped retry batch.
- **Keep healthy and settled-fork poll snapshots (`internal/sync/poll_scan.go`, `internal/sync/codex_unresolved_forks.go`, `internal/sync/engine.go`):** `PollProviderRootsGrouped` inspects per-group outcomes from `reconcileProviderRootsGroupedWithOutcomes` and keeps `afterRecon` snapshots for groups that succeeded or returned only tracked unresolved Codex fork deferrals (`isSettledUnresolvedCodexForkOnlyError`), and `afterSync` snapshots for changed-path syncs with only tracked unresolved Codex fork deferrals. Hard errors, mixed multi-page errors, overflowed retry lists, parent-inventory changes, and non-Codex deferred retries still discard snapshots so they retry normally.

## Tradeoffs and limits

- Settling is in-memory per `Engine` instance. After a daemon restart, each unresolved fork is checked once on its first pass so a parent that arrived while the daemon was stopped is picked up immediately, and then settles on the next pass if the parent is still absent.
- S3-backed Codex roots conservatively return `hasParent = true` from `HasCodexParentRollout` because S3 parents live outside local directory inventories and must go through full parse hydration.

## Where to look

- `internal/sync/codex_unresolved_forks.go` for the settling guard, epoch-guarded lazy waiter seeding from SQLite, cross-root wake-up, and `isSettledUnresolvedCodexForkOnlyError`.
- `internal/sync/watch_batch_sync.go` and `internal/sync/watcher.go` for multi-error-aware `watchBatchDeferOnlyError`, strict `deferOnly` error composition, and lifecycle token acknowledgement.
- `internal/sync/poll_scan.go` for per-group `afterRecon` and settled-only `afterSync` snapshot retention.

Fixes #3347

title: Reuse identical embedding chunks across messages
body:
AgentsView sends the same text to the embedding provider again when identical chunks appear in different messages or sessions, even when an indexed chunk already has that vector.

Cache vectors by embedding profile and exact document input, then reuse them across message and session boundaries during incremental builds. Keep old vectors available until the new build finishes so replaced messages can supply matching chunks.

This extends https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3345, which reuses unchanged chunks when the same message grows.

title: Let users choose which message roles get embedded
body:
AgentsView gives people no way to keep user prompts searchable while skipping assistant replies, so they must exclude an entire agent to reduce local embedding work.

Add a role choice to semantic indexing so users can select user messages, assistant messages, or both. Apply the same choice during sync and backstop scans, and update only the affected indexed messages when it changes.

This complements https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3354, which filters by agent and cannot retain user prompts from an excluded agent.

body:

title: fix(remote-sync): name remote sessions by the host's installation identity in exports
body:
Per-machine reporting exports now name a remote-synced host's sessions by that host's installation identity, the same identity the host's own archive uses. A consumer that collects exports from both archives can then recognize one machine and count its activity once. Before this, the collector named those sessions by the configured `host`, so the same work appeared under two machine names.

This is a user-facing fix for anyone who runs AgentsView on a machine and also syncs that machine into another archive with `[[remote_hosts]]`.

- **Remote side:** `ResolveTargets` adds the archive's `installation_id` to the targets it serves over HTTP and SSH.
- **Collector:** remote sync records it per host as `machine_origin:<host>` in `pg_sync_state`. `loadMachineIdentities`, which already resolves `machine_alias:` entries for reporting and the change stream, now reads these records too. An alias still wins.
- **What stays the same:** session rows keep the host as their machine, so filters, pruning, mirrors, and labels behave as before. `machine_alias:` was not reused because it is a filter redirect for rows that adoption rewrote.
- **Change stream:** recording or changing a host's origin publishes that host's sessions again, each under its own revision, so their `machine_id` updates and paging readers receive every session once.
- **Rebuilds:** a full resync and an attached archive rebuild keep the recorded origins, as they keep machine aliases and labels.
- **Limits:** an older remote sends no identity, and its sessions keep `host`. A host cannot claim the collector's own identity. A remote that changes identity moves all of its history to the new one.

On my own setup, a collector syncing a Linux machine over SSH exported that machine's activity under its host name. The machine's own archive exported the same hour, with the same agent-minutes, under its installation identity. Serving targets from this branch on that Linux machine now returns its installation identity.

Review `internal/db/machine_origins.go`, especially the republish statement, and the precedence change in `internal/db/reporting_machines.go`.

The new target field changes the API contract, so the server reports API version 30. `internal/apiclient/client.gen.go` gains only the two generated fields. A local regeneration with a different generator version rewrote unrelated code, so I kept only those lines.

title: perf(search): speed up broad first-page ranking
body:
On a 2.2 GB archive with 12,000 sessions and 1.2 million messages, all containing `code`, the first `code` page now returns 30 sessions in about 0.5 seconds instead of 6.4. Each request used a fresh server with an empty kept-page cache and returned 30 results. Values are medians of three runs per build and resource setting.

| `code` search, fresh server | 4 CPUs, 8 GB | Uncapped |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First page, seconds | 6.4 → 0.51 (13x) | 6.4 → 0.52 (12x) |
| Page two, seconds | 6.4 → 0.52 (12x) | 6.7 → 0.53 (13x) |
| Cursor 630, crossing the tier boundary, seconds | 6.5 → 5.4 (1.2x) | 6.6 → 5.4 (1.2x) |

SQLite relevance searches over 65,536 matches use `rowid` tiers, including project/date filters. Highest 65,536 rowids form tier one; sessions rank by relevance within tiers. Lower-rowid messages and image text follow, then session names. Strong lower-rowid matches can trail weaker higher-rowid ones. `sort=recency` skips tiers; underfilled pages or past-tier cursors use full tier-ordered ranking.

Measured separately as a direct read-only database search, without the API, kept-page cache, or 4-CPU limit, the issue's 30-day filter (`q=code`, `limit=30`, `date_from=2026-06-01`, `date_to=2026-06-30`) returned 30 results in 4.81–4.92 s before the filter-tier change and 0.55–0.56 s after, over three runs each.

Closes https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3350

title: feat(vector): limit embedding to chosen agents
body:
People who search by meaning can choose which agents AgentsView embeds.

With `agents = ["claude"]`, Codex sessions stay out of the local message index.

- After-sync builds, the periodic backstop, and `embeddings build` use the list.
- Removing an agent from the list deletes its vectors; adding one back backfills older sessions.
- An empty or omitted list includes all agents; unknown names fail config load when vector search is enabled.
- The filter applies only to local message embeddings; keyword search, Recall, and hosted PostgreSQL keep their current behavior.

- Set the list under `[vector]`:

```toml
[vector]
agents = ["claude"]
```

Closes https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3354

title: fix(antigravity): separate reasoning effort from model names
body:
User-facing benefit: Antigravity sessions using different reasoning levels of the same model (such as `Gemini 4 Neon (High)` and `Gemini 4 Neon (Low)`) now group under one model slug (`gemini-4-neon`) in `agentsview report usage daily`, the Usage dashboard, and stored messages, while showing the recorded reasoning level in the model badge through `messages.reasoning_effort`.

Previously, `extractAntigravityChatModelName` in `internal/parser/antigravity.go` returned `ChatModelMetadata.model_display_name` (field 21) verbatim as both the message model and usage event model, leaving `messages.reasoning_effort` empty. When field 21 was absent, `resolveAntigravityModelName` also appended `-low`, `-medium`, or `-high` from `executor_metadata` onto the slug. That workaround predated `messages.reasoning_effort` and split one model's spend across each reasoning level and across title-cased display names versus canonical slugs from other agents.

This change extends the existing `messages.reasoning_effort` field used by Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and Posit Assistant, and pairs it with a scoped in-place upgrade in `internal/db/data_version_scope.go` (data version 186 for `antigravity` and `antigravity-cli`, preserving session and source identities).

### Model and effort resolution

Inspecting 37 local `antigravity-cli` SQLite databases showed why the parser cannot simply prefer field 19 (`response_model`) over field 21 (`model_display_name`):

| Field 21 (`model_display_name`) | Field 19 (`response_model`) | Executor field 28 | Resolved `model` | `reasoning_effort` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Gemini 4 Neon (High)` | `gemini-4-neon` | `gemini-4-neon-high` | `gemini-4-neon` | `high` |
| `Gemini 4 Neon (Low)` | `gemini-4-neon` | `gemini-4-neon-low` | `gemini-4-neon` | `low` |
| `Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)` | `gemini-3-flash-a` or `gemini-default` | `gemini-3-flash-agent` | `gemini-3.5-flash` | `high` |
| *(absent)* | `gemini-3.7-flash-exp-b` | `gemini-3.7-flash-high` | `gemini-3.7-flash` | `high` |

`resolveAntigravityModel` in `internal/parser/antigravity.go` extracts both fields, strips recognized reasoning levels (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `thinking`) from parenthesized display suffixes or trailing hyphenated slugs, and converts plain multi-word display labels to lowercase hyphenated slugs. When `response_model` canonicalizes to the same model as the stripped display label (for example `Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)` with `claude-opus-4-6`), it adopts `response_model` as the wire slug. Internal serving aliases (`gemini-3-flash-a`, `gemini-default`) stay ignored when the display label names the product model, while observed serving canary suffixes (`-exp-b`) still reconcile against a covering executor range without touching distinct `-exp` models like `gemini-2.0-flash-exp`.

`applyAntigravityBrainStepMetadata` and `extractAgyGeneratorUsage` in `internal/parser/antigravity_cli.go` carry the resolved `ReasoningEffort` onto brain-transcript and trajectory-sidecar assistant messages. `pricing.DisplayNameModelID` remains in place so archived orphan sessions whose source `.db` files are gone continue to price.

Running a branch build against an isolated copy of 37 real `antigravity-cli` conversation databases produced 346 `gemini-4-neon` and 126 `gemini-3.5-flash` usage events (zero split `(High)`/`(Low)` models), populated `messages.reasoning_effort` (`high` on 342 Neon and 111 Flash replies, `low` on 1 Neon reply), and reported a single `gemini-4-neon` entry in `agentsview report usage daily --since 2026-11-23 --until 2026-11-23 --breakdown --offline --no-sync`.

### Where to look

- `internal/parser/antigravity.go` (`extractAntigravityGenerationModels`, `resolveAntigravityModel`, `resolveAntigravityDisplayModel`) holds the display-name, response-model, and executor reconciliation logic.
- `internal/parser/antigravity_cli.go` propagates `ReasoningEffort` through brain-transcript metadata transfer and sidecar generation usage.
- `internal/db/db.go` and `internal/db/data_version_scope.go` bump `dataVersion` to 186 and scope the in-place reparse to `antigravity` and `antigravity-cli`.
- `docs/internal/session-format-sources.md` updates the Antigravity CLI format provenance entry (with routine `mdformat` rewrapping of pre-existing paragraphs applied by the pre-commit hook).

title: [image_text] v0.48.0: Claude Code tool-result images are stripped at ingest — zero occurrences created, nothing is ever OCR-indexed
body:
### Environment
- AgentsView v0.48.0 (commit 14ab8dd), macOS arm64, daemon mode
- `[image_text]` enabled with a loopback GLM-OCR-compatible endpoint

### Summary
Tool-result images from Claude Code sessions (Anthropic wire format:
`{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":...,"data":...}}` inside a
`tool_result` block) never produce `image_text_occurrences` rows. The stored
`tool_result_events.content` ends up as an **empty string** — the image block is
stripped with no asset offload and no hash reference — so the whole image-text
pipeline has nothing to index.

### Evidence
1. Session JSONL contains a genuine inline image in a tool_result (verified).
2. After ingest, the corresponding `tool_result_events` row has
   `tool_use_id` preserved but `content` = `''` (length 0).
3. `image_text_occurrences` / `image_text_cache` stay at 0 rows forever; the
   one-shot backfill (`stats.image_text_occurrences_backfill_v2`) consumed its
   flag on a database that had no retained images, so enabling the feature later
   never re-scans. `agentsview sync --full` (reparse of 1536 sessions) also
   produced zero occurrences.
4. No assets directory is ever created under the data dir, so
   `ReadRetainedImage(item.Content, item.Index, db.AssetsDir(), ...)` has no
   source to read.
5. The projection layer (`toolImageBlock` in `internal/db/tool_result_images.go`)
   matches blocks by `image_url` (OpenAI-style data-URI form). Anthropic
   `source.base64` image blocks appear to fall outside that shape.

### Expected
Either the image bytes (or an asset reference + sha256) survive ingest so
occurrences can be derived, or the hash is recorded at parse time before any
stripping — per the v0.48 release note "restart the daemon to index new and
retained images".

### Repro
Minimal session file (UUID filename) in a watched Claude projects dir:
one assistant `tool_use` + one user `tool_result` whose content array holds a
base64 image block. Sync; observe empty `tool_result_events.content` and zero
occurrences.

The loopback service side is verified working: our GLM-OCR-compatible endpoint
returns the pinned `model: "glm-ocr"` and `deployment_fingerprint`, passes all
element validation, and the daemon accepts it — only the ingest side never
calls it.

title: HTTP remote sync: unreadable file makes POST /archive fail with a hard 500 (no full-archive fallback)
body:
### Environment
- Collector + remote both v0.48.0; remote is a Debian-based NAS running the
  daemon as an unprivileged user; collector connects over a high-latency
  Tailscale path

### Summary
A single file under a sync target that the daemon user cannot read
(`open ...: permission denied`, e.g. written by a root Docker container into
`~/.claude/projects`) turns every `POST /api/v1/remote-sync/archive` into a
500. The manifest stage succeeds (Lstat only needs directory traversal), so
the collector keeps requesting a delta containing that file, gets a hard 500
each time, and marks the whole host failed — indefinitely.

### Observed 500 body
```
open /home/hobby/.claude/projects/-volume1-docker-dysync/memory/dysync-troubleshooting.md: permission denied
```

### Analysis
- `BuildManifest`/`manifestWalk` tolerate `os.IsNotExist`, but a file whose
  *stat* succeeds and *open* fails (EACCES) still enters the manifest.
- `WriteArchiveFiles` then errors before streaming anything, and the handler
  converts that into a bare 500.
- The collector's delta fallback ("a delta request is rejected after a
  manifest succeeded; the collector retries once with a full archive") does
  not trigger for a 500, so there is no self-healing path.
- Notably, a *missing* file in `DeltaFiles` is handled gracefully (skipped,
  200) — only the exists-but-unreadable case hard-fails.

### Suggestion
Treat EACCES on an archive member like a vanished file (skip it), or answer
with a refusal status the collector already maps to full-archive fallback.

Workaround we used: `find ~/.claude -type f ! -readable` + `chmod a+r` on the
offending files.

title: fix(remotesync): skip unreadable child entries in manifest and archive streams
body:
Fixes #3366

## Problem
When a readable directory under a remote sync root contains a file or child subdirectory that the daemon user cannot open/read (`EACCES` / `os.ErrPermission`, such as a root-owned container file whose parent directory still allows `Lstat`), remote sync gets stuck failing indefinitely:
1. `BuildManifest` (`internal/remotesync/manifest.go`) uses `os.Lstat`/`WalkDir` and advertises the unreadable file in `/api/v1/remote-sync/manifest`.
2. `WriteArchiveFiles` (`POST /api/v1/remote-sync/archive` delta) and `WriteArchive` (full archive fallback) both only ignore `os.IsNotExist(err)` on source entries and fail with `permission denied` (HTTP 500 or truncated stream if bytes already started streaming).

## Fix
- **`internal/remotesync/archive.go`:** Added `isSkippableArchiveError` (`os.IsNotExist` or `os.IsPermission` / `errors.Is(..., os.ErrPermission)`) and applied it in `writeOptionalArchiveFile`, `writeArchiveFile`, `writeArchiveFiles`, and inaccessible child entries/subdirectories in `writeArchivePath`. Both `path != cleanRoot` (unreadable root directory, `0000`) and `filepath.Dir(path) != cleanRoot` (`entry.Info()` failing `Lstat` on direct children of a non-searchable root, `0400`) fail loudly instead of returning an empty archive.
- **`internal/remotesync/manifest.go`, `manifest_readable_unix.go`, `manifest_readable_windows.go`:** Excluded unreadable regular files (`archiveFileReadable`: `unix.Faccessat(..., AT_EACCESS)` with `probeOpenReadable` fallback on `ENOSYS`/`EINVAL`/`ENOTSUP`/`EOPNOTSUPP` on Unix; `probeOpenReadable` on Windows) and inaccessible child subdirectories inside `manifestWalk` while failing loudly on unreadable (`0000`) or non-searchable (`0400`) roots, so the collector does not repeatedly request delta fetches for unreadable entries while surfacing them automatically once permissions are restored.
- **Tests:**
  - `internal/remotesync/archive_unix_test.go` (`!windows`): `TestUnreadableArchiveMembersAndChildDirsAreSkipped` (including `0o000` files/subdirs and `0o400` child subdirs) and `TestBuildManifestAndWriteArchiveFailOnUnreadableRoot` (`0o000` and `0o400` populated roots).
  - `internal/remotesync/archive_windows_test.go` (`windows`): `TestUnreadableArchiveMembersAreSkippedOnWindows` (explicit deny-read DACL).
  - `internal/server/huma_routes_remote_sync_internal_test.go` + `_unix_test.go` + `_windows_test.go`: HTTP end-to-end tests covering direct delta `POST /api/v1/remote-sync/archive` (`200 OK`) and `RemoteSync.Run` two-pass sync without churn.

## Verification
Observed locally on Windows at `5e81a2a` (Unix `0o000`/`0o400` `chmod` tests and `golangci-lint` run on CI; Windows DACL tests exercise the permission-denied `open` path locally):
- `gofmt -s -l`, `git diff --check`, and `go fix -diff -tags fts5 ./internal/remotesync/... ./internal/server/...` — clean
- `go vet -tags fts5 ./internal/remotesync/... ./internal/server/... ./internal/sshremote/...` — passed
- `go test -tags fts5 -race -count=1 -v ./internal/remotesync -run TestUnreadableArchiveMembersAreSkippedOnWindows` (`1.780s`) and `TestRemoteSyncArchiveHTTP_SkipsUnreadableFileOnWindows` (`2.470s`) — passed
- `go test -tags fts5 -race -count=1 ./internal/server -run "TestRemoteSync|TestIssue1492"` (`5.402s`) and `go test -tags fts5 -race -count=1 ./internal/remotesync` filtered to non-symlink suites (`19.746s`) — passed

title: test(cli): wait for the failing child process before checking its log
body:
`TestBackgroundServeFailureIncludesCurrentLaunchOutput/autostart=true` intermittently reports `server did not become ready within 1s` instead of including `opening database: permission denied`. It failed once and passed on retry in the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45315668430/attempts/1).

The test starts a copy of its own test binary as a helper process. The parent starts its one-second readiness timer as soon as the process launches, while the child still has to initialize, write its error, and exit. If the timer wins, the parent reports a readiness timeout before it can observe the child's exit and include the log. This ordering also exists on the default branch.

Wait for the helper to close its stdout pipe on exit before the test's launch callback returns. The application still waits for and reaps the child itself, and the test still checks that the returned error includes this launch's stderr and log path while excluding stale output. Both explicit background startup and automatic startup use the synchronized helper.

A real server can also take longer than its readiness budget, so a timeout is valid production behavior. The flaky assertion comes from this test requiring the exit path without first arranging for the helper to exit. The change only adjusts the test fixture.

Model used: GPT-6 (Codex).

title: fix(test): remove clock precision assumptions from Cursor sync tests
body:
`TestCursorSyncDefersMemberEventsUntilTeamPoll` intermittently fails in the Windows command tests and passes on retry. This happened in two saved runs: [First failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45260239448/attempts/1) and [Later failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45317629897/attempts/1). The original assertion output is unavailable. On the default branch, the test requires the saved poll timestamp to be strictly earlier than the team-roster request timestamp.

The usage sync reads the clock after fetching team usage, then requests the team roster. The roster handler reads the clock again. Those ordered reads can return the same timestamp, causing the strict comparison to fail even when the sync assigns events correctly. The adjacent refresh test also relies on consecutive syncs getting different timestamps. Equal clock readings can occur in production, but these strict time comparisons exist only in the tests; event ownership depends on which events the team fetch returned.

Use Go's controlled test clock to exercise equal timestamps in the ownership test and distinct timestamps in the refresh test. A controlled-clock reproduction fails at the original strict comparison and passes when equality is allowed. Keep the checks that a member-only event stays unassigned until the next team fetch and that the second sync refreshes previously covered hours. This changes only tests and leaves the sync behavior unchanged.

Model used: GPT-6 (Codex).

title: fix(parser): normalize Anthropic base64 tool_result image blocks
body:
Fixes #3365

### Why
When a Claude Code (or shared Anthropic-format) session contains a `tool_result` content array with inline image blocks (`{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":"image/png","data":"..."}}`), `parseToolResult` preserves `ContentRaw`, but downstream ingest (`ingest.PairToolResultsContext`) and incremental subagent link writes (`sync.writeIncremental`) decode it via `parser.DecodeContent`.

Previously, `DecodeContent` (and `toolResultContentLength`) only extracted `"text"` and `"result"` strings from array content and ignored `"type":"image"` blocks. As a result:
- `tool_result_events.content` and `tool_calls.result_content` became `""` (or omitted the image block),
- `db.ProjectToolResultImages` / `db.RetainedToolResultImages` saw zero images (no `assets/` offload, no retained `input_image` blocks), and
- `image_text_occurrences` stayed at 0 rows so the `image_text` OCR pipeline never received any work.

### What changed
- **Anthropic base64 image normalization (`internal/parser/content.go`)**:
  - Updated `decodeImageBearingContentArray` / `toolResultBlockImageURL`, `decodeContent`, and `toolResultContentLength` so arrays containing valid Anthropic base64 image blocks (`type == "image"`, `source.type == "base64"`, valid `image/*` `media_type`, non-empty `data`) normalize into deterministic JSON arrays holding canonical `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:<mime>;base64,<data>"}` blocks alongside any non-empty `"text"` / `"result"` blocks in their original order.
  - Non-base64 `url` image sources, invalid/non-image media types, empty base64 payloads, text-only arrays, and OpenAI `input_image` arrays stay unchanged so plain-text decoding and existing subagent-link tests remain backwards-compatible.
- **Scoped upgrade (`internal/db/db.go`, `internal/db/data_version_scope.go`)**:
  - Bumped `dataVersion` from `188` to `189` and declared `dataVersionScopes[189]` for all providers that pass `ContentRaw` arrays through `toolResultContentLength` and/or raw unquoted JSON arrays into `DecodeContent`: `claude`, `cowork`, `qoder`, `icodemate`, `openclaude`, `amp`, `cursor`, `factory`, `iflow`, `openclaw`, `qclaw`, `devin`, `openhands`, `zcode`, `pi`, `omp`, `omo`, `prime-agent`, `stepcode`, `direct-api`, `tau`, `commandcode`, `qwen`, `qwenpaw`, `gemini`, `goose`, `grok`, `fx`, `cline`, `zencoder`, `workbuddy`, `deepseek-tui`, `kiro`, `codebuff` (including `freebuff` via `ProviderStoredAgents`), and `posit-assistant`.
  - Recorded `189-408953c13b0f5b28f2708570d963929e997e8f20abf9aeeece0d803953879e9d.json` in `internal/parser/testdata/data-version-output-digests/`.
- **Tests**:
  - `internal/parser/parser_test.go`: `TestDecodeContent_ToolResultImages` and `TestExtractTextContent_AnthropicToolResultImage`.
  - `internal/parser/zcode_test.go`: `TestZCodeToolResultImageBlockNormalized`.
  - `internal/db/data_version_scope_test.go`: `TestToolResultImageDecodeUpgradeScopes` (`188 -> 189` full scope check).
  - `internal/db/data_version_scope_integration_test.go`: `TestClaudeToolResultImageUpgradeReparsesAndIndexes` and `TestZCodeToolResultImageUpgradeReparsesAndIndexes` (verifies upgrading unchanged Claude JSONL and Z Code SQLite archives from `188 -> 189` reparses in place (`fullRebuild == false`), populates stored tool results + `result_content_length`, retains images on `GetAllMessages`, and creates `image_text_occurrences`).
  - `internal/sync/tool_result_images_test.go`: `TestClaudeToolResultImagesRetainedOffloadedAndIndexed` (verifies real Claude JSONL `SyncAll` under both `keep` and `offload` policies populates `RetainedToolResultImages`, writes offloaded asset files, queues `PendingImageText`, and resolves `ReadRetainedImage`).

### Verification
Run on Windows (`56f6cd4`, rebased on `41d82e2`):
- `gofmt -s -w` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- `go vet -tags "fts5" ./internal/parser ./internal/ingest ./internal/db ./internal/sync ./cmd/agentsview`: passed.
- `go test -tags "fts5" -race -count=1 ./internal/parser -run "TestParsedOutputMatchesDataVersion|TestDecodeContent|TestExtractTextContent|TestZCode"`: passed (`3.678s`).
- `go test -tags "fts5" -race -count=1 ./internal/db -run "ToolResult|StripImage|MigrateImage|ImageText|DataVersion|ZCode|PiSkill"`: passed (`7.816s`).
- `go test -tags "fts5" -race -count=1 ./internal/sync -run "ToolResult|Image|Claude|ZCode|Incremental"`: passed (`70.782s`).
- `go test -tags "fts5" -race -count=1 ./internal/ingest`: passed (`3.241s`).

title: perf(reporting): size each digest date's rows to that date
body:
## TL;DR

`agentsview export digest` over 30 days used more memory than it needed: each date copied its rows into a buffer sized for the whole range. Each date now copies only its own rows, which cuts the digest's peak memory by up to 1.4x with the same output.

## Why

Since #1830, the digest loads source rows once for the whole range, then builds each date from them. A date keeps only a small share of those rows, but its copy reserved room for all of them. A 30-day joint digest benchmark went from about 220 MiB to about 1.6 GiB of peak memory at #1830.

Peak anonymous memory of a 30-day digest, same output before and after:

| Archive | Before | After | Speed-up |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Synthetic, 3,000 sessions x 40 turns in one month | 492 MiB | 346 MiB | 1.42x |
| Real Claude and Codex sessions, one month | 198 MiB | 175 MiB | 1.13x |

## Reviewer notes

- **Look at `forDate` in `internal/db/reporting_source.go`.** The date-selection rules are unchanged.
- **The digest still holds the whole range's source rows.** #1830 keeps them to read the archive once, so peak memory stays above a single-day export.

title: test(e2e): inspect the active SSE stream in shared-live broadcast test
body:
## Summary

Stabilizes `frontend/e2e/shared-live.spec.ts` (`several visible session tabs share live updates (fallback: broadcast)`) by asserting against the single active `/api/v1/events` stream instead of `requested.at(-1)`.

- **Cause:** When tabs navigate under slower BroadcastChannel election (observed on WebKit), a newly navigated tab can briefly open and close a single-session `/api/v1/events?session=...` request after the leader tab has already opened the combined multi-session stream. Because the leader's active stream already carries all three sessions, no further request is issued and `requested.at(-1)` stays stuck on the closed single-session URL until the 15s timeout expires.
- **Change:** Store `Map<http.ServerResponse, string>` for `active` streams and poll `singleActiveSessions()` so the test verifies both that exactly one `/api/v1/events` stream is active and that it subscribes to every expected session ID.

title: Collector-only server: resync flag never clears, every remote sync forced full (v0.48.0)
body:
## Summary

On a server that only collects from `[[remote_hosts]]` (no local agent session files), the data-version resync can never succeed. `NeedsResync()` therefore stays `true` for the life of the process, and **every scheduled remote sync runs as a forced full import** (`full_reason=explicit-full`, `invalidate_all` / `force_full_parse_all`). With a remote of ~15 GB, that means re-downloading and re-extracting the whole mirror and re-parsing every session on every interval, indefinitely.

## Version / setup

- agentsview v0.48.0 (linux/amd64, commit 14ab8dd), SQLite archive (~8 GB `sessions.db`, ~13k sessions). The same behavior was present on v0.46.1.
- Runs as a systemd service: `agentsview serve`, plus a separate `agentsview mcp` service.
- Config: three `[[remote_hosts]]` entries, `transport = "http"`, `interval = "5m"`. No local agent homes on this machine; everything comes from the remotes.
- Mirrors on the collector: ~15 GB, ~16 GB and ~0.1 GB.

## What happens

At every startup:

```
database upgrade requires full resync
resync: aborting swap, 0 synced / 0 failed / 0 total: kept the existing archive: the rebuild found no session files, but the archive has 13355 sessions from files
startup archive rebuild failed: resync-build worker pass reported aborted (kept the existing archive: ...)
startup sync incomplete; opening watcher dispatch with retry coverage: ...
```

After that, every scheduled remote sync is full:

```
Running scheduled remote sync for <remote>...
remote sync archive: host=<remote> encoding="zstd" wire_bytes=1379929702 download_duration=2m49s extract_duration=2m52s
file sync: 7108 synced, 71 skipped in 12m56s
remote sync delta import: host=<remote> ... sessions_synced=7108 sessions_total=7180 ... full_reason=explicit-full journal_outcome=retired ...
```

- Across 4.5 days of logs: **698 of 698** remote imports (all three remotes) were `full_reason=explicit-full`.
- `<data-dir>/remote-mirrors/<remote>.changes.json` is rewritten every cycle as `{"full_import":true,"full_import_reason":"explicit-full","force_full_parse_all":true,...}`.
- Restarting does not help: the flag is set again when the DB opens and the resync aborts again.

## Impact

- One remote is sent as a full ~1.0–1.5 GB zstd archive (~15 GB extracted) on every cycle. Every remote's sessions are fully re-parsed: ~7k files in 6–13 min, ~5.5k files in ~7.5 min.
- Cycles take longer than the 5-minute interval, so the server syncs back to back around the clock.
- Measured from `/proc/<pid>/io` for `agentsview serve` over 23.5 h: **write_bytes ≈ 691 GB (~8 MB/s avg, ~700 GB/day)**, read_bytes ≈ 1.9 TB, and cancelled_write_bytes ≈ 146 GB (mirror files replaced). Bursts reach ~120 MB/s during extract.
- That is most of the host's SSD writes, and it caused I/O-wait stalls for unrelated workloads sharing the disk.

## Relevant logic (v0.48.0)

- `cmd/agentsview/main.go`, `remoteHostSyncFunc`: scheduled remote syncs call `runRemote(ctx, cfg, database, rh, database.NeedsResync())`, so the stale flag becomes `Full=true`.
- `internal/db/db.go`: `NeedsResync()` returns `dataStale`. It is set on open ("database upgrade requires full resync") and cleared only by `MarkDataCurrent()`, which is called from the successful local resync swap in `internal/sync/engine.go`.
- `internal/sync/engine.go`: the resync swap guard aborts with "the rebuild found no session files, but the archive has N sessions from files". On a remote-only collector, local discovery is always empty, so this guard always fires and `MarkDataCurrent()` is never reached.
- `internal/remotesync/http.go` / `prepare.go`: with `Full=true` and an empty `FullReason`, the import is treated as the legacy explicit full (`InvalidateAll` + `ForceFullParseAll`).

Related but different triggers: #2911 (deferred source keeps `archive_stale` set), #2180 (data-version upgrades force a full rebuild).

## Expected

- A data-version upgrade on a remote-only collector should finish once: rebuild from the remote mirrors (or mark data current after the first successful full remote import per host).
- After that, scheduled remote syncs should go back to incremental / delta imports.
- At minimum, a scheduled remote sync should not be forced to `explicit-full` forever because of a local resync that can never apply.

## Suggested fix (any of)

1. In the resync swap guard, treat "no local sources configured/discovered, but remote hosts exist" as a successful (no-op) local pass. Call `MarkDataCurrent()` once the remote hosts have each completed a full import at the current data version.
2. Pass a scoped reason (e.g. data-rebuild, which already exists) instead of `NeedsResync()` → legacy explicit-full for scheduled remote syncs, and clear it per host after one successful full import (`RemoteImportDataVersion` already tracks this per host).
3. Log a clear warning, and expose it in `sync status`, when `NeedsResync()` has stayed true across N scheduled remote syncs.

Workaround for now: raise the `interval` of the largest remote to reduce the write volume.

title: test(sync): avoid duplicate lifecycle wake in macOS fallback test
body:
`TestDarwinWatcherLifecycleFailureFallsBackToPolling` creates the intermediate directory after `watcher.Start()` and then calls `backend.signalLifecycle()`. Because `darwinWatchBackend.Start()` already sends an initial lifecycle wake, creating the directory right after `Start()` can let the startup wake perform the first `addAncestor` attempt and open fallback before the test's manual `signalLifecycle()` arrives. While fallback is open, `processFallbackTransition()` returns `false` until native recovery is due, so that second wake falls through to `processLifecycle(true)` and runs `addAncestor` a second time, failing the `attempts == 1` assertion even with `retryInitial = time.Hour`.

Create the intermediate directory after `RegisterRoots` (while it is still missing so `RegisterRoots` watches the ancestor) and before `watcher.Start()`, removing the extra manual `signalLifecycle()` so `Start()` drives the single advance attempt deterministically.

Note: `internal/sync/watcher_darwin_test.go` is `darwin`-only and could not be executed locally on Linux; the macOS FSEvents CI job covers it.

title: fix(remotesync): stage SQLite snapshots in the user cache
body:
Remote sync uses SQLite's online backup API to stage a coherent database before adding it to the archive. That temporary file can be as large as the database. On my setup, a 1.55 GB Hermes database previously failed to stage when the system temporary filesystem had only about 1.1 GB free. In an isolated run against a copy of that database with `TMPDIR` unset, I observed the snapshot in the user cache and the archive successfully contained the full 1.55 GB database.

This changes only where the existing snapshot writer stages its file. An explicit `TMPDIR` still takes precedence, and an unavailable cache directory falls back to the normal temporary directory. The cache filesystem still needs room for one snapshot per in-flight transfer. The cache selection and the platform-independent defaults/override coverage are in `internal/remotesync`.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Codex <codex@openai.com>
Model used: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol

title: perf(remotesync): refresh SQLite snapshots with sqlite3_rsync over SSH
body:
A small write to a large remote SQLite database can cause the existing SSH mirror sync to download another complete database snapshot in the archive. This extends the streaming manifest path from #2430: retain only manifest entries for SQLite snapshot targets, then let `sqlite3_rsync` update those files in place when available. A successful transfer stays in the mirror import journal but is omitted from the archive request. Other files, HTTP sources, and failed or unavailable rsync transfers keep using the archive path. `AGENTSVIEW_NO_SQLITE3_RSYNC=1` opts out.

On my real 1.55 GB Hermes `state.db`, an isolated collector pulled the database over SSH via `sqlite3_rsync`; the subsequent archive carried about 4.6 MB of other source files without re-sending the database. The mirror database opened and contained 16,951 source sessions. That was an initial mirror population, not a measured speedup on incremental runs. The key review points are manifest identity stamping and preserving the journal entry when a database leaves the archive request.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Codex <codex@openai.com>
Model used: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol

title: fix(frontend): keep transcript load error stable during background retry
body:
When an initial transcript load fails with a transient HTTP 5xx error, `MessagesStore.doLoadSession` sets `loadError` and queues a background `reload()` that calls `fullReload()` up to `MAX_LOAD_ATTEMPTS` times (300ms apart).

Previously, two things raced with a user clicking **Retry** during those background attempts:
1. `fullReload()` unconditionally set `this.loading = true`, which caused `MessageList.svelte` to unmount `<LoadError>` (and its **Retry** button) and replace it with `<LoadingState>` while each background retry ran. A click arriving across that transition could miss the button between `mousedown` and `mouseup` (notably on WebKit in `load-failures.spec.ts`).
2. `retryLoad()` called `loadSession(id)` without canceling an in-flight background reload, so if `this.loading` was `true` when `retryLoad()` ran, `loadSession()` returned early without starting a new request.

This change:
- Keeps `this.loading` false in `fullReload()` when `this.loadError` is already shown so `<LoadError>` and its **Retry** button stay mounted while background retries run (still updating `modelInfo` and clearing `loadError` if a background retry succeeds).
- Cancels any in-flight reload in `retryLoad()` before calling `loadSession(id)` when retrying an empty transcript, ensuring an explicit Retry click always starts a fresh load.
- Adds a unit test in `frontend/src/lib/stores/messages.test.ts` covering both invariants.

title: fix(remote-sync): allow collector-only resync and stop explicit-full loop
body:
## Summary

Fixes both parts of collector-only ([[remote_hosts]]) archive upgrades getting stuck in an infinite explicit-full remote sync loop:

1. **Exclude configured [[remote_hosts]] ID prefixes during local rebuilds (internal/archivesource/rebuild.go, internal/remotesync/import.go):**
   - ^Grchivesource.RebuildContributors now populates UnavailableContributorIDPrefixes with <host>~ (emotesync.HostIDPrefix) for each configured cfg.RemoteHosts entry.
   - On collector-only servers with zero local sessions, esyncBuildLocked now computes localOldFileSessions == 0, preserves all remote sessions via CopyOrphanedDataFromExcluding (without relaxing active contributor safety checks when remote contributors are explicitly attached), swaps the rebuilt database, and clears NeedsResync().
2. **Stop forcing FullImportExplicit on scheduled remote sync ticks (cmd/agentsview/main.go):**
   - emoteHostSyncFunc no longer passes database.NeedsResync() as  ull = true (which became FullImportExplicit / InvalidateAll on every interval while NeedsResync() remained set).
   - Scheduled remote syncs pass  alse so emotesync.RemoteSync.Prepare drives a one-time, mirror-based FullImportDataRebuild (or ScopedDataVersionProviders) per host via RemoteImportDataVersion / SetRemoteImportDataVersion, returning to incremental delta imports afterward without re-downloading unchanged mirror files.

## Verification

- internal/archivesource/rebuild_test.go: added TestRebuildContributorsIncludesRemoteHostPrefixes.
- cmd/agentsview/sync_worker_test.go: added TestCollectorOnlyUpgradeResyncClearsNeedsResyncAndPreservesRemoteSessions.
- cmd/agentsview/main_test.go: updated TestRemoteHostSyncFuncDoesNotForceFullWhenDatabaseNeedsResync and added TestCollectorOnlyScheduledRemoteSyncDoesNotLoopFullAfterUpgrade (against a mirror-capable HTTP remote test server).
- Ran go vet -tags fts5 and CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags fts5 -count=1 across ./internal/archivesource, ./internal/remotesync (excluding 4 Windows admin symlink tests), ./internal/sync -run TestResync, ./internal/server -run TestPrepareHTTPRebuild|TestRunRemoteSyncRequest, and ./cmd/agentsview resync/remote/sync-worker suites.

Closes #3375

title: ci: let release command checks fetch modules when the Go proxy fails
body:
The Released commands CI job failed once in the [Failing CI run](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45467435288/job/138705995245) while downloading `go.kenn.io/kit@v0.38.0`: `stream error: stream ID 7; INTERNAL_ERROR; received from peer`. This job checks documented commands against the latest released binary.

The Go module proxy failed during the shared action's build. CI already allows Go to fetch directly from the module source after a proxy error, but GitHub does not pass the caller workflow's environment variables into a reusable workflow. The release-command workflow therefore used Go's default policy, which stops on this error.

Give the release-command workflow the same `GOPROXY` setting as the other Go workflows. `GOPROXY` controls where Go downloads modules; the `|direct` suffix permits a source download after any proxy error. This preserves checksum verification and the command checks, and also covers checks triggered by a published release. In an isolated reproduction using the exact module version and a loopback proxy returning HTTP 500, the default policy failed and the direct fallback succeeded. This is a CI dependency-download failure and does not change the shipped application.

Model used: Codex
