title: feat(vector): choose which message roles get embedded
body:
People who run local embeddings can now embed only their prompts and skip assistant replies, which are most of the text the embedder reads. On one archive, replies were 85.5% of indexed characters, and Ollama averaged about 4 CPU cores over an hour of embedding. `roles = ["user"]` takes that 85.5% out of the queue; the CPU saving is estimated from that share.

```toml
[vector]
roles = ["user"]   # or ["assistant"]; empty or both embeds both
```

Semantic search then finds a session by what you asked, and you read the reply there. Text that appears only in a reply stays in keyword search. Before, the only way to cut embedding work was removing a whole agent from `[vector] agents`, which dropped its prompts too.

Sync, the periodic backstop, and `embeddings build` apply `roles`, and changing it re-embeds only messages that enter scope. Recall and hosted PostgreSQL embeddings ignore it. The persisted schema doesn't change; removing `roles` restores both roles, including on an older build.

Closes https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3359

title: perf(vector): reuse embeddings across messages and sessions
body:
Semantic search can reuse identical chunks across messages and sessions. This extends https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3355 beyond one growing message.

| Scenario | Characters sent to encoder |
| --- | ---: |
| Same chunk in a new session | 4,000 → 0 |
| Message replaced with mostly the same text | 4,019 → 19 |

These local runs used a fake encoder. The first upgrade backfill took 164 seconds and added 447 MB on a copied 920,388-chunk index; a separate vector cache would add 2.8 GB.

An older version can leave chunk pointers missing, so a later match may need a new embedding. If a build fails after replacing a message, its old chunks remain available for retry.

Closes https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3358

title: source sync --full: a reader's open transaction discards the rebuild, and one-shot mode still exits 0
body:
`agentsview source sync --full` builds a replacement archive and swaps it in over `sessions.db`. If another process holds a read transaction on `sessions.db`, the final WAL checkpoint before the swap times out after about 5 s, and the rebuild is thrown away. Refusing to swap under a reader is reasonable. The problem is how the failure is reported. Run one-shot (`AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1`, no daemon running), the command prints `Sync complete: 0 sessions synced` and **exits 0**, and only `debug.log` records the failure. Through the daemon it exits 1, but its hint points somewhere else.

**Versions.** Observed with the v0.47.0 release binary (`agentsview v0.47.0 (commit 1079cb632051e8c9cbad2dcc945a60643c756d81, built 2026-11-09T14:59:58Z)`, GitHub release asset `agentsview_0.47.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz`) on macOS 26.6.2 (arm64). v0.48.0 and `main` at `7c47aec9` were read, not run: the code below is the same in both.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
export AGENTSVIEW_DATA_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON=1
agentsview source sync            # build an archive; any sessions will do

# another process holds a read transaction for 30 s
{ echo 'BEGIN; SELECT count(*) FROM sessions;'; sleep 30; } |
  sqlite3 "$AGENTSVIEW_DATA_DIR/sessions.db" &
sleep 1
agentsview source sync --full; echo "exit=$?"
```

The measured run held the transaction with a Python `sqlite3` connection that ran `BEGIN` and a `SELECT` and left the transaction open. A `sqlite3` shell inside `BEGIN`, as above, holds the same kind of read lock.

### What happens

One-shot, output trimmed:

```
  Closing current database before swap...
  Closing current database before swap completed in 5.474s
  Discovering sessions...
  Discovering sessions completed in 28ms
Sync complete: 0 sessions synced in 5.735s
Database: 52 sessions, 203 messages
exit=0
```

The progress line calls the failed close "completed". No `Swapping rebuilt database into place` line appears, `sessions.db` is still the old file, and only `debug.log` says why: `resync: close orig db: final wal checkpoint: wal checkpoint busy`. In a daemon run, a transaction that ended 2 s into the wait let the swap finish.

Through the daemon (`agentsview daemon start`, `AGENTSVIEW_NO_DAEMON` unset, the same reader):

```
fatal: daemon sync: daemon sync error: {"error":"swap resync database: final wal checkpoint: wal checkpoint busy"}
hint: check the named host in [[remote_hosts]] in config.toml, or omit --host to sync all configured sources; run `agentsview source sync --help` for flags and examples
```

### Where the failure is lost (`main` at `7c47aec9`)

1. The in-process resync closes the writer for its write barrier ([internal/sync/engine.go:2857–2864](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/sync/engine.go#L2857-L2864), [:2584](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/sync/engine.go#L2584)). So the swap's `CloseConnections` runs the final checkpoint on a fresh connection: `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, under the DSN's 5 s busy timeout, reports busy and becomes `ErrWALCheckpointBusy` ([internal/db/db.go:5910–5914](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/db/db.go#L5910-L5914), [:5935–5943](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/db/db.go#L5935-L5943), [:1380](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/db/db.go#L1380)).
2. `swapResyncDatabaseLocked` logs it, marks the stats aborted with a warning, deletes the replacement and returns the error ([internal/sync/engine.go:2965–2979](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/sync/engine.go#L2965-L2979)).
3. `resyncAllLocked` drops that error (`stats, _ = …`, [:2739–2744](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/sync/engine.go#L2739-L2744)). `syncThenRunLocked` then answers the aborted resync with an incremental pass whose stats replace the resync's, warning included ([:3378–3385](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/sync/engine.go#L3378-L3385)). That pass is the `Discovering sessions` above.
4. An error that did get through would not change the exit status either. `runLocalSync` only logs it to `debug.log` ([cmd/agentsview/sync.go:788–796](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/cmd/agentsview/sync.go#L788-L796)), the summary is printed regardless ([:846–850](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/cmd/agentsview/sync.go#L846-L850)), and `doSync` returns `false` after a local sync ([:232–245](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/cmd/agentsview/sync.go#L232-L245)), so `runSync` never exits 1 ([:46–50](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/cmd/agentsview/sync.go#L46-L50)). The daemon branch, by contrast, calls `fatal("daemon sync: %v", err)` ([:187](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/cmd/agentsview/sync.go#L187)). This step is also why the `local sync failed: …` line in #2461 appeared only in `debug.log`.
5. The daemon-mode hint is the one every `sync` failure gets ([cmd/agentsview/cli_diagnostics.go:268–269](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/cmd/agentsview/cli_diagnostics.go#L268-L269)).

The same resync path also runs when the archive's data version is behind the binary ([cmd/agentsview/sync.go:827](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/cmd/agentsview/sync.go#L827), [internal/sync/engine.go:3377](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/7c47aec91505f08e2b0f23ee850a3392a6b19b17/internal/sync/engine.go#L3377)). Whether a blocked rebuild there ends the same way was not tested.

In v0.48.0 the same code sits at `engine.go` L2730–2735, L2956–2970 and L3363–3370, `sync.go` L788–796, and `db.go` L5870–5871 and L5883–5905.

### Expected

A full resync whose replacement is not installed exits non-zero and says why on stderr. For example: `full resync not installed: another connection holds a read transaction on sessions.db (final WAL checkpoint busy after 5s); the archive is unchanged; retry once that connection closes`. The summary should not say `Sync complete` for a rebuild that was discarded.

### Suggested fix

- Carry the swap error out of `resyncAllLocked` and `syncThenRunLocked` (or record it in `SyncStats`), and keep the swap's warning when the incremental fallback runs.
- Have `runLocalSync` return its error, and have `doSync` exit through `fatal` on it, as the daemon branch does.
- Give `ErrWALCheckpointBusy` its own message and hint (another connection holds the archive) instead of the `[[remote_hosts]]` one.
- Optionally, retry the final checkpoint for a bounded time before discarding a long rebuild.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Server stays offline while an upgrade reparses one agent's sessions
body:
AgentsView refuses every connection after an upgrade that bumps a scoped data version, until it finishes reparsing that agent's sessions. On a machine with 72,765 Claude session files, the server stayed down for more than 20 minutes after updating to a build that includes https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3370, which moved the data version from 188 to 189 for some agents. The UI, the MCP server, and every client that reads through the server got "connection refused" for the whole time.

The server should start listening first and serve the existing rows while the scoped reparse runs, the same way https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3344 already does for ordinary startup sync. Rows from unaffected agents are current. Rows from the agent being reparsed are one data version behind, which is what users saw a minute before the upgrade.

Today `runServe` only defers the startup worker until after listening when `ArchiveResyncState` reports nothing to do. A pending scoped upgrade sets `dataStale`, so startup runs the full worker before binding the port. Schema repairs and full rebuilds can keep blocking: they change what the server can read. A scoped reparse leaves the schema alone.

title: fix(codex): skip Claude Code command text in session titles
body:
Codex can import Claude Code sessions. If one started with a slash command like `/model`, AgentsView used the command's `<command-name>` text as the session title. The session lists and Top Sessions showed raw markup.

The title is now the first user message that is not a command envelope or other text that Claude Code injects. The check is the one the Claude parser already has: `isCommandEnvelope` and `isClaudeSystemMessage`. A forked session gets its title the same way. The transcript stays as written. A fork finds its rows by the stored text, so a rewrite would duplicate them.

Data version 190 reparses Codex, TraeX, Augure Code, and Open Interpreter sessions in place. Codex checkpoints move to version 7.

Limits:

- A typed prompt that starts with a slash (`/tmp is full`) still becomes the title.
- A session whose source file is gone keeps its old title.

26 Codex sessions in my archive have a raw `<command-name>` title. I have not run this build on them yet. The tests use synthetic rollouts.

Start at `observeFirstMessage` in `internal/parser/codex.go` and the title loop in `internal/sync/codex_fork.go`.

title: Muse Personal: scheduled and background runs aren't classified as automated
body:
### Problem / motivation

Muse Personal sessions (v0.48.0) are never classified as automated: every one gets `is_automated = false` and an empty `session_kind` (`muse_personal_test.go` asserts the empty kind). Most are Muse's own scheduled jobs and background passes. On one agent that's about 2,580 of 3,700 sessions, against about 98 real chats, and they crowd lists, counts, search and embeddings, which the existing "Automated Session Detection" is meant to prevent.

### Proposed solution

Muse records the run type. Every item line has a top-level `source` (`$.source`). In the Muse Personal parser, mark the session automated, regardless of message count (as roborev is), when the **first user-role item's** `source` is one of:

- `scheduler.cron`: scheduled jobs (1,501)
- `runtime.self_improvement`: background upkeep (1,478)
- `runtime.feed` (173), `runtime.proactivity` (90), `runtime.browser_input` (82), `runtime.action` (47)

That flags 2,581 sessions and no real chats. Real chats use plain `runtime`, a voice source (`runtime.voice_audio`, `runtime.voice_companion_history`, `runtime.voice_s2s_record.user`) or `runtime.onboarding`.

Notes:
- Use the first user-role item, not the first item: context items come first (52 real chats start with a `runtime.skill_invalidation` item, and `runtime.chats` only ever appears on an opening context item).
- Plain `runtime` also covers subagent runs and delegated assignments. Leave it unclassified; the one-message gate plus a built-in prefix for `[Subagent Context] You are running as a subagent (depth ` handles those.
- Ignore the message count for `scheduler.cron`: about half of those runs get injected follow-ups (approvals), which shouldn't make them look like conversations.
- Suggested test: fixtures for each source above, plus a real chat whose first item is a context stamp.

<details>
<summary>Evidence (one Muse Personal agent, about 3,700 sessions)</summary>

- `source` is present on 70,850 of 70,850 item lines; the session header line has none.
- 2,663 sessions have exactly one user message and 178 have four or more. Some jobs run every 10–15 minutes, which is over a hundred sessions a day.
- Counts above are by the first user-role item's `source`. The six machine sources flag 2,581 sessions; a manual review found no real chats among them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Current workaround and why it isn't enough</summary>

This user-config block, tested on the same data, flags about 2,585 sessions (with the one-message gate) and matches nothing from other agents in a shared PostgreSQL database:

```toml
[automated]
prefixes = [
  "[WORKER TASK]\njob_id: ",
  "## Step instructions\n",
  "[Subagent Context] You are running as a subagent (depth ",
  "[Web Artifact Task Request]\n\nartifact_slug: ",
  "## Available lanes\nweb, social, tracking, schedule",
  "# Ideas tab composer\n\nYou write the top rail of this user's Ideas tab.",
  "Find useful, timely ways to help this person with their day. Use the research direction in your system message",
  "Choose which opportunities, completed studies and app or device updates would help this person enough to deserve a message.",
  "Carry out this assignment end to end, then report the result.",
]
substrings = [
  "Muse, this user's personal agent. This background run",
]
```

Limits:
- The one-message gate lets through job runs that receive an injected follow-up: about 750 `[WORKER TASK]` sessions stay unflagged.
- Every Muse user has to discover these envelopes, and the list breaks silently if Muse rewords its prompts.
- With PostgreSQL sync, the list must be byte-identical on every machine that opens the shared database: `backfillIsAutomatedPG` (`internal/postgres/automated_audit.go`) re-flags rows with whichever classifier is running, so a machine without the list flips the flags back.

</details>

title: pg push is latency-bound on high-round-trip links (per-session statements)
body:
### Problem / motivation

`replica pg push` is limited by round trips, not by the database. A first load over a high-latency link takes hours. Pushing about 3,700 Muse Personal sessions (about 81,000 messages) with agentsview v0.48.0 from Muse's hosted machine runs at about 20 sessions a minute, about 3 hours in total. That machine reaches PostgreSQL only through an HTTP CONNECT tunnel over a relayed Tailscale path, so every round trip is long; the same data pushes quickly from a machine on the LAN.

The database is waiting on the client: sampling `pg_stat_activity` for the pusher's backend 40 times over 10 seconds found it `idle in transaction` / `Client:ClientRead` 38 times. Statements go out one at a time, per session (`DELETE FROM session_plan_usage WHERE session_id = ...`, `INSERT INTO tool_calls (...)`, ...), and commit about every 50 sessions. #331 reduced round trips for sessions that don't need writing (candidate window and fingerprint checks); sessions that do need writing still cost many sequential round trips each, across child-table deletes and the session, message, tool-call and usage inserts.

### Proposed solution

Send each write batch (the existing ~50-session chunk) in one round trip: queue every session's deletes and upserts in a pgx batch (or pipeline mode) and send it once, and use `COPY FROM` for `messages` and `tool_calls` (as #331 suggested). A first load over a high-latency link would then be limited by bandwidth instead of RTT × statement count. Incremental pushes are already fast and shouldn't change.

To reproduce and measure: push a few thousand sessions to a local PostgreSQL with added latency (for example `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 150ms`), and compare sessions per minute before and after.

### Alternatives considered

- Set-based deletes and inserts across the whole chunk (`DELETE ... WHERE session_id = ANY($1)`, multi-session `INSERT ... SELECT FROM unnest(...)`): fewer round trips without pipeline mode.
- Waiting it out: the slowdown is mostly a first-load and re-push problem, but it affects every hosted or remote machine (Muse Personal is collected on Meta's hosted machine, per `docs/configuration.md`).

title: Multi-word content search takes minutes when a single word takes seconds
body:
A multi-word content search over the last 30 days runs for more than 6 minutes on a long-used archive, while the same search for one word returns in 4.5 seconds. An agent asking AgentsView "which session said ask opus and fable" waited 14 minutes for an answer, and other requests timed out behind it because the search held one of the server's few read connections the whole time.

Multi-word searches should finish in about the time a single-word search does. The per-word ranking from https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3227 can narrow to the messages that hold the rarest word first, or to the trigram index the exact-phrase path already uses, before counting common words such as "and" or "ask" across every message in range. A search that still runs long should stop and free its connection, as https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3260 proposes.

Measured on build `7c47aec` (Linux, local SQLite, about 380,000 embedded messages), one request at a time against `/api/v1/search/content` with `date_from` 30 days back and `limit=20`:

| Pattern | Mode | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `fable` | substring | 4.5 s |
| `ask opus and fable` | substring | over 400 s (client gave up) |

The server log showed the earlier run of that search holding a read connection in `scanContentRows` for 5 min 17 s, and a regex search holding another for over 2 minutes, while the reader pool reported tens of thousands of requests waiting for one of its 4 connections.

title: fix(sync): fail source sync when a full resync is not installed
body:
Fixes #3389.

**Benefit for users:** `agentsview source sync --full` no longer reports success when its rebuild was thrown away. Before, if another program held a read transaction on `sessions.db`, such as an open `sqlite3` shell, the swap timed out and the rebuilt archive was discarded. Run without a daemon, the command still printed `Sync complete` and exited 0. Now it exits 1 and says why:

```
  Closing current database before swap stopped after 5.026s
fatal: another connection holds a read transaction on the archive, so its WAL checkpoint could not finish: full resync not installed, archive unchanged: final wal checkpoint: wal checkpoint busy
hint: close other programs reading sessions.db, such as a sqlite3 shell, then retry; run `agentsview source sync --help` for flags and examples
```

I ran the issue's reproduction against a scratch data directory with a built binary. With a `sqlite3` shell holding `BEGIN; SELECT ...`, the command printed the output above and exited 1. After the shell closed, the same command rebuilt the archive and exited 0.

## What changed

- **Engine (`internal/sync/engine.go`).** `resyncAllLocked` used to drop the swap error. `syncThenRunLocked` then ran an incremental pass whose stats replaced the failed resync's. Now an operational resync failure is returned from `SyncThenRun` and the incremental pass is skipped. The worker-backed daemon resync already did this: it surfaces "failed" builds and falls back only on a safety abort. The in-process path now matches. Safety aborts, such as a rebuild that found no sessions, still fall back as before.
- **Direct `source sync` (`cmd/agentsview/sync.go`).** `runLocalSync` used to write errors only to `debug.log`. It now returns them, and `doSync` exits through `fatal`, as the daemon branch already does. Unfinished attachment ingestion stays a warning, because the session history is already committed and later syncs retry it. A failed sync no longer prints the `Sync complete` summary, and its last progress phase reads "stopped after" instead of "completed in".
- **Hint.** A busy WAL checkpoint (`db.ErrWALCheckpointBusy`) gets its own message and hint instead of the `[[remote_hosts]]` hint. The daemon's sync error event now carries code `archive_busy` for this error, next to the existing `sync_running`, so the daemon path gives the same hint without matching error text. `openapi.yaml` and the generated client describe the new code.

## Behavior change to review

A direct `source sync` with no remote hosts now exits non-zero on any sync error it used to log and ignore, such as `local sync processing incomplete` or a canceled run. This is intended (the issue's step 4), but it can change the exit status of scripts that run the command.

## Limits

- With `[[remote_hosts]]` configured, a daemon sync runs the unified rebuild through `/sync/remotes`. That path turns any abort into `ErrUnifiedRebuildAborted` before it builds the response, so a busy checkpoint there still gets the generic unified-rebuild message. Carrying the code through needs a new error code in the remote-sync response, so it is left for a follow-up.
- The final checkpoint still gives up after the 5 s busy timeout. The issue's optional bounded retry is not included.

title: feat(usage): show the day's total in the cost over time tooltip
body:
## Why

On the Usage page, hovering a day on the "Cost over time" chart lists each
project, model, or agent for that day, but not the day's total. To see how much
a day cost in all, or how many tokens it used, you had to add the rows up by
hand. This adds that total to the tooltip. It is a user-facing improvement to
the Usage page.

## What it does now

- The tooltip shows a bold **Total** row right under the date, above the
  per-series breakdown, with a divider like the date header's.
- In cost mode it shows the day's total cost; in token mode, the day's total
  tokens. It works the same in the smooth, lines, and bars views, since all
  three draw the same stacked series.
- When only one series has usage that day, the total would repeat that row, so
  it is left out.
- The label is a new `usage_tooltip_total` message, added to every locale.

![Cost over time tooltip showing the Nov 5 total ($54.26) above project-delta ($53.83) and project-beta ($0.44), matching the Peak Day summary card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3afa0c35-f125-4464-aac7-34f3ca1da7cc)

## Design decisions

- **The total counts only what the chart draws.** It is the sum of the rows the
  tooltip lists. Series hidden by the project, model, or agent filters are not
  counted, so the total matches the height of the stack under the cursor. It
  can differ from the summary cards when filters hide series; I chose to match
  the chart because the tooltip describes the chart.
- **It sums the raw values, not the rounded rows.** Each row is rounded to the
  cent on display, so the total can differ by a cent from adding the displayed
  rows. Summing raw microdollars is exact and matches the "Peak Day" card for
  the same day.
- The rows and the total come from one derived list, so they cannot disagree.
  The existing per-row formatting moved into a small `fmtTooltipValue` helper
  that both use.

## Where to look

- `frontend/src/lib/components/usage/CostTimeSeriesChart.svelte`: the
  `tooltipRowsForPoint` and `tooltipTotal` derived values, the new tooltip
  markup, and the `.tooltip-total` styles.
- `CostTimeSeriesChart.test.ts`: four new cases covering the cost total, the
  token total, hidden series left out, and no total for a single series.

I ran it on my own local archive and the tooltip showed each day's total above
the breakdown. On the e2e fixture archive, hovering Nov 5 showed
`Total $54.26` above `project-delta $53.83` and `project-beta $0.44`, the same
figure as that day's "Peak Day" card.

title: Restricted archive_content rehashes the whole Claude transcript on every append
body:
## What happened

With `archive_content = "transcripts"` (or `"usage"`), each append to a Claude Code session file makes the daemon hash the whole file, twice. Long sessions that are kept alive with `/compact` grow to hundreds of MB, so every watcher event reads that much.

Observed on macOS arm64, v0.47.0, SQLite archive about 1 GB, about 2,300 sessions. One active session JSONL was 194 MB (16 compactions over three weeks), another 162 MB. From `debug.log`:

```
sync: changed paths: 1 path(s) matched 1 source(s): 1 updated ... 1 source(s) read to check their content (193.8 MiB); took 4.855s
sync: changed paths: 3 path(s) matched 3 source(s): 3 updated ... (51.3 MiB); took 4m48.992s
sync: changed paths: 23 path(s) matched 8 source(s): 4 updated ... (254.7 MiB); took 4m17.787s
db: InsertMessages (115 msgs): 49.546s (lock wait 0s)
sqlite reader pool: 34 requests waited 13.787s in total for one of 4 connections over the last 5m0s
```

While this ran, CLI reads failed with `local daemon owns the SQLite archive but is not responding`, because the 1 s `/api/ping` check timed out. `parser_checkpoints` had 0 rows.

v0.48.0 helps a lot (#3144, #3192, #3232, and `background_sync_interval`): the daemon went from about 38% CPU to near 0. But each sync of the active session still reads the whole file (`206.3 MiB ... took 10.757s` on the first sync after upgrading).

## Cause

Claude's append checkpoint (#2681) is turned off whenever `OmitsToolContent()` is true:

- `internal/sync/checkpoint.go:79` falls back to the full-source fingerprint (`claudeSourceSet.Fingerprint`, `internal/parser/claude_provider.go:835`).
- `internal/sync/engine_incremental.go:567` skips the resumable hash, so the hash to store is recomputed from offset 0 (`ComputeFileHashPrefix`, `internal/sync/hash.go:65`).
- `internal/sync/checkpoint.go:364`, `internal/db/checkpoint.go:147`, `internal/db/messages.go:1820` and `:2593` drop or delete the checkpoint.

The reason is in #1564: "Restricted Codex archives omit parser checkpoints whose resumable hash state can contain source bytes." That is true: `crypto/sha256`'s `MarshalBinary` keeps the unprocessed tail of the current 64-byte block, up to 63 source bytes.

## Proposal

For Claude, keep checkpoints in restricted modes, but save the hash state only at a 64-byte boundary.

- At an offset that is a multiple of 64, the SHA-256 block buffer is empty, so the marshaled state holds only the chaining values and the length. No source bytes are stored.
- Save the state at `floor(offset/64)*64`. On the next append, re-read the at most 63 bytes from that boundary to the old offset from the file, then continue hashing the new bytes.
- Claude's checkpoint cursor is already empty (`engine_incremental.go:590`), and the tail anchor is a digest. So the hash state is the only blob that could hold source bytes.
- Codex keeps the current behavior, because its cursor carries parser state.

A quick check with Go 1.27 `crypto/sha256`: marshaling after 100 bytes contains source bytes, after 128/192/256 bytes it does not, and resuming from the 192-byte state gives the same digest as hashing the whole input.

Tests I would add:

1. In `transcripts` mode, two appends read about the appended size, not the file size.
2. The stored hash-state blob contains no source bytes. Hash a known marker string and assert the blob does not contain it.

If this direction works for you, I can send a PR. If you prefer another approach, for example a size plus tail-digest check without a resumable hash in restricted modes, that would also fix it for us.

title: fix(events): keep the shared events stream open when a watched session changes
body:
Hosted users keep their session tabs and archive updates live when one watched session changes revision. Today that revision change ends the shared `/api/v1/events` connection, so every open session tab disconnects and archive updates pause until the client reconnects.

This follows up https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3302, which moved tabs onto one shared events stream. That change means one session's revision can now interrupt every tab.

Now only the changed session's watch reacts:
- If the session still resolves, its existing monitor reports the update with `session_updated` and keeps watching from the new revision.
- If it no longer resolves, the stream sends `session_missing` for that ID and stops watching it until the client reconnects.

Other session watches and `data_changed` events continue on the same connection. `session_missing` can now arrive mid-stream as well as at connect time, and `docs/session-api.md` documents this.

Needed by https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3403

title: fix(live): skip unchanged tab refetches on matching handoff markers
body:
When you navigate in one of several open tabs, a healthy shared-stream handoff now skips refetching in unchanged session tabs whose readiness marker matches. Before, each handoff replayed readiness to every tab, so unchanged ones refetched their transcript, session, and child sessions. One handoff on a SQLite subset of three archived parents and five children (522 messages):

| HTTP requests from the unchanged tab | Before → After |
|---|---|
| Transcript | 1 → 0 |
| Session detail | 2 → 0 |
| Child sessions | 1 → 0 |

The tab whose session changed still reloads, and archive handoffs keep the behavior accepted in https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3302. On SQLite, the server reads the parent and its direct children in one query to build the marker. Child-list and timing reads stayed at one each. Hosted watch-state costs were not measured.

`/api/v1/events` adds an SSE `id` to `session_ready` and versioned `session_updated`. It hashes session and child versions plus watch state where available. It is empty when a required read fails, and an empty marker or stream error means tabs refetch. The BroadcastChannel fallback stops its one-second heartbeat in tabs with no subscriptions. A six-minute Chrome 158 run, fallback leader hidden:

- One stream for the two visible sessions in all 359 samples.
- No subscription heartbeats from the hidden leader.
- A database write refreshed only its own session.
- The returning tab rejoined the same stream.

title: fix(parser): wait for initializing Codex state index tables
body:
## TL;DR

**User-facing benefit and developer experience:** The SessionStart launcher hook now waits when Codex is still creating or migrating `state_5.sqlite`, and `TestCaptureLaunchParentCodexIndexAppears/index` no longer flakes with `no such table: _sqlx_migrations`. `CodexIndexedSessionKey` now checks `sqlite_master` before reading `_sqlx_migrations` and `threads`, returning an `os.ErrNotExist` error until both tables exist.

## Why

Codex opens `state_5.sqlite` with `create_if_missing(true)` before SQLx creates `_sqlx_migrations` and runs the migrations that create `threads`. Querying either table in that window returned a SQLite schema error (`no such table: _sqlx_migrations` or `no such table: threads`), which `recordLaunchParent` treated as fatal and aborted launcher linking. The same race hit `TestCaptureLaunchParentCodexIndexAppears/index` on CI (for example, Windows CI run `45590917235`), because the test's 300ms `synctest` wait aligned with the hook's 100ms + 200ms retry tick while `testutil.WriteCodexState` was between its `CREATE TABLE` statements.

## Reviewer notes

- **Future migrations stay rejected.** `CodexIndexedSessionKey` checks `MAX(version) > 64` in `_sqlx_migrations` before checking whether `threads` exists, so a future schema still falls back immediately to the thread ID.
- **Corrupt files still fail.** A non-SQLite file still fails when `sqlite_master` is queried.
- **Atomic test fixture.** `testutil.WriteCodexState` writes to a temporary file and installs it with `atomicfile.Replace`, and `TestCaptureLaunchParentCodexIndexAppears` waits 250ms so the hook goroutine is durably parked during fixture updates.
- **Limit.** If `state_5.sqlite` remains uninitialized past the hook's 1s missing-index window, `recordLaunchParent` falls back to the bare Codex thread ID.

title: fix(daemon): wait for background startup to release its start lock
body:
## TL;DR

**User-facing benefit:** Running `agentsview daemon restart` or `agentsview daemon stop` right after a background start no longer fails with a false `startup is still in progress` error. Background launchers now wait for the child daemon to release its start lock after writing its runtime record, before releasing `serve.background.lock` and returning.

## Why

During startup, a background server writes its runtime record and then calls `UnmarkDaemonStarting` to delete `startup-state.json` and unlock the start lock. `waitForBackgroundServeReadyWithPolicy` previously returned as soon as `FindWritableDaemonRuntime` saw the runtime record, so the parent released `serve.background.lock` while `IsDaemonStarting` was still true. A command that acquired `serve.background.lock` during that handoff window saw `IsDaemonStarting` as true and failed with `startup is still in progress; runtime publication may have failed`, as seen in `TestRestartDeploymentAuthSaveAuthority/background/external_restart_with_auth`.

## How

`probeBackgroundServeReady` checks both `FindWritableDaemonRuntime` and `IsDaemonStarting` in the readiness loop and timeout reprobe. Normal runtime records wait for `IsDaemonStarting` to clear, matching `waitForExternalServeStartup` and foreground startup. Startup-state fallback runtimes still return immediately because they intentionally keep the start lock as their active marker.

title: fix(sync): prevent split-brain broadcast leadership across tabs
body:
## TL;DR

**Benefit for users:** Open session tabs using BroadcastChannel live updates no longer open duplicate `/api/v1/events` streams or trigger extra transcript reloads when a new tab loads slowly. `LiveBroadcast` now elects a single leader with Web Locks, and `LiveHub` batches port registration on leader start and failover.

## Why

In WebKit CI ([e2e webkit job](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45504766955/job/138837164535)), `frontend/e2e/shared-live.spec.ts` (`fallback: broadcast`) failed when a follower tab sent a second `/messages` request while another session updated (`Expected: 1, Received: 2`). Tracing WebKit showed that during slow page loads, WebKit fired a new tab's 200 ms election timer before delivering queued `BroadcastChannel` replies from the active leader. The new tab briefly elected itself leader and opened its own `/api/v1/events` stream alongside the leader's combined stream, delivering a second `session_ready` after the initial watch gate had cleared.

## How

- **Web Locks leader election (`frontend/src/lib/api/liveBroadcast.ts`).** Tabs with active subscriptions coordinate leadership through `navigator.locks` so only one tab opens `/api/v1/events` at a time, and closing the leader hands off leadership immediately. The lock holder ignores frames a previous leader sent before the handoff, so the new leader keeps its stream open. A 1 s idle grace period avoids leadership churn on brief visibility toggles while still stopping the heartbeat timer when idle. Environments without Web Locks keep the `BroadcastChannel` election fallback, stepping down immediately when a superior leader appears and dropping frames from inferior senders.
- **Batched leader sync (`frontend/src/lib/api/liveHub.ts`).** `LiveHub.batch()` lets `LiveBroadcast` register all known peer ports before opening one combined `/api/v1/events` stream on leader start or failover, avoiding a throwaway single-session stream on the first port.

## Reviewer notes

- **Limits.** Non-secure HTTP origins (where `navigator.locks` is unavailable) still use the `BroadcastChannel` election fallback, though immediate step-down and sender checks prevent two hubs from delivering duplicate frames to the same tab.
- **Scope after rebase.** Marker-based `session_ready` suppression in `LiveHub` and `/api/v1/events` already landed in #3403; the rebased diff keeps that marker handoff intact and limits changes to `LiveBroadcast` leadership and `LiveHub.batch()`.

## Links

- [Failing WebKit CI job](https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/actions/runs/45504766955/job/138837164535)
- Related prior work: #3374, #3403

title: fix(parser): count unmirrored Codex usage records
body:
## Summary

Codex sessions now count every model response's usage once. Before, a
response whose `token_usage_record` had no matching `token_count` lost
its tokens, and reasoning tokens were never stored.

## Motivation

Codex writes a `token_usage_record` for each response and usually repeats
the same per-call counters in the next `token_count`, often after
`response_item` lines. Only TraeX read records.

- **Records count for every Codex-family agent.** Each record stays
  pending until the next usage event. A `token_count` with the same
  per-call counters is the record's mirror and is skipped. Any other
  `token_count` counts.
- **Dedup.** Records dedupe on their counters plus `response_id`, including
  when a repeated record follows its mirrored `token_count`. Records without
  a response ID dedupe on their counters. Repeated `token_count` events still
  dedupe on the whole `info` object.
- **Reasoning.** `reasoning_output_tokens` is stored as
  `reasoning_tokens`. It is part of `output_tokens`, and
  `ModelRates.CostForTokensScoped` bills it only when output is zero
  (#2980), so it is not charged twice.
- **Incremental parses.** The cursor checkpoint moves to version 8 and
  keeps the pending state, record digest, and response ID, so an append that
  splits a record from its mirror matches a full parse. An older checkpoint
  makes the next append a full parse.
- **Data version 190** re-parses Codex, TraeX, Augure Code and Open
  Interpreter. Sessions without records parse as before. TraeX and Augure
  Code rows with reasoning output now also carry `reasoning_tokens`.

| One large local Codex rollout (25,737 records) | `main` | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Uncached input tokens | 103,584,641 | 103,592,168 |
| Output tokens | 8,111,077 | 8,111,351 |
| Cache-read tokens | 4,063,263,360 | 4,063,408,512 |
| Reasoning tokens | 0 | 2,690,798 |

The rollout has one record with no mirror, and the difference from
`main` is exactly that response's usage. Its reasoning total matches the
sum of `reasoning_output_tokens` across all records.
`parse-diff --agent codex --fail-on-change` reports 0 changed sessions.

Tests cover a mirror with and without lines in between, a lone record,
repeated records, equal counters from different responses, a repeated
`token_count` after a mirror, an incremental parse split between record
and mirror, and the version 8 checkpoint round trip.

## Verification

- `make build-release` passed.
- `TMPDIR=/private/tmp GOMAXPROCS=4 go test -tags fts5 -count=1 -p 4 ./internal/parser/... ./internal/db/...` passed for parser, db, and db/git.
- `TMPDIR=/private/tmp GOMAXPROCS=4 go vet -tags fts5 ./internal/parser/... ./internal/db/...` passed.
- An isolated full sync of a copy of the rollout matched the target totals exactly.
- `parse-diff --agent codex --fail-on-change` reported 1 examined, 1 identical, and 0 changed.
- The source rollout's size, mtime, and SHA-256 were unchanged before and after verification.
- `golangci-lint` was not run because the repository's `kennnolint` plugin is unavailable.

Stack fit: uses the repository's existing Go parser, SQLite, Makefile, and test conventions. No new dependencies or services.

title: fix(search): bound local content search waits
body:
Local SQLite substring, regex, and terms searches stop after two minutes and free the reader. Hybrid search applies the same bound to its keyword phase, after semantic search.

Repeated broad local searches exceeded the client timeout, even when one search returned in seconds.

The deadline also covers time spent waiting for a reader connection or a bulk-read slot.
- FTS-mode and semantic-only searches keep their existing waits.
- CLI and MCP follow-up searches share the first search's keyword deadline.
- The API returns HTTP 504 when a scan times out.
- If MCP's optional total-count scan times out, MCP still returns the sized first page, without a total.

Refs https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3394

title: Archive-wide substring search scans tool content
body:
AgentsView's archive-wide substring search can take seconds or minutes even when it returns only a small page.

Give tool input and result text a selective substring candidate index that stays current as transcripts change, then apply exact matching to those candidates. This lets agents search tool activity across an archive without reading every tool body.

The current substring path defaults to messages, tool inputs, and tool results, and also searches thinking text. Its trigram candidate index covers message and thinking text, while tool sources use `LIKE`; searches walk sessions until they fill the page. One representative archive-wide single-word replay took 15.9 seconds, and transcript waits reached 7.3 minutes.

This targets single-word searches over tool content. Multi-word search work is tracked at https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3394, and the wider MCP lookup benchmark is tracked at https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3287.

title: Archive-wide regex search scans the full scope
body:
AgentsView's archive-wide regex search can take a minute or more even with a date window and a small result limit.

Derive safe required literals from the regex, use them to select candidate rows from an index, and apply the exact regex only to those candidates. Keep a bounded fallback for patterns with no usable literal.

In a 30-day transcript sample, 94 archive-wide regex calls had a 58-second median and a 30-minute worst case; 70 patterns had no literal prefix, and 72 had fewer than three prefix characters. Most already had a date window of 30 days or less. A median-nearest archive replay took 71.7 seconds. Current regex search uses only a literal prefix as its SQL prefilter, and scans the full scope when the pattern has no prefix.

This targets regex candidate planning. Search time bounds are tracked at https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3260 and https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/pull/3415. Multi-word substring search is tracked separately at https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3394.

title: Devin: sync pass hard-fails on sessions.db row with no messages and no cli\transcripts\<id>.json
body:
## Summary

A Devin-Desktop session row in `%APPDATA%\devin\cli\sessions.db` that has **zero parseable messages** AND no `cli\transcripts\<id>.json` file fails the entire `agentsview sync` pass, every run — one bad row out of 2499 sessions poisons the sync.

## Mechanism (v0.46.1, verified against `main` `internal/parser/devin.go`)

1. `parseDevinSession` stats `cli/transcripts/<id>.json` — absent for this session.
2. Falls back to `parseDevinSessionFromMessageNodes`, which returns `ok=false` when `len(messages)==0` (~line 456).
3. Caller emits `missing devin transcript <id>` and the worker pass reports `failed`.

## Trigger (real-world)

`mangrove-truck` — a ghost session row created 2026-11-07T00:34:19Z, `created_at == last_activity_at`, 0 `message_nodes`, title from a session that never ran. It was the only row in 2499 sessions to fail; every sync pass reported `1 sessions synced, 1 failed`.

## Suggestion

Treat the no-transcript + zero-message case as a **skip / zero-message session** rather than a pass failure — the `sessions.db` row itself carries complete metadata (title, timestamps, cwd, backend_type), so ingesting a `message_count=0` record is faithful and keeps the pass healthy.

## Verified workaround

Writing a minimal transcript `{"steps":[],"agent":{"model_name":"..."},"timestamps":{...}}` to `cli\transcripts\<id>.json` unblocks the pass — sync then reports `2499 sessions synced, 0 failed` and ingests the ghost row with `message_count=0`.

## Environment

- agentsview v0.46.1 (2026-10-23 build) — parser behavior unchanged through v0.48.0
- Windows 11, Devin Desktop (current build, `cli\sessions.db` + `acp-messages\` layout — no `cli\transcripts\` dir written by the runtime)

title: feat(sessions): link launched runs without setup hooks
body:
If you run `codex exec` or `claude -p` from a Claude Code or Codex session, the run now shows under that session even if you never ran `agentsview agent setup`.

- Before, without the SessionStart hook that setup installs, the run listed as its own top-level session.
- On the next sync, the run nests in the launching session's Subagents group, and `get_child_sessions` returns it.
- Runs archived before this change link too. A Codex launcher needs its transcript file for this, since that file records the folder each command ran in.
- A run links only when exactly one session launched it, on the same machine, in the run's folder, within 60 seconds before the run started.
- A run stays at the top level when another session might have launched it. Examples are a nearby `$BIN exec` or `sudo "$BIN" exec`, or a `cd` that may have failed.
- Printed text such as `echo 'codex exec'` or `git commit -m "codex notes"` doesn't count as a launch.
- A link recorded by the hook or `agentsview session parent` always wins over an inferred one.

The design choice was which clears should stop inference. Say a user clears the link on run R under session P:

- If only clearing an inferred link blocks inference, clearing a hook's link is undone on the next sync, because P's command still points at R.
- If any clear blocks, R stays without a parent until someone sets one again, such as with `agentsview session parent`.
- This PR blocks on any clear, so a link the user clears stays cleared.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark, 1440 × 900 CSS px viewport, 420 × 280 CSS px crop at 2× | ![Launched run listed as its own session, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a89cc581-ff49-4e33-8a32-89b7c3a9f1f3) | ![Launched run nested under its launcher's Subagents group, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf614dfc-725b-4031-a906-cd2c9985e4e4) |
| Light, 1440 × 900 CSS px viewport, 420 × 280 CSS px crop at 2× | ![Launched run listed as its own session, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5301bb2-84fa-4bd5-83a5-ef407f0a558a) | ![Launched run nested under its launcher's Subagents group, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06db0051-6ad6-4eeb-8917-a36aaf496207) |

This changes the schema and data version:

- `session_external_parents` gets an `inferred` column.
- A new `session_parent_inference_blocks` table records clears.
- `tool_calls` gets a `working_directory` column.
- `dataVersion` goes to 190, so older binaries refuse an upgraded archive.
- Inferred links don't carry over when the archive is rebuilt, and the new archive works them out again. Clears and recorded links carry over.

title: fix(activity): count automated headless reviews as automated
body:
## TL;DR

Automated headless Claude Code and Codex runs, such as Roborev review panels, were counted as **Subagents** in Activity reports and charts. They now count as **Automated**, and real subagents stay in Subagents. Existing SQLite and PostgreSQL archives update on open without reparsing transcripts.

## Why

Parentless `claude -p` runs (`entrypoint = "sdk-cli"`) and `codex exec` runs (`session_kind = "non-interactive"`) were always stored as `relationship_type = "subagent"`. Activity checks for subagents before it checks `is_automated`, so automated Claude reviews landed in Subagents. Roborev's oversized-diff prompt handoff (`Read the complete task prompt from "..."`) and sessions launched with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=roborev` were not recognized as automated at all.

## How

- **Matching.** `IsAutomatedSessionMetadata` also checks `entrypoint == "roborev"`, and the handoff prefix joins the built-in automated prefixes.
- **Which runs move.** an automated, parentless run moves to Automated only when its subagent role was guessed from its headless shape (`relationship_inferred`) and no spawner or launcher ever linked it (`spawn_linked`). Both are new columns, written when the session is stored. Grok children that their summary marks as subagents, and children whose launcher was later deleted, stay in Subagents.
- **Moving back.** `parser_relationship_type` keeps the original role, so a run returns to Subagents when its automation pattern is removed or it grows past one user turn.
- **PostgreSQL.** PostgreSQL gets the same three columns and the same rule. A one-time full push fills them for existing rows. The automation audit marks only the row versions it checked, so a push that lands during an audit is checked on the next run.
- **Export.** Export sends the relationship the importing machine's parser would produce, so the importer applies its own automation rules. The manifest format is unchanged.
- **Backfill.** `classifierAlgorithmVersion` 4 reclassifies existing archives on open and bumps `local_modified_at` so pushes pick up the changes.

On real data, `agentsview report activity` over an isolated archive of five real Claude review transcripts reported 5 automated, 0 subagents, and 0 interactive sessions. The transcripts covered panel members, a custom template in `[automated] prefixes`, and an oversized-diff handoff.

## Reviewer notes

- **Start here.** `SessionRelationship` and `isParentlessHeadlessWorker` in `internal/db/sessions.go`, `reconcileParentlessWorkers` in `internal/db/automated_audit.go`, and `clearableHeadlessWorkerPG` in `internal/postgres/automated_audit.go`. These must agree.
- **No parser data-version bump.** The new facts live in an unexported `db.Session` field and columns computed at write time, so `TestParsedOutputMatchesDataVersion` is unchanged.
- **Known limits.** Grok headless sessions stored before this change keep Subagents until a Grok reparse. A spawn record does not travel with an export. Sessions written through hosted raw projection carry no spawn record.

Model used: Gemini 4 Neon, Claude Opus 5.5

Co-authored-by: Antigravity <noreply@google.com>

title: perf(postgres): pipeline new sessions' writes in pg push
body:
`replica pg push` is limited by round trips on a slow or distant link: each new session waits on about 20 sequential statements. In https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3393, a first push of about 3,700 sessions over a relayed tunnel ran at about 20 sessions a minute, or 3 hours.

User-facing benefit: people who load a PostgreSQL replica over such a link now get new sessions pushed about 40 times faster. With 100 ms of added latency, 100 new sessions push in 5.5 s instead of 225 s. Incremental pushes of sessions already in PostgreSQL take the same time as before.

| Push time, 100 new sessions of 20 messages | 20 ms latency | 100 ms latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Later push | 51 s → 1.6 s (32x) | 225 s → 5.5 s (41x) |
| Target's first push | 58 s → 6.9 s (8.4x) | 248 s → 28 s (8.9x) |

What changed:

- Writes for each group of up to 50 sessions PostgreSQL has no row for go out as one pipelined pgx batch.
- The batch runs the existing writers and SQL. It skips only reads that cannot match a new session, and reads existence, exclusions, and published commit links once per group.
- Sessions keep their order: queued writes are sent before any session that takes the old path.
- The batch sends early once it holds 8 MiB, so a long transcript is not buffered whole.

Safety:

- The batched session upsert only inserts, so a row another push created meanwhile is never overwritten.
- The last batch rechecks exclusions for every ID a session can be purged under.
- Any conflict or failed statement rolls the group back and rewrites it one statement at a time, as before.

Not covered:

- Changed sessions already in PostgreSQL, including `--full` re-pushes, keep the one-statement-at-a-time path.

`COPY FROM` lost because messages and tool calls already go out as one multi-row insert per session, so it barely cuts round trips. The table comes from a benchmark that pushes through a TCP proxy adding fixed latency to a local PostgreSQL 16. A first push also includes about 200 round trips of one-time setup, such as model pricing, that this change leaves alone.

Reviewer attention is most valuable on `pushBatchAttempt` in `internal/postgres/push.go` and the new `internal/postgres/push_new_session_batch.go`.

Fixes https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3393

Model used: Opus 5.5

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix(parser): classify Muse Personal runs as automated or subagent
body:
Muse Personal stores the runs Muse starts itself in the same transcript format as conversations, so AgentsView shows every one of them as a conversation. On one installation, Muse started 3,834 of 3,939 sessions itself: scheduled jobs, upkeep passes, delegated tasks, and subagents.

User-facing benefit: Muse users see their own conversations by default, without writing `[automated]` patterns. Before, those 3,834 runs crowded session lists, counts, and search, and a hand-written pattern list missed scheduled runs that received an injected follow-up.

What changed:

- **Run type from `source`.** AgentsView reads the top-level `source` of each session's first user item, in sequence order, not the first item, which can be a context stamp.
- **Scheduled jobs and upkeep are Automated.** `scheduler.cron`, `runtime.action`, `runtime.self_improvement`, `runtime.feed`, and `runtime.proactivity` get the new `muse-background` kind, which counts as automated at any message count, like roborev.
- **Delegated work and subagents are Subagent workers.** `runtime.browser_input`, plain `runtime` whose first line is one of the two delegated-assignment openers, and plain `runtime` whose first line is the `[Subagent Context]` banner use the existing `non-interactive` kind, so they stay searchable as subordinate content.
- **Subagent runs nest under their requester.** Muse records no structured parent, but the banner is followed by a `- Requester agent id:` line, and each Muse Personal agent owns one session with the same ID. The envelope's `Your session` line is ignored because it names the run itself in only 87 of 128 cases.
- **Existing archives reparse in place.** Data version 190 reparses Muse Personal sources and keeps session IDs. No other provider is touched.
- **Synthetic sample data.** `internal/parser/testdata/muse_personal/sources/` has one sample per run type, as asked in the issue.

Scheduled jobs count as Automated rather than Subagent: Muse runs them over a hundred times a day with no parent, and parentless Subagents appear as sidebar roots and get embedded.

On the real archive, the rule gives 3,536 Automated, 298 Subagent, 100 Interactive, and 5 sessions with no user item, with no conversation in the first two groups and all 128 subagent requesters resolving. The issue's earlier count of about 2,580 missed `message_parts` items.

Not covered:

- Delegated runs record no parent, so they appear as sidebar roots.
- If Muse rewords an opener or the banner, those runs fall back to conversations.
- Sessions whose transcripts are gone keep their old classification.
- A machine on an older build that opens a shared PostgreSQL database can clear the automated flag until every machine upgrades.

`TestServeRestartServesSessionsBeforeStartupSync` now rewinds to the newest data version that reparses Claude, since a Muse-only version broke it.

Open question for maintainers: would you rather treat scheduled jobs as headless workers too? That is a one-line change.

Reviewer attention is most valuable on the first-user-item rule and the requester parent link in `internal/parser/muse_personal.go`.

Fixes https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/issues/3392

title: perf(sync): keep append checkpoints when archive_content is restricted
body:
With `archive_content = "transcripts"`, appends to long Claude Code sessions and Codex rollouts no longer cost a full-file read. Only the appended bytes are hashed once a session has a checkpoint, as in full mode (#2681). With `"usage"`, this applies to Claude only. Long sessions kept alive with `/compact` reach hundreds of MB, and on those every watcher event used to read the whole file twice.

## What changed

Restricted modes turned off parser checkpoints because a `crypto/sha256` resume state buffers the input after the last 64-byte block, which is up to 63 transcript bytes (#1564). At an offset that is a multiple of 64 that buffer is empty, so the marshaled state holds only the chaining values and the byte count.

- In restricted modes, the database rewinds the saved hash state to `floor(offset/64)*64` when it writes the checkpoint. The chaining values already cover every complete block, so `blockAlignedSHA256State` only clears the buffer and rounds the count down, with no extra read. The sync engine does not track this: on the next append the gate takes the state's offset from its own byte count (`db.SHA256StateOffset`), re-reads the at most 63 bytes from there to the committed offset, checks that this reproduces the stored digest, and continues through the new bytes in the same read. A changed byte in that window rejects the checkpoint.
- Claude's checkpoint has no cursor, and the tail anchor is a digest.
- A Codex cursor (`codexCursorState`) holds the model, reasoning effort, service tier, cwd, agent path, two digests, a few flags, the last task event (`task_started`, `task_complete`, or `turn_aborted`), and the IDs, names, and positions of up to eight pending tool calls. It never holds message text or tool input or output. Transcript archives already store all of these fields, so they now keep Codex checkpoints.
- Usage archives store no tool call names or IDs except for subagent calls, so they still keep no Codex checkpoint.
- The database decides what restricted archives store. Every checkpoint write goes through `upsertParserCheckpointTx`, which aligns the state and then checks it with `ParserCheckpointBlobs.keptUnder`. A payload passes only when its hash state is a SHA-256 state at a block boundary with an all-zero block buffer, and its cursor is empty or, in transcript archives, decodes as a current Codex cursor (`parser.IsCodexCursor`). Otherwise the write deletes the session's checkpoint. Unknown encodings are refused. Usage-only clearing applies the same check to stored rows.

## Tradeoffs and limits

- Full mode stores the same blobs as before, and the append gate still opens the file once. Because a state's offset comes from the state, checkpoints written under one policy keep resuming after a switch to the other.
- A restricted resume re-reads up to 63 bytes already hashed.
- No schema or data-version change. Restricted archives have no checkpoints today. For Claude, the first append after upgrade reads the file once to create one, as full mode already does. For Codex, the next full parse creates one.
- After a full archive switches to a restricted mode, its existing checkpoints, raw trailing bytes included, stay until the session next changes, as before this change. That write stores a block-aligned state, or drops the checkpoint where the policy keeps none: Codex checkpoints in usage archives are removed by usage-only clearing.
- The block-boundary check depends on the `crypto/sha256` binary encoding. If Go changes it, the check fails closed and restricted archives go back to full reads.

## Where to look

- `internal/db/checkpoint.go`: `upsertParserCheckpointTx`, `keptUnder`, `SHA256StateOffset`, and `blockAlignedSHA256State`.
- `internal/sync/checkpoint.go`: `checkpointKept` (the read gate) and `resumeHashDigests`.
- `internal/sync/engine_incremental.go`: the resume starts at the offset the stored state records.
- `internal/sync/claude_checkpoint_test.go` and `internal/sync/codex_restricted_checkpoint_test.go`: a marker line at offset 63 mod 64 lands in the full-mode state and stays out of the restricted state. Two appends read no file content for the freshness check. The Claude tests also cover a committed offset on a block boundary and a same-size rewrite between the boundary and the offset, which the gate rejects.
- `internal/db/checkpoint_test.go`: restricted upserts and incremental writes store states aligned, and delete the checkpoint for unknown state encodings and unknown cursors.

## Real data

I copied a 194 MiB Claude Code session and a 5.8 MiB Codex rollout into scratch data dirs with `archive_content = "transcripts"`, ran `serve`, and appended three batches of lines taken from the end of the same file. "Read" is the changed-path log's "read to check their content" figure.

| Session | Binary | Append 1 | Append 2 | Append 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude, 194 MiB | main | 194.4 MiB read, 955 ms | 194.4 MiB, 825 ms | 194.4 MiB, 1.341 s |
| Claude, 194 MiB | this branch | 194.4 MiB, 818 ms (creates the checkpoint) | 0 B, 533 ms | 0 B, 376 ms |
| Codex, 5.8 MiB | main | 5.8 MiB, 208 ms | 5.8 MiB, 92 ms | 5.8 MiB, 21 ms |
| Codex, 5.8 MiB | this branch | 0 B, 337 ms | 0 B, 46 ms | 0 B, 26 ms |

On main, each Claude append also re-hashes the file from offset 0 to store the new hash. The files were in the page cache for these runs. The issue's machine, with a 1 GB archive under write contention, took seconds to minutes per pass. In both stored states the block buffer was all zeros and the byte count was a multiple of 64, and the stored hash matched the file.

Closes #3400

title: feat(embeddings): switch servers with one command
body:
Semantic search users can switch embedding servers in one command, replacing config edits and restarts. It rebuilds messages and Recall when enabled and waits for direct builds when the daemon is off.

```
agentsview index embeddings switch https://embed.example/v1 \
  --model embeddinggemma --dimension 768 \
  --api-key-file ~/.config/agentsview/api-key
```

`switch` keeps the same model's recipe and limits; new models get defaults. It reuses vectors only when model, dimension, and recipe match, and saves config after a successful server check.

On a scratch archive holding one copied local session, it saved a local endpoint, restarted the daemon, and built the message index. Before shows a full rebuild, and `switch` runs a plain build.

title: perf(search): narrow regex search by its required text
body:
People searching a SQLite archive with a regex that requires selective fixed text now get results in seconds, even when it opens with a boundary or case flag.

SQLite search now uses fixed text from anywhere in the pattern; PostgreSQL and ClickHouse still use only the prefix. Median times on a real SQLite archive, default sources, identical results:

| Pattern shape | 30 days (s) | All time (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required literal | 72 → 1.8 (41x) | 68 → 1.9 (36x) |
| No match | 140 → 9.2 (15x) | |
| Short prefix | 29 → 9.0 (3.2x) | 58 → 13 (4.6x) |
| Case-folded | 45 → 30 (1.5x) | 46 → 29 (1.6x) |

A literal plus digits slowed from 7.0 s to 8.4 s (30 days) and 12 s to 14 s (all time). SQLite regexes without usable fixed text still scan in batches, bounded by the two-minute local deadline.

Closes #3417
